questions.explanation: Only 1. Statement 2 - Incorrect: Dhrupad, Khayal, Tappa, Chaturang, Dhamar are styles of Hindustani Music, not Carnatic.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: Which of the following is called the cyclic arrangement of time units in Hindustani Classical music?
questions.explanation: Tala. Jati is the classification of a Raag based on the number of notes employed in its Aaroh and Avroh. The Raga is a melodic scale composed of basic seven notes. The exposition preceding the composed verses is called alap. The major vocal forms associated with Hindustani classical music are the khayal, dhrupad, dhammar, Tarana and thumri.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Carnatic Music: 1. Padam in Carnatic music is a lyrical composition, usually in the form of a love poem, often expressing devotion or deep emotions. 2. Padam in Carnatic music is primarily a patriotic poem sung to praise the motherland. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1. A type of lyrical composition that often deals with themes of love, devotion, or emotions. It is known for its expressive and emotive qualities. Some key terminologies: raga, tala, krithi, varnam, pallavi, anupallavi, charanam, alapana, javali, tillana, swaram.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: Which statement about Syama Sastri is correct?

options.a: His famous composition is Pancharatna Kritis.
options.c: A crater on planet mercury is named after him.
options.d: He is one among the trinity of Carnatic Music.

questions.answer_text: He is one among the trinity of Carnatic Music.
questions.explanation: The Trinity of Carnatic Music are also known as the three Jewels of Carnatic Music. They are credited with creating a new era in Carnatic music history by bringing about a noticeable change in the existing tradition. Tyagaraja: A Telugu composer known for his Pancharatna Kritis. Muthuswami Dikshitar: A Sanskrit and Manipravalam composer. Syama Sastri: A Telugu and Sanskrit composer.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: How many basic talams are there in Indian Classical Carnatic music?
questions.explanation: 7 talas in Carnatic music: Dhruva, Matya, Jampa, Ata, Triputa, Rupaka, Eka. Carnatic Music: Composed of a system of Ragam (Raga) and Thalam (Tala), it has a rich history and tradition. It developed in states of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: Consider the following statements about folk traditions of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh: 1. questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: What is Miyan ki Todi in Hindustani music ?
questions.explanation: Raag. Miyan ki Todi, often simply referred to as Todi or Darbari Todi is a Hindustani classical raga which gave its name to the Todi thaat, one of the ten types of classical music according to the musicologist Bhatkhande. Ragas from the Todi raganga (class of ragas) include Bilaskhani Todi, Gujari Todi (also called Gurjari Todi), Desi Todi, Hussaini Todi, Asavari Todi and Bahaduri Todi.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Indian folk music: 1. Maand is a folk music tradition of Gujarat, mainly performed during Navaratri with sticks (dandiyas). 2. Lavani is a folk music and dance form of Rajasthan, developed in the royal courts of Jaipur. Which of the above statements is/are correct?

Statement 2 – Incorrect: Lavani is from Maharashtra, not Rajasthan. It is known for its powerful rhythm and expressive dance style.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: In which Gharana do singers perform the Khandhar Vani and Gauhar Vani?
questions.explanation: Darbhanga Gharana. It originated in Darbhanga, Bihar in the 17th-century. It is a gharana of the Hindustani classical music dhrupad thought to have been started by Radhakrishna and Kartaram. Gauhar vani developed the raga or unadorned melodic figures. The Dagarvani emphasized melodic curves and graces. The Khandar vani specialised in quick ornamentation of the notes.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: To which Hindustani music Gharana are the Gundecha brothers related?

Hindustani Music Gharanas and founders: Gwalior (Nanthan Khan); Agra (Hajisujan Khan); Rangeela (Faiyyaz Khan); Jaipur Atrauli (Alladiya Khan); Kirana (Abdul Wahid Khan).

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: Which architectural style is best described by the following features: ribbed vaults, pointed arches, flying buttresses, and stained-glass windows ?
questions.explanation: Gothic. The Gothic style of architecture originated in Europe and is characterized by ribbed vaults, pointed arches, flying buttresses, and stained-glass windows. European colonists, especially the British, introduced the Gothic style in India during the colonial period. This style merged with Indian elements, resulting in the Indo-Gothic (Victorian) style. Indo-Gothic (Victorian) Style Features: Large and elaborate constructions with thinner walls than Indo-Islamic. Pointed arches instead of curved ones. Spacious windows and cruciform (cross-shaped) church plans. Use of modern materials like steel, iron, and poured concrete. Examples: Victoria Memorial (Kolkata), Gateway of India (Mumbai), Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (Mumbai).

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a monument with its architectural style?
questions.explanation: Qutub Minar - Indo-Islamic. The Khajuraho Temples belong to the Nagara style of Hindu temple architecture, not French. The Qutub Minar in Delhi, built by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and completed by Iltutmish, is an outstanding example of Indo-Islamic architecture combining Islamic motifs with Indian craftsmanship. The India Gate in New Delhi was designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens and reflects the Indo-European/Colonial style, not Rajput. The Lotus Temple, built in 1986, belongs to the modern expressionist style of the Bahá’í faith, not Mughal.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: What does the term "Duckworth -Lewis Method" relate to in cricket?

options.d: Calculating revised target in rain - affected matches

questions.answer_text: Calculating revised target in rain - affected matches
questions.explanation: The Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) Method is a mathematical formula used in limited-overs cricket (ODIs and T20s) to set a fair target for the team batting second when play is interrupted, usually by rain. It works on the principle that a team’s scoring resources depend on two factors – overs remaining and wickets in hand. If overs are lost, the DLS method recalculates the target based on the resources available to the chasing team compared to those of the team batting first.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: What was the role of the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) in the Technology Mission on Oilseeds ?

options.d: To manage oilseed procurement and processing

questions.answer_text: To manage oilseed procurement and processing
questions.explanation: To manage oilseed procurement and processing. The Technology Mission on Oilseeds (TMO) was launched in 1986 to reduce India’s dependence on edible oil imports and achieve self-sufficiency in oilseeds production. The National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), which had earlier spearheaded Operation Flood in the dairy sector, was entrusted with the task of managing oilseed procurement, storage, and processing under the TMO. NDDB played a key role in establishing oilseed cooperatives on the model of dairy cooperatives, ensuring that farmers received fair prices and that the supply chain was strengthened. This initiative eventually contributed to India achieving the status of an “Oilseed Revolution” in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

questions.explanation: To reduce trade barriers and enhance economic cooperation. The BIMSTEC Free Trade Area (FTA) aims to promote free trade among member countries by reducing tariffs, removing trade barriers, and improving market access. The ultimate goal is to enhance economic integration and cooperation among BIMSTEC nations (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, and Thailand).

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: What is the function of the cache memory in a computer’s memory hierarchy?

options.a: To provide permanent storage for data and files.
options.b: To store frequently used data for faster access by the CPU.
options.c: To control the flow of data between the CPU and memory.
options.d: To manage the allocation of memory resources to different programs.

questions.answer_text: To store frequently used data for faster access by the CPU.
questions.explanation: Cache memory is a chip - based computer component that makes retrieving data from the computer's memory more efficient. It is an extremely fast memory type that acts as a buffer between RAM and the CPU. It holds frequently requested data and instructions so that they are immediately available to the CPU when needed. It is costlier than main memory or disk memory but more economical than CPU registers.

options.a: Both A and R are false.
options.b: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.c: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.question: Identify the correct statement with reference to the Padma awards.

options.d: The names of the awardees are never published in the Gazette of India.

questions.answer_text: The Padma Awards are given annually.
questions.explanation: Padma Awards, which were instituted in the year 1954, are announced every year on the occasion of Republic Day. The award is given in 3 categories, namely, Padma Vibhushan for exceptional and distinguished service; Padma Bhushan for distinguished service of a high order; and Padma Shri for distinguished service. The total number of awards to be given in a year (excluding posthumous awards and to NRI/foreigners/OCIs) should not be more than 120. The award does not amount to a title and cannot be used as a suffix or prefix to the awardees’ name.

ULPIN is only for urban areas and not rural land.
questions.explanation: 1, 2, and 3 only. The Unique Land Parcel Identification Number (ULPIN) assigns a unique ID to every land parcel in India, just like an “Aadhaar for land.” This ensures uniformity in land records nationwide. Each land parcel is given a 14-digit alphanumeric number derived from the precise geo-coordinates (latitude & longitude) of the plot. ULPIN helps in tracking ownership history, resolving disputes, preventing duplication/fraud, and improving transparency in transactions. ULPIN is applicable to both rural and urban areas, not just urban land.

The Vesara style is a hybrid architectural form that evolved during the early medieval period in southern India, especially under the rule of the Chalukyas of Badami. It blends features from both the Nagara style (prevalent in North India) and the Dravidian style (dominant in South India). While Nagara temples typically have beehive-shaped shikharas (towers), and Dravidian temples have pyramidal vimanas and elaborate gateways (gopurams), the Vesara style incorporates elements of both—creating a unique synthesis. This architectural style is especially visible in temples like the Durga Temple at Aihole, the Lad Khan Temple, and the Virupaksha Temple at Pattadakal.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: In which year was the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) established in India?
questions.explanation: 1972. The Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) is a statutory body that was established under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry for the promotion of the export of marine products from India.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: Since 2000, Euro norms are followed in India under the name ______ Stage Emission Standards for four wheeled vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bharat. Vehicle emission norms were introduced in India in 1991 for petrol and in 1992 for diesel vehicles.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: When was the Editors Guild of India founded?
questions.explanation: 1978. It was established with the twin objectives of protecting press freedom and raising the standards of editorial leadership of newspapers and magazines.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: Where was the first factory of the Indian Iron and Steel Company (IISCO) set up?
questions.explanation: Hirapur. IISCO Steel Plant of Steel Authority of India Limited is an integrated steel plant located at Hirapur (later to be called Burnpur) in the Asansol subdivision of Paschim Bardhaman district, West Bengal.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: Where is the Rumi Darwaza located?
questions.explanation: Lucknow. It is an imposing gateway that was built by Nawab Asaf-Ud-Daula in 1784.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: In the context of forest conservation, Navadanya Movement was founded in 1987 by ______.
questions.explanation: Vandana Shiva. Navdanya is an Indian-based non-governmental organization that promotes biodiversity conservation, biodiversity, organic farming, the rights of farmers, and the process of seed saving.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: How many windows are there on the outside walls of Hawa Mahal of Jaipur?
questions.explanation: 953. Hawa Mahal of Jaipur was designed by Lal Chand Ustad.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: In which color are the railway lines and telephone lines shown in the topographic map?
questions.explanation: Black - Railroads, boundaries, telephone lines. Brown - Topographic contours. Blue - Lakes, streams, irrigation ditches and other hydrographic features Red - Land grids and important roads.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: Which of the following was previously known as 'the Lady Willingdon Park'.
questions.explanation: Lodhi Garden. Lady Willingdon Park was inaugurated in April 1936.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: Which ISO certification pertains to Environmental Management Systems?
questions.explanation: 14001. ISO 22000 - It is an international standard for food safety established by the International Organization for Standardization.

questions.subject: Static G.K.
questions.question: Who designed the logo for Lokpal in India?
questions.explanation: Prashant Mishra. The logo of Lokpal: LOK - people and PAL - caretaker, i.e. "caretaker of people”.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following is considered the oldest known civilization of the Indian subcontinent ?
questions.explanation: The Indus Valley Civilization (2500–1750 BCE). It flourished in present-day northwest India and Pakistan with major sites like Harappa and Mohenjo-daro, well known for urban planning, drainage systems, and trade. Indus Valley Civilization was a Bronze Age civilization noted for its advanced urban planning. The Vedic Civilization came later (1500 BCE onwards), while the Maurya (4th century BCE) and Gupta (4th century CE) empires emerged much later.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In the following questions, a statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a statement of Reason (R). Select the correct option from the following: Assertion (A): Rows of circular brick platforms at Harappa were used for religious ceremonies. Reason (R): These platforms were found to contain wheat and barley grains.

options.a: Both A and R are false
options.b: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
options.c: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: A is false, but R is true. At Harappa, archaeologists discovered rows of circular brick platforms, but there is no conclusive evidence that they were used for religious ceremonies; thus, the assertion is false. However, these platforms did contain remains of wheat and barley grains, suggesting their association with granary storage or processing of food grains, not rituals. The Harappan Civilization (Indus Valley Civilization) was first discovered in 1921 at Harappa, in present-day Punjab, Pakistan, by Daya Ram Sahni, an officer of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). A year later, in 1922, another important site, Mohenjo-daro, was discovered in Sindh by R.D. Banerjee.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Harappan site Banawali: 1. Banawali is located in the Fatehabad district of Haryana. 2. Excavations revealed only Harappan cultural phase, without any Pre-Harappan remains. 3. The site was excavated by Dr. R.S. Bisht, and both the citadel and lower town were fortified. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 and 3 only. Banawali in Haryana was excavated by R.S. Bisht and it shows fortified citadel and lower town. It had Pre-Harappan, Harappan, and Bara phases, so statement 2 is incorrect.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Iron Age sites in western and southern India: 1. Tekwada is an Iron Age site located in Gujarat. 2. Hallur is an Iron Age site in Karnataka. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 2 only. Tekwada is an Iron Age site located in Maharashtra.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are true about the Iron Age ? 1. The establishment of large cities took place on the basis of sizeable surplus. 2. The ceramic associated with this age was Painted Grey Ware. 3. The Indus Valley Civilization flourished during the Iron Age.
questions.explanation: Only 1 and 2. The Indus Valley Civilization flourished during the Bronze Age, not the Iron Age. The civilisations that flourished during the Iron Age were Greece, Rome, Persia and India.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct ?

options.a: Harappan culture spread only to Sindh and Punjab.
options.b: The script of the Harappan culture has been deciphered by historians.
options.c: At burials in Harappan sites the dead were generally laid in pits.
options.d: Granaries in the Indus Valley Civilization were found in Harappa only.

questions.answer_text: At burials in Harappan sites the dead were generally laid in pits.
questions.explanation: Harappa was discovered in 1921-22 by Daya Ram Sahni. It is located on the banks of the Ravi River in Sahiwal (formerly Montgomery) district, Punjab, Pakistan. The city is divided into three main sections: the Citadel, the Middletown, and the Lower Town. The Harappans sourced copper from present-day Rajasthan. Significant findings include two rows of six granaries, workers' quarters, two sandstone statues depicting human anatomy, a sculpture of a dog attacking a deer, and small bullock carts (known as ekkas).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the below statements is/are correct ? Statement 1 : Mohenjo-Daro was discovered by R.D. Banerji in 1922. Statement 2 : Drains exiting from Mohenjo-Daro had sandstone doors that were closed at night to prevent vagrants from entering the city.
questions.explanation: Only Statement 1. Mohenjo-Daro was discovered by R.D. Banerji in 1922, but the drains had wooden, not sandstone, doors.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the following cultural periods with their associated pottery traditions: List I – Cultural Period List II – Associated Pottery A. Harappan Age 1. Painted Grey Ware (PGW) B. Iron Age 2. Painted Red Ware C. Vedic Age 3. Black-and-Red Ware 4. Early Harappan Red Ware
questions.explanation: A–4, B–3, C–1. Harappan Age - Early Harappan Red Ware (with painted designs). Iron Age - Black-and-Red Ware. Vedic Age - Painted Grey Ware (PGW culture, especially Later Vedic).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Mohenjodaro (Sindh, Pakistan) yielded a paved bathroom, the bronze Dancing Girl, the Bearded Priest, and the Great Granary. 2. Lothal (Gujarat) had a brick dockyard for berthing ships and also provided evidence of rice cultivation in Harappan context. 3. Banawali (Haryana) was the Harappan site where the dockyard was discovered. Which of the above statements is/are incorrect ?
questions.explanation: 3 only. The dockyard was found at Lothal, not Banawali. Evidence of rice cultivation is indeed reported from Lothal (Harappan context).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In Harappa, the granary had rows of ______ brick platforms for threshing the grains.
questions.explanation: Circular. Granaries of the Indus Valley Civilization were discovered in two key regions: Mohenjodaro and Harappa. Mohenjodaro, located south of the Indus River, is a major site where the Great Granary, the largest building, was found.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the architectural features of Indus Valley Civilisation: 1. The prominent architectural feature of Indus Valley towns was the citadel, which was usually fortified, except at Chanhudaro. 2. Major cities had grid-based town planning, burnt brick houses, and advanced underground drainage systems, such as Dholavira’s water reservoirs. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Both statements accurately describe the town planning and architecture of Indus Valley Civilisation.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Select the correct alternative on the basis of the given statements on the cities of Harappan civilisation. Statement I: Most of the Harappan cities were divided into two parts: Higher Town and Lower Town. Statement II: The archaeologists describe the lower part of the towns as Citadel.

options.a: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
options.d: Neither Statement I nor Statement II is true.

questions.explanation: Only Statement I is true. The Harappan cities were typically structured into two distinct sections. The part to the west was generally smaller in area but higher in elevation, which archaeologists refer to as the Citadel. In contrast, the section to the east was larger in size but lower in elevation, commonly known as the Lower Town.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Fire altars were found in which of the following groups of Harappan cities ?
questions.explanation: Kalibangan and Lothal. Findings of different Indus valley civilization sites : Kalibangan - Lower fortified town, Boustrophedon style, Wooden drainage, Copper Ox, Evidence of earthquake, Wooden plough, Camel’s bone. Lothal - Port Town, Evidence of Rice, Graveyard, Ivory scale, Copper dog. Mohenjo-Daro - Prepared Garments, Temple-like Palace, Pashupati seal, Statue of a dancing girl, The Great Bath, The Great Granary etc.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Indus Valley sites is now located in Pakistan ?
questions.explanation: Harappa. The Indus valley civilization (Bronze Age) is also called the Harappan culture. Other Important Sites : Sutkagendor (Dast river, Balochistan); Chanhudaro (Pakistan, Indus river); Kalibangan (Rajasthan, Ghaggar river); Lothal (Gujarat, Bhogva river); Alamgirpur (Meerut, Hindon river).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Pottery was first traceable to which period of ancient Indian history ?
questions.explanation: Neolithic. Pottery has been discovered in the early villages of Mehrgarh. The Palaeolithic (the first and longest part of the Stone Age) was a period of prehistory when humans made stone tools.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In India, the practice of erecting megaliths began about _____ago.
questions.explanation: 3000 years. A megalith is a large stone that has been used to construct a pre - historic structure or monument. Type - Clairn Circles type of Megalith (grave/memorial) were the stone pieces set in a circular shape around the grave. Menhir (standing stone), Capstone (Single megaliths placed horizontally over burial chambers), Dolmen (A large capstone on two or more support stones creating a chamber). Megalith Sites - Nilaskal (Karnataka), Hanamsagar (Karnataka), Junapani (Maharashtra), Hire Benakal (Karnataka), etc.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Arrange the following sites in chronological order based on earliest evidence of settlement: 1. Mehrgarh 2. Harappa 3. Mohenjodaro 4. Kalibangan
questions.explanation: 1-2-3-4. Mehrgarh – Neolithic site (~7000 BCE), considered the oldest agricultural settlement in the Indian subcontinent. Harappa – Early Harappan phase (~3300 BCE), discovered in 1921 by Dayaram Sahni. Mohenjodaro – Mature Harappan phase (~2600 BCE), discovered in 1922 by R.D. Banerji. Kalibangan – Harappan site in Rajasthan (~2500 BCE), known for fire altars and ploughed fields.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): Bhimbetka is famous for prehistoric rock paintings. Reason (R): These paintings mainly depict scenes of hunting, dancing, and animal figures from the Mesolithic period.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. Bhimbetka, located in Madhya Pradesh, is known for its prehistoric rock shelters and paintings. These artworks, dating mainly to the Mesolithic period, depict hunting scenes, dancing figures, and various animals, reflecting the lifestyle and beliefs of early humans.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): Ostrich egg shells have been found from the Palaeolithic sites in India. Reason (R): Daojali Hading in Assam yielded large quantities of ostrich remains.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false.
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false. Ostrich egg shells have indeed been found from Palaeolithic sites in India, such as Patne in Maharashtra, which confirms that Assertion (A) is true. However, Reason (R) is false because Daojali Hading is not a Palaeolithic site; it is a Neolithic site in Assam, and it has not yielded ostrich remains but rather jadeite stone and other Neolithic artefacts.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following metals was used to make weapons and tools in Harappan cities ?
questions.explanation: Copper was the first metal used in Indus Valley (Bronze Age civilization) to make tools, utensils, and other objects. Other metals used were lead, gold, bronze and silver.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Harappan brought Gold from present-day _______ in India.
questions.explanation: Karnataka. Gold ornaments are found at both Mohenjo-daro and Harappa. Other materials they imported: Copper - Brought from present-day Rajasthan, and from Oman in west Asia. Tin - Brought from present-day Afghanistan and Iran. Precious stones - Brought from present-day Gujarat, Iran and Afghanistan.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following types of house remains were found in Mehrgarh site of Harappan civilization ?
questions.explanation: Square or rectangle. Major findings at Mehrgarh are evidence of animal bones and the remains of houses. Mehrgarh was discovered in 1974 by Jean-Francois Jarrige. It is the first place where people started growing barley and wheat, reared the sheep and goat as it was one of the oldest villages.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Arrange the following periods in chronological order: 1. Mesolithic 2. Palaeolithic 3. Neolithic 4. Chalcolithic
questions.explanation: 2 → 1 → 3 → 4. The sequence begins with the Palaeolithic Age (Old Stone Age), followed by the Mesolithic Age (Middle Stone Age), then the Neolithic Age (New Stone Age), and finally the Chalcolithic Age (Copper–Stone Age). Each stage represents advancements in tools, lifestyle, and technology, moving from hunting–gathering to agriculture and

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the following archaeological sites with their respective periods: List I – Archaeological Site List II – Period A. Chirand 1. Neolithic B. Burzahom 2.Neolithic-Chalcolithic C. Hunasagi 3. Palaeolithic D. Mehrgarh 4. Neolithic to Early Harappan
questions.explanation: A–1, B–2, C–3, D–4. Chirand – Neolithic site in Bihar. Burzahom – Neolithic-Chalcolithic site in Jammu & Kashmir. Hunasagi – Palaeolithic site in Karnataka (stone-cutting tools found). Mehrgarh – Neolithic to Early Harappan site in Balochistan (Pakistan).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the following Harappan sites with their present-day locations: List I – Harappan Site List II – Present-day Location A. Shortughai 1. Gujarat B. Balakot 2. Rajasthan C. Nageswar 3. Afghanistan D. Kalibangan 4. Pakistan (Sindh/ Balochistan region)
questions.explanation: A–3, B–4, C–1, D–2. Shortughai – Afghanistan (Harappan trading post linked to lapis lazuli mines). Balakot – Pakistan (Sindh/Balochistan coast, known for shell working). Nageswar – Gujarat (famous for shell manufacturing). Kalibangan – Rajasthan (known for fire altars and ploughed fields). Vedic Age (1500 BC to 600 BC)

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements in the context of the Vedas. 1. The Vedas are called Shruti. 2. The Rigveda consists of ten Mandalas. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Vedas are sruti ("what is heard") distinguishing them from other religious texts, which are called smrti ("what is remembered"). Hindus consider the Vedas to be apauruṣeya, which means "not of a man, superhuman" and "impersonal, authorless". The Rigveda is the oldest Veda and contains 1,028 hymns (suktas) comprising about 10,600 verses.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the following Rigvedic Gods with their respective roles: God Role 1. Agni a. God of fire; acts as a mediator between gods and humans 2. Indra b. Warrior god; destroyer of Vritra (demon of drought) 3. Varuna c. God of rain and upholder of cosmic order 4. Yama d. God of death 5. Soma e. Sacred plant and its ritual drink; associated with immortality
questions.explanation: 1-a, 2-b, 3-c, 4-d, 5-e. In the Rigveda: Agni is the fire god and messenger between gods and men; Indra is the warrior god and Vritra’s slayer; Varuna controls rain and maintains Rita (cosmic order); Yama is the first mortal and god of death; Soma is both a sacred plant and its intoxicating ritual drink, linked to immortality.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: According to the Ashrama system of Vedic life, which of the following was the third stage of life ?
questions.explanation: Vanaprastha, where a person handed over household responsibilities to the next generation, took an advisory role, and gradually withdrew from the world. The four stages of the ashrama system are : Brahmacharya (Student's life), Grihastha (household life), Vanaprastha (retired life), Sannyasa (renounced life).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Vedangas are Hindu auxiliary disciplines linked to the study of the Vedas. 2. There are seven Vedangas in total. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: only 1. Statement 1 is correct because the Vedangas are considered the “limbs of the Vedas,” aiding in the proper understanding, pronunciation, and interpretation of the Vedic texts. There are six Vedangas, not seven, which include Shiksha (phonetics), Kalpa (ritual), Vyakarana (grammar), Nirukta (etymology), Chandas (meter), and Jyotisha (astronomy). Statement 2 is incorrect, as the total number of Vedangas is six.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: According to the Varna system that was prevalent in the Vedic period, which of the following was NOT a Varna ?
questions.explanation: Samiti. The traditional caste system consists of a hierarchy of four castes (varnas) - Brahmins (priests and teachers), Kshatriyas (rulers and warriors), Vaishyas (merchants and cultivators), and Shudras (servants).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Rig Vedic Samhita: 1. Rig Veda consists of 10 Mandalas. 2. The Gayatri Mantra is found in Mandala 2. 3. Mandala 10 contains the Purusha Sukta, which explains the origin of the four Varnas. Which of the above statements is/are incorrect ?
questions.explanation: 2 only. Statement 2 is incorrect — Gayatri Mantra is in Mandala 3, not Mandala 2. Rig Veda is the oldest of the four Vedas. It is a collection of 10,600 verses and 1,028 hymns. Each mandala consists of Suktas which are basically eulogies. The 10th mandala contains the Purusha Sukta which explains the four Varnas were born from the mouth, arms, thighs and feet of the Brahma or Purusha. Mandala 9 is completely devoted to Soma.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following is the earliest literary record of Indian culture ?
questions.explanation: Rigveda. There are four Vedas: Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the ancient names of rivers with their present names: (A) Asikni 1. Beas (B) Vitasta 2. Jhelum (C) Purushni 3. Ravi (D) Vipasha 4. Chenab
questions.explanation: A–4, B–2, C–3, D–1.Ancient names of Indian Rivers - Vitasta (Jhelum), Purushni (Ravi), Shatudri (Satluj), Vipasha (Beas), Sadanira (Gandak), Drishdvati (Ghaghara).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Vedas is found in two recensions, black and white, and is full of rituals to be performed publicly or individually ?
questions.explanation: Yajurveda : Notable Upanishads of Yajurveda - Brihadaranyaka, Isha, Taittriya, Katha, and Maithri.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which of the following Vedas was Dasarajna war (the war of ten kings) mentioned ?
questions.explanation: Rigveda (Book of Mantras). Dasarajna war was fought between King Sudas of the Bharata tribe and a confederation of ten tribes, including the Puru, Yadu, Turvasa, Anu, Druhyu, Alina, Paktha, Bhalanas, Shiva, and Vishanin. The battle took place on the banks of the Parushni (Ravi) river.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The main (chief) social unit of the Aryans was______ .
questions.explanation: Jana (Tribes). Gana - Tribal or clan based assemblies, Parishad - A small body similar to Samitis/sabhas consisting exclusively of Brahmins, Rajan - A kind of Chief or King.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Vedas: 1. Rig Veda is the oldest Veda and contains hymns mainly dealing with magic spells and charms. 2. Sama Veda is mainly a collection of chants and musical notations. 3. Atharva Veda contains a collection of magic spells and charms to ward off evil spirits and diseases. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 2 and 3 only. Rig Veda does not deal with magic spells and charms. Rig Veda has about 1,028 hymns (suktas) and 10,600 verses (richas). These hymns are mainly dedicated to various deities such as Indra, Agni, Varuna, Soma, Usha, etc.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Indian philosophy: 1. The Purva Mimansa school of philosophy was founded by Jaimini. 2. Kapila is regarded as the founder of the Samkhya school of philosophy. 3. Patanjali is associated with the Yoga school of philosophy. Which of the above statements are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1, 2 and 3. Purva Mimansa (‘Prior Study’) also known as Dharma Mimamsa and Karma Mimamsa (‘Study of Actions’). The six principal Hindu darshans are Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, and Vedanta. Badarayana - Author of Brahma Sutra or Vedanta Sutra. Patanjali - Philosophy of Yoga sutra. Kapila - Philosophy of Sankhya. Vyasa - Author of the Mahabharata, Vedas and Puranas.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: India was named 'Bharat' after the name of the Bharat clan. In which of the following Vedas is this clan first mentioned ?
questions.explanation: Rigveda. There are 1028 Suktas in 10 Mandals (Chapters).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The language of the Aryan texts was:
questions.explanation: Sanskrit was the first language spoken in India. Ardhamagadhi Prakrit was a Middle Indo-Aryan language. Prakrit is a group of vernacular Middle Indo-Aryan languages spoken in India between the third and seventh century BCE.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Rigvedic deities: (A)Agni was worshipped as the fire-god during the Rigvedic period. (B) Sindhu was regarded as a river goddess in the Rigveda. (C) Usha was worshipped as the goddess of night.goddess of dawn. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: (A) and (B) only. Usha was worshipped as the goddess of dawn.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In the Rig Veda there is a hymn in the form of a dialogue between Sage Vishvamitra and two rivers that were worshipped as goddesses. Which are these rivers ?
questions.explanation: Beas and Sutlej. The most prominent river in the Rig Veda is Saraswati.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the ‘Gotra’ practice in ancient India is true ?

options.a: Men and women were expected to marry within the same gotra.
options.b: People belonging to the same gotra were regarded as descendants of the person after whom the gotra was named.
options.c: Women retained their father’s gotra after marriage.
options.d: Each gotra was named after a famous king.

questions.answer_text: People belonging to the same gotra were regarded as descendants of the person after whom the gotra was named.
questions.explanation: Gotra originally referred to the seven lineage segments of the Brahmans (priests), who trace their derivation from seven ancient seers: Atri, Bharadvaja, Bhrigu, Gotama, Kashyapa, Vasishtha, and Vishvamitra.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Purusha Sukta: 1. Purusha Sukta is a hymn from Rigveda. 2. It is dedicated to Lord Shiva, described as the great Purusha. 3. Purusha Sukta is one of the Pancha Suktam, which includes Vishnu Suktam, Sri Suktam, Bhu Suktam, and Nila Suktam. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 and 3 only. Statement 2 is incorrect because Purusha Sukta is dedicated to Lord Vishnu, not Lord Shiva.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Jain temple at Pattadakal was built by ________.
questions.explanation: Rashtrakuta. Other temples made by Rashtrakutas - The Kailasanatha Temple in Ellora, the Navalinga Temples in Pattadakal.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Jain Tirthankaras: (A)Ayodhya is recognized as the birthplace of the first Tirthankara, Rishabhdev. (B) Ayodhya is also the birthplace of the fourth Tirthankara, Abhinandannath. (C) Varanasi is the birthplace of the first and fourth Tirthankaras. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: (A) and (B) only. Rishabhdev, the first Jain Tirthankara, was born in Ayodhya.Abhinandannath, the fourth Jain Tirthankara, was also born in Ayodhya.Varanasi holds a very important place in Jain traditions. It is recognized as the birthplace of three Jain Tirthankaras 23rd Tirthankara Parshvanatha, 7th Tirthankara Suparshvanatha and 11th Tirthankara Shreyansanatha.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following describes the Medhi part in Buddhist structure ?

options.a: The circular terrace between the railing and dome
options.b: Ceremonial gateways in front of stupas
options.c: A low wall to enclose the structure
options.d: The umbrella-shaped structure placed at the top of the structure

questions.answer_text: The circular terrace between the railing and dome
questions.explanation: All forms of Buddhist architecture include three primary structures: vihara, stupa, and chaitya-griha.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct in context of Buddhist architecture ? i. The Uddeshika stupa was created as a memorial. ii. Paribhogika stupa contained the buried bodily remains of Buddh. iii. Bharhut stupa is situated in Uttar Pradesh.
questions.explanation: Only i and ii. Bharhut stupa (Madhya Pradesh) is known for its early Buddhist reliefs and carvings.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: During which of the following rules did Buddhism get split into two schools - Hinayana and Mahayana in the fourth Buddhist council ?
questions.explanation: Kushana. The Fourth Buddhist Council was held in 72 AD at Kundalvana, Kashmir, under the Kushan king Kanishka. It was led by Vasumitra, with Asvaghosa as his deputy, and marked the division of Buddhism into two sects: Mahayana and Hinayana.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A) : The Shailendra rulers were great patrons of Buddhism. Reason (R) : They built the Borobudur stupa in Java, which is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.The Shailendra rulers of Java were devoted followers of Buddhism and extended great patronage to Buddhist culture and architecture. Their most remarkable contribution was the construction of the Borobudur stupa, one of the largest Buddhist monuments in the world, which today is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Stupas are a symbol of which of the following religions ?
questions.explanation: Buddhism. Stupas were burial mounds prevalent in India from the vedic period. Stupas typically consist of several elements, including a circular base or platform, a hemispherical dome or Anda, a spire or Harmika, and a parasol or Chhatra. Sanchi Stupa in Madhya Pradesh is the most famous of the Ashokan stupas.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The tall sculptures on the Bharhut Stupa are the depictions of ________.
questions.explanation: Yakshas and Yakshinis. (nature spirits in Indian mythology linked to prosperity and fertility). These figures symbolize the connection between the spiritual and natural worlds and showcase the integration of local traditions into Buddhist art.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Dhamek Stupa: 1. Dhamek Stupa is located at Kushinagar. 2. It was originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in 249 BCE. 3. The present structure of Dhamek Stupa was built around 500 CE, replacing the earlier construction. Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect ?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Dhamek Stupa is not located at Kushinagar; it is in Sarnath. Both statements 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Indo-Greek kings was mentioned in the Buddhist text Milindapanho as Milinda ?
questions.explanation: Menander I. The Milinda Panha is a dialogue between the Indian Buddhist sage Nagasena and the 2nd-century BC Indo-Greek king Menander I.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement from among the following.

options.a: ‘Sanchi Stupa’ is situated in Madhya Pradesh.
options.b: ‘Bavikonda Stupa’ is situated in Andhra Pradesh.
options.c: ‘Dhamek Stupa’ is situated in Uttar Pradesh.

questions.explanation: Piprahwa Stupa is located in Uttar Pradesh near the town of Piprahwa, close to the India-Nepal border, this site is renowned for its archaeological significance.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following is the largest Stupa in India ?
questions.explanation: Kesariya Stupa (Bihar): It was discovered in 1958 during an excavation led by K.K Muhammed. Shanti Stupa (Leh): It was built in 1991 by Japanese Buddhist Bhikshu Gyomyo Nakamura.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A) : Ashvaghosha wrote the Buddhacharita, the biography of Buddha. Reason (R) : Ashvaghosha was the court poet of King Kanishka.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Both are true, and R correctly explains A. Ashvaghosha was the court poet of king Kanishka. Other writers and books: Nagarjuna - Mulamadhyamakakarika. Vasumitra - Mahavibhasa. Charaka - Charaka Samhita.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Identify the Stupa based on the given characteristics: 1. Built by Mauryan emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. 2. Located in Madhya Pradesh. 3. Declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989.
questions.explanation: Sanchi Stupa is the oldest Stupa of the Buddhist period. Originally built with bricks by Ashoka, it was later enlarged during the Shunga dynasty with stone railings and gateways (Toranas). The Stupa enshrines relics of the Buddha. It is one of the best-preserved stupas in India and an important center of Buddhist art and architecture. UNESCO declared it a World Heritage Site in 1989.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: ____was the first woman to be ordained as a bhikkhuni in Buddhism.
questions.explanation: Mahapajapati Gotami. Sanghamitta was an Indian Buddhist nun and the eldest daughter of Ashoka. Sujata fed Gautama Buddha a bowl of kheera, a milk-rice pudding, ending his six years of asceticism. Venerable Dhammananda Bhikkhuni is the first fully ordained Theravadin nun in Thailand.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: With reference to Buddhist architecture, what does chaitya mean ?
questions.explanation: Prayer Hall. It is a rectangular hall with a semi-circular apse at one end, which contains a stupa or relic chamber. Other types of architecture : Stupa - It contained the Buddha's ashes. Vihara - Residence hall for the monks.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The rules made for the Buddhist "Sangha” were written down in a book called _______.
questions.explanation: Vinaya Pitaka. Buddhist teachings were divided into Three Pitakas at the First Buddhist Council in 483 BC. Vinaya Pitaka: It consists of rules of conduct and discipline applicable to the monastic life of the monks and the nuns. It was compiled by Upali, and was written in Pali language.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Identify the Buddhist architectural structure based on the given characteristics: 1. Served as meditation cells and living quarters for monks. 2. Commonly used by wandering monks during the rainy season. 3. Famous examples are found at Ajanta, Ellora, Nasik, Karle, Kanheri, and Bagh.
questions.explanation: Viharas – These were monasteries consisting of small cells arranged around a courtyard. They served as dwelling places and meditation halls for Buddhist monks, especially during the rainy season. Some of the finest rock-cut viharas are located at Ajanta and Ellora (Maharashtra), Nasik, Karle, Kanheri, and Bagh.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Buddha meditated for days on end under a peepal tree at_____where he attained enlightenment.
questions.explanation: Bodh Gaya. Gautam Buddha (Siddharta, Sakyamuni & Tathagata). Father: Suddhodana, Mother: Mayadevi. Birth Place (563 B.C.): Lumbini (Nepal), Capital of Sakya republic. Teachers: Alarakalama and UdrakaRamputra. Enlightenment : At age of 35 under the Peepal tree at Uruvela (Bodhgaya) on banks of river Niranjana (Falgu). Mahaparinirvana (483 B.C.): At Kushinagar at age of 80. Sign:- Lotus and Bull - Birth, Horse - Renunciation, Bodhi Tree - Enlightenment, Dhammachakra Pravartana (Sarnath) - First sermon.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: What was the pedestrian path for devotees to wave in homage to Stupa called in Buddhist architecture ?
questions.explanation: Medhi. Features of Stupa - Medhi (A circular terrace), Toranas (wall with decorated gateways), Anda (hemispherical mound), Chattra (A central pillar supporting a triple-umbrella form), and Harmika (A square railing).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Lion Capital of Ashoka: 1. The Lion Capital was built to commemorate the death (Mahaparinirvana) of Buddha. 2. It was originally erected at Sarnath by Emperor Ashoka. 3. It was adopted as the National Emblem of India in 1950. Which of the statements given above is incorrect ?
questions.explanation: 1 only – The Lion Capital was not built to mark Buddha’s death, rather it commemorates the First Sermon (Dharmachakra Pravartana) delivered at Sarnath. Emperor Ashoka erected it at Sarnath, and it was later adopted as the National Emblem of India in 1950.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct ? I. Gautama Buddha belonged to a small gana known as the Sakya gana and was a Kshatriya. II. Gautama Buddha passed away at Kusinara.
questions.explanation: Both I and II. Important places related to the life of Buddha are - Birth (Lumbini); Enlightenment (Bodh Gaya at Bihar); His first Sermon also known as Dharma-Chakra-Pravartana (Sarnath); His death or Mahaparinirvana in Kushinagara (Pali: Kusinārā), Uttar Pradesh.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The earliest Buddhist texts were written in:
questions.explanation: Pali. Pali canon, also called Tipitaka (Pali: “Triple Basket”), is the complete canon, first recorded in Pali, of the Theravada (“Way of the Elders”) branch of Buddhism.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Gandhara School of Art: 1. Marble stone was mainly used in this art style. 2. It was patronized by the Kushanas. 3. It shows a strong influence of Greek art. Which of the statements given above are correct ?
questions.explanation: 2 and 3 only – Statement 1 is incorrect because Gandhara art used grey sandstone, not marble. It was developed under the Kushanas (esp. Kanishka) and shows a strong Greek (Hellenistic) influence, therefore also called Greco-Buddhist art.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the Mahajanapada with its capital:
questions.explanation: 1-a, 2-b, 3-d, 4-c. Vatsa: Capital was Kaushambi (near modern Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh). Magadha: Capital was Rajagriha (later shifted to Pataliputra). Kuru : The capital was Indraprastha (near modern Delhi). Avanti : The capital was Ujjayini (in present-day Madhya Pradesh).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: When did the second urbanisation in Ganga Valley take place ?
questions.explanation: 6th Century BCE. This era witnessed the development of kingdoms and Mahajanapadas like Magadha, Kosala, and Vatsa, alongside advancements in agriculture, trade, and administration. The First urbanisation in India took place during the Harappan civilization.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following dynasties of Magadha during the Mahajanapada period: 1. Haryanka Dynasty 2. Shishunaga Dynasty 3. Nanda Dynasty 4. Maurya Dynasty Which of the following gives the correct chronological order ?
questions.explanation: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4. The Haryanka dynasty (544–412 BCE) was the first ruling dynasty of Magadha, founded by Bimbisara. It was followed by the Shishunaga dynasty (412–344 BCE). After that came the powerful Nanda dynasty (344–322 BCE). Finally, the Maurya dynasty (322 BCE onward) rose, starting with Chandragupta Maurya, marking the foundation of the Mauryan Empire.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: How many Mahajanapadas were there during the age of Buddha ?
questions.explanation: 16. The references of 16 Mahajanapadas are found in Anguttara Nikaya (Buddhist literature) and Bhagwati Sutra (Jain texts). The list of the 16 Mahajanapadas includes: Anga (Champa), Magadh (Rajgriha/Girivraja, later Pataliputra), Kasi (Kasi), Vatsa (Kausambi), Kosala (Sravasti), Saurasena (Mathura), Panchala (Ahichchhatra), Kuru (Indraprastha), Matsya (Viratnagar), Chedi (Sothivati/Banda), Avanti (Ujjain/Mahishmati), Gandhara (Taxila, Purushapura), Kamboj (Rajapura), Asmaka (Paithan/Pratisthan), Vajji (Vaishali), Malla (Kusinara).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the following Mahajanapadas with their modern-day locations: List I (Mahajanapada) List II (Modern Location) A. Kosala 1. Malwa and Madhya Pradesh B. Magadha 2. Rawalpindi (Pakistan) C. Gandhara 3. Uttar Pradesh D. Avanti 4. Gaya and Patna (Bihar)
questions.explanation: A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1. Modern day names of other Mahajanapadas: Munger and Bhagalpur (Anga), Gaya and Patna (Magadha), Banaras (Kashi), Prayagraj (Vatsa), Malwa and Madhya Pradesh (Avanti), Rawalpindi (Gandhara), North Bihar (Vajji), Jaipur (Matsya), Meerut and Haryana (Kuru), Western Uttar Pradesh (Shurasena and Panchala), Bundelkhand region (Chedi), Rajouri, Hajra and North -West Frontier Province (Kamboja), Banks of Godavari (Asmaka or Assaka), Deoria and Uttar Pradesh (Malla).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Rulers of Mahajanapadas in ancient India collected taxes on crops at the rate of _____ of what was produced.
questions.explanation: 1/6th. Rulers of mahajanapadas in ancient India collected a tax called 'Bhaga' from the Farmers in their region.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the founder of the Maurya Empire ?

options.c: Ashoka Column A: Mahajanapada Column B: Capital 1. Vatsa a. Kaushambi 2. Magadha b. Rajagriha 3. Kuru c. Ujjayini 4. Avanti d. Indraprastha

questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya. The Maurya Empire was founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 321 BCE with the guidance of his teacher and advisor Chanakya (Kautilya). He overthrew the Nanda dynasty of Magadha and established the first large-scale empire in India. Capital: Pataliputra (modern Patna, Bihar). Chandragupta defeated Seleucus Nicator (Alexander’s general) in 305 BCE and signed a treaty, giving Seleucus 500 war elephants. His reign laid the foundation of a strong centralized administration described in Arthashastra (by Chanakya). Later, he abdicated the throne, became a Jain monk, and died at Shravanabelagola (Karnataka). His successors were Bindusara (son) and Ashoka the Great (grandson).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In the context of Mughal administration, who were referred to as Shaikhzadas or Hindustanis?

options.a: Central Asian nobles of Turkic origin serving the Mughals
options.b: Rajput converts elevated to noble ranks for loyalty
options.c: Persian-trained officers recruited from Safavid Iran
options.d: Indigenous Muslims who held administrative posts under Mughal rule

questions.answer_text: Indigenous Muslims who held administrative posts under Mughal rule
questions.explanation: In Mughal administration, the nobility was divided into different groups based on ethnicity and origin, such as Turanis (Central Asians), Iranis (Persians), Afghans, Rajputs, and Deccanis. The term Shaikhzadas or Hindustanis referred to Indian-born Muslims, often descendants of early Muslim settlers or local converts, who rose to prominence in the Mughal bureaucracy and military. Unlike the foreign-born nobles, these Hindustanis had deeper local connections and played an important role in balancing the power structure of the Mughal nobility.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Mauryan ruler is credited with the establishment of the spy system in his empire ?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya. Chandragupta Maurya (321–297 BCE) founded the Mauryan Empire with the guidance of Chanakya, defeating the last Nanda ruler at Pataliputra. After the Seleucid-Mauryan war, he gained territories west of the Indus in exchange for 500 war elephants and also married Seleucus’s daughter. His empire expanded across most of India except Kalinga and the far south. Later, Chandragupta converted to Jainism and died by fasting at Shravanabelagola, having migrated there with Acharya Bhadrabahu. Greek ambassador Megasthenes visited his court and wrote Indica, describing Pataliputra and the division of Indian society into seven classes.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: With reference to the city administration of Mauryan Empire, consider the following statements. A) Megasthenes put light on the Mauryan city administration. B) The city council was divided into six committees. C) City administration was well planned. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: A, B, C. The Mauryan Empire, founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 321 BCE, was the first major empire in India. It stretched from the Oxus Valley to the Kaveri Delta, covering most of the subcontinent, with its capital at Pataliputra, a city fortified with 64 gates and 570 towers. Megasthenes, a Greek historian, documented India in his work Indica.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Edicts of Ashoka: 1. Rock Edict XIII describes the Kalinga war and Ashoka’s remorse after it. 2. Pillar Edict II defines Dhamma as compassion, truthfulness, and purity of life. 3. The Rummindei inscription marks Ashoka’s visit to the birthplace of Buddha at Lumbini. 4. The Kandahar Greek Edicts were written in Prakrit and Chinese. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1, 2 and 3 only. Rock Edict XIII: Mentions the Kalinga war and Ashoka’s change of heart. Pillar Edict II: Defines Dhamma. Rummindei Inscription: Marks Ashoka’s pilgrimage to Lumbini. Kandahar Greek Edicts were written in Greek and Prakrit, not Chinese.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The name ‘Piyadassi’ is associated with whom among the following Mauryan kings ?
questions.explanation: Ashoka. "Piyadasi" is an honorific epithet that means "He who regards others with kindness", "Humane", or "He who glances amiably".

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Deimachus, who was a Greek ambassador, came to India during the reign of the Mauryan king, ______.
questions.explanation: Bindusara also known as "Amitrochates" or "Amitragata" by the Greeks, was the son of Chandragupta Maurya. Bindusara patronized the Ajivikas and was taught by the Ajivika Brahmin Pingalavatsa.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka – Identify the incorrect statement: A. Rock Edict XIII highlights the Kalinga War and Ashoka’s remorse. B. Rock Edict XII talks about Ashoka’s duties as a ruler and his commitment to Dharma. C. Rock Edict X focuses on the ruler’s responsibilities and promotion of Dharma. Which of the above statements is/are incorrect ?
questions.explanation: B only. Statement B is incorrect: Rock Edict XII does not talk about ruler duties; it emphasizes tolerance and respect for all religions. Statement A is correct: Rock Edict XIII mentions the Kalinga War and Ashoka’s remorse. Statement C is correct: Rock Edict X describes the duties of the ruler and commitment to Dharma.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following generally used to head the provincial administration under the Mauryas ?
questions.explanation: Kumara. The 18 Tirthas were key officials in ancient administration, including roles like Mantrin (Chief Minister), Purohita (Priest), Senapati (Army Commander), Yuvaraja (Prince), Dauvarika (Chief of Palace Attendants), Antarvamsika (Chief of the King’s Guards), Prasasta (Magistrate), Samahata (Collector General), Samnidhata (Chief Treasurer), and Pradesta (Commissioner). Other roles included Nayak (Town Guard), Paur (Town Chief), Karmanta (Mines Superintendent), Dandpala (Army Officer), and Durgapala (Fort Guardian).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following was NOT one of the basic attributes of Ashokas' Dhamma ?
questions.explanation: Celibacy. Ashoka's Dhamma, as outlined in his Edicts, emphasized the following basic attributes: Ahimsa (Non-violence), Secularism (Separation of religion and state), Political unification (Unity and harmony among subjects).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following envoys was sent by Seleucus I to the court of Chandragupta Maurya ?
questions.explanation: Megasthenes. He was an ancient Greek historian, diplomat, and ethnographer who authored the famous work “Indica”, providing valuable insights into the Mauryan Empire, including its administration, society, geography, and culture.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Ashokan rock edicts declares prohibition of animal sacrifice ?
questions.explanation: Major Rock Edict - I. There are 14 Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka in three languages (Prakrit, Aramaic and Greek) and two scripts (Brahmi and Kharosthi). Major Rock Edicts: II - It mentions social welfare under Dhamma. Major Rock Edict III - It declares that respect for parents and for all living things, including Brahmanas and Sramanas, is a virtue. Major Rock Edict IV - Consideration and non-violence to animals and courtesy to relations. Major Rock Edict XIII - It mentions Ashoka’s victory over Kalinga.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): Ashoka sent his son Mahendra and daughter Sanghmitra to spread Buddhism in Sri Lanka. Reason (R): Ashoka was the third Mauryan king and a devoted follower of Dhamma who promoted Buddhism abroad. Codes:

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. Ashoka, as a devoted follower of Dhamma, actively propagated Buddhism. He sent Mahendra and Sanghmitra to Sri Lanka to spread the teachings, making the assertion correct. The reason correctly explains why Ashoka undertook this mission.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Bhabru-Bairat rock edicts mainly depicting Ashokas' conversion to Buddhism are found in ______.
questions.explanation: Rajasthan. Bhabru is the only inscription in the Boustrophedon script (bi-directional script from right to left and left to right in an alternate line).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who requested the Syrian king to send a Greek philosopher ?
questions.explanation: Bindusara was the second Mauryan Empire, father of Ashoka, and son of Chandragupta (founder of Mauryan empire). Syrian King Antiochus-I sent his ambassador Deimachus to the court of Bindusara.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Barabar Cave, famously known for depicting Ashokas' inscription, is situated at_______.
questions.explanation: Gaya, Bihar. The Barabar Caves, located in the Makhdumpur region of Jehanabad district, Bihar, date back to the Mauryan period (3rd century BCE) and were built by Emperor Ashoka for Ajivaka ascetics. The caves include Karan Chaupar, Lomas Rishi, Sudama, and Visvakarma Caves.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following rulers was defeated in the battle for Pataliputra by Chandragupta Maurya ?
questions.explanation: Dhana Nanda. He was the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty, and his defeat marked the establishment of the Mauryan Empire in India.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following Mauryan rulers was the first, who tried to convey his messages to his subjects concerning the idea and practice of dhamma through inscriptions ?
questions.explanation: Ashoka was the third emperor of the Mauryan Dynasty. To propagate the policy of dhamma, he used the medium of edicts. These edicts were used to communicate between the King (Ashoka) and his subjects. Few inscriptions were addressed to the Buddhist Samgha.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following was a Ceylonese chronicle that acted as an important literary source of the Mauryan empire ?
questions.explanation: Mahavamsa - It was written by Mahanama in Pali language. Literary Sources of Mauryan Period: "Arthashastra” (Kautilya), “Indica” (Megasthenes).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Chandragupta Maurya: (A)Chandragupta Maurya was the founder of the Mauryan Empire. (B) He fasted to death at Shravanabelagola following Jainism. (C) His Greek name was Megasthenes, and he captured Pataliputra in 322 BCE by defeating Dhanananda of the Nanda dynasty. Which of the above statements is/are incorrect ?
questions.explanation: C only. Chandragupta Maurya’s Greek name was Sandrocottos, not Megasthenes. Megasthenes was the Greek historian who visited Chandragupta’s court.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: What was the function of an officer called Samaharta ?
questions.explanation: Tax assessment. Officers during the Mauryan administration: Shulkadhyaksha (Officer-in-charge of royal income), Koshadhyaksha (Treasury officer), Lakshanadhyaksha (Coin minting), Rajjukas (Land measurer), Yukta (Subordinate revenue officer), Sannidata (Treasury head), Panyadhyaksha (Office of commerce department).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Emperor Ashoka conquered Kalinga after how many years of his coronation ?
questions.explanation: 8 years. Ashoka fought the Kalinga War in 261 BC. King Ashoka (268 - 232 BC) was the third king of the Mauryan Empire.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Mauryan provincial administration: A. The Mauryan Empire was divided into Janapadas (provinces), each headed by a Mahamatra. B. Each province had a Kumar or Kumara appointed as provincial governor. C. The Rajjukas were officials in charge of agriculture and land revenue collection. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: A and C only. No position called Kumar/Kumara existed as governor; provinces were administered by Mahamatras.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: How many classes of Indian society are mentioned in Megasthenes book Indica ?
questions.explanation: 7. They were Brahmins (upper class), Philosophers, Farmers, Herders, Artisans, Military, Overseers, Councillors and Assessors.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: According to Kautilya's Arthashastra, the Commanding Officer of the cavalry in the Mauryan administration was known as:
questions.explanation: Ashwadhyaksha. Officers in Mauryan Empire: Mantrin (Chief Minister), Senapati (Commander-in -Chief), Yuvraj (Crown prince), Shulkadhyaksha (Officer in-charge of royal income), Prashasti (Prison head), Koshadhyaksha (Treasury officer), Vyabharika (Chief Judge), Dandapala (Head of Police), Annapala (Head of food grains department), Pradeshika (District administrator), Hastyadhyaksha (Chief Commander of Elephant Corps), Rathadhyaksha (Chief Commander of Chariot Corps) and Nayaka (City security officer).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Mauryan pillar capital found at _____is popularly known as the Lion Capital.
questions.explanation: Sarnath Lion Capital - Erected by Ashoka (Around 250 BCE) in commemoration of Dhammachakra pravartana or the first sermon of Buddha. The Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath is the Indian National Emblem.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): Arthashastra is the manual of Mauryan administration and military organisation. Reason (R): It was authored by Varahamihira in Sanskrit.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, R is false
options.d: A is false, R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, R is false
questions.explanation: A is true, R is false. Arthashastra was authored by Kautilya (Chanakya/Vishnugupta), not Varahamihira. Varahamihira authored Brihat Samhita, which deals with astrology, architecture, and planetary calculations.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Nagarjuni Caves were donated to which of the following sects by Mauryans ?
questions.explanation: Ajivika - It was founded by Goshala Maskariputra. It is based on the philosophy that the affairs of the entire universe were ordered by a cosmic force called Niyati that determined all events, including an individual’s fate. The seven caves were created by Mauryan time for the Ajivika Sect.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: As per the contents mentioned in Asokan inscriptions, how many major political centres were there in the Mauryan empire ?
questions.explanation: Five. The five major political centres of the Mauryan empire were located at Pataliputra, Taxila, Ujjain, Tosali and Suvarnagiri.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): The Mauryan Empire maintained a state monopoly over mining and trade. Reason (R): Kautilya’s Arthashastra prescribes state control over mines, forests, salt, and trade to increase revenue.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, R is false
options.d: A is false, R is true

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. The Mauryan state directly controlled resources and trade, as prescribed in Arthashastra, to ensure revenue and economic stability.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Mauryan ruler was called Amitrochates by the Greeks ?
questions.explanation: Bindusara. He was the son of Chandragupta Maurya and was the second Mauryan emperor of India whose reign from 297 - 273 BCE.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: There were several cities in the Mauryan empire. Which of the following cities was located on the southernmost side ?
questions.explanation: Brahmagiri. The Maurya Empire: Founder - Chandragupta Maurya, Capital - Pataliputra (modern Patna). Three important rulers of the Mauryan Empire - Chandragupta, his son Bindusara, and Bindusara’s son, Ashoka.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following places does not contain the major inscription of Ashoka ?
questions.explanation: Sanchi. It is a famous Buddhist site with several stupas and monasteries. Language used in Ashoka’s inscriptions - Prakrit. Ashoka's name is only used in four of these locations: Maski, Brahmagiri (Karnataka), Gujjara (Madhya Pradesh) and Nettur (Andhra Pradesh).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Identify the correct statements regarding the Pillars of Ashoka: A. The Pillars of Ashoka were primarily built to spread the policies of Dharma. B. All Pillars of Ashoka were erected during the reign of Chandragupta Maurya. C. The Seventh Pillar Edict mentions Dhamma Mahamattas and is the longest among all pillar edicts.
questions.explanation: A and C only. Pillars were erected by Ashoka, not Chandragupta Maurya.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which caves are considered as the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India dating back to the Maurya period ?
questions.explanation: Barabar and Nagarjuni caves - Located in Jehanabad district of Bihar, Constructed by Emperor Ashoka for the benefit of Ajivika ascetics. They were cut from a single solid granite block.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Somewhat before the time of the Mauryan empire, about ____years ago, emperors in China began building the Great Wall.
questions.explanation: 2400. Emperor Qin Shi Huang ordered construction of the Great Wall around 221 B.C. It was meant to protect the northern frontier of the empire from pastoral people.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Pushyamitra, who was the commander of Brihadratha, the last Mauryan emperor, killed the king and established a new dynasty. Which of the following was his dynasty ?
questions.explanation: Shunga Dynasty Founder - Pushyamitra Sunga. Ruled - From 185 BCE to 73 BCE. Last Ruler - Devabhuti. Kanva Dynasty Founder - Vasudeva Kanva. Ruled - From 73 BCE to 28 BCE. Last Ruler - Susarma. Satavahana Dynasty Founder - Simuka . Famous Ruler - Gautamiputra Satakarni.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Ashoka appointed____to solve the social problems in his region.
questions.explanation: Dhamma Mahamatta. Tirthas: The highest category of officials in the administration. There were 18 Tirthas. Amatyas: High ranking officials almost like present-day secretaries. The important officials in the revenue department are Sannidhata: Chief treasury, Samaharta: collector general of revenue. Yuktas: Subordinate officers responsible for the Empire’s revenue. Rajjukas: Officers in charge of land measurement and boundary-fixing.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct ? I. Most of Ashoka’s inscriptions were written in Brahmi script. II. Many of Chanakya’s ideas were written down in a book called the Arthashastra.
questions.explanation: Both I and II. Brahmi Script was deciphered by James Prinsep.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Ashokan Minor Rock Edicts are found in different parts of India. Which of the following is NOT a find spot of Ashokan Minor Rock Edicts in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Rupnath. Minor rock edicts of Ashoka - Kandahar (Afghanistan), Lampaka (Afghanistan), Bahapur (Delhi), Bairat (Rajasthan), Bhabru (Rajasthan), Gujarra (Madhya Pradesh), Rupnath (Madhya Pradesh), Panguraria (Madhya Pradesh), Sasaram (Bihar), Barabar Caves (Bihar), Rajula-Mandagiri, Andhra Pradesh, Suvarna Giri (Andhra Pradesh), Brahmagiri (Karnataka), Jatina￾Rameshwara, Karnataka, Siddapur (Karnataka), Maski (Karnataka), Nittur (Karnataka), Udegolam (Karnataka), Palkigundu and Gavimath (Karnataka).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding 'Kantakasodhana' court: 1. Kantakasodhana literally means “removal of thorns.” 2. It was a type of civil court prevalent in the Mauryan Empire. 3. Kautilya’s Arthashastra mentions cases that are subject to Kantakasodhana. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 and 3 only. Kantakasodhana was not a civil court, but a criminal court in the Mauryan Empire dealing with serious offenses.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following published a set of Ashokan inscriptions in 1877 ?
questions.explanation: Alexander Cunningham. He was the founder of the Archaeological Survey of India.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements : A. Rudrasena II belonged to the Gupta dynasty. B. He married Prabhavatigupta, daughter of Samudragupta. C. Chandragupta II was the founder of the Vakataka dynasty. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: None of the above. Rudrasena II belonged to the Vakataka dynasty, not the Gupta dynasty. He married Prabhavatigupta, daughter of Chandragupta II, not Samudragupta. Chandragupta II was a Gupta ruler, not founder of the Vakataka dynasty (which was founded by Vindhyashakti).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The _____were tributary chiefs of the Gupta dynasty. They established an independent kingdom in western India. Dhruvasena II was the most important ruler of this kingdom.
questions.explanation: Maitrakas established Valabhi as their capital and ruled until the middle of the eighth century. Dhruvasena II was a contemporary of Harshavardhana and was married to his daughter. Hsuan Tsang tells us that Dhruvasena II attended Harsha’s assembly at Prayaga (Allahabad). Maukharies ruled over Kannauj, a city in western Uttar Pradesh, they were also the subordinate rulers of the Guptas and used the title of samanta.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was the author of 'Brihat Katha Kosh' ?
questions.explanation: Harisena. He was a Sanskrit writer and poet in the court of Samudragupta. "Brihat Katha Kosh" is a collection of ancient Indian folk tales and legends. Bhavabhuti is believed to be the court poet of King Yashovarman of Kannauj. His famous plays are Mahaviracharita, Malatimadhava.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Kalidasa: I. Kalidasa was a famous poet and playwright in ancient India. II. He was patronized by Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) of the Gupta dynasty. III. His notable works include Abhijnanasakuntalam, Meghaduta, and Raghuvamsa. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: I, II and III. Kumarasambhava describes the birth of Lord Kartikeya. Meghaduta, A lyrical poem (Kavya) where a yaksha sends a message to his wife via a cloud.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Harisena, the author of Prayag Prashasti, was the court poet of which of the following Gupta emperors ?
questions.explanation: Samudragupta. He was the son and successor of Chandragupta I and was the greatest ruler of the Gupta dynasty. The Allahabad Pillar inscription, also called Prayag Prashasti, was composed by Harishena.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Gupta emperor Chandragupta I was the first ruler to adopt which of the following titles ?
questions.explanation: Maharajadhiraja. Chandragupta I, the son of Gupta king Ghatotkacha and grandson of the dynasty's founder Sri Gupta, is referred to as Maharaja in the Allahabad Pillar inscription, while his successor, Kumaragupta, adopted the title "Mahendraditya."

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Fa Hien visited India during the reign of which of the following Gupta emperors ?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta II, also known as Vikramaditya, was the third ruler of the Gupta Empire. He is often identified with King Chandra from the Delhi iron pillar inscription. Notable Travellers and Their Visits - Abdul Razzak (Iran): Deva Raya II. Francois Bernier (France): Shah Jahan, Ibn Batuta (Morocco): Mohammed Bin Tughlaq, Megasthenes (Greece): Chandragupta Maurya, Thomas Roe and William Hawkins (Britain): Jahangir, Hwien Tsang (China): Harsha Vardhana.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the practice of Sati. Identify the incorrect statement: I.
