The Lodi dynasty was the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, ruling from 1451 to 1526. Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect ?
questions.explanation: 2 only. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Khilji dynasty ruled from 1290 to 1320, not 1320 to 1414.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Ibn Battuta, who visited India during Delhi Sultanate, originally belonged to which country ?
questions.explanation: Morocco. Ibn Battuta visited India in 1333 during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, who appointed him as the qazi (judge) of Delhi. Other notable foreign travelers : Hiuen Tsang (China) - Harshavardhana's court; Al-Beruni (Persia) - Came with Mahmud of Ghazni; Francois Bernier (France) - Shahjahan and Aurangzeb's court.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In reference to the Delhi Sultanate, what was the ‘Group of Forty’?

options.a: They were mostly powerful Turkish slaves of Iltutmish, who took power in the interregnum following Sultana Raziyya’s killing.
options.b: They were forty military archers who distinguished themselves by their bravery in the Delhi Sultanate.
options.c: They were forty banjara leaders who transferred military supplies in times of war.
options.d: They were forty Rajput nobles who planned a coup to dethrone Qutb ud Din Aibak in 1210.

questions.answer_text: They were mostly powerful Turkish slaves of Iltutmish, who took power in the interregnum following Sultana Raziyya’s killing.
questions.explanation: The 'Group of Forty' (Chalisa) in the Delhi Sultanate was a council of powerful Turkish slaves, formed by Iltutmish to assist in governance.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Vijayanagara Empire: 1. The Vijayanagara Empire was established in 1336 during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq . 2. Its first capital was Madurai. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Only 1. Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 by Harihara and Bukka during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq . The capital was Hampi, not Madurai.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following systems of the Delhi sultanate had a influence on the Bahmani and Vijayanagar kingdoms ?
questions.explanation: Iqtadari System:- Introduced by Shamsuddin IIltutmish (3rd Sultan of Delhi). Provision - Under this system, the land of the empire was divided into several large and small tracts called Iqta and assigned these Iqtas to his soldiers, officers and nobles. Administrative Terms used in Sultanate Period: Dabir (Secretary), Faujdar (Commander of army), Sipahsalar (Commander), Amil (Revenue officer), Diwan (Office: the central secretariat).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: During the Sultanate of Delhi, the term "Ulema" was associated with ______.
questions.explanation: Learned theologians and Jurists. Officers in Delhi Sultanate - State Level: Amil (Revenue Officer), Barid (Intelligence agents), Khwaja (Accounts Officer), Kotwal (Head of city law and order), Muhatasib (Head of municipality law and order), Muftis (Expounder of law).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was the daughter of Iltumish, a ruler of Slave Mamluk dynasty ?
questions.explanation: Razia Sultan. In 1236, Razia Sultan (Mamluk dynasty), succeeded her father to the Sultanate of Delhi. She sent an expedition against Ranthambore to control the Rajputs. Mamluk dynasty (1206 to 1290) - Founded by Qutbuddin Aibak (Lakh Baksh).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Under the Delhi Sultanate, a religious tax _____was imposed on the wealthy and rich Muslims in India.
questions.explanation: Zakat. Zakat tax was abolished by Sikander lodi. Firoz Shah Tughlaq introduced four types of taxes based on the Quran. They were Kharaj (Land tax), Khams (Tax on booty captured in war), Jizya (Imposed on non muslim), and Zakat.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding writers of the Delhi Sultanate period: 1. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri (1260), written in Persian by Minhaj-us-Siraj. 2. Hasan Nizami wrote Fatwa-i-Jahandari, regarded as the first official history of the Delhi Sultanate. 3. Ziauddin Barani authored Taj-ul-Maasir during the reign of Iltutmish. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Only 1. Fatwa-i-Jahandari was written by Ziauddin Barani, not Hasan Nizami. Taj-ul-Maasir was written by Hasan Nizami, not by Ziauddin Barani.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Zafar khan was a famous General of which of the following rulers of the Delhi Sultanate ?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khilji’s Generals : Hizabruddin (Zafar Khan), Almas Beg (Ulugh Khan), Malik Kafur (Taj al-Din Izz al-Dawla), Nusrat Khan (Malik Nusrat Jalesari). Muhammad bin Tughlaq (Jauna Khan): Introduced token currency.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following rulers ruled before Prithviraj Chauhan over Delhi ?
questions.explanation: Ananga Pala Tomar - founded Delhi in 1052. An inscription of Vikram Samvat 1383 in the Delhi Museum confirms the founding of Delhi by the Tomars.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the author of Tarikh - i - Mubarak Shahi which is a Persian language chronicle of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.explanation: Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi. Amir Khusrau (Books - ‘Tughlaq Nama’, ‘Nuh Sipihr’, ‘Khazain ul Futuh’ ).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the ruler of Delhi sultanate when Ibn Batuta came to India?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Bin Tughlaq was the ruler of the Delhi sultanate when Ibn Batuta came to India. Muhammad bin Tughluq was the Sultan of Delhi from 1324 to 1351 from the Tughlaq Dynasty.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Balban and Bengal: Statement 1: After the revolt and death of Tughril Beg, Balban appointed his son Bughra Khan as the governor of Bengal. Statement 2: Balban introduced the practice of Jaziya tax on Hindus as part of his theory of kingship.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.explanation: After Nasir-ud-din Mahmud died in 1266, Ghiyasuddin Balban (1266-1287) ascended the throne. He was also the first muslim ruler to formulate the ‘theory of Kingship’. Balban introduced the practice of Sijda (prostration) and Paibos (kissing the feet of Monarch). Tughril Beg revolted against Balban, Sultan of Delhi, and declared himself as an independent ruler of Bengal in 1279.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following departments of Delhi Sultanate was reorganized by Balban ?
questions.explanation: Diwan-i-Arz (Department of Military). Central Departments of Delhi Sultanates: ‘Diwan-i-Risalat’ - Department of Appeals, ‘Diwan-i-Bandagan’- Department of Slaves, ‘Diwan-i-Qaza-i-Mamalik’ - Department of Justice, ‘Diwan-i-Ishtiaq’ - Department of Pensions, ‘Diwan - i - Mustakhraj’- Departments of Arrears, ‘Diwan-i-Khairat’ - Department of Charity, ‘Diwan-i-Kohi’- Department of Agriculture, ‘Diwan -i-Wizarat’ - Head Wazir, ‘Diwan -i-Waqoof’ - Department of Revenue.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Sultan Balban: Statement 1: Balban was the ninth Sultan of the Slave dynasty who focused more on consolidation of his empire rather than territorial expansion. Statement 2: Balban is remembered for formulating the ‘Din-i-Ilahi’ doctrine during his reign.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.explanation: Ghiyasuddin Balban (Reigned : 1266–1287) was the ninth sultan of the Slave dynasty of Delhi. He belonged to the famous group of 40 Turkic slaves of Iltutmish. He was the first Muslim ruler to formulate the 'theory of kingship' similar to the 'theory of the divine right of the kings'. He established the military department “Diwan-i-Arz”.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Raziya Sultan was the first and only female ruler of the Sultanate, who ascended the throne in:
questions.explanation: 1236 AD. Razia Sultana was the daughter of Iltutmish and served as the Sultan of Delhi from 1236 to 1240. She was married to Malik Altunia, the governor of Bathinda. She was buried in Kaithal, Haryana. She was imprisoned by Malik Ikhtiyar-ud-din Altunia in the Qila Mubarak Fort (Bathinda). The book "Razia Queen of India" was written by Rafiq Zakaria about her life.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Delhi sultans introduced two coins, namely silver tanka and copper jital ?
questions.explanation: Iltutmish (1210 - 1236). He was a slave and son-in-law of Qutubuddin Aibak, considered the real founder of Delhi Sultanate.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Balban followed the tradition of ‘Sijda and Pabos’ from which of following traditions ?
questions.explanation: Persian. 'Sijda' refers to the act of prostration or bowing down, and 'Pabos' refers to the kissing of the monarch's feet.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following Delhi Sultanate rulers took the policy of ‘blood and iron’ to deal with the Mewati community ?
questions.explanation: Balban. The policy of 'blood and iron' implied being ruthless to the enemies, use of sword, harshness and strictness and shedding blood. Ghiyas ud din Balban was the ninth sultan of the Mamluk/Slave dynasty of Delhi.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Mameluke style of architecture belongs to which dynasty ?
questions.explanation: Slave dynasty (1206 - 1290) - It is also known as the Mamluk Dynasty. Established by - Qutbuddin Aibak (1206 - 1210). Capitals - Lahore . Famous buildings built by rulers of the slave dynasty: Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, Qutub Minar, Adhai Din ka Jhonpra, Tomb of Nasir-ud-Din Mohammed, Tomb of Shams-ud-Din Iltutmish.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Delhi sultan, who succumbed to injuries as a result of his fall from horse, was ______.
questions.explanation: Qutubuddin Aibak (Known as Lakh Baksh). He was the slave of Muhammad Ghori and was the first sultan of Delhi Sultanate. He established the slave dynasty (Mamluk dynasty). Famous Ruler of Slave Dynasty (1206 AD-1290 AD): Qutbuddin Aibak (1206-1210), Shamsuddin Iltutmish (1210-1236), Raziya Sultan (1236-1240), Balban (1266-1287).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Iltutmish: Statement 1: The Tomb of Iltutmish was built in 1388 AD. Statement 2: Iltutmish introduced the gold coin “Mohur” as the standard currency of the Delhi Sultanate.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true

questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect: Iltutmish’s tomb was built in 1235 AD, not 1388 AD. Statement 2 is incorrect: He introduced Tanka and Jital, not the gold Mohur.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who started the practice of celebrating Nauroz during the Delhi Sultanate period ?
questions.explanation: Ghiyasuddin Balban. Nowruz is the Iranian New Year, also known as the Persian New Year.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Statement 1: Balban served as Naib (Deputy) to Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud. Statement 2: Balban served as Naib to Sultan Razia.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.explanation: Balban served as Naib (Deputy) to Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud (1246–1266 AD), the eighth ruler of the Slave dynasty. During this period, Balban gained administrative and military experience, which later helped him become Sultan in 1266 AD. On the other hand, Razia Sultan (1236–1240 AD) was the first Muslim woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate, but Balban never served as her Naib.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following revolted against Balban, Sultan of Delhi, and declared himself as an independent ruler of Bengal in 1279 ?
questions.explanation: Tughril Beg. Balban (Mamluk dynasty or Slave Dynasty) - Ghiyas-ud-Din Balban appointed his own son Bughra khan as governor of Bengal. Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah Tughluq also known as Nasiruddin, was the last sultan of the Tughlaq dynasty.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who occupied Badaun (A.D. 1197-98) and appointed Iltutmish as its first Muslim Governor ?
questions.explanation: Qutbuddin Aibak {1206- 1210 (First ruler of Slave Dynasty /Mamluk Dynasty)}: He established the first Muslim dynasty and was also known as Lakh Baksh. He died in Lahore, Pakistan after falling from a horse ride.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Qutub Minar is an example of ______ architecture.
questions.explanation: Indo - Islamic. Indo-Islamic architecture is the architecture of the Indian subcontinent produced for Islamic patrons and purposes. Famous Examples - City of Mandu (Madhya Pradesh), Taj Mahal (Agra), Gol Gumbaz (Karnataka), Jama Masjid (Delhi) etc.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: What is the approximate height (in metres) of the Qutub Minar situated in Delhi ?
questions.explanation: 73 (239.5 ft. approx). Qutub Minar has five storeys. It was started in 1199 by Qutb ud-Din Aibak, completed in 1220 by his son-in-law Iltutmish. UNESCO (1993). Other Important Minars - Charminar, Hyderabad (1591) by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, height is 48.7 m (160 ft).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Statement 1: Nizam ul-Mulk Junaidi was the Wazir of Sultan Iltutmish. Statement 2: Nusrat Khan was appointed as the Wazir of Iltutmish.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.explanation: Sultan Iltutmish, who ruled from 1210 to 1236 AD, appointed Nizam ul-Mulk Junaidi as his Wazir. He played an important role in administration and strengthening the Delhi Sultanate. On the other hand, Nusrat Khan was not associated with Iltutmish as Wazir.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Ghiyasuddin Balban, ruler of the Slave dynasty, took up the title of _____.
questions.explanation: Zil-i-Ilahi (shadow of God). Ghiyas ud din Balban - Abolished Chahalghani (Council of 40 nobles), introduced Persian customs as sizdah (prostration), paibos (kissing feet of sultan), established Diwan-i-Ariz (defence department).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which of the following forts was Razia Sultan imprisoned by Malik Ikhtiyar-ud-din Altunia ?
questions.explanation: Qila Mubarak in Bathinda, built by Raja Dab. Jaigarh fort in Jaipur was built in 1726 AD by Jai Singh II. Golconda fort in Golconda was built by Qutb Shahi dynasty. Mehrangarh fort in Jodhpur was built by Rao Jodha.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the market reforms of Delhi Sultans: 1. Alauddin Khalji set up three separate markets in Delhi for grain, cloth, and horses/slaves/cattle. 2. The market superintendent appointed by Alauddin Khalji was called Diwan-i-Arz. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Alauddin Khalji introduced strict market control to prevent price rise. He established three separate markets in Delhi for grain, cloth, and horses/slaves/cattle. To enforce the system, he appointed a market superintendent called Shahna-i-Mandi, not Diwan-i-Arz (which was the military department created by Balban).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The first southern campaign of Alauddin Khilji in 1307-08 AD was led to which of the following regions ?
questions.explanation: Devagiri (modern-day Daulatabad, Maharashtra). This campaign marked the beginning of the Delhi Sultanate's expansion into southern India. Alauddin Khilji (1296 -1316) was the second sultan of the Khilji dynasty. Campaigns of Alauddin Khilji: Gujarat (1299), Ranthambore (1301), Chittor (1303), Malwa (1305), Madurai (1311), Dwarasamudra (1310-1311).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who amongst the following Delhi Sultanate rulers sent his army under Malik Kafur’s command to conquer South India ?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khilji. Malik Kafur - also known as 'Hazar Dinari’ was a slave of Ala-ud-din Khilji who led his army in the battle against Ramachandra of Devagiri. Administrative Reforms - implemented the system of "dagh Pratha ," branding horses, and "Huliya Pratha (a system of ranks)" keeping records of soldiers.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Sultans of Delhi set up the officers like Barid (intelligence officer) and Munhiyans (secret spies) to control the market?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji, ruler of the Delhi Sultanate, is known for implementing significant market reforms and establishing strict price controls and market regulations.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following Sultans framed a series of regulations to weaken the power of nobles ?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khilji (Khilji Dynasty 1290-1320): He made nobles pay land tax for their holdings. This curbed the excess of wealth owned by nobles. The nobles were also ordered not to have social gatherings or intermarriages without his permission. The group of nobles, called "The Forty".

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Amir Khusrau: 1. He was known as Tuti-e-Hind and was a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya. 2. He popularized Qawwali, a form of music derived from the Arabic word qaul. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Amir Khusrau, a celebrated poet and musician of the Sultanate period, was called Tuti-e-Hind and is credited with popularizing Qawwali.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Sultans of Delhi was appointed as Amir-i-Tuzuk (Master of Ceremonies) before becoming the Sultan ?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji (1296 - 1316). He was the second ruler of Khilji dynasty after Jalaluddin Khilji (Founder - ‘Khalji Dynasty’). He was also appointed Arizi-i-Mumalik (Minister of War) during the reign of Jalaluddin Khilji and laid the foundation of his capital Siri in 1303 A.D.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the first to mention the incident of Jauhar in Persian ?
questions.explanation: Amir Khusrau. ‘Jauhar’ - The collective self-immolation by women in order to escape capture and forced into slavery by invaders in face of imminent defeat.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: During Alauddin Khilji's reign, the cloth market was known as______.
questions.explanation: Sarai-i-Adl (Place of justice). Alauddin Khilji, under his market policy, built three markets of foodgrain, precious clothes and slave cattle near Kushke Sabz (Hara Rajmahal) within the Badaun gate in Delhi. These were government - aided markets.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate to start military expeditions into southern India ?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji (1296-1316):- He was the second ruler of the Khilji dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which monument of Khilji dynasty in Delhi has the utilization of red sandstone ?
questions.explanation: Alai Darwaza. Built by Allaudin Khilji the Sultan of Delhi in 1311 AD. Moti Masjid - Aurangzeb (Delhi). Victoria memorial - George V (Kolkata). Charminar - Mohammed Quli Qutub Shah (Hyderabad).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Shahna-i-Mandi was the officer responsible for maintaining a register of merchants to ensure adequate supply of goods. 2. Alauddin Khilji established only one central market in Delhi, where all commodities were sold together. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Only 1. Alauddin Khilji established three markets at Delhi—for food grains, for cloth & daily-use goods, and for horses, slaves & cattle..

questions.subject: History
questions.question: How many types of taxes were in the reign of the ruler Alauddin Khalji ?
questions.explanation: 3 types of taxes: Jaziya (religious tax on Hindu community), Ghari tax (tax on Houses), and Chari tax (tax on cattles).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Begumpuri mosque was built during the reign of which of the following rulers of the Delhi Sultanate ?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Tuglaq . He was the eighteenth Sultan of Delhi, ruling from February 1324 to 1351. The eldest son of Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq, founder of the Tughlaq dynasty, he built the Begumpur Mosque (Jam'i Masjid of Jahanpanah) in the capital, Jahanpanah.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was the first sultan of Delhi Sultanate to visit the Ajmer shrine of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti ?
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Tughlaq, originally known as Junakhan, ascended the throne in 1324. He is remembered for his efforts to maintain the administrative and political unity of India. In 1327 A.D., he successfully captured Warangal, a significant event in his reign.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Muhammad Tughlaq founded the Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi. 2. The Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi was established mainly to strengthen the army. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Only 1. Muhammad Tughlaq set up the Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi to bring more land under cultivation. He also promoted agriculture by reducing agrarian cesses and providing agricultural loans called Sondhar.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which amongst the following Sultans shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad ?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Bin Tughlaq: He shifted his capital from Delhi to the more centrally located Devagiri in Maharashtra, which was renamed Daulatabad. His Five Disastrous Projects are: Taxation in the Doab, Transfer of Capital, Khurasan Expedition, Qarachil Expedition, Introduction of Token Currency.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who invaded India during the rule of Tughlaq Dynasty ?
questions.explanation: Timur. During the reign of Nasir-ud-din Mahmud Tughlaq, Timur invaded India in 1398 A.D., leading to the decline of the Tughlaq dynasty.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following cities of Delhi was founded by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq ?
questions.explanation: Tughluqabad. Ghiyasuddin Tuglaq (reign period : 1320-1324) - Founder of Tughlaq dynasty (1320-1414 AD). Tughalq was the longest-ruling dynasty of Delhi sultanate. City and founder: Siri - Alauddin khilji; Jahanpanah - Muhammad bin Tughlaq; Qila-i-Rai Pithora - Prithviraj Chauhan.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Arrange the following rulers of the Tughlaq dynasty in chronological order: 1. Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq 2. Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq 3. Firuz Shah Tughlaq
questions.explanation: 1 – 2 – 3. The Tughlaq dynasty was founded by Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq (1320–1325). He was succeeded by his son Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq (1325–1351). The next ruler was Firuz Shah Tughlaq (1351–1388), remembered for irrigation works, Diwan-i-Khairat, and other welfare measures.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who amongst the following raised the banner of revolt against Nasiruddin Khusrau ?
questions.explanation: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq or Ghazi malik (1320-1324 AD) - He was the governor of Punjab during the reign of Allauddin khilji. He was the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty who fought against Mongols, and started Tughlaqabad Fort construction.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The author of Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi, Yahya Sirhindi claims that the founder of____dynasty of Delhi sultanate was a descendant of Prophet Muhammad.
questions.explanation: Sayyid. Khizr Khan defeated Sultan Daulat Khan and occupied Delhi, and founded the Sayyid dynasty in 1414. Capital : Delhi. Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi contains the history of Muhammad Ghori and his rulers up to the third ruler of the

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Arrange the following rulers of the Sayyid Dynasty in chronological order: 1. Alauddin Alam Shah 2. Khizr Khan 3. Mubarak Shah 4. Muhammad Shah
questions.explanation: 2 – 3 – 4 – 1. Khizr Khan (1414–1421) – Founder of the Sayyid dynasty. Mubarak Shah (1421–1434) – Constructed Mubarakbad city and appointed Hindu nobles in his court. Muhammad Shah (1434–1445). Alauddin Alam Shah (1445–1451) – Last ruler, surrendered Delhi to Bahlul Lodi in 1451.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate finally annexed Jaunpur into the empire of Delhi Sultanate ?
questions.explanation: Lodi dynasty was founded by Bahlol Lodi, the last ruling dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, ruling from 1451 to 1526. In AD 1476, Bahlol Lodi defeated the Sultan of Jaunpur and annexed it to the Delhi Sultanate. He also brought the ruler of Kalpi and Dholpur under the Suzerainty of Delhi.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was the last sultan of Delhi sultanate ?
questions.explanation: Ibrahim Lodi was the last Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526), he became Sultan in 1517 after the death of his father Sikandar Khan Lodi. In 1526, he was defeated and killed in the Battle of Panipat by Babur, giving way to the emergence of the Mughal Empire in India.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following dynasties of Delhi Sultanate founded Agra city ?
questions.explanation: Lodi dynasty (1451 - 1526). It was founded by Bahlul Lodi (1451 to 1489 AD). Sultan Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504. Famous Historic City and their Founder: Fatehpur Sikri (Uttar Pradesh) - Akbar, Hampi (Karnataka) - Harihara I and Bukka Raya I, Udaipur (Rajasthan) - Udai Singh II, Warangal (Telangana) - Kakatiya dynasty.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding mosques of Delhi Sultanate: 1. Moth ki Masjid in Delhi was built during the Lodi dynasty. 2. Begumpuri Mosque in Delhi was constructed during the reign of the Lodis. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Only 1. Moth ki Masjid was built in 1505 by Wazir Miya Bhoiya during the Lodi dynasty. Begumpuri Mosque was constructed under Muhammad bin Tughlaq, not the Lodis.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: “Double Dome” feature of Indo-Islamic architecture was introduced by which dynasty of Delhi Sultanate ?
questions.explanation: Lodi Dynasty (1451-1526). Double dome - Built of two layers. There is one layer inside which provides a ceiling to the interior of the building. The other layer is the outer one which crowns the buildings. Example - Humayun's Tomb.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Sharqi dynasty: 1. The dynasty was founded by Khwajah-i-Jahan Malik Sarwar in 1394. 2. The Sharqi dynasty ruled over the Agra Sultanate. 3. The dynasty came to an end after the defeat of Sultan Hussain Shah by Bahlul Lodi in 1479. Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect ?
questions.explanation: Only 2. The Sharqi dynasty did not rule over Agra; it ruled the Jaunpur Sultanate. It was founded in 1394 by Khwajah-i-Jahan Malik Sarwar. It ended in 1479 after Sultan Hussain Shah Sharqi was defeated by Bahlul Lodi.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: How did the administrative roles of rajas differ from those of zamindars under the Mughal system

options.a: Zamindars were subordinate tax officers under the rajas, appointed directly by the emperor.
options.b: Rajas and zamindars performed identical roles but differed in their religious affiliations.
options.c: Rajas governed broader regions and held a higher status, while zamindars primarily managed land revenue collection.
options.d: Zamindars exercised complete political control, whereas rajas held only ceremonial titles.

questions.answer_text: Rajas governed broader regions and held a higher status, while zamindars primarily managed land revenue collection.
questions.explanation: Under the Mughal administrative system, rajas (especially Rajput rulers and other local kings) governed large territories and had higher political status. Zamindars, on the other hand, were land revenue collectors and intermediaries who managed smaller areas, often villages or clusters of villages. They were important for revenue administration but did not hold sovereignty like rajas.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following best explains the reason to held Qandhar strategically important for the Mughals?

options.a: It provided direct naval access to the Red Sea for Mughal expeditions.
options.b: It served as a religious pilgrimage center linking India with Central Asian Sufi shrines.
options.c: It was a crucial trade hub connecting the Arabian Sea with the Persian Gulf.
options.d: It controlled key land routes between Kabul and Herat and acted as a fortified military outpost.

questions.answer_text: It controlled key land routes between Kabul and Herat and acted as a fortified military outpost.
questions.explanation: Qandhar (Kandahar, Afghanistan) was a key Mughal frontier, controlling routes between Central Asia, Persia, and India. Served as a fortified military outpost and trade gateway. Its strategic value led to repeated Mughal–Safavid conflicts under Akbar, Jahangir, and Shah Jahan.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: What led to the decline of Timurid power in the second half of the 15th century ?

options.a: Economic decline due to maritime trade shifts

questions.explanation: The Timurid Empire, founded by Timur (Tamerlane) in the late 14th century, began to weaken in the second half of the 15th century. The main reasons were: Rise of the Uzbeks under Muhammad Shaybani, who consolidated power in Central Asia and displaced the Timurids from Transoxiana (Samarkand and Bukhara). Timurid princes were also engaged in internal conflicts, but the decisive blow came from the expanding Uzbek power. The fall of Timurid authority in Central Asia eventually forced Babur, a Timurid prince, to seek opportunities elsewhere, leading to the foundation of the Mughal Empire in India (1526).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements in the context of the Mughal Rule. 1. The Mansabdari System was introduced by Akbar in 1571. 2. The Second Battle of Panipat was fought in 1556. 3. Maharana Pratap Singh of Mewar was a contemporary of Babur. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Maharana Pratap Singh was a contemporary of the third Mughal emperor Akbar. He is notable for leading the Rajput resistance against Akbar's expansionist policies, including in the Battle of Haldighati (1576) and the Battle of Dewair (1582). The Second Battle of Panipat was fought between Akbar and Hemu. The mansabdari system was basically a grading system in order to rank the officers based on their ranks and salaries.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was the guru of Tansen ?
questions.explanation: Swami Haridasa. The famous musician Tansen was one of the Navratnas (nine gems) in the court of Emperor Akbar, who bestowed the title 'Mian' upon him.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was given the charge of looking after the imperial household during the Mughal administration ?
questions.explanation: Mir Saman. Mir Bahri (mir-i-bahr) - Responsible for the maintenance of the river and seaports. Mir Bakshi - Headed military department, nobility, information and intelligence agencies. Mir-e-aatish - Head of the ordinance department.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding foreign travelers to India: 1. Jean-Baptiste Tavernier, a French jeweler, traveled to India several times during the Mughal period, especially in the reign of Shah Jahan. 2. Antonio Monserrate was a Spanish missionary who came to India during the reign of Shah Jahan. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Jean-Baptiste Tavernier, a French jeweler, visited India six times during Shah Jahan’s reign, making Statement 1 correct. Antonio Monserrate, however, was a Spanish missionary who came during Akbar’s reign, not Shah Jahan’s, so Statement 2 is incorrect. Hence, Tavernier’s association is with Shah Jahan, while Monserrate’s is with Akbar.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who built the Pathar Ki Masjid in Patna, Bihar ?
questions.explanation: Parwez Shah (Son of Mughal Emperor Jahangir) built “Pathar Ki Masjid” on the banks of River Ganga, Patna (Bihar) in 1621.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: On 12 August____the Mughal emperor appointed the East India Company as the Diwan of Bengal.
questions.explanation: On 12 August 1765, the Mughal emperor (Shah Alam II) appointed the East India Company as the Diwan of Bengal.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: ____in Gujarat was the emporium of western trade during the Mughal Period.
questions.explanation: Surat. It grew famous for all types of textiles, particularly cotton textiles.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Mughal court chronicles are written in _____
questions.explanation: Persian. Mughal chronicles such as the Akbar Nama were written in Persian. Some of the famous Books during Mughal Reign are Humayun Nama was written by Gulbadan Begum, Tuzuk - E Babari - Babur, Akbar Nama- Abul Fazl, Tarikh E Akbari - Abul Fazl, Tahakik E Hind- Albiruni, Laila Majnu- Amir Khasuru, Shahnamah- Firdousi etc

questions.subject: History
questions.question: With reference to the Land Revenue System of Mughal Empire, the term ' was the amount assessed.
questions.explanation: Jama. The arrangements for collection of land revenue consisted of two stages : first assessment and then actual collection. The Jama was the amount assessed whereas the Hasil was the amount received or collected. Banjar was the worst kind of land that was left out of cultivation for five years or upwards.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Mughal prince translated the Upanishads into Persian in 1657?
questions.explanation: Dara Shikoh. He was the eldest son and heir-apparent of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan. He completed the translation of fifty upanishads from their original Sanskrit to Persian in 1657 so that they could be studied by muslim scholars.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the Mughal Emperor at the time of Battle of Plassey ?
questions.explanation: Aziz-ud-din Alamgir II. Alamgir II (Reign - 1754-1759) was the fifteenth Mughal Emperor.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the battles of Babur: Statement 1: The Battle of Khanwa (1527) was fought between Babur and Rana Sanga. Statement 2: The Second Battle of Panipat (1527) was fought between Babur and Hemu.

options.c: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect
options.d: Statement 1 is incorrect, Statement 2 is correct

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect
questions.explanation: The Battle of Khanwa in 1527 was fought between Babur and Rana Sanga, and Babur emerged victorious, strengthening his control over northern India, making Statement 1 correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Second Battle of Panipat occurred in 1556 between Hemu and Akbar, not involving Babur.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The real name of Babur, the founder of Mughal dynasty in India was:
questions.explanation: Zahiruddin Muhammad. Real names of some Mughal emperors include: Humayun - Nasir al-Din Muhammed, Akbar - Jalal- ud-din Muhammad Akbar, Jahangir - Muhammad Salim, Aurangzeb - Muhi-ud-din-Muhammad.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Medini Rai of Chanderi, Hasan Khan of Mewat and Mahmud Lodi joined Rana Sanga with their forces to fight against which of the following Mughal rulers ?
questions.explanation: Babur. He was a descendant of Genghis Khan and Timur, founded the Mughal Empire in northern India .

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The battle of Khanwa was fought between the forces of the Babur and the Rajput forces led by:
questions.explanation: Rana Sanga.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the use of Gunpowder in North India: Statement 1: Babur made the use of gunpowder common in North India to defeat his enemies. Statement 2: Ibrahim Lodi introduced gunpowder in the Deccan region for the first time.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.explanation: Babur was the first to use gunpowder effectively in North India, especially in the First Battle of Panipat (1526) against Ibrahim Lodi. This new technology gave him an advantage over Indian rulers who depended on cavalry and war elephants.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the eldest of four sons of Babur ?
questions.explanation: Humayun - The second ruler of the Mughal empire. The Afghan soldier Sher Shah Suri defeated him at the war in Chausa 1539 and Kannauj in 1540. Humayun was the first person who developed a citadel in Delhi, named as “Din Panah”.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The first battle of Panipat took place between Babur and ____.
questions.explanation: Ibrahim Lodi. The First Battle of Panipat was fought in 1526. Second Battle of Panipat (1556): Hemu Vikramaditya and Akbar . Third Battle of Panipat (1761): Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following Mughal Emperors had assumed the title of Padshah ?
questions.explanation: Babur. He was the first Timurid ruler who, after his conquest of Kabul (1507), assumed the title of Padshah which means "king of kings" or "emperor in persian".

questions.subject: History
questions.question: After years of wandering Babur seized Kabul in______.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The famous monument, Aram Bagh, was built by Babur. It is located in ______.
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh. Aram Bagh - Built by Babur in 1528 in Agra. Monuments Built by Babur: The avenue garden in Kabul, the Panipat Mosque and the Kabuli Bagh Mosque.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Where was Babur buried for the first time in 1530 ?
questions.explanation: Agra. On December 26, 1530, Babur died at Agra. His body was first laid at Arambagh in Agra but was later taken to Kabul, where it was buried.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Name the Mughal emperor known for promoting Persian art and literature ?
questions.explanation: Humayun (1530–40, 1555–56) is remembered for introducing Persian art and culture into Mughal India. Influenced by Safavid traditions during exile in Persia. Invited Persian painters, poets, scholars after restoration. Mir Sayyid Ali & Abdus Samad came to his court, laying the base of Mughal miniature painting, later expanded under Akbar, Jahangir, and Shah Jahan. Shah Jahan – Famous for architecture (Taj Mahal, Red Fort) rather than literary patronage. Akbar – Promoted Indo-Persian culture, translation of texts, but the Persian literary wave began with Humayun. Jahangir – Great patron of naturalistic painting and fine arts, but not the pioneer of Persian literature.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Arrange the following Mughal emperors in chronological order of their rule: 1. Akbar 2. Humayun 3. Babur 4. Shah Jahan
questions.explanation: 3 → 2 → 1 → 4. The chronological order of the Mughal emperors is: Babur (1526–1530), followed by his son Humayun (1530–1540, restored 1555–1556), then Akbar (1556–1605), and later Shah Jahan (1628–1658).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: As per the Timurid tradition, Humayun had to share power with his brothers. Humayun had the control of Delhi, Agra and Central India, while his brother Kamran controlled which of the following regions ?
questions.explanation: Afghanistan and Punjab. Kamran Mirza was the second son of Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire. He was the brother of Humayun, who was born Nasir-ud-Din Muhammad in Kabul. Humayun was the second Emperor of the Mughal Empire, ruling over present-day Pakistan, Northern India, Afghanistan, and Bangladesh from 1530 to 1540 and again from 1555 to 1556.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements: Statement 1: The Battle of Chausa was fought between Humayun and Sher Shah Suri in 1539. Statement 2: Sher Shah Suri was defeated by Humayun in the Battle of Chausa.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.explanation: The Battle of Chausa (1539) occurred between Humayun and Sher Shah Suri, where Humayun suffered a major defeat. Sher Shah Suri emerged victorious, which strengthened his claim to power in North India.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Sher khan defeated Humayun in the battle of Chausa and Kanauj and forced him to flee to______.
questions.explanation: Iran. Sher Khan, an ethnic Pashtun, defeated Humayun in the battles of Chausa (1539) and battles of Bilgram/Kannauj (1540), forcing Humayun to flee to Iran. After these victories, Sher Khan crowned himself Farid al-Dīn Sher Shah and founded the Sur Dynasty.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following cities was built by Humayun in Delhi ?
questions.explanation: Dinpanah. Humayun’s Contribution to Architecture: Humayun's Tomb (UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993) - It was built by his widow Biga Begum (Hajji Begum), Purana Quila (Delhi) - Built as a part of the new city Dinpannah.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which State of India is Sher Shah's Tomb located ?
questions.explanation: Bihar (Sasaram). Tombs of Mughal Emperors - Gardens of Babur (Kabul, Afghanistan), Humayun's Tomb (New Delhi), Akbar's Tomb (Sikandra, Uttar Pradesh), Tomb of Jahangir (Lahore, Pakistan), The Taj Mahal (Agra), Tomb of Aurangzeb (Ahmednagar).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following medieval rulers focused his attention on the construction of sarais (shelter) for the convenience of travellers ?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri (1540-1545): Administrative reforms - Introduction of Rupiya, Built Grand-Trunk Road, Staged Dak-Chowkis in Sarais.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The historical Sher-Shah Suri Marg runs between ______.
questions.explanation: Delhi and Amritsar. The Grand Trunk Road (formerly known as Uttarapath, Sarak-e-Azam and Badshahi Sarak) - Part of National Highway (12, 27, 19, 44, 3) in India.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Humayun’s Tomb situated in Delhi is built by ______.
questions.explanation: Biga Begum. The architect was Mirak Mirza Ghiyath.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Mirza Kamran was the brother of which of the following Mughal emperors?
questions.explanation: Humayun and son of Babur and Gulrukh Begum. He came to India in 1538.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Mughal emperor did Maharana Pratap face in the Battle of Haldighati ?
questions.explanation: Akbar. The Battle of Haldighati (1576) was fought between Maharana Pratap of Mewar and the Mughal forces under Man Singh I of Amer, representing Emperor Akbar. It was triggered by Maharana Pratap’s firm refusal to accept Mughal suzerainty. Babur: He was the founder of the Mughal Empire and fought against Maharana Pratap's grandfather, Rana Sanga, at the Battle of Khanwa in 1527. Jahangir: He was Akbar's son and successor. As prince Salim and later as emperor, he continued the campaign against Mewar, which was then ruled by Maharana Pratap's son, Amar Singh I.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Akbar’s first expedition towards Deccan was sent to Ahmednagar under the leadership of Prince Murad and _____.
questions.explanation: Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan. Akbar was the third Mughal emperor, and he ruled over India from 1556 to 1605.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the following Navratnas of Akbar with their respective roles: Column A (Navratnas) Column B (Positions) 1. Raja Todar Mal (a) Defence Minister 2. Abul Fazl (b) Prime Minister and chief advisor 3. Abdul Rahim (c) Revenue Minister 4. Tansen (d) Culture Minister and Singer
questions.explanation: 1 → c, 2 → b, 3 → a, 4 → d. Navratnas of Akbar : Abul Fazl - Prime Minister and chief advisor. Faizi - Education Minister. Birbal - Foreign Minister. Raja Man Singh - Chief of Staff of Akbar’s Mughal Army. Tansen - Culture Minister and Singer. Abdul Rahim Khan-I-Khana - Defence Minister. Mullah Do Piyaza - Home Minister. Fakir Aziao-Din - Religious Minister.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: After the death of Humayun, the 13 year-old Akbar was coronated in 1556 at Kalanaur in ________.
questions.explanation: Punjab. Akbar was crowned at Kalanaur on February 14, 1556, following the sudden death of Humayun, who died after falling from the stairs of the Dinpanah library. At just 13 years old, Akbar came to power under the guidance of his guardian, Bairam Khan. He later defeated Hemu in the Second Battle of Panipat, securing control over Delhi.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Akbar’s Navratnas: Statement 1: Tansen, originally named Ramtanu Pandey, was one of the Navratnas in the court of Akbar. Statement 2: Amir Khusro was also one of the Navratnas of Akbar.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.explanation: Tansen, a legendary musician known as “Sangeet Samrat,” was indeed one of Akbar’s Navratnas. However, Amir Khusro was not part of Akbar’s court; he lived earlier during the Delhi Sultanate under Alauddin Khilji.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was the Vakil under the reign of Mughal Emperor Akbar, who received the title of Khan-i-Khanan ?
questions.explanation: Bairam Khan. A prominent Mughal noble and military commander who served as Akbar's regent and chief minister during the early years of his reign.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which amongst the following statements is correct about Mughal emperor Akbar ?

options.a: He founded a new religion called ‘Din-e Ilahi’.
options.b: He fought and won the third battle of Panipat against the Hindu King Hemu
options.d: He was highly educated and knew many languages.

questions.answer_text: He founded a new religion called ‘Din-e Ilahi’.
questions.explanation: He founded a new religion called ‘Din-e-Ilahi’. The theory of Din-e-Ilahi means belief in one God. The first initiated disciples of Din-i-Ilahi during emperor Akbar included Birbal, Prince Salim, and Abul-Fazl ibn Mubarak.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who amongst the following Mughal emperors got classical Hindu mythological texts Ramayana and Mahabharata translated into Persian ?
questions.explanation: Akbar was the 3rd Mughal emperor (1556 to 1605). The Mahabharata was translated by Faizi and `Abd al-Qadir Bada'uni and named Razmnama. Literature under the rule of Akbar: Akbarnama (Autobiography of Akbar) and Ain-i-Akbari written by Abu'l-Fazl.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Akbar are true? 1. He introduced the Mansabdari system. 2. He defeated and merged the state of Bijapur in his empire. 3. He made Fatehpur Sikri his capital.
questions.explanation: Only 1 and 3. The Mansabdari system was a system of ranking government officials and military generals in the Mughal Empire, which was introduced by Emperor Akbar in 1571. Aurangzeb, the sixth Mughal emperor (1658-1707), sent his armies to conquer the Deccan Sultanates. He annexed Bijapur in 1685 and Golconda in 1687.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: When Akbar introduced Mansabdari system, _____was the lowest grade of Mansabdar.
questions.explanation: Ten. The term mansabdar refers to an individual who holds a mansab, meaning a position or rank. It was a grading system used by the Mughals to fix rank, salary and military responsibilities. During Akbar's reign, the lowest rank allotted was 10, and the highest was that of 10,000.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: When was Khandesh merged into the Mughal empire by Akbar ?
questions.explanation: 1601. Khandesh was situated in the Tapti valley, Maharashtra. It was founded by Malik Raja Faruqi. Major military campaigns by Akbar - In 1568 the Sisodiya capital of Chittor was seized and in 1569 Ranthambore.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the defence of Chittorgarh Fort: Statement 1: Jaimal and Patta were the Rajput warriors entrusted with defending the fort of Chittor against Akbar in 1567–1568. Statement 2: The Siege of Chittorgarh was led by Sher Shah Suri against the Mewar kingdom.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.explanation: Jaimal and Patta heroically defended the fort of Chittorgarh during Akbar’s siege of 1567–1568. The campaign was not led by Sher Shah Suri but by Akbar, who eventually captured the fort after a fierce battle.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Tansen, the music legend, was a courtier in which of the following courts before coming to Akbar ?
questions.explanation: Rewa. Tansen was initially the court singer of King Ram Chand. His original name was RamaTanu Pandey. Tansen was the title given to him by Raja Vikramjit of Gwalior.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding land classification during Akbar’s reign: Statement 1: Chachar was the land that was always cultivated and never allowed to lie fallow. Statement 2: Polaj was the ideal land that remained under continuous cultivation without being left fallow.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.explanation: Chachar was land left fallow for three to four years, not land cultivated continuously. Polaj was the most fertile land that remained under constant cultivation and was never allowed to lie fallow.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following cities was the first planned city of the Mughals ?
questions.explanation: Fatehpur Sikri. It is located near Agra in Uttar Pradesh. It was built by the Mughal Emperor Akbar in the 16th century. Fatehpur Sikri was built during 1571 and 1585. Fatehpur Sikri was declared as UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 1986.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: When was the Battle of Tukaroi fought where Akbar defeated the Sultanate of Bengal and Bihar ?
questions.explanation: 1575. The Battle of Tukaroi (Battle of Bajhaura/ Moghalmari) - Fought at Balasore (Odisha) in which Akbar (Mughal Emperor) defeated Daud Khan Karrani (Ruler of Bengal). The battle led to the Treaty of Katak in which Daud Khan Karrani ceded the whole of Bengal and Bihar, retaining only Odisha.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: ____administration became the model followed by the great emperor Akbar when he consolidated the Mughal Empire.
questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri's. Although the Suri dynasty ruled for only a short period i.e. 15 years, it introduced an administration that borrowed elements from Alauddin Khilji and made them more efficient.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Ain-i Akbari, a document on life of Mughal ruler Akbar does not contain information about ______
questions.explanation: Ancestors. Abul Fazl (Akbar’s court historian) wrote a three-volume history of Akbar’s reign, titled Akbar Nama. The first volume (Akbar’s ancestors), second volume (events of Akbar’s reign) and The third (the Ain-i Akbari). Ain-i Akbari is divided into five volumes .

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Ajmer became the suba headquarters under the ______.
questions.explanation: Mughals. Ajmer Subah - One of the original 12 subahs of Mughal Empire (1526 - 1858). It was established during Akbar's administrative reforms of 1572–1580. The last Mughal - Bahadur Shah Zafar.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which year was Kashmir annexed to the Mughal Empire by Akbar ?
questions.explanation: 1586. Military Conquests of Akbar (Mughal Emperor, 1556-1605): Malwa (conquered in 1562), Gondwana region of central India (1564), Gujarat (1573), Mewar (1576), both Bihar and Bengal (1576).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: As described in ‘Ain-i-Akbari’ by Abul Fazl-i-Allami, ‘gaz’ (unit of measuring length) was divided into equal parts called ______.
questions.explanation: tassuj.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following issued Mahzarnama in 1579 ?
questions.explanation: Akbar issued Mahzarnama in 1579. It is a declaration that gives authority to change the religious laws of Islam.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the foundation of Murshidabad: Statement 1: The city of Makhsudabad, later known as Murshidabad, was built by Mughal emperor Akbar. Statement 2: Murshidabad got its present name from Nawab Murshid Quli Khan.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.explanation: Murshidabad was not built by Akbar; rather, it developed later and was renamed by Nawab Murshid Quli Khan in the early 18th century after his own name. Akbar is known for constructing Fatehpur Sikri, starting Din-i-Ilahi, and promoting cultural synthesis.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In the context of Mughal administration, which of the following is the most appropriate definition of ‘Abwab’ ?

options.a: A clerk in the government treasury
options.c: A tax levied on the lands over and above the original rent

questions.answer_text: A tax levied on the lands over and above the original rent
questions.explanation: A tax levied on the lands over and above the original rent in Mughal India all temporary and circumstantial taxes and impositions levied by the government over and above regular taxes were called “abwab”.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Mughal emperor is known for his extensive autobiography, Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri?
questions.explanation: Jahangir. The Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, also known as the Jahangirnama, is the autobiography of the fourth Mughal Emperor, Jahangir. Written in Persian, this memoir details the events of the first nineteen years of his reign, along with his personal reflections on art, politics, and family. Akbar: Akbar's reign is chronicled in the Akbarnama, which was written by his court historian, Abul Fazl. Shah Jahan: The history of Shah Jahan's reign is recorded in the Padshahnama, authored by the court historian Abdul Hamid Lahori.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Amar Singh of Mewar: Statement 1: Amar Singh was the son of Rana Sanga and accepted Mughal service during the reign of Aurangzeb. Statement 2: Amar Singh was the Sisodiya ruler of Mewar who surrendered to Akbar in 1600.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true

questions.explanation: Amar Singh was not the son of Rana Sanga but the son of Maharana Pratap. He did not submit to Akbar or Aurangzeb but to Jahangir in 1615, marking the end of prolonged Mughal–Mewar conflict.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who succeeded in securing trading concessions for the East India Company from Mughal Emperor Jahangir?
questions.explanation: Thomas Roe was an English diplomat sent by the East India Company in 1615. John Mildenhall was the first British explorer to make an overland journey to India. Captain William Hawkins was an English sea captain who visited the court of Jahangir in 1608.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following wrote the biography of Jahangir known as Iqbalnama-i Jahangiri ?
questions.explanation: Mutamid Khan. He was in the court of Mughal Emperor Jahangir (4th Mughal ruler, 1605 to 1627). ‘Iqbalnama-i Jahangiri’ book was written in Persian and it covers the first 19 years of Jahangir's reign. Inayat Khan wrote” Shajahanama”. Abdul Rahim Khan translated “Babarnama” to the Persian language.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Sarai Nurmahal is a centrally protected monument of India. It is situated in which state of India ?
questions.explanation: Punjab (Jalandhar). Shalimar Bagh, the Begum Shahi Mosque, and the Bachcha Taj are the monuments built by the Jahangir (Fourth Mughal emperor).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Mehrunnisa married Emperor Jahangir in ______.
questions.explanation: In 1611, Jahangir married Mehrunnisa who was known as Nur Jahan (Light of World). She encouraged Persian art and culture in the court.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Battle of Samugarh was fought between Aurangzeb and which Mughal prince ?
questions.explanation: Battle of Samugarh (29 May 1658). Part of the Mughal war of succession (1657–1658) after Emperor Shah Jahan fell ill. The main contest was between Dara Shikoh (Shah Jahan’s eldest son) and Aurangzeb. Other brothers, including Murad Baksh and Shuja, also joined in different stages, but the decisive battle was fought at Samugarh (near Agra) between Aurangzeb and Dara Shikoh. Dara Shikoh was defeated, paving the way for Aurangzeb’s capture of Agra and later imprisonment of Shah Jahan.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Identify the Mughal emperor who was imprisoned for the rest of his life in Agra after the war of succession among his sons.
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan (Mirza Shahab-ud-din Baig Muhammad Khan Khurram). He was the fifth Mughal emperor and reigned from 1628 to 1658. Aurangzeb declared himself emperor in 1658 and imprisoned Shah Jahan in Agra Fort until his death in January 1666.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the succession of Shah Jahan: Statement 1: Shah Jahan chose his eldest son Dara Shikoh as his successor to the Mughal throne. Statement 2: Dara Shikoh defeated Aurangzeb in the Battle of Deorai (1659) and became emperor.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan nominated his eldest son Dara Shikoh as his successor. However, Aurangzeb contested this claim and defeated Dara Shikoh in the Battle of Deorai (1659). Dara was executed, and Aurangzeb ascended the throne.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following has written the ‘Badshah Nama’ ?
questions.explanation: Abdul Hamid Lahori - A historian and traveler who later became a court historian of Shah Jahan. “Badshah Nama” (Padshahnama) is the official history of Shah Jahan.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The mausoleum of the Taj Mahal was designed by ______.
questions.explanation: Ustad Ahmad Lahori was the chief Mughal architect during the reign of Shah Jahan. He was responsible for the construction of the Taj Mahal in Agra and the Red fort in Delhi.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The art of decoration, called Pietra dura became popular during whose reign ?
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan. Pietra dura - An inlay technique using cut and fitted, highly polished colored stones to create images. Some other buildings and monuments by Shah Jahan:- Red Fort (Delhi), Jama Masjid (Delhi), Shish Mahal (Agra) and Shalimar Bagh (Lahore).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Ahmadnagar was finally annexed by the Mughals in_______
questions.explanation: In 1632, during the period of Shah Jahan, Ahmednagar was merged into the Mughal empire. Malik Ahmed was the founder of Ahmednagar (Maharashtra), who established the Nizam Shahi dynasty.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following had been given the title of ‘Sultan Buland Iqbal’ by Shah Jahan ?
questions.explanation: Dara Shikoh (Eldest Son of Shah Jahan). Sultan Buland Iqbal (Prince of High Fortune) - Title given on 10 September 1642. His works - Majma -ul-Bahrain (Mingling of Two Oceans), Sirr-i-Akbar (Great Mystery). He was executed in 1659 by Aurangzeb in the war of succession.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Mughal Emperor issued the Deccan campaign against the Marathas and spent significant time in the region ?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb. The Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb (1658–1707) launched the most extensive Deccan campaign in Mughal history. After the death of Shivaji in 1680, Aurangzeb personally moved to the Deccan and remained there for 27 years (1680–1707) until his death at Ahmednagar. His primary aim was to crush the rising Marathas and annex the Deccan Sultanates of Bijapur (1686) and Golconda (1687). He succeeded in capturing Bijapur and Golconda, but the Marathas under Sambhaji, Rajaram, and later Tarabai continued their guerrilla warfare. The prolonged war drained the Mughal treasury, weakened the army, and overstretched administration. His Deccan obsession is considered a major reason for the decline of the Mughal Empire after his death. The campaign also led to the rise of Maratha power, which eventually filled the vacuum left by declining Mughal authority.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Mughal ruler was responsible for the execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur in the year 1675 ?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb. Guru Tegh Bahadur was the ninth Sikh Guru, often venerated as the ‘Protector of Humanity’ (Srisht-di-Chadar) by the Sikhs. He founded Anandpur Sahib.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Under whose rule did the Mughal empire achieve its largest territorial limits?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb (1658 - 1707) ascended the throne in 1658 after eliminating all competitors, including Dara Shukoh, Shuja, and Murad, in a war of succession.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Rathor Rajputs of Marwar: Statement 1: The rebellion of the Rathor Rajputs of Marwar began due to Akbar’s interference in their succession politics. Statement 2: Babur suppressed the Rathor rebellion of Marwar during his reign.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true

questions.explanation: The Rathor Rajput rebellion of Marwar occurred due to Aurangzeb’s interference in their internal politics and succession disputes, not because of Akbar or Babur. Akbar generally maintained friendly alliances with Rajputs, while Babur fought mainly against Afghan and Rajput confederacies during his short reign.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Under which of the following Mughal emperors were the Marathas a major challenge to the sovereignty of the Mughals ?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb (Reign : 1658-1707) - He was the sixth Mughal Emperor and also known as Zinda Pir (living saint), Fakir, and Darbesh. He gave the French permission to build a factory in Surat in 1667.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Under whose reign was the maximum number of books in Persian on classical Indian Music written ?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb (1658 - 1707). He reimposed Jizya and Pilgrim tax in 1679 and ended the celebration of Navroz.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Mughal Emperor has attempted to vandalise the Kailash Temple at Ellora ?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb {Alamgir, original name MuḥI al-Din Muḥammad (1658 to 1707)} - He stopped music and alcohol in the court and also the activities of ‘jharokha’ (public audience).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Guru Nanak Dev Ji: Statement 1: Guru Nanak Dev Ji was the third Sikh Guru and Gurpurab marks his birth anniversary. Statement 2: Guru Nanak Dev Ji was the first Sikh Guru and the founder of Sikhism.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.explanation: Guru Nanak Dev Ji, born in 1469 at Talwandi (now Nankana Sahib, Pakistan), was the first Sikh Guru and the founder of Sikhism. Gurpurab is celebrated to commemorate his birth anniversary. He was not the third Guru.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: After the death of Shri Guru Gobind Singh, the Sikhs revolted against the ______ under the leadership of Banda Bahadur.
questions.explanation: Mughals. Guru Gobind Singh is famous for his creation of the Khalsa (Pure) , the military brotherhood of the Sikhs.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following Sikh spiritual gurus is said to have assisted Khusrau, the rebellious son of Jahangir ?
questions.explanation: Guru Arjun Dev assisted Khusrau, the rebellious son of Jahangir. He compiled the first official edition of the Sikh scripture called the Adi Granth, which later expanded into the Guru Granth Sahib. He completed the construction of the Golden Temple in Amritsar.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following Sikh Gurus laid the foundation of ‘Khalsa Panth’ ?
questions.explanation: Guru Gobind Singh laid the foundation of ‘Khalsa Panth’ on April 13, 1699, situated in Punjab. It is a name given to the religious structure and the community that manages the affairs of the global Khalsa community.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Maratha ruler founded the Maratha Empire in 1674, proclaiming himself Chhatrapati ?
questions.explanation: Shivaji. Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj is regarded as the founder of the Maratha Empire. Through guerrilla tactics and strategic battles against the Adilshahi Sultanate and the Mughals, he established an independent Swarajya. In 1674, at Raigad Fort, he was coronated and assumed the title Chhatrapati, formally marking the birth of the Maratha Empire. Sambhaji – Shivaji’s eldest son, succeeded him in 1680 as the second Chhatrapati. Shahu – Shivaji’s grandson, became Chhatrapati in the early 18th century; during his reign, the Peshwas rose as the de facto rulers. Bajirao I – The most famous Peshwa under Shahu, a brilliant general who expanded Maratha power across India.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Maratha revenue system: Statement 1: Bhoga was the twenty-five percent land revenue collected by the Marathas in the Deccan. Statement 2: Sardeshmukhi was an additional ten percent levy on lands where the Marathas claimed hereditary rights.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.explanation: Chauth, not Bhoga, was the twenty-five percent tax imposed by the Marathas to prevent raids. Sardeshmukhi was an additional 10% levy on lands under Maratha hereditary claims. Bhoga belonged to the Gupta period and was a tax on gifts, fruits, flowers, etc.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Baji Rao I or Baji Rao Ballal was the son of ________.
questions.explanation: Peshwa Balaji Vishwanath (1713- 1720). He was the first of a line of hereditary Peshwas from the Bhat family. Baji Rao I (1720-40) - Succeeded Balaji Vishwanath. He was the Seventh Peshwa (Prime Minister) of the Maratha Empire and one of the greatest exponents of Guerrilla tactics after Shivaji. Maratha families: Shindes (Gwalior), Holkars (Indore), Gaikwads (Baroda), Bhosles (Nagpur), Peshwas (Poona).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was a famous ruler of the Maratha dynasty ?
questions.explanation: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. The Maratha Empire formerly existed from 1674 with the coronation of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and ended in 1818 with the defeat of Peshwa Bajirao II at the hands of the British East India Company. Wars fought by Shivaji - Battle of Pratapgad (1659), Battle of Purandar (1665), Battle of Sinhagad (1670), Battle of Sangamner(1679), etc.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which confederation of Sultanates defeated the Vijayanagara Empire in the Battle of Talikota ?
questions.explanation: Deccan Sultanates. The Battle of Talikota (1565) was fought between the Vijayanagara Empire (ruled by Aliya Rama Raya) and the combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates - Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar, and Berar. The Vijayanagara Empire was founded by the brothers Harihara and Bukka Raya in 1336 AD.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the leader that defeated Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara in the Battle of Raichur ?
questions.explanation: Adil Shah of Bijapur. The Battle of Raichur (1520) was fought between Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara and Ismail Adil Shah of Bijapur over the Raichur Doab. Though Krishnadevaraya initially won, Adil Shah of Bijapur was the ruler who opposed him in this decisive conflict.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The founders of Vijayanagar empire, Harihara and Bukka Raya were the ministers of:
questions.explanation: Kampili. The Vijayanagara Empire was established in 1336 by the brothers Harihara and Bukka Raya of the Sangama dynasty, who belonged to the Yadava clan of the Chandravamsa lineage. Between 1336 and 1565, Vijayanagara was ruled by three different dynasties: the Sangama, Saluva, and Tuluva dynasties. The last dynasty was the Aravidu dynasty, which ruled until the seventeenth century.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding foreign travellers to Vijayanagar: Statement 1: Domingo Paes, a Portuguese traveller, visited the Vijayanagar empire during the reign of Krishnadevaraya. Statement 2: Niccolò de' Conti visited the Vijayanagar empire during the reign of Krishnadevaraya.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.explanation: Domingo Paes, a Portuguese traveller, visited the Vijayanagar empire during Krishnadevaraya’s reign and described its prosperity and military strength. Niccolò de' Conti, however, visited India earlier during the rule of Devaraya I, not Krishnadevaraya.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following was the last dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire ?
questions.explanation: Aravidu dynasty. The Vijayanagara Empire had four dynasties: Sangama dynasty (1336-1485 CE), Saluva dynasty (1485-1505 CE), Tuluva dynasty (1505-1570 CE), Aravidu dynasty (1570-1646 CE).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Vijayanagara rulers: 1. Achyuta Deva Raya assumed the title of 'Establisher of the Yavana kingdom’. 2. Krishna Deva Raya founded Nagalapuram in memory of his mother.
questions.explanation: Only 2 is correct. The title 'Establisher of the Yavana kingdom’ was taken by Krishna Deva Raya, not Achyuta Deva Raya. Krishna Deva Raya founded Nagalapuram in memory of his mother.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Vijayanagara empire included people from different cultural regions. Which of the following regions was NOT a part of it ?
questions.explanation: Maratha. The Vijayanagara Empire primarily included the regions of Tamil, Karnataka, and Telugu-speaking areas. Maratha region was ruled by the Yadava Dynasty and later the Bahmani Sultanate during Vijayanagara's peak.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: What was the dominant source of income in the Vijaynagar Empire ?
questions.explanation: Land revenue. Vijayanagar empire: Sources of income - Land Revenue, tributes, and gifts from vassals and feudal chiefs, customs at ports.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following Vijaynagar rulers married his daughter to Firuz Shah Bahmani ?
questions.explanation: Dev Raya I. In 1406 -07, Firuz Shah the ruler of the Bahmani Sultanate, defeated Deva Raya-I, the ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire. Dynasty and Ruler: Sangama Dynasty - Harihara I and Bukka ; Saluva dynasty - Narasimha Deva Raya, Thimma Bhupala, Narasimha Raya II. Tuluva dynasty- Krishnadeva Raya.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The founders of Vijayanagara Empire were the feudatories of which of the following dynasties ?
questions.explanation: Kakatiya.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The origin of 'Carnatic music' is related to which of the following Dynasties ?
questions.explanation: Vijayanagar. Carnatic Music: Purandara Dasa - A poet-composer of Vijayanagar is the ‘Father of Carnatic Music’.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Vijayanagara emperor Krishnadeva Raya founded a suburban township near Vijayanagara called Nagalapuram after his ______.
questions.explanation: Mother.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The local communities of merchants were known as______in the Vijayanagara empire.
questions.explanation: Kudirai Chettis (Horse merchants). Rachavarus (Rajulu) - Associated with the ruling dynasty (rulers and generals were actually Sudras). Narapati (Rayas) - Lord of Men. Gajapati - lord of elephants.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the following terms with their correct description: List I (Groups/Terms) List II (Description) A. Pattanulkars 1. Cavalrymen B. Bargir 2. Commercial agent C. Gomashta 3. Silk weavers from Gujarat migrated to Vijayanagar D. Shiqdar 4. Head of Administrative unit (Shiqq)
questions.explanation: A-3, B-1, C-2, D-4. The Pattanulkars were silk weavers who migrated from Gujarat to the Vijayanagar state, contributing to its textile industry. Bargirs were cavalry soldiers used in medieval armies, especially in the Maratha period. Gomashtas acted as commercial agents for trade and merchants. Shiqdar was the administrative head of a Shiqq, responsible for revenue and law enforcement.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Amara-Nayakas were in the Vijayanagara Empire.
questions.explanation: Military commanders. They were given territories to govern by the Raya and used to collect taxes and other dues from the peasants, traders and craftspersons of the area. Gramas (villages), Gauda (village headman), Sthalas (sub districts), Nadus (districts), {Mandalams or rajyas (provinces)}, Land tax (sist).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: While historians use the term Vijayanagara Empire and contemporaries of this empire described it as the______.
questions.explanation: Karnataka Samrajyamu. Vijayanagara Empire (1336 -1646) - Established by Harihara and Bukka on the banks of river Tungabhadra.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Raichur Doab: Statement 1: Raichur Doab refers to the fertile land lying between the rivers Krishna and Tungabhadra. Statement 2: The Vijayanagar rulers mainly fought the Bengal kingdom for control over Raichur Doab.

options.c: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect
options.d: Statement 1 is incorrect, Statement 2 is correct

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect
questions.explanation: The Raichur Doab indeed lies between the rivers Krishna and Tungabhadra, making Statement 1 true. However, the Vijayanagar Empire did not fight Bengal for this land; the conflict was with the Bahmani Sultanate, making Statement 2 false.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which battle led to the destruction of the Vijayanagara empire ?
questions.explanation: Battle of Talikota (Rakshasi–Tangadi) - It was fought on 23 January 1565 between the Vijayanagara Empire and an alliance of the Deccan sultanates. Aliya Rama Raya (King of the Vijaynagar Empire) was defeated and killed in the battle, which eventually led to the political collapse of the Vijayanagara Empire. The Battle of Raichur - Fought between the Vijayanagara Empire and the Sultanate of Bijapur in 1520.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Provida style of architecture belongs to which empire ?
questions.explanation: Vijayanagar Empire Architectural Wonders of Vijayanagara: Queen’s Bath, Lotus Mahal, Elephant stables, Royal platform, Water tanks.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Anantraj Sagar Tank was built by the _______rulers.
questions.explanation: The Vijayanagara empire built the Anantraj Sagar water storage tank using a 1.37 km long dam on the Maldevi river. Maldevi river runs through the Nellore district in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh and empties into the Pennar river.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Peshwa signed the treaty of Bassein with the East India Company ?
questions.explanation: Baji Rao II. The Treaty of Bassein (1802): It was signed between Lord Wellesley and Baji Rao II. Other Treaty: Treaty of Surat (1775) was signed between Raghunath Rao and the British. The Treaty of Salbai (1782) was signed between the Maratha Empire and the British East India Company.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Tripartite Treaty of 1838: Statement 1: The Tripartite Treaty was signed by Shah Shujah, Maharaja Ranjit Singh, and the English East India Company. Statement 2: The Governor-General of India at the time of this treaty was Lord Auckland.

options.c: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect
options.d: Statement 1 is incorrect, Statement 2 is correct

questions.explanation: The Tripartite Treaty of 1838 was concluded between Maharaja Ranjit Singh of Punjab, Shah Shujah of Afghanistan, and the English Company to reinstall Shah Shujah on the Afghan throne. At that time, Lord Auckland was the Governor-General of India.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In 1850, Kashmir was sold under which of the following treaties to the Dogra dynasty of Jammu ?
questions.explanation: Treaty of Amritsar - It was executed by the British East India Company and Raja Gulab Singh of Jammu after the First Anglo-Sikh War.
