Ryotwari System - The peasants or cultivators were regarded as the owners of the land. The cultivators had to pay annual taxes directly to the government. Introduced by Thomas Munro and Alexander Read in 1820 in the Madras and Bombay presidency.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: When was the Secretary of State for India made responsible for the Government of British India by bringing about changes in the Home Government?
questions.explanation: 1858. Charter Act 1858 - The term Governor General changed to Viceroy for the British crown. The first viceroy was Lord Canning. The act ended ‘The Doctrine of Lapse’. It ended the Dual government scheme initiated due to Pitt’s India Act.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In 1942, the British government sent the______mission to India.
questions.explanation: Cripps. It was sent to India to secure Indian cooperation for the British war efforts. It was headed by Sir Richard Stafford Cripps. Gandhi called it 'A post-dated cheque drawn on a failing bank'.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The result of the English Education Act of 1835 was to make ____ as a medium of instruction for____ education.
questions.explanation: English, Higher. English Education Act (1835) was proposed by William Bentinck on the advice of Macaulay. Reforms by William Bentick : The abolition of Sati, the suppression of female infanticide and Thuggee, the abolition of lawlessness, and the abolition of human sacrifices.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Charter Act of 1813 extended the East India Company's rule in India to another _____ years.
questions.explanation: 20. The Charter Act of 1813 (The East Indian Company Act 1813) - Features: It ended the monopoly of the East India Company over commercial trade except trade with China and trade in tea with India.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The objective of Simon Commission was to________.
questions.explanation: Simon Commission - It was appointed by the British Government in 1927 under the chairmanship of John Simon (other members were Pathick Lawrence and Clement Atlee) to review the workings of Government of India (GOI) Act, 1919 and suggest measures.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which act of the British Parliament was also known as East India Company Act 1793?
questions.explanation: The Charter Act, 1793. The act was passed by the British Parliament to renew the charter of the East India Company to trade within India for next 20 years. It was passed during the tenure of Sir John Shore (1793 -1798).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In_____, the British government enacted a legislation banning the use of printed cotton textiles - chintz - in England. Interestingly, this Act was known as the Calico Act.
questions.explanation: 1720. The cotton textiles which the Portuguese took back to Europe, along with the spices, came to be called "calico". Calico Act , Reason - Textile makers in England were Unable to compete with Indian textiles. Highest cotton producing state (Gujarat).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Indian states was the first to sign a subsidiary alliance with the British ?
questions.explanation: Hyderabad. In this system, an Indian ruler had to maintain British troops in his state, either by giving some of his territories or by paying for the maintenance of the troops. It was first introduced by the French East India Company Governor Joseph Francois Dupleix, Later used by Lord Wellesley, Governor-General of India (1798 to 1805).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Empress of India Act: 1. The original name of the Act was the Royal Titles Act, 1877. 2. It officially recognized Queen Victoria as the Empress of India. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 2 only. Statement 1 Incorrect: The correct original name is the Royal Titles Act, 1876, not 1877.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Acts of 1947 regulates the Indian labor law with regard to trade unions as well as individual workmen ?
questions.explanation: Industrial disputes Act 1947. The Rowlatt Act 1919 authorized the arrest, for 2 years without trial, of any person suspected of terrorism living in British India. Indian Council acts (1861, 1892, and 1909). Charter Acts (1793, 1813, 1833, and 1853).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Act passed by British Government of India abolished the Council of India ?
questions.explanation: Government of India Act 1935 were as follows: Abolition of provincial dyarchy and introduction of dyarchy at centre. Abolition of Indian Council and introduction of an advisory body in its place. Provision for an All India Federation with British India territories and princely states.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Sharda Act of 1929: 1. The Sharda Act fixed the marriageable age for girls at 14 years and boys at 18 years. 2. The Act was sponsored by Harbilas Sarda.

options.c: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
options.d: Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True

questions.explanation: Both statements are True. The Sharda act fixed the marriageable age for girls at 14 years and 18 years for boys. It was sponsored by Harbilas Sarda. Pitt’s India act (1784), Rowlatt Act (1919), Vernacular press act (1878).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which year through the Indian Official Secrets Act was freedom of press curbed ?
questions.explanation: 1904. It was enacted during the time of Lord Curzon, Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905 curbed the freedom of Press. Later this act was replaced by the Official Secrets act 1923.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In 1877, which of the following viceroys organized a durbar to acknowledge Queen Victoria as the Empress of India ?
questions.explanation: Lord Lytton organized a durbar to acknowledge Queen Victoria as the Empress of India. This was the culmination of the transfer of control of British India from the East India Company to the Crown.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The capital of the British Indian Empire was transferred from Calcutta to Delhi in:
questions.explanation: 1911. The British government believed that ruling India from Delhi was easier and more convenient than from Calcutta. Therefore, Delhi was officially announced as the capital of British Raj by Emperor George V, on December 12, 1911.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: By which British statute were Indian representatives, for the first time, allocated seats for election in Indian Legislative Councils ?
questions.explanation: Indian Councils Act, 1892. The act made a limited and indirect provision for the use of election in filling up some of the nonofficial seats both in the Central and provincial legislative councils.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. General Dyer imposed Martial Law in India in 1920, under which public gatherings of more than two people were prohibited. 2. The office of the first Accountant General in India was established in 1858, the same year the British Crown took over administration from the East India Company. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 2 only. Statement 1 is wrong: General Dyer imposed Martial Law in 1919 (not 1920), in response to the Rowlatt Act protests, which culminated in the Jallianwala Bagh massacre. Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movements

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movements
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Partition of Bengal was announced in 1905 by Lord Curzon. 2. The Surat Split of the Indian National Congress took place in 1909 between the Moderates and Extremists. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Statement 2 – Incorrect: The Surat Split took place in 1907, not 1909, between the Moderates (led by Gopal Krishna Gokhale) and the Extremists (led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai).

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movements
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Rakhi-tying movement: 1. In 1905, Rabindranath Tagore encouraged Hindus and Muslims to tie rakhis on each other’s hands as a mark of unity. 2. This movement was connected with the Rowlatt Act of 1919. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Statement 2 - Incorrect: The rakhi movement was linked with the Partition of Bengal (1905), not the Rowlatt Act of 1919.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movements
questions.question: What was the Swadeshi Movement called in the state of Andhra Pradesh ?
questions.explanation: Vande Mataram Movement. The Swadeshi Movement started in August 1905 from Calcutta Town Hall against Lord Curzon’s decision of dividing the province of Bengal. The partition led to protest meetings in Bengal under which the pledge to boycott foreign goods was first taken. Leaders of the movement - Poona and Bombay (Lokmanya Tilak), Punjab (Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh), Delhi (Syed Haider Raza), Madras (Chidambaram Pillai).

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movements
questions.question: What is the official reason given by Britishers after partition of Bengal in 1905 ?
questions.explanation: Administrative Convenience. The real reason for the partition was to divide and weaken the growing nationalist movement in Bengal. After Partition Swadeshi movement gained even more momentum, and the British were forced to revoke the partition in 1911.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movements
questions.question: Assertion (A): Before the Partition of Bengal in 1905, Bengal was the biggest province of British India, consisting of parts of Bihar and Orissa. Reason (R): Lord Curzon announced the Partition of Bengal in 1905 to separate the largely Muslim eastern areas from the largely Hindu western areas.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Partition of Bengal in 1905 {Lord Curzon announced the partition of Bengal on 20th July 1905, reorganization separated the largely Muslim eastern areas from the largely Hindu western areas}.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movements
questions.question: Which of the following parties supported the move for partition of Bengal ?
questions.explanation: All India Muslim League supported the move for partition of Bengal. Founders of All India Muslim League are Muhammad Ali Jinnah, Aga Khan III, Khwaja Salimullah, Hakim Ajmal Khan, Waqar-ul-Mulk. It was founded on 30 December 1906.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movements
questions.question: Moved by the Swadeshi Movement, ______ painted his famous image of Bharat Mata portraying her as an ascetic figure.
questions.explanation: Abanindranath Tagore painted his famous image of Bharat Mata portraying her as an ascetic figure in 1905. The painting is depicted as a saffron-clad divine woman, holding a book, sheaves of paddy, a piece of white cloth, and a rosary in her four hands.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Once the Time Magazine had mocked Gandhiji's physical size but to whom do it compare his martyrdom later on?
questions.explanation: Abraham Lincoln. Time magazine in its earlier coverage had mocked Mahatma Gandhi’s small physical stature. However, after his assassination on 30 January 1948, Time compared Gandhi’s martyrdom to that of Abraham Lincoln, recognizing the magnitude of his sacrifice for peace and freedom. Like Lincoln, Gandhiji was portrayed as a leader who gave his life for unity and justice in his nation.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): Gandhi’s first Satyagraha in India was launched in Bardoli in 1917. Reason (R): Pandit Raj Kumar Shukla invited Gandhi to Champaran to study the grievances of indigo farmers.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: A is false, but R is true. India's first Civil Disobedience movement, launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1917, was prompted by Pandit Raj Kumar Shukla, who urged him to address the plight of Indigo farmers. Mahatma Gandhi organised the Kheda Satyagraha (1918) in Gujarat. Gandhi also led the Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918) after returning from South Africa. The Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) was led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel for the farmers of Bardoli.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the Viceroy of India when Mahatma Gandhi started Dandi March on 12 March 1930 ?
questions.explanation: Lord Irwin (1926-1931). Other Events During his tenure: Simon Commission to India (1927); Harcourt Butler Indian States Commission (1927); Nehru Report (1928); Deepavali Declaration (1929); Lahore session of the Congress (Purna Swaraj Resolution) 1929; First Round Table Conference (1930); Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931). Mahatma Gandhi led the Dandi March (Salt March) in 1930, accompanied by a group of 78 followers, as a nonviolent protest against the British salt monopoly.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which year was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed ?
questions.explanation: 1931. The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on March 5, 1931, between Mahatma Gandhi and Lord Irwin, the Viceroy of India (1926-1931). The pact ended the Civil Disobedience Movement, initiated by Gandhi with the Salt March, and was signed before the Second Round Table Conference in London.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Round Table Conferences: 1. Mahatma Gandhi attended only the Second Round Table Conference. 2. Mahatma Gandhi participated in all the three Round Table Conferences held in London. Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect ?
questions.explanation: Only 2. Gandhi ji went only to the Second Round Table Conference (1931). He did not attend the First (1930) or Third (1932) Round Table Conferences.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which of the following places did Mahatma Gandhi, along with other Indians, establish the Natal Congress to fight against racial discrimination ?
questions.explanation: South Africa. The Natal Indian Congress, founded by Mahatma Gandhi in 1894, aimed to combat discrimination against Indians in South Africa. Gandhiji, born on 2 October 1869, returned to India on 9 January 1915.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Dandi March was started by Mahatma Gandhi from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930. 2. The Quit India Movement was launched in 1930 alongside the Salt Satyagraha to strengthen the freedom struggle. Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect ?
questions.explanation: 2 only. Gandhi began the Dandi March on 12 March 1930 and reached Dandi on 5 April 1930 to break the salt law. The Quit India Movement was launched later in 1942, not in 1930.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following leaders had gone to Lucknow to invite Mahatma Gandhi to see the plight of the peasants in Champaran ?
questions.explanation: Raj Kumar Shukla. The local Congress leaders Brajkishore Prasad and Raj Kumar Shukla first met Mahatma Gandhi at the Lucknow session of the Indian National Congress in 1916 and invited Mahatma Gandhi to have first-hand experience of the plight of Champaran peasants. Gandhi arrived in Champaran on April 15, 1917, to address the grievances of the peasants who were forced to grow indigo under oppressive conditions.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the following Pacts with the year in which they were signed: Column A (Pacts) Column B (Years) 1.Gandhi–AmbedkarPact (Poona Pact) A. 1931 2.Gandhi–Irwin Pact B. 1932 3. Lucknow Pact C. 1916 4. Delhi Pact (Rajendra Prasad –Liaquat Ali Pact) D. 1947
questions.explanation: 1–B, 2–A, 3–C, 4–D. The Communal Award was announced by the British Prime Minister, Ramsay MacDonald, on 16 August 1932, based on the report of the Indian Franchise Committee (Lothian Committee). This award accorded separate electorates for Muslims, Europeans, Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Depressed classes (78 seats), and even to the Marathas for some seats in Bombay. Gandhi - Ambedkar Pact is also known as the Poona Pact. Madan Mohan Malaviya signed it on behalf of Gandhi. It provided for the Joint electorate, reserved seats (147) for depressed classes and 18% seats reserved for the central legislature.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi called a halt to the Non-Cooperation Movement after the Chauri Chaura incident. Where among the following places is Chauri Chaura located ?
questions.explanation: Gorakhpur. Chauri Chaura, a town in Uttar Pradesh was the site of a violent clash on February 4, 1922, during the Non-Cooperation Movement. Protestors set a police station on fire, resulting in the deaths of 22 policemen inside.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 resulted in the abolishment of the Tinkathia System. Reason (R): The Tinkathia System forced peasants to cultivate wheat on 3/20th of their landholdings for British planters.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false. Champaran Satyagraha (1917) was Gandhi's first protest in India against forced indigo farming. Brajkishore Prasad and Raj Kumar Shukla first met Mahatma Gandhi at the Lucknow session of the Indian National Congress in 1916 and invited him to have first-hand experience of the plight of Champaran peasants.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Non-Cooperation Movement launched in 1920 included boycott of foreign goods, promotion of spinning wheels, and picketing at liquor shops. 2. The resolution of Poorna Swaraj was passed at the Lahore session of the Indian National Congress in 1920 as part of the Non-Cooperation Movement. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 only. The resolution for Poorna Swaraj (complete independence) was passed at the Lahore session of the Indian National Congress in December 1929, under the leadership of Jawaharlal Nehru. He hoisted the Indian tricolor flag on the banks of the Ravi river. The non-cooperation movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920 to persuade Indians to withdraw their cooperation from the British government and advocate for self-governance.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Gandhiji gave his slogan of ‘Do or Die’ during which of the following Movements/Satyagrahas ?
questions.explanation: The Quit India Movement (also known as the August Movement) was launched by the Indian National Congress on August 8, 1942. Other key movements by Mahatma Gandhi include the Civil Disobedience Movement (1930), the Kheda Satyagraha (1918) in Gujarat, demanding relaxation in revenue collection for peasants, and the Champaran Satyagraha (1917), opposing the Tinkathia system, which forced peasants to grow indigo on 3/20th of their land.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Vallabhbhai Patel and____ helped Gandhi in Kheda by organising his tour of the villages and urging the peasants to stand firm against the government.
questions.explanation: Indulal Yajnik. Mahatma Gandhi returned to India on 9 January 1915.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Mahatma Gandhi returned his Kaisar-i-Hind medal in 1920 as a protest against the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre. 2. Rabindranath Tagore returned his Kaisar-i-Hind medal in protest against the same massacre.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false. Kaiser - e - Hind title was given to Mahatma Gandhi by Governor-General of India Lord Hardinge in 1915 for his services during the Boer War (1899 - 1902). Gandhi returned his title in response to the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (13th April 1919). Rabindranath Tagore returned his Knighthood title in response to the massacre.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In 1918, Mahatma Gandhi successfully led a strike of _____.
questions.explanation: Mill workers. Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918) - This is considered the first hunger strike led by Gandhi.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Kheda Satyagraha of 1918: 1. The Kheda Satyagraha was launched against the British demand for high land revenue despite crop failure and plague outbreak. 2. The movement was organised mainly by the Patidar peasants of Gujarat under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Kheda Satyagraha of 1918 was a satyagraha movement in the Kheda district of Gujarat in India organized by Mahatma Gandhi during the period of the British Raj. The peasant-Patidar community of Kheda, who refused to accept a 23 percent tax increase imposed on them despite a devastating crop failure and an outbreak of plague and cholera, served as the focal point of this satyagraha.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: When did depressed classes get the reserved seats in provincial and central legislative councils, but they were to be voted in by the General electorate ?
questions.explanation: September 1932. Poona Pact - Agreement between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar - Seats reserved for the depressed classes were increased from 71 to 147 in provincial legislatures and 18 percent of the total in the Central Legislature.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Gandhiji, aged____, arrived in India in 1915 from South Africa.
questions.explanation: 46. Gandhiji (born on 2nd October 1869 in Porbandar, Gujarat) went to South Africa in 1893 as a lawyer, settling first in Durban before moving to Johannesburg.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The quote “Be the change you wish to see in the world” is attributed to Mahatma Gandhi. 2. The quote “Give me blood, and I will give you freedom” was also said by Gandhi.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is True

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi other Famous Quotes: “A man is but the product of his thoughts. What he thinks, he becomes.”, “Nobody can hurt me without my permission.”

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which of the following years, did Subhas Chandra Bose refer to Mahatma Gandhi as the “Father of the Nation” ?
questions.explanation: 1944. Subhas Chandra Bose called Mahatma Gandhi the ‘Father of the Nation’ in a radio address from Singapore on 6 July 1944.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Khilafat Movement: 1. The All-India Khilafat Conference of November 1919 was held at Delhi. 2. Leaders like the Ali brothers, Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, Ajmal Khan, and Hasrat Mohani played a key role in this movement. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. In early 1919, the All India Khilafat Committee was formed under the leadership of the Ali brothers (Maulana Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali), Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, Ajmal Khan and Hasrat Mohani, to force the British Government to change its attitude to Turkey.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following called Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose a patriot of patriots ?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi. Rabindranath Tagore called Subhash Chandra Bose a 'Desh Nayak'. The famous slogan given by Subhas Chandra Bose: “Dilli Chalo, Jai Hind”, "Give me blood, I will give freedom". Subhas Chandra Bose Autobiography: “The Indian Struggle”.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following events occurred as an after-effect of the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (13th April 1919) ?

options.a: Hunger strike to settle disputes between the mill owners and the workers
options.b: Individual princes could sign a separate agreement with the British
options.c: Hunter Commission was appointed by the British Government
options.d: Popularisation of Charkha and Khadi and Jail Bharo by Congress volunteers.

questions.answer_text: Hunter Commission was appointed by the British Government
questions.explanation: The Hunter Commission came to India in 1919 under the leadership of William Hunter to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh massacre. Another Hunter Commission was on Indian Education, prepared in 1882 by William Wilson Hunter.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason for slowing down the Non-cooperation Movement ?

options.a: Due to the absence of alternative Indian institution, boycott of British Institutions posed a problem.
options.b: Leaders of the movement shifted their focus towards domestic work thus created a void.
options.c: Many lawyers resigned but then absence of income for a longer period of time compelled them to rejoin.
options.d: Khadi cloth was often more expensive than mass-produced mill cloth and poor people could not afford to buy it.

questions.answer_text: Leaders of the movement shifted their focus towards domestic work thus created a void.
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi started the Non- Cooperation Movement on 4 September 1920. Lord Chelmsford was the viceroy of British India during the Non-Cooperation Movement. The Chauri -Chaura incident was the driver of subsequent withdrawal of the Non -Cooperation Movement.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which of the following years was the civil disobedience campaign completely Ceased ?
questions.explanation: 1934. It began with the famous Dandi March of Gandhiji, on 12 March 1930.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): During the Quit India Movement of 1942, Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the Indian flag at Gowalia Tank Maidan in Mumbai. Reason (R): Sarojini Naidu was popularly called the "Grand Old Lady of the Independence Movement."

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false. Aruna Asaf Ali popularly known as the 'Grand Old Lady' of the Independence Movement.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was the only martyr of the Quit India phase of the freedom movement who was hanged ?
questions.explanation: Kushal Konwar. Facts of Quit India Movement - The Quit India Resolution was passed by the Congress Working Committee on 8 August 1942 in Bombay. ‘Quit India’ or ‘Bharat Chodo 'slogan was given in this movement . Gandhiji gave the slogan to the people – ‘Do or die’; It is also known as the India August Movement or August Kranti.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding newspapers started by Mahatma Gandhi: 1. Indian Opinion was founded by Mahatma Gandhi in South Africa in 1903, along with M. H. Nazar. 2. Young India and Navajivan were newspapers later published by Gandhi after his return to India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. The Indian Opinion was an important newspaper established in 1903 in Durban, South Africa, by Mahatma Gandhi and M. H. Nazar. It was a primary communication organ of the Natal Indian Congress

questions.subject: History
questions.question: C Rajagopalachari led the Salt Satyagraha in which of the following states ?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu. Salt March (Dandi Satyagraha, 12th March 1930 to 6th April, 1930 ) was an act of nonviolent civil disobedience led by Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi. Other leaders - K. Kelappan (Malabar), Gopabandhu Chaudhary (Orissa).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Given below are the two columns. Column A consists of Events or terms and column B consist of correct descriptions. Match the column A with correct description in Column B Column A Column B A.Anglo-Russian rivalry 1. Opened Sindh's rivers and roads to British trade. B. Subsidiary Treaty 1839 2. Forced on the Amirs of Sindh before annexation. C. Sir Charles Napier 3. Had commercial value; attracted British interest. D. River Sindh 4. Led military campaign to annex Sindh; called it a "rascality." E. Treaty of 1832 5. Led Britain to expand influence in Afghanistan and Persia
questions.explanation: A-5, B-2, C-4, D-3, E-1. The Anglo-Russian rivalry (The Great Game) compelled Britain to expand its influence in Afghanistan and Persia to counter Russia. The Subsidiary Treaty of 1839 was imposed on the Amirs of Sindh before annexation. Sir Charles Napier led the campaign to annex Sindh and famously called it a “rascality”. The River Sindh held great commercial value, attracting British interest. Finally, the Treaty of 1832 opened Sindh’s rivers and roads to British trade.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following best captures the broader geopolitical shift triggered by the decisive defeat of the Nawab of Carnatic's forces in their confrontation with European powers ?

options.a: It revealed systemic vulnerabilities in native military structures, prompting European companies to transition from trade to political hegemony.
options.b: It disillusioned European companies, resulting in a strategic withdrawal from inland military affairs.
options.c: It consolidated indigenous authority, forcing European traders into commercial treaties under local oversight.
options.d: It established a stable dual -administrative system between Indian principalities and foreign chartered companies.

questions.answer_text: It revealed systemic vulnerabilities in native military structures, prompting European companies to transition from trade to political hegemony.
questions.explanation: The defeat of the Nawab of Carnatic’s forces exposed the weakness of traditional Indian armies against the disciplined, technologically advanced European forces. This marked a turning point where European trading companies, especially the British, realized the possibility of extending political control beyond commerce. Gradually, their role shifted from merchants to power brokers in Indian politics. Thus, the Carnatic wars laid the foundation for European political dominance in India.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Given below are assertion and reason, read the statements and choose the correct option. Assertion: The Treaty of Paris (1763) limited French settlements in India to trading posts only. Reason: The French could no longer station troops or fortify their factories after the treaty.

options.a: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Paris (1763) ended both the Seven Years’ War and the Third Carnatic War, marking the British East India Company’s decisive victory over the French in India. After the Battle of Wandiwash, France lost its political influence and was limited to trading in its enclaves. The First Carnatic War (1746–1748) ended with the Treaty of Aix-La-Chapelle, the Second Carnatic War (1749–1754) with the Treaty of Pondicherry, and the Third Carnatic War (1758–1763) with the Treaty of Paris.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Given below are assertion and reason, read the statements and choose the correct option. Assertion(A): Sir Charles Napier justified the annexation of Sindh on moral and legal grounds. Reason(R): He described it as a "useful humane piece of rascality."

options.a: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: A is true, but R is false.
options.c: A is false, but R is true.
options.d: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.answer_text: A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation: A is false, but R is true. Annexation of Sindh (1843): Carried out by Sir Charles Napier after the Battle of Miani. Napier himself admitted that the conquest was not morally or legally justified. He cynically remarked on the annexation, calling it a "useful humane piece of rascality", thereby acknowledging its dubious morality.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Porto Novo (1781): 1. The battle was fought between Hyder Ali of Mysore and the British East India Company led by Sir Eyre Coote. 2. The battle was part of the Second Anglo-Mysore War, in which Hyder Ali played a key role before his death in 1782. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. The Battle of Porto Novo (1781) was fought between Hyder Ali and the East India Company (EIC), led by Sir Eyre Coote. Hyder Ali was a key figure in the Anglo-Mysore Wars. The First Anglo-Mysore War (1767–1769) was fought between Hyder Ali and the EIC. The Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780–1784) also saw Hyder Ali leading the Mysore forces; however, he died during the conflict, after which his son, Tipu Sultan, continued the war.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following battles is considered the formal beginning of the British Raj in India?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey took place in Bengal on June 23, 1757. British East India Company troops, led by Robert Clive, confronted the forces of Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal, along with his French allies. The British East India Company won this battle.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): The Battle of Buxar was fought in 1764 between the British East India Company and the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah, and Shah Alam II. Reason (R): After the Battle of Buxar, Shah Alam II granted the Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa to the British East India Company.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Battle of Buxar : Fought between the British East India Company and the combined armies of Mir Qasim (Nawab of Bengal), Shuja-ud-Daulah (Nawab of Awadh), and the Mughal Emperor, Shah Alam II. The British East India Company was led by Hector Munro. The Britishers won this battle. The Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II - granted the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the East India Company.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Where was the first jute mill set up in India?
questions.explanation: Rishra (West Bengal, 1855). First Jute mill (Acland Mill) - Established by British entrepreneur George Acland and Bengali financier Babu By Sumber Sen in Bengal Presidency. Central Research Institute for Jute and Allied Fibers is located in West Bengal. National jute Board formed by National Jute board Act, 2008 under the Ministry of Textile. In 1854, the first modern cotton mill was established in Mumbai by Cowaszee Nanabhoy Davar.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Statement 1: Cotton and jute industries existed in India during the British rule. Statement 2: The iron and steel industry in India was started only after independence.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false. British rulers never permitted modernization nor did they encourage the growth of industries. The unbalanced and lopsided growth structures were a legacy of British rule in India. The first iron and steel mill was established in 1907, in Jamshedpur by Tata Iron and Steel Company.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In the 18th century, the development of cotton industries in Britain resulted in _________ .

options.a: Increase in demand of Indian textile in Britain
options.b: Decline of textiles production in India
options.c: Increase in demand of Indian textile in India
options.d: Decline of British textiles industries in India

questions.answer_text: Decline of textiles production in India
questions.explanation: Reason for decline: Export of textiles to England became more and more difficult because the British Government imposed high duties on Indian textiles. Thorp Mill (1764) - The first water-powered cotton mill in the world was constructed at Royton, Lancashire (England). The first cotton textile mill (India) - Established at Fort Glastor near Kolkata (1818).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In 1600, the East India company acquired a charter from_________.
questions.explanation: Queen Elizabeth I. By the Charter (1600 A.D), they got the sole right to trade with the East, without competition from other British traders. The Company's ships first arrived in India, at the port of Surat, in 1608.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The first English factory was set up on the banks of the river _______ in 1651.
questions.explanation: Hugli. First English factory (Temporary) in India - Masulipattam (1611). First English factory (Permanent) in India - Surat (1613). First factory of other European Companies in India: Dutch - Masulipatnam (Andhra Pradesh) in 1605, Portuguese - Calicut (Kerala) in 1500, French - Surat (Gujarat) in 1668.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correct regarding the East India Company army? I. Sawar — Men on horses II. Musket — A heavy gun used by infantry soldiers
questions.explanation: Both l and II.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The British East India Company captured Pondicherry (Puducherry) from the French in the year ______.
questions.explanation: 1761. Pondicherry got its freedom from the French on 1st November 1954. The Union Territory of Puducherry comprises the erstwhile French colonies viz. Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which monument was built in 1924 to welcome King George V and Queen Mary?
questions.explanation: Gateway of India. The Gateway of India is an Arch-Monument built in the early 20th century in the city of Mumbai.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT TRUE about Rash Behari Bose?

options.a: He founded Indian Independence League in Tokyo in 1942.
options.b: He was an important figure in the Ghadar Movement and in the formation of the Azad Hind Fauj.
options.c: He was honoured with the prestigious title 'Order of the rising sun'.
options.d: He was independent India's first Commander-in-Chief of Indian Army.

questions.answer_text: He was independent India's first Commander-in-Chief of Indian Army.
questions.explanation: The first Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army after independence was General Sir Robert Lockhart, and the first Indian to hold the post was Field Marshal K. M. Cariappa, who took command in 1949.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Barindra Kumar Ghosh, Abhinash Bhattacharya and Bhupendranath Dutta were associated with which movement in March 1906?
questions.explanation: Swadeshi movement. In March 1906, Barindra Kumar Ghosh, Abhinash Bhattacharya, and Bhupendranath Dutta started the revolutionary Bengali weekly newspaper Jugantar. This publication served as the mouthpiece for the revolutionary organization Anushilan Samiti and was a key part of the radical nationalist stream that emerged during the Swadeshi movement, which began in 1905.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding revolts in India during British rule: Statement 1: Tirot Sing, a Khasi chief, played a leading role in the Khasi uprising against the British from 1829 to 1833. Statement 2: The Singpho Rebellion took place in Bengal during the late 18th century.

options.c: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect
options.d: Statement 1 is incorrect, Statement 2 is correct

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect
questions.explanation: Tirot Sing, also known as U Tirot Sing Syiem, was a Khasi chief in the early 19th century. The Khasi uprising (Anglo-Khasi War) was a conflict between the Khasi people and the British Empire that took place from 1829 to 1833. The Sanyasi Uprisings took place in Bengal between the periods of 1770- 1820s. Poligar Revolt fought between the British and the Poligars, feudal lords in southern India. The Singpho Rebellion of 1830 took place in Assam.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The planned large-scale disruption of rail communications and the seizure of arms in Bengal were undertaken under the leadership of _____.
questions.explanation: Jatin Mukherjee, also known as Bagha Jatin, was a prominent revolutionary leader in Bengal during the early 20th century who fought against British colonial rule. He was a key member of the Anushilan Samiti, a revolutionary organization that planned large-scale armed resistance against the British.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Chittagong Armoury Raid: Statement 1: The Chittagong Armoury Raid was led by Surya Sen, also known as Master Da. Statement 2: The raid took place on April 18, 1930, in present-day Bangladesh.

options.c: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
options.d: Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True

questions.explanation: Both statements are True. Surya Sen is also known as Master Da. He founded The Indian Republican Army. The Chittagong Armoury Raid took place on April 18, 1930, in Chittagong (now in Bangladesh). Ras Bihari Bose was the founder of the 'Indian Independence League’. He chaired the Indian Independence League in 1942 to formally launch the Indian National Army.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Sido and Kanhu were leaders of which of the following tribal rebellions?
questions.explanation: Santhal Rebellion (Hul revolt) began in 1855, led by Sidhu, Kanhu, Chand, Bhairav, and their sisters Phulo and Jhano. The Malabar rebellion (Moplah rebellion) was an armed uprising by the Mappila Muslims of Kerala in 1921. The Kol rebellion (1829-39) was led by Buddhu Bhagat, Madara Mahato, and Joa Bhagat in the Chota Nagpur region. The Munda Rebellion, led by Birsa Munda, took place in the Ranchi area in 1899-1900.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which of the following years was VD Savarkar sent to Andaman Jail by the British?
questions.explanation: 1911. Vinayak Damodar Savarkar was sent to the Cellular Jail on the punishment of 'Kala Pani’ under the Nashik Conspiracy Case for the murder of the Collector of Nashik District, Jackson. While serving his sentence in the Cellular Jail, he wrote the epic 'Kamala' on the prison walls.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In 1910, The United India House at Seattle, USA, was set up by _________.

options.b: Tarak Nath Das and GD Kumar

questions.answer_text: Tarak Nath Das and GD Kumar
questions.explanation: Tarak Nath Das and GD Kumar. They were Indian revolutionaries who collaborated to promote Indian independence from British rule. Shyamji Krishna Varma founded the Indian Home Rule Society, India House, and The Indian Sociologist in London. Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and his brother Ganesh Damodar Savarkar established the Abhinav Bharat Society, also known as the Young India Society, in 1904.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following groups/parties was started in San Francisco, United States of America during the Indian National Movement?
questions.explanation: Ghadar Party : Founded in 1913 in the U.S. as the Hindi Association of the Pacific Coast, it aimed to free India from British rule. It was founded by Sohan Singh Bhakna and Lala Har Dayal.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee wrote a novel Anand Math based on which of the following rebellions/revolts?
questions.explanation: Sanyasi Rebellion. The Sanyasi Uprisings took place in Bengal between the periods of 1770- 1820s. The Sanyasis rose in rebellion after the great famine of 1770 in Bengal which caused acute chaos and misery. However, the immediate cause of the rebellion was the restrictions imposed by the British upon pilgrims visiting holy places among both Hindus and Muslims. The national song of India, 'Vande Mataram’, is an excerpt taken from the novel Anand Math written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Bombay Presidency Association (1885): Statement 1: The Bombay Presidency Association was founded in 1885 by Badruddin Tyabji, Pherozeshah Mehta, and K.T. Telang. Statement 2: Zakir Husain was one of the founders of the Bombay Presidency Association.

options.c: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
options.d: Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True

questions.answer_text: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
questions.explanation: Badruddin Tyabji was the third President (in 1887) of the Indian National Congress and the first Muslim to hold that position. Other Political organisations and founder: London Indian Society (1865) - Dadabhai Naoroji. East India Association (1866) - Dadabhai Naoroji. Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870) - G.V. Joshi, S.H. Sathe, S.H. Chiplonkar and Mahadev Govind Ranade.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: What was the name of the campaign led by the Ali brothers and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad to save the Ottoman Caliphate as a symbol of unity among the Muslim community?
questions.explanation: Khilafat Movement. It was a political campaign that took place from 1919 to 1922 in British India. It was a protest against the British government's policies towards Turkey and the planned dismantling of the Ottoman Empire after World War I. The Faraizi movement was started by Haji Shariatullah in 1818. The Ahmadiyya movement was founded by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad in 1889. Syed Ahmed Barelvi started the Wahabi Movement in the 1820s.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was executed as an accomplice to the murder of AMT Jackson ?
questions.explanation: Krishnaji Gopal Karve. Jackson murder case also known as Nasik Conspiracy (Year 1909). Anant Laxman Kanhere shot Jackson, the Collector of Nashik, at Vijayanand theatre. Kanhere was a member of the Abhinav Bharat society. The event led to the arrest of Savarkar. Abhinav Bharat Society was a secret society founded by Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and his brother Ganesh Damodar Savarkar in 1904.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following revolutionists was associated with the Anushilan Samiti?
questions.explanation: Jatindra Mohan Sengupta. Anushilan Samiti was founded by Satish Chandra Bose and Barrister Praanath Mitra. Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev were members of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA), involved in the Lahore Conspiracy Case of 1929.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In 1908 Khudiram Bose along with _________ was involved in throwing a bomb at a carriage believing it to be occupied by Kingsford, the then sitting judge of Muzaffarpur.
questions.explanation: Prafulla Chaki was an Indian revolutionary associated with the Jugantar group of revolutionaries. Khudiram Bose was among the youngest martyrs of India's freedom struggle against the British. At just 15, he had joined Anushilan Samiti and took part in several revolutionary activities against the British Raj. He was executed on August 11, 1908, in Muzaffarpur jail in Bihar.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: During British rule in India, who among the following unfurled the flag of India in Germany in 1907?
questions.explanation: Madam Bhikaji Cama. She founded the ‘Paris Indian Society’. Annie Besant (British socialist) - Founded Home rule league in India and she was first woman president of Indian National Congress (INC). Sarojini Naidu - First Indian woman president of the INC. Sucheta Kriplani holds the distinction of being India's first female Chief Minister, serving the state of Uttar Pradesh.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following revolutionaries was one of the co-founders of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) which got established in 1928 at Ferozeshah Kotla in Delhi?
questions.explanation: Bhagat Singh. The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA), formerly known as the Hindustan Republican Army (HRA) was founded by Ram Prasad Bismil, Sachindra Nath Bakshi, Sachindranath Sanyal, and Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee. HRA was established in October 1924 in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, by revolutionaries including Ram Prasad Bismil, Jogesh Chatterjee, Chandrashekhar Azad, Yogendra Shukla, and Sachindranath Sanyal. HRA took to socialist ideas, under Chandrashekhar Azad leadership, in 1928.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the following leaders with the related years: List I (Events/Positions) List II (Years) A. Khudai Khidmatgars 1929 B. First Law Minister 1947 C. Forward Bloc 1939 D.Non-CooperationMovement 1920
questions.explanation: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, also known as 'Frontier Gandhi' and 'Bacha Khan', was a prominent freedom fighter and advocate of non-violence. He became the first non-Indian to receive Bharat Ratna in 1987. B.R. Ambedkar was the first Law Minister of India and the architect of the Indian Constitution. Subhas Chandra Bose was an Indian nationalist and the founder of the All India Forward Bloc. Mahatma Gandhi was an Indian lawyer and anti-colonial nationalist, renowned for his principles of non-violence.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The 'Servants of India Society' was the brainchild of which of the following leaders ?
questions.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded - Ranade Institute of Economics (1908). He started an English weekly newspaper, The Hitavada (The people's paper). Servants of India Society was founded in 1905. Chitranjan Das is popularly known as Deshbandhu. Lala Lajpat Rai - Punjab National bank.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: On 8th April 1929, who among the following two revolutionists threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly?

options.b: Bhagat Singh and Ram Prasad Bismil

questions.explanation: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt. They threw bomb against the passage of the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill which would reduce the civil liberties of citizens. They were members of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association. On 23rd March, 1931 Bhagat Singh was hanged in the Lahore jail at the age of 23.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who is regarded as the 'Mother of Indian Revolution' ?
questions.explanation: Madame Cama : She is famous for hosting the precursor to the Indian National Flag on foreign soil (Stuttgart in Germany).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): Lala Lajpat Rai died due to injuries sustained during the Anti-Simon Commission protest in 1928. Reason (R): The Simon Commission, sent to India in 1928, included Indian members to represent the people’s voices.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false. Lala Lajpat Rai (Freedom fighters) was also called ‘Punjab Kesari’ and 'Lion of Punjab'. Bal Gangadhar Tilak - Founded the Home Rule League in 1916. Simon Commission - Indian Statutory Commission, group of seven Members, not a single Indian member in it, Headed by Sir John Simon. Simon Commission came to India in 1928.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following, along with her close associates, started the secret congress radio during the Quit India Movement?
questions.explanation: Usha Mehta. Awards - Padma Vibhushan (1998).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The statement- "We shall die to awaken the nation" was made by.
questions.explanation: Bagha Jatin (Jatindranath Mukherjee) - Born on 7th December 1879 in Kayagram (Nadia district) present-day Bangladesh. He acquired the moniker ‘Bagha Jatin’ when he single-handedly killed a Bengal tiger in 1906. Bir Tikendrajit Singh - He was a prince of the independent Kingdom of Manipur.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which freedom fighter was involved in the Kakori Train Action in 1925, for which the British government condemned him to death?
questions.explanation: Ram Prasad Bismil. Kakori Train Action - It was a train robbery (part of Kakori Conspiracy) that took place on 9 August 1925, near Lucknow. It was organised by the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA). Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, and Roshan Singh were hanged on 19 December 1927. Rajendra Nath Lahiri hanged on December 17, 1927.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Revolutionary Socialist Party was established in ________.
questions.explanation: 19 March 1940 by Tridib Chaudhuri. It has its roots in the Bengali liberation movement Anushilan Samiti and the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association . The first general secretary of the party was Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about famous patriotic slogans: 1. The words “Sarfaroshi ki tamanna ab hamare dil me hai, dekhna hai zor kitna baazu-e-qaatil mein hai” were composed by Ramprasad Bismil. 2. The slogan “Tum Mujhe Khoon Do, Mai Tumhe Azadi Dunga” is associated with Bhagat Singh. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Ramprasad Bismil (poet, writer, freedom fighter) - He participated in the Mainpuri Conspiracy of 1918, and the Kakori Conspiracy of 1925. Subhash Chandra Bose - “Jai Hind” & “Tum Mujhe Khoon Do, Mai Tumhe Azadi Dunga”. Mahatma Gandhi - “Karo ya Maro”. Muhammad Iqbal - “Sare Jahan Se Achha Hindustan Hamara”. Bankim Chandra Chatterjee - “Vande Mataram”. Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya - “Satyameva Jayate”.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following revolutionaries stated during his trial that "he did not wish to glorify the cult of the bomb and pistol but wanted a revolution in society"?
questions.explanation: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929. Sachindra Nath Sanyal was co-founder of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) in 1924. Barindra Kumar Ghosh (younger brother of Sri Aurobindo) published the Bengali weekly Jugantar patrika (1906).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following revolutionaries was associated with Swadesh Bandhav Samiti?
questions.explanation: Ashwini Kumar Dutta founded the Swadesh Bandhab Samiti on 6 th August 1905 in Barisal district (Bangladesh). Weekly paper: Barisal Hitaishi. He was responsible for the creation of the Cooperative Hindustan Bank in 1908.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following organized the armed rebellion against the British Raj in 1879 in Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: Vasudev Balwant Phadke - Known as the First Revolutionary and also the ‘Father of militant nationalism in India.’ Birsa Munda also known as Dharti Aaba (Father of Earth), belonged to the Munda tribe in the Chotanagpur Plateau area.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Communist Party of India was founded at ________ in October 1920.
questions.explanation: Tashkent. M.N. Roy (Manabendra Nath Roy), Abani Mukherji, founded the Communist Party of India (CPI) in 1920 in Tashkent (now the capital of Uzbekistan). The Communist Party of India was officially formed (1925) in Kanpur. Its founders included M. N. Roy, his wife Evelyn Trent, Abani Mukherji, and M. P. T. Acharya (Mandayam Parthasarathi Tirumal Acharya).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Koraput Revolution occurred in ______ during the Quit India Movement.
questions.explanation: Odisha. Koraput revolution {On August 25, 1942, 19 people died on the spot in police firing at Paparandi in Nabarangpur (Odisha). More than a thousand were jailed in Koraput district (Odisha). Veer Lakhan Nayak (Gandhi of Odisha) was hanged}. Quit India movement (8 August 1942 - 1944) - led by Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Bharat Naujawan Sabha is INCORRECT?

options.b: Bhagat Singh became its founding secretary
options.d: It started political work among the youth, peasants, and workers

questions.explanation: Bharat Naujawan Sabha was founded in Lahore (1926) by Bhagat Singh.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): The Indigo Revolt in Bengal began as a non-violent strike in 1859 when ryots refused to cultivate indigo. Reason (R): The Indigo Revolt was led by Bishnu Charan Biswas and Digambar Biswas of Nadia district, Bengal.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Digambar Biswas and Bishnu Biswas of Nadia district Bengal led the Indigo revolt. This Revolt began as a nonviolent strike in March 1859, as the ryots of a village in Bengal's Nadia district all agreed to refuse to grow any more indigo.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following revolutionaries was arrested by the British as an accused in the Alipore Bomb Conspiracy Case?
questions.explanation: Kanailal Dutta was among the 33 revolutionaries who got arrested in the Emperor vs Aurobindo Ghosh (Alipore Bomb Case). The Alipore Bomb case was a historic trial in which the British Government tried to implicate Sri Aurobindo in various revolutionary activities.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: At which of the following jails was Khudiram Bose sent to the gallows?
questions.explanation: Muzaffarpur. Khudiram Bose was arrested for trying to assassinate British judge Douglas Kingsford, he was executed on August 11, 1908, in Muzaffarpur jail in Bihar.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following persons was associated with the Chittagong Armoury Raid?
questions.explanation: Ardhendu Dastidar.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and its aftermath: Statement 1: Michael O’Dwyer, responsible for the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, was assassinated in Caxton Hall, London. Statement 2: Udham Singh carried out the assassination in 1940 as an act of revenge for the massacre.

options.c: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect
options.d: Statement 1 is incorrect, Statement 2 is correct

questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. Udham Singh. O'Dwyer, was shot dead at a joint meeting of the East India Association and the Central Asian Society in Caxton Hall, in retaliation for the massacre in Jallianwala Bagh Amritsar.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following assassinated Sir William Hutt Curzon Wyllie in London?
questions.explanation: Madan Lal Dhingra was an Indian revolutionary independence activist. While studying in England, he assassinated Sir William Hutt Curzon Wyllie, a British official, cited as one of the first acts of revolution in the Indian independence movement in the 20th century.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Veer Surendra Sai was a freedom fighter from:
questions.explanation: Odisha. Veer Surendra Sai started his revolt against British rule long before 1857 and continued his guerrilla war against the British authority from 1857 till 1864 long after 1857 the struggle led by the Rani of Jhansi, Tantia Tope, Kunwar Singh and others had subsided.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the first general secretary of the All India Farmer’s Congress?
questions.explanation: NG Ranga. He was a freedom fighter from Andhra Pradesh and also received Padma Vibhusan from the President of India for his contributions to the peasants' movement.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was a leader who led a revolt against British rule from North East India?
questions.explanation: Rani Gaidinliu was a Naga spiritual and political leader who led a revolt against British rule in India. At the age of 13, she joined the Heraka religious movement established by her cousin Haipou Jadonang in Manipur.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements: Statement 1: Bal Gangadhar Tilak’s Home Rule Movement was mainly active in Maharashtra. Statement 2: Annie Besant’s Home Rule Movement was mainly active in Punjab. Which one of the above statements is correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 only. Bal Gangadhar Tilak launched his Home Rule Movement in 1916. It was primarily centered in Maharashtra, which was his home base. He had significant influence and following in this region. He published his ideas through his newspapers "Kesari" (in Marathi) and "Mahratta" (in English) from Maharashtra.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following organisations, divided into two branches, was established by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant?
questions.explanation: Home Rule League. In April 1916, Tilak founded the Indian Home Rule League, with its headquarters in Poona. The league's first meeting was held in Belgaum. In September 1916, Annie Besant founded the All-India Home Rule League, based in Madras. Organizations and their founders : Indian Association - Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose; Theosophical Society - Helena Blavatsky, Henry Steel Olcott, William Quan Judge.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): Mahatma Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922. Reason (R): The Chauri Chaura incident in the United Provinces turned the movement violent when protesters set a police station on fire, killing policemen.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Chauri Chaura Incident took place at Chauri Chaura in the Gorakhpur district of United Provinces (now Uttar Pradesh) in British India. The police there fired upon a large group of protesters participating in the non-cooperation movement. In retaliation, the demonstrators attacked and set fire to a police station, killing all of its occupants. The incident led to the deaths of three civilians and 22 policemen. Mahatma Gandhi halted the non-cooperation movement on 12th February 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Indian National Army was formed in which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: Singapore. The Indian National Army (INA), also known as the Azad Hind Fauj, was a collaborationist armed unit of Indian supporters that fought under the command of the Japanese Empire. It was founded by Mohan Singh in September 1942 during World War II.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Being the President of the Indian National Congress, who among the following had called for complete independence from the British Raj in 1929?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru. He was an Indian freedom fighter who later became the first Prime Minister of India. In December 1929, he was chosen as the President of the Indian National Congress during its annual session in Lahore. At this event, he raised the tricolour flag on the banks of the Ravi River.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: On 31 October 1940, who among the following was arrested for offering individual Satyagraha to protest against India’s forced participation in the Second World War ?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru. On 31 October 1940, Jawaharlal Nehru was arrested for participating in individual Satyagraha, protesting against India’s forced involvement in the Second World War. During this period, Nehru also engaged in limited Civil Disobedience and spent approximately nine years in jail between 1921 and 1945.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Indian National Army (INA): 1. It was founded by Mohan Singh in September 1942 in Southeast Asia during World War II. 2. Subhas Chandra Bose later became the supreme leader of the INA. 3. Rabindranath Tagore was one of the commanders of the INA. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. Indian National Army (INA) was a collaborationist armed unit of Indian collaborators that fought under the command of the Japanese Empire. It was founded by Mohan Singh in September 1942 in Southeast Asia during World War II. Some notable people associated: Mohan Singh, Habib ur Rahman, Lt. Col Hori Lal Verma.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: What is the name of the famous British social reformer known for founding the Indian Home Rule League in 1916 ?
questions.explanation: Annie Besant. Annie Besant, an Irish theosophist, started the Home Rule movement in India in 1916, demanding self-government similar to the Irish Home Rule League. She founded the Home Rule League in Madras in September 1916 and established over 200 branches across India.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements: Statement 1: Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre. Statement 2: The Simon Commission was set up in 1919 to investigate the incident. Which of the above statements is/are true?
questions.explanation: 1 only. The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on April 13, 1919, when British troops, led by General Dyer, fired on a peaceful crowd in Amritsar, killing hundreds. In protest, Mahatma Gandhi returned the Kaiser-i-Hind title in 1920. The Hunter Commission was set up in 1919 to investigate the incident.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was one of the founders of the Swaraj Party?
questions.explanation: Chittaranjan Das. The Swaraj Party, initially called the Congress Khilafat Swaraj Party, was established in 1923 by Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru. This formation took place after the Gaya Annual Conference of the Indian National Congress in December 1922. Other important organizations and their founders: Indian National Congress (1885): Founded by A.O. Hume. All India Kisan Sabha (1936): Sahajanand Saraswati. Azad Hind Fauj (1943): Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Satyagrahas was started by Dr B R Ambedkar in 1927?
questions.explanation: Mahad Satyagraha: It is also known as the Chavdar Tank Satyagraha, begun in Mahad (Raigad), Maharashtra. It centered around the Chavdar Tank, a public water source that was reserved exclusively for upper castes.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following leaders founded the women's wing of Congress in 1940 ?
questions.explanation: Sucheta Kriplani (First female Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh from 1963 - 67). She sang Vande Mataram on 14th August 1947 in the opening session of Parliament.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: On 15 August 1947, the first prime minister of India, Jawaharlal Nehru, raised the Indian National Flag above the __________ of Red Fort in Delhi.
questions.explanation: Lahori Gate. The National Flag of India was adopted on 22 July 1947, Designed by Pingali Venkayya.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who moved the resolution proposing that the National Flag of India be a 'horizontal tricolor of saffron, white and dark green in equal proportion '?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru. The Tricolour was adopted as our national flag at a Congress Committee meeting in Karachi in 1931.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of 'Tiger Legion' or 'Free India Legion'?
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose - founder of 'Azad Hind Fauj'. 'Tiger Legion' was formed in 1941 with the help of the German Government to fight against the British.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Komagata Maru incident: 1. The Komagata Maru, carrying Indian passengers, was denied permission to land in Canada in 1914. 2. The ship was denied entry at Sydney harbour in Australia. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. The Komagata Maru was a coal-transport steamship that had been converted into a passenger ship by Hong Kong-based businessman Gurdit Singh. It set off from Hong Kong in April 1914, reaching Vancouver’s harbour a month later with 376 people on board, most of them Sikhs. The steamship eventually ended up back in India on 29th Sep 1914 at Budge Budge, Calcutta.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The origin of Directive Principles of State Policy can be traced to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Karachi Resolution (1931). The Karachi Session of Congress in 1931 was presided by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Gandhi Irwin Pact - 5 March 1931. It marked the end of civil disobedience.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters was one of the founders of the Fergusson College in Pune in 1885 ?
questions.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak. Other Co-founding members of Fergusson College :- Vaman Shriram Apte, Vishnushashtri Chiplunkar, Mahadeo Ballal Namjoshi and Gopal Krishna Agarkar.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das gave up their legal practices during which Movement ?
questions.explanation: Non-Cooperation Movement (1920 - 1922). It was organized by Mahatma Gandhi to obtain self governance. Many lawyers gave up their practices such as Motilal Nehru, C.Rajagopalachari, Saifuddin Kitchlew, Vallabhbhai Patel, Asaf Ali, T. Prakasam and Rajendra Prasad.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: When was Alluri Sitarama Raju arrested ending a two-year armed tribal struggle?
questions.explanation: May 1924. He was publicly executed in Koyyuru on May 7 after being tied to a tree and shot. His final resting place (tomb) is at Krishna Devi Peta, 111 km from Visakhapatnam. In August 1922, he launched the Rampa Rebellion (Manyam Rebellion) against the British. During this rebellion, he was helped by Bobbili Dora. The Prime Minister has unveiled a bronze statue of Alluri Sitharama Raju in Andhra Pradesh to celebrate 125th birth anniversary on 4th July 2022.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which year, the Koya rebellion took place in the eastern Godavari tract?
questions.explanation: 1879-1880. The Koya Revolts rose under Tomma Sora during 1879-80. Other important revolts are Kol Mutiny (1831), Ho and Munda Uprisings (1820-1837), The Santhal Rebellion (1855-56), Ramosi Uprising (1822- 1829), etc.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which of the following regions did Baba Ramchandra mainly lead the peasant struggle during colonial rule?
questions.explanation: Awadh. He led a peasant movement in Awadh against Talukdars and Landlords.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: At which of the following places did C. Rajagopalachari break the salt law in the year 1930 ?
questions.explanation: Vedaranyam. C. Rajagopalachari broke the salt law in 1930 at Vedaranyam, a small coastal town in the then Tanjore District. The first Indian governor of free India was C. Rajagopalachari.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: What was the name of the women's regiment in the Indian National Army founded by Subhash Chandra Bose?
questions.explanation: Rani of Jhansi Regiment.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): Maharaja Bodhchandra Singh signed the Instrument of Accession with the Government of India on 11 August 1947. Reason (R): The Instrument of Accession provided for Manipur’s full merger into India immediately in 1947.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false.
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false. Bodhchandra Singh, signed the Instrument of Accession on 11 August 1947, with the assurance of Manipur's internal autonomy. This agreement marked Manipur's entry into the Union of India, though full integration followed with the Manipur Merger Agreement in 1949.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was one of the founders of the Congress Socialist Party?
questions.explanation: Ram Manohar Lohia. Congress Socialist Party (Socialist caucus within the Indian National Congress) - Founded in 1934. Other founders - Jayaprakash Narayan and Acharya Narendra Dev.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which city was the Jhanda Satyagraha or Flag Satyagraha of 1923 held ?
questions.explanation: Nagpur. Flag Satyagraha is a part of civil disobedience during the Indian independence movement.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: _______was executed at Lahore in November 1915 for his role in the Ghadar Conspiracy in February 1915.
questions.explanation: Kartar Singh Sarabha. Ghadar Conspiracy (1915) - Plan to initiate a pan-India mutiny in the British Indian Army during World War by the Ghadar Party (United States), the Berlin Committee (Germany), the Indian revolutionary underground in British India and the German Foreign Office.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following methods was used by the villagers during the Chipko Movement?
questions.explanation: The Chipko Movement, which began in the Himalayan region of Uttarakhand in the 1970s, is globally recognized for its unique and powerful method of non-violent protest. The name "Chipko" itself means "to stick" or "to hug" in Hindi. The villagers, particularly women, would physically embrace the trees to form a human shield, preventing the loggers and contractors from felling them. This simple yet profound act symbolized their deep connection to the forest and became an iconic form of environmental activism.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who set up a Dayanand Anglo Vedic school in Lahore?
questions.explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai. The Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) School was established in Lahore in 1886 by Lala Lajpat Rai and his associates to propagate the ideals of Swami Dayanand Saraswati (founder of Arya Samaj). Later, it grew into the DAV College Trust and Management Society, which runs many educational institutions across India even today. Its aim was to provide modern education (science, English, mathematics) along with teachings of the Vedas and Arya Samaj philosophy.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements with regard to Satnami Movement of Central India. a) The movement was founded by Ghasidas. b) The movement was to improve the condition of leather workers. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both a and b. Guru Ghasidas, a 19th-century advocate of the Satnami sect, founded the Satnami community in Chhattisgarh, promoting Satnam (truth) and equality. His teachings share similarities with Hinduism and Buddhism. The Satnami movement was led by non-Brahman leaders who worked to empower marginalized communities.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Ahrar Movement in British India is/are incorrect? 1. Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was one of the founders of the Ahrar Movement. 2. The Ahrar Movement was founded after the Quit India Movement of 1942.
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was an Indian independence activist, writer, and a senior leader of the Indian National Congress. After India’s independence, he became the first Minister of Education. The Ahrar Movement was started by Muslims who had lost faith in the Khilafat Movement. It was founded by Maulana Muhammad Ali, Hakim Ajmal Khan, Hasan Imam, Maulana Zafar Ali Khan, and Mazhar-ul-Haq .

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following participated in the All-World Religious Conference (Parliament of Religions) held in 1893 in Chicago?
questions.explanation: Swami Vivekananda was a disciple of Ramakrishna. He gave his famous speech at the Parliament of World Religions in Chicago in 1893. He established the Belur Math in West Bengal, and Ramakrishna Mission in 1897.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who founded the Prarthana Samaj in Mumbai in 1867?
questions.explanation: Atmaram Pandurang. Prarthana Samaj was founded with an aim to make people believe in one God and worship only one God.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: When was a Madrasa opened in Kolkata to promote the study of Arabic, Persian and Islamic law?
