questions.explanation: 1781 C.E. It was set up by Warren Hastings of the first Governor General of East India Company. Other universities and colleges: Aligarh Muslim University, originally as the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College (1875), Jamia Millia Islamia (1920), Darul Uloom Deoband (1866), Osmania University (1918).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): Tarabai Shinde was the author of the book Stree Purush Tulana, published in 1882. Reason (R): Stree Purush Tulana highlighted women’s superiority over men and rejected the idea of gender equality.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false.
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false. Tarabai Shinde (1850-1910) was a pioneering Indian social reformer and writer who advocated for women's rights. Her notable work, "Stree Purush Tulana" (A Comparison Between Women and Men), published in 1882, critiqued the patriarchal society and argued for gender equality. Swarnakumari Devi : She was the first Indian Woman editor (the editor of the women’s journal Bharati). Usha Mehta wrote the book “Mahatma Gandhi and Humanism”. Pandita Ramabai : She wrote the High Caste Hindu Women, Stree Dharma Neeti, American Encounter.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Samata Sainik Dal was formed in 1927 by whom among the following personalities?
questions.explanation: BR Ambedkar. He founded ‘Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha' in 1924 to promote and uplift the education of untouchables. Mahatma Gandhi founded - Harijan Sevak Sangh in 1932. Narayana Guru founded the Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam (SNDP) in 1903.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Raja Rammohun Roy and his reform activities: 1. Raja Rammohun Roy founded the Atmiya Sabha in 1814 in Kolkata, marking the beginning of modern socio-religious reform in India. 2. He co-founded the Brahmo Sabha in 1828, which later developed into the Brahmo Samaj. 3. The Atmiya Sabha was founded by Keshab Chandra Sen in 1814. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. Raja Rammohun Roy, known as "the Father of Indian Renaissance," was an Indian reformer and writer who co-founded the Brahmo Sabha in 1828, leading to the formation of the Brahmo Samaj, a significant socio-religious reform movement. Honored with the title of Raja by Mughal emperor Akbar II, his influence marked the beginning of modern thought in Kolkata, particularly with the establishment of the Atmiya Sabha in 1814.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Sikh reform movements was started in 1873 in Amritsar?
questions.explanation: Singh Sabha Movement. It was a reform organization for Sikhs, with the first Sabhas established in Amritsar in 1873 and Lahore in 1879. The Babbar Akali Movement: It was founded at the Sikh Educational Conference in Hoshiarpur in 1921. The Gurudwara Reform Movement (Akali Movement) was started in Amritsar in 1920.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who founded the Arya Samaj in Mumbai in 1875 ?
questions.explanation: Swami Dayanand Saraswati, an Indian philosopher, is known for his work Satyarth Prakash and the slogan “Go Back to the Vedas.” He also initiated the Shuddhi Movement. Debendranath Tagore founded the Tattvabodhini Sabha in 1839 and joined the Brahmo Samaj (founded by Raja Rammohan Roy in 1828) in 1842. The Ramakrishna Mission was established by Swami Vivekananda in May 1897 at Belur Math, West Bengal.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: With reference to Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, consider the following statements. i) He protested child marriage and polygamy. ii) Due to his efforts, the first Hindu Widow Remarriage Act, 1856, was introduced. iii) He was primarily known for his scholarship in Persian language. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: i, ii. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar's efforts led to the passage of the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act (Act XV) on July 16, 1856, legalizing widow remarriage in India under East India Company rule. Drafted by Lord Dalhousie and enacted by Lord Canning, the law took effect on July 26, 1856.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding social reform movements in British India: 1. Guru Ghasidas led the Satnami Movement to uplift the social conditions of leather workers. 2. The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Guru Ghasidas in the early 19th century. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Guru Ghasidas, the Guru of Satnam Dharma, was a Satnami saint and renowned scholar from Chhattisgarh in the early 19th century. He began preaching in the deep forests of Chhattisgarh, spreading his teachings. The Satnami movement, also known as Satnampanth or Sadhanpanth, was a social and religious movement in India that challenged the caste system and the prevailing political and religious authorities.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which was the first socio-religious organisation established in Bombay in 1840 to work for the annihilation of caste?
questions.explanation: Paramhans Mandali : Founder - Durgaram Mehtaji. Dharma Sabha was formed in 1830 in Calcutta by Radhakanta Deb, primarily for the defense of Hindu orthodoxy.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Phule in 1873 to promote education and social rights among the underprivileged. Reason (R): The Prarthana Samaj, founded by Jyotiba Phule, aimed at uplifting lower castes and women in Pune.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false.
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false. Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Phule in 1873, It is also known as the Society of Seekers of Truth. Its aim was to access social rights and civil liberties for people of lower castes, underprivileged and women. Jyotiba Phule (a social activist) - Established the first school for girls in India in Pune in 1848. Dalit term was first used by him.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was the pioneer of widow remarriages in Maharashtra and also started a girls' school in Poona along with his wife?
questions.explanation: Jyotirao Govindrao Phule. He was a prominent social reformer from Maharashtra who dedicated his life to eradicating untouchability and caste discrimination. Together with his wife, Savitribai, he played a key role in promoting women's education in India, founding the first girls' school in 1848 at Bhidewada, Pune. Major Publications: Tritiya Ratna, Gulamgiri, and Shetkarayacha Aasud.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the following movements with their respective founders: a. Faraizi Movement I. Sayyid Ahmad of Rae Bareli b. Mohammedan Literary Society II. Sir Syed Ahmad Khan c. Indian Patriotic Association III. Nawab Abdul Latif d. Wahabi Movement IV. Haji Shariatullah

options.a: a - IV, b - III, c - Il, d - I
options.b: a - III, b - IV, c - II, d - I
options.c: a - Il, b - I, c - IV, D - III
options.d: a - I, b - II, c - III, d - IV

questions.answer_text: a - IV, b - III, c - Il, d - I
questions.explanation: a - IV, b - III, c - Il, d - I. Other Movement/Organisation and their Founders: Bhoodan movement - Acharya Vinobha Bhave, Servants of India Society - GK Gokhale, Khudai Khidmatgar - Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan, Arya Samaj - Dayanand Saraswati, Self-respect Movement - EV Ramaswamy Naicker, Tattvabodhini Sabha - Debendranath Tagore, Abhinav Bharat - Vir Savarkar, and Narmada Bachao - Medha Patkar.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in Aligarh: 1. The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College was founded by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan in 1875 to promote Western education among Muslims. 2. The college was modeled on the pattern of Oxford and Cambridge universities and later developed into Aligarh Muslim University. 3. The college was originally established by Syed Ameer Ali with support from the British government. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. In 1875, Sir Syed Ahmed Khan founded the Muhammadan Anglo Oriental College on the pattern of Oxford and Cambridge universities. The college later grew into Aligarh Muslim University. He started the Aligarh movement to promote western education among muslims. He established the Scientific Society in 1864.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Henry Louis Vivian Derozio, a teacher at Hindu College, Calcutta, in the 1820s, promoted radical ideas and encouraged his pupils to question all authority. Referred to as the _________ his students attacked tradition and custom, demanded education for women and campaigned for the freedom of thought and expression.
questions.explanation: Young Bengal Movement. Other Reform Organisations and its Founders : The Brahmo Samaj (1828) - Raja Ram Mohan Roy, The Veda Samaj (1864) - Keshab Chandra Sen and K. Sridharalu Naidu, The Prarthana Samaj (1867) - Atmaram Pandurang.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Self-Respect Movement in Tamil Nadu: 1. The Self-Respect Movement was started by E. V. Ramasamy (Periyar) in 1925. 2. The Self-Respect Movement was initiated in 1910 with the aim of promoting British education among upper castes. Which of the above statements is/are true?
questions.explanation: 1 only. The Self-Respect Movement was a social and political movement in South India that sought to achieve equality and social justice for people oppressed by the caste system. The movement was initiated by E. V. Ramasamy (also known as Periyar).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following is associated with the Theosophical Society?
questions.explanation: Annie Besant had come to India in 1893. She laid the foundation of the Central Hindu College in Benaras in 1898. The Theosophical Society: Theosophy represents the wisdom at the core of all religions when stripped of superstitions and excesses. It was founded by Madame H. P. Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott in New York (United States) in 1875. In 1882, they shifted their headquarters to Adyar (Madras Presidency).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following is NOT associated with the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha?
questions.explanation: Syed Ahmed Khan. The Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha was a social reform organization founded in 1851 by Parsis in Bombay (now Mumbai) to promote reform in the ancient Zoroastrian religion. It was composed of Dadabhai Naoroji, J.B. Wacha, S.S Bengalee and Naoroji Furdonji, with the funding from K.N. Kama.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct about Prarthana Samaj? A. Prarthana Samaj or ‘Prayer Society’ in Sanskrit, was a movement for religious and social reforms. B. Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1863 by Dadoba Pandurang and his brother Atmaram Pandurang.
questions.explanation: Only A. The Prarthana Samaj was established in Bombay by Dr. Atma Ram Pandurang in 1867. Aim - To remove caste restriction, abolish child marriage, encourage women education and promotes widow remarriages. Members - R.C. Bhandarkar and Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Sree Narayana Guru considered the differences based on caste and religion as meaningless and advocated the principle of ‘One Caste, one Religion and one God’ for all. He belonged to which of the following organisations?
questions.explanation: Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam. Sree Narayana Guru: In 1888, he built a temple dedicated to Lord Shiva at Aruvippuram which was against the caste-based restrictions of the time.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): Kandukuri Veeresalingam pioneered the movement for widow remarriage and girls’ education in the Andhra region. Reason (R): Sree Narayana Guru was regarded as the father of the Telugu Renaissance movement in Andhra Pradesh.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false.
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false. Kandukuri Veeresalingam (1848-1919) was a social reformer and writer from Andhra Pradesh. He is considered as the father of the Telugu Renaissance movement. He also fought against child marriage and the dowry system.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following organizations was founded in Poona, Satara and other towns of Maharashtra that worked against Brahmanical orthodoxy and tried to reform Hinduism?
questions.explanation: Paramahansa Mandali - It was a secret socio-religious group, established in 1849, in Bombay and was closely related to Manav Dharma Sabha which was founded in 1844 in Surat.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the following associations with the class whose interests they primarily represented: List I List II 1. Landholders’ Society (1838) A. Merchants and businessmen 2. Bombay Association (1852) B. Landlords (Zamindars) 3. Madras Native Association (1852) C. Educated middle-class elites 4. Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870) D. Political awareness in Madras region
questions.explanation: 1–B, 2–A, 3–D, 4–C. Landholders’ Society also known as the Zamindari Association is considered to be the first political association of modern India. It was formally launched in Calcutta in March 1838. Raja Radhakant dev, Dwarkanath tagore, Prasanna Kumar Tagore, Rajkamal Sen and Bhabani Charan Mitra were its founding members.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who started the temple entry movement in 1927 ?
questions.explanation: Bhimrao Ambedkar. It was a movement to allow lower caste people to enter temples. Dalits Movements led by Bhimrao Ambedkar: The second biggest movement for the entry of untouchables in the famous Kalaram temple of Nashik in 1930. Mahad Satyagraha (1927) was a movement for the Dalits to get the right to drink water from the tank.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Visva Bharati a famous educational institute was founded in 1921 by:
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore. Visva-Bharati University: It is located in Shantiniketan, West Bengal and became the world's first "living heritage university".

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who established Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan to promote education and culture?
questions.explanation: Dr. Kanhaiyalal Maneklal Munshi. Bhartiya Vidya Bhawan - A charitable public trust founded on November 7, 1938.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who had founded the first Women’s University in India ?
questions.explanation: Dhondo Keshav Karve (Maharishi Karve)- He founded the first women university (SNDT Women's University) in 1916 in India. Awards - Bharat Ratna (1958), Padma Vibhushan (1955). The Widow Remarriage Association was founded by Vishnu Shastri Pandit.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: __________ was the first woman to be accorded the title Pandita by the faculty of Calcutta University for her exceptional knowledge of Sanskrit.
questions.explanation: Ramabai Sarasvati was an Indian social reformer, a pioneer in the education and emancipation of women in India. She was the first woman to be accorded the titles of Pandita. She was one of the 10 women delegates of the Congress session of 1889. In the late 1890s, she founded Mukti Mission at Kedgaon village, and established Sharada Sadan (Home of Wisdom), a school for widows, in Mumbai. In 1919, the king of England bestowed on her the Kaiser-I - Hind award.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who is known as the founder of the Widow Remarriage Association (1861)?
questions.explanation: Mahadev Govind Ranade. Widow Remarriage Association - Started by Vishnu Shastri Pandit in 1856. Aim - Promote widow remarriage and campaigned against Child Marriage. Karsondas Mulji - He started the 'Satya Prakash' in Gujarati in 1852 to promote the remarriage of widows. Organization founded by Mahadev Govind Ranade - Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870), Vaktrutvottejak Sabha (1875).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which language was the work of Raja Ram Mohan Roy, 'Gift to Monotheists' originally written ?
questions.explanation: Persian. Raja Ram Mohan Roy: Father of Modern India’s Renaissance. Given the title ‘Raja’ by Akbar II (Mughal Emperor).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Narayana Guru: 1. He was a social reformer from the Ezhava community who strongly opposed the caste system. 2. He was born in the state of Kerala and propagated the idea of “One caste, one religion, one God for all.” Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Shri Narayan Guru led a reform movement against the injustice in the caste-ridden society of Kerala in order to promote spiritual enlightenment and social equality. His famous quote: "One caste, one religion and one god for all".

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following founded the Indian Association along with Anand Mohan Bose?
questions.explanation: Surendranath Banerjee. Indian Association of Calcutta (1876), Aimed to unify Indian people on a common political programme and create a strong public opinion on political questions.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following organized Sarvajanik Ganesh Utsav to inculcate national sentiments among the masses?
questions.explanation: Lokmanya Tilak (Bal Gangadhar Tilak): Tilak launched the Indian Home Rule League in April 1916 at Belgaum (Annie Besant launched the Home Rule League in September 1916 at Madras). His famous declaration “Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it”. The British Government termed him as the "Father of Indian Unrest".

questions.subject: History
questions.question: 'The Deccan Sabha' was founded by which of the following nationalists?
questions.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale. He became president of Indian National Congress (INC) in Benaras session (1905).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Mohammedan Literary Society founded in Calcutta in 1863 was founded by:
questions.explanation: Nawab Abdul Latif (Father of muslim renaissance in Bengal). Lord Lytton gave him The title of "Nawab''. Lord Dufferin gave him the title of Nawab Bahadur. Mohammedan Literary Society was a literary society of Muslims in British India.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the following social reformers/newspapers with the community or society they primarily addressed: List I List II 1. Dadabhai Naoroji – Rast Goftar A. First Indian newspaper in Hindi 2. Raja Ram Mohan Roy – B. First English newspaper in Samvad Kaumudi India 3. James Augustus Hicky – Bengal Gazette C. Reform among Parsis 4. Pt. Jugal Kishore Shukla – Udant Martand D. Hindu socio-religious reform Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: 1–C, 2–D, 3–B, 4–A. Rast Goftar ("The Truth Teller") was an Anglo-Gujarati paper operating in Bombay that was started in 1854 by Dadabhai Naoroji and Kharshedji Cama and championed social reform among Parsis in Western India. Publishers and their Newspaper : James Augustus Hicky - “Bengal Gazette”, Pt. Jugal Kishore Shukla - “Udant Martand”, Raja Ram Mohan Roy - “Samvad Kaumudi” and “Mirat-ul-Akbar”, Madhusudan Ray - “Hindoo Patriot”, Devendra Nath Tagore - “Indian Mirror”.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following devoted his life for the upliftment of widows and established the Widow Remarriage Association in 1893?
questions.explanation: D K Karve. Karve’s autobiographical works: Atmawrutta (1928) in Marathi, and Looking Back (1936) in English. Awards - Bharat Ratna (1958), Padma Vibhushan (1955).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Indian social reformers: 1. Raja Ram Mohan Roy was the first social reformer to recognize modern education as a means for spreading progressive ideas in India. 2. He founded institutions like the Vedanta College (1825) and organizations such as Atmiya Sabha (1815) and Brahmo Samaj (1828). Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Raja Ram Mohan Roy (Father of modern India), Organizations founded : Brahmo Samaj (1828, Kolkata), Atmiya Sabha (1815, Kolkata). He founded the Vedanta College in 1825.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Aligarh Movement, which was largely responsible for the revival of Muslims in India?
questions.explanation: Sayyid Ahmad Khan. Mirza Ghulam Ahmad - Founder of the Ahmadiyya movement. Muhammad Allama Iqbal wrote the famous song 'Saare jahan se achha'. He is also known for giving birth to the 'idea of Pakistan'.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar and Mahadev Govind Ranade carried out their work of religious reforms in Maharashtra through which of the following organisations?
questions.explanation: Prarthana Samaj (1867).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was one of the founders of Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha or Religious Reform Association?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji. He presided over the second session of Indian National Congress at Kolkata (1886). Keshab Chandra Sen - He established Indian Reform association (1870), Member of Brahmo Samaj (1828). Atmaram Pandurang: Founded - Prarthana Samaj (1867) with the help of Keshab Chandra Sen.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who founded the Tattvabodhini Sabha that was set up to explore spiritual truth?
questions.explanation: Debendranath Tagore (Father of Rabindranath Tagore) founded the Tattvabodhini Sabha in 1839. He joined the Brahmo Samaj in 1842.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following is NOT associated with Brahmo Samaj?
questions.explanation: Atmaram Pandurang founded Prartahana Samaj (1867), Other members - R.C. Bhandarkar and Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade. Objective - Women Education, Widow remarriage and Disapproval of caste system.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Veda Samaj of Madras was inspired by the________.
questions.explanation: Brahmo Samaj (1828). It denounced polytheism and opposed idolatry. Deobandi Movement (1866) : Founder - Mohammad Qasim Nanotavi and Rashid Ahmed Gangohi.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Principal of a Sanskrit College who represented a blend of Indian and Western culture was ________ .
questions.explanation: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar ("Father of Bengali Prose"). Hindu Widow Remarriage Act of 1856 was enacted with the efforts of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about women-led movements in India: 1. Rani Gaidinliu was associated with the Heraka movement, which arose in the 1920s among the Zeliangrong people. 2. The Nisha Bandh movement was led by Rani Gaidinliu to fight against alcoholism in the late 1970s. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Heraka was a socio-religious movement that arose in the 1920s in the Zeliangrong territory. Meira Paibi : This movement was founded in 1977 in Kaching district. Nupi Lan : There were two demonstrations led by women against the colonial authorities in Manipur, British India. In 1904, The second Nupi Lan began in 1939 in response to rice exports during World War II. Nisha Bandh : The women's movement developed in the late 1970s. Its origin is attributed to the Meitei women's activism to fight against alcoholism and drug addiction.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Some of Swami Dayanand's followers started a network of schools and colleges called D.A.V. What does 'A' stand for in D.A.V.?
questions.explanation: Anglo. The acronym DAV translates as 'Dayanand Anglo Vedic', the melange of the Vedas and Modernity. Mahatma Hansraj established the first DAV School at Lahore on June 1, 1886. Other Educational Establishments in India: 1835 - Calcutta Medical College and the Elphinstone College of Bombay. 1857 - University of Bombay, Calcutta, and Madras. 1882 - The University of Punjab. 1887 - The University of Allahabad.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The ________ was started by the Sikh reformers to purify their religious places by removing the evil social practices that had slowly crept into them.
questions.explanation: Akali Movement (Gurdwara Reform Movement).Namdhari Movement (Kuka Movement) - A Sikh reform movement that began in the Punjab region of India (Founded by Baba Ram Singh in 1857). Ghadar Movement: President - Sohan Singh Bhakna, Founded - 15 July 1913, Dissolved - January 1948, Preceded by - Pacific Coast Hindustan Association. Nirankari Movement - It was a social reform movement for Sikhism (founded by Baba Dyal Das in 1851).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Ahmadiyya forms a sect of Islam which originated from India. It was founded by___________in 1889.
questions.explanation: Mirza Ghulam Ahmad. The Ahmadiyya Movement was founded on liberal principles and principles of a universal religion for all humanity. After his death the movement was led by elected successor Hakeem Noor-ud-din. Mir Nisar Ali (Titu mir) - Narkelbaria movement, 1831. Haji Shariatullah - Faraizi movement. Shah Walliullah - Wahabi movement.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following founded the Widow Remarriage Association?
questions.explanation: Pandit Vishnu Shastri.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Lala Lajpat Rai was an active member of which organisation?
questions.explanation: Arya Samaj. It promoted the study of the Vedas and the Upanishads, and it advocated for social reform, including the abolition of caste discrimination.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the founder of Dharma Sabha ?
questions.explanation: Radhakanta Deb founded it in 1830 in Calcutta. The Dharma Sabha was a conservative Hindu society. It campaigned against the Hindu Widow Remarriage Act, 1856. Chief public organ - Bengali newspaper “Samachar Chandrika” {Editor - Bhabani Charan Bandyopadhyay (Secretary of Dharma Sabha)}.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Annie Besant laid the foundation of the Central Hindu College in______ in 1898 where both Hindu religion and Western scientific subjects were taught.
questions.explanation: Banaras. Annie Besant: A British socialist, educationist and women’s rights activist. She came to India in 1893.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: When was the Dev Samaj founded in Lahore by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri?
questions.explanation: 1887. Dev Samaj is a Hindu reform movement that was founded in response to the perceived ills of orthodox Hinduism.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): Satguru Ram Singh was the leader who started the Kuka Movement. Reason (R): The Kuka Movement was aimed at purifying Sikhism and opposing social evils as well as British rule.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: The Kukas, a sect within Sikhism, formed with a motive to purify Sikhism. Baba Dayal Das: founded the Nirankari Movement. Balak Singh: An Indian Sikh religious leader who founded the Namdhari sect. Thakur Singh Sandhawalia: Founder of Singh sabha.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who emphasized the worship of God as Nirankar (Formless) in Punjab?
questions.explanation: Baba Dayal Das - Founder of the Nirankari Movement. He emphasized the worship of god as Nirankar (formless). Baba Ram Singh - The leader of the Kuka movement in Punjab. Maharaja Ranjit Singh (“Sher-e-Punjab” or "Lion of Punjab") - First Maharaja of the Sikh Empire. Guru Gobind Singh - The tenth and last Sikh Guru.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The first session of All India Depressed Classes congress was held at __________ in 1930.
questions.explanation: Nagpur. 'Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha (Outcastes Welfare Association)’, 1923.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Pandita Ramabai: 1. She founded the Arya Mahila Samaj to promote women’s education and social reform. 2. She was the first woman to be awarded the titles Pandita and Sarasvati for her knowledge of Sanskrit. 3. She was the founder of the Depressed Class Mission in Mumbai in 1906. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. Pandita Ramabai (women's rights & education activist). She was the first woman to be awarded the titles of Pandita as a Sanskrit scholar and Sarasvati after being examined by the faculty of the University of Calcutta. She was awarded with the Kaiser-i-Hind Medal for community service in 1919. She was one of the ten women delegates of the Congress session of 1889.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In 1930, _________ led a satyagraha for the rights of untouchables’ entry to the Kalaram temple at Nasik.
questions.explanation: Dr B.R. Ambedkar. In 1920, he began the publication of the weekly Mooknayak (Leader of the Silent) in Mumbai with the help of Shahu of Kolhapur. His important writings: ‘The Annihilation of Caste’, ‘Who Were the Shudras’, ‘The Untouchables’, ‘Riddles in Hinduism’, etc.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following was known as the forerunner of the Brahmo Samaj?
questions.explanation: Atmiya Sabha. Brahmo Samaj {Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded Brahmo Sabha in 1828, Aim - worship of the eternal God. It split into two in 1866 (Brahmo Samaj of India led by Keshub Chandra Sen and Adi Brahmo Samaj led by Debendranath Tagore), Prominent Leaders: Debendranath Tagore, Keshub Chandra Sen, Pt. Sivnath Shastri, and Rabindranath Tagore}.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following pairs of Newspapers/Journals and their founders/editors: 1. Nibandhmala – Vishnushastri Chiplunkar 2. Prabhakar – Gopal Hari Deshmukh 3. Kesari – Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak 4. Pudhari – Swami Vivekananda How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Only three. Vishnushastri Chiplunkar was the founder/editor of Nibandhmala, a Marathi literary magazine. Gopal Hari Deshmukh is writer of Prabhakar newspaper. Kesari (Marathi newspaper, 1881, Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak). Pudhari (Marathi daily, 1937). (Newspaper/ Journal – Founder):- Udbodhan, 1899, Swami Vivekananda. Independent, 1919, Motilal Nehru. Tahzib -ul-Akhlaq, 1871, Sir Syed Ahmed Khan.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha was established at ___________.
questions.explanation: Bombay.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Vidhava Vivaha Uttejaka Mandal (Society for Encouragement of Widow Marriage) was established in __________ in the second half of the nineteenth century.
questions.explanation: Bombay Presidency. It was established by Vishnushastri Pandit in 1866. Hindu Widow Remarriage Act (1856) was passed by Lord Canning with the efforts of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar. Sati Practice was abolished by William Bentinck in 1829 with the efforts of Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Begums of Bhopal founded a primary school for girls in the early twentieth century at _____.
questions.explanation: Aligarh. The Begums of Bhopal played a vital role, from the early 20th century, in promoting education among Muslim women. They founded a primary school for girls at Aligarh. Nawab Begum was the founding Chancellor of Aligarh Muslim University.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the following social reformers with the organizations they were associated with: 1. Dadoba Pandurang – Paramhansa Sabha 2. V R Shinde – Depressed Class Mission 3. Tulsi Ram – Radha Swami Satsang 4. G G Agarkar – Deccan Education Society Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 and 4. Paramhansa Sabha was founded by Dadoba Pandurang. V R Shinde founded the Depressed Class Mission in Mumbai in 1906. Radha Swami Satsang was founded by Tulsi Ram in 1861.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following wrote the Brahmo Covenant, which was a statement of the creed of the Brahmo Samaj and made a list of the duties and obligations of its members?
questions.explanation: Debendranath Tagore. He was the founder in 1848 of the Brahmo religion, which today is synonymous with Brahmoism. In 1863 he founded Shantiniketan (“Abode of Peace”).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was NOT a Nayanar saint?
questions.explanation: Andal. The Nayanars were a group of 63 poet-saints living in Tamil Nadu during the 6th to 8th centuries CE who were devoted to the Hindu god Shiva. Along with the Alwars, their contemporaries who were devoted to Vishnu, they influenced the Bhakti movement in early medieval South India.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a correct match of Dargah and its respective location?

options.b: Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki Dargah - Delhi

questions.explanation: Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya Dargah is the Dargah of the Sufi saint Khwaja Nizamuddin Auliya. It is located in the Nizamuddin West area of Delhi

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following is known as the 'father of Muslim renaissance' in Bengal?
questions.explanation: Nawab Abdul Latif Khan. His title, Nawab, was awarded by the British in 1880. He was one of the first Muslim in nineteenth century India to embrace the idea of modernization. Indian National Congress and Its Sessions

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: Who was the first woman to be the president of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: Annie Besant became the president of the Indian National Congress in 1917, at a time when India’s freedom movement was gaining momentum. A British-born social reformer and theosophist, Annie Besant played a vital role in promoting Indian self-rule and education. Her election as Congress president marked a significant moment in Indian history, symbolizing both the inclusion of women in the political sphere and the growing international support for India's independence movement.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: With whose participation did the Anushilan group join forces when the Bengal Congress broke up into two factions after the death of CR Das?
questions.explanation: J.M. Sengupta. After the death of Chittaranjan Das (C.R. Das) in 1925, the Bengal Provincial Congress Committee split into two factions — the moderates and the radicals. The radical faction was led by J.M. Sengupta, a close associate of C.R. Das. The Anushilan Samiti, a revolutionary nationalist group that had been involved in militant activities against British rule, found ideological alignment with Sengupta’s more assertive and left-leaning stance. As a result, many members of the Anushilan group aligned themselves with J.M. Sengupta’s faction to continue pushing for more aggressive nationalist policies from within the Congress.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: Consider the following sessions of the Indian National Congress and their Presidents: 1. Bombay, 1885 – W.C. Banerjee 2. Madras, 1887 – Badruddin Tyabji 3. Belgaum, 1924 – ? 4. Lahore, 1929 – Jawaharlal Nehru Who presided over the Belgaum Session of 1924?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi. The 39th session of INC at Belgaum was held on December 26, 1924. INC Sessions: Bombay, 1885 (W.C. Banerjee) - First session; Madras, 1887 (Badruddin Tayabji) - First Muslim President; Allahabad, 1888 (George Yule) - First English President; Lahore, 1929 (Jawaharlal Nehru); Haripura, 1938 (Subhas Chandra Bose) - Bose’s first term as President.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: Where was the 1912 session of the India National Congress held in Bihar?
questions.explanation: Bankipore. The 27th session of the Indian National Congress in 1912 was presided over by Raghunath Narasinha Mudholkar. In December 1922, the session was held in Gaya under Chittaranjan Das, while the 53rd session took place in 1940 at Ramgarh, near Ranchi, led by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: Who amongst the following became the president of the second session of the Indian National Congress held in Calcutta in December 1886 ?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Nauroji. The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay in December 1885 with seventy-two delegates. W.C. Banerjee served as its first president, while A.O. Hume took office as the General Secretary. Dadabhai Naoroji also presided over the 9th session in 1893 (Lahore), and the 22nd session in 1906 (Calcutta).

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: The Indian National Congress formally took up the Swadeshi call in its Benaras session of 1905 under the presidency of _________.
questions.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale. INC Sessions and its President : First Session (Bombay in 1885) - W.C. Bannerjee, Second Session (Calcutta in 1886) - Dadabhai Naoroji, 1919 (Amritsar) and 1928 (Calcutta) - Motilal Nehru, 1929 (Lahore) - Jawaharlal Nehru, 1934 (Bombay) - Rajendra Prasad.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: The Quit India Resolution was ratified in the_________ session of Indian National Congress to launch the movement.
questions.explanation: Bombay session. This session took place at the Gowalia Tank Maidan (August Kranti Maidan), on August 8, 1942, where Mahatma Gandhi gave his famous "Do or Die" speech. The resolution was moved by Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Indian National Congress: 1. The resolution of Purna Swaraj was passed at the Lahore Session of 1929 presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru. 2. The Karachi Session of 1931 adopted the resolution of Purna Swaraj. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. On 19 December 1929, the Indian National Congress passed the historic ‘Poorna Swaraj’ (total independence) resolution at its Lahore session, with Jawaharlal Nehru elected as its President. A public declaration was made on 26 January 1930, a day the Congress urged Indians to celebrate as ‘Independence Day.’

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: __________ was elected as the president of the third session of Indian National Congress.
questions.explanation: Badruddin Tyabji. Wyomesh Chandra Banerjee was the first president, presiding over the inaugural session in 1885, while Annie Besant became the first woman to hold the position in 1917.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: All India Kisan Sabha was founded in 1936 at Indian National Congress (INC) ________ Session as All India Kisan Congress.
questions.explanation: Lucknow. Swami Sahajananda Saraswati, who founded the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha in 1929, also led the formation of the All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS) during the Indian National Congress' Lucknow Session in 1936. The AIKS, also known as the Akhil Bharatiya Kisan Sabha.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: Indian National Congress celebrated the first Independence Day in Colonial India on _____________ .
questions.explanation: 26 January 1930. The Indian National Congress passed 'Complete Swaraj' in its Lahore session on 19 December 1929. The president of this session was Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: Who led the Indian National Congress at its first annual session?
questions.explanation: WC Banerjee. Important Congress sessions: First Session - held at Bombay in 1885. Second Session - held at Calcutta in 1886, President - Dadabhai Naoroji. Third Session - held at Madras in 1887, President - Syed Badruddin Tyabji (first muslim President). Fourth Session - held at Allahabad in 1888, President - George Yule (first English President). 1896 session (Calcutta) President - Rahimtullah Sayani, National Song ‘Vande Mataram’ sung for the first time by Rabindranath Tagore.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Indian National Congress: 1. Annie Besant was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress, presiding over its 1917 Calcutta Session. 2. Sarojini Naidu was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Annie Besant : First woman who presided over the Calcutta session (1917) of Indian National Congress. Sarojini Naidu - First Indian women president of Indian national congress (1925, Kanpur session) and the first woman Governor of the United Provinces in 1947.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: Which flag of the Indian National Congress was adopted in 1931?

options.a: A two colour flag with charkha made by cloth
options.b: A tricolour flag made by Khadi with a Charkha symbol
options.c: One colour flag with charkha symbol
options.d: A blue colour flag made by cloth

questions.answer_text: A tricolour flag made by Khadi with a Charkha symbol
questions.explanation: Ad - Hoc Flag Committee : Formed in 1947 under Rajendra Prasad. Pingali Venkayya - Designer of National Flag of India (1921). The national flag was adopted on July 22, 1947. Ratio of the length to the breadth of the Indian Flag - 3:2. The national flag of India was first hoisted on 7th August, 1906 in Kolkata at the Parsee Bagan Square (Green Park). The first Indian flag was hoisted on a foreign land by Madame Bhikaji Cama (1907 - Germany).

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: In the 1939 Tripuri Congress Presidential Election, Pattabhi Sitaramayya was defeated by:
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose was elected as President of the Haripura Congress Session in 1938. He resigned as congress president in April 1939. Dr. Rajendra Prasad replaced Subhas Chandra Bose as the new congress president.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Congress–Muslim League understanding: 1. The Congress and the Muslim League reached a historic agreement during the Lucknow Session of 1916. 2. The Lucknow Pact was signed under the presidentship of Bal Gangadhar Tilak. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Lucknow (1916) - President: A.C. Majumdar; Lucknow Pact signed between Congress (Bal Gangadhar Tilak) and Muslim League (Muhammad Ali Jinnah) to build political consensus; Unity between two factions - Moderates and Extremists of Congress.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: Which among the following sessions of Indian National Congress was the first session to be presided by a lady ?
questions.explanation: Calcutta - (Annie Besant, 1917).

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Indian National Congress sessions: 1. In the Madras session of 1927, the Indian National Congress set up an All Parties Conference to draft a Constitution for India. 2. In the Gaya session of 1922, C. R. Das presided and the Swaraj Party was formed after breaking away from the Congress. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Indian National Congress (INC) session 1927 (Madras): President - M A Ansari. INC session 1915 (Bombay): President - Satyendra Prasanna Sinha. Importance - Constitution of the Congress was altered to admit the delegates from the extremist section. INC session 1922 (Gaya): President - C R Das. Importance - CR Das and other leaders broke away from INC, Formation of Swaraj Party. INC session 1932 (Delhi): President - Amrit Ranchhorddas Seth.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: The split in Indian National Congress occurred in ________ .
questions.explanation: 1907. The Surat Split was the splitting of Indian National Congress into two groups - Moderates and Radicals.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: The Indian National Congress was established when 72 delegates from all over the country met at Bombay in December _______.
questions.explanation: 1885. Founder: Allan Octavian Hume. First President: W.C. Bannerjee. First meeting - Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College (Bombay). Prominent delegates included Dadabhai Naoroji, Surendranath Banerjee, Badruddin Tyabji, Pherozeshah Mehta, W. C. Bonnerjee, S. Ramaswami Mudaliar, S. Subramania Iyer, and Romesh Chunder Dutt.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: Who among the following was the President of the Indian National Congress during the 1915 session?
questions.explanation: Satyendra Prasanna Sinha. 1895 - Surendranath Banerjee, 1909 - Madan Mohan Malaviya, 1916 - Ambica Charan Mazumdar.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: How many delegates participated in the second session of Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: 434, Held (December 27-30, 1886, Calcutta), President (Shri Dadabhai Naoroji), Congress decided to set up Provincial Congress Committees across the country.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: In which of the following sessions of the Indian National Congress did George Yule become the President in 1888?
questions.explanation: Allahabad.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: In which of the following years did the resolution at the Karachi Session of the Indian National Congress dwell on how Independent India’s Constitution should look?
questions.explanation: 1931. In 1928, Motilal Nehru and other Congress leaders drafted a constitution for India.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: Assertion (A): In September 1923, Maulana Abul Kalam Azad presided over the special session of the Indian National Congress. Reason (R): He became the youngest man to be elected as the President of the Congress at the age of 35.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was also a noted writer, poet and journalist. He was a prominent political leader and was elected as Congress President in 1923 and 1940.

questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Indian National Congress and Its Sessions
questions.question: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress when India won its freedom in the year 1947 ?
questions.explanation: J. B. Kripalani (Acharya Kriplani) was the president of the Indian National Congress during the transfer of power. He was the husband of Sucheta Kripalani, who was the first woman chief minister (Uttar Pradesh).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the All-India Muslim League: 1. The All-India Muslim League was founded in Dhaka in 1906 during the tenure of Lord Minto II. 2. The government accepted the League’s demand for separate electorates for Muslims in 1916. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. The All-India Muslim League was formed during the tenure of Lord Minto II, who served as the Viceroy of India from 1905 to 1910. The League was founded in Dhaka, British India (Bangladesh), in 1906 and supported the partition of Bengal. It sought separate electorates for Muslims, a demand that was conceded by the government in 1909.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Lucknow Pact was signed in ____________ by Congress and the Muslim League to work in alliance for representative government.
questions.explanation: 1916. INC session Lucknow (1916) - President: A.C. Majumdar. Lucknow Pact was signed between Congress (Bal Gangadhar Tilak) and Muslim League (Muhammad Ali Jinnah) to build political consensus.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In __________ the Muslim League had moved a resolution demanding “Independent States” for Muslims in the north - western and eastern areas of the country
questions.explanation: 1940. All-India Muslim League established in Dhaka in 1906. Founder: Nawab Khwaja Salimullah. First Honorary President: Aga Khan III. Headquarters: Lucknow. 1st Session: Karachi (1907).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Muslim League observed ______ as ‘Direct Action Day’.
questions.explanation: 16 August 1946. Muhammad Ali Jinnah declared 16 August as 'Direct Action Day' and called for Muslims all over the country to 'suspend all business'. Direct Action Day, also known as the 1946 Calcutta Killings.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): Aurobindo Ghose was the first principal of the Bengal National College established in 1906. Reason (R): The Bengal National College was founded by the Indian National Congress during its Surat session of 1907.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false. Aurobindo Ghose was an Indian philosopher, yogi, poet, and nationalist. He also worked as a journalist, editing newspapers such as Bande Mataram. The Alipore Bomb Case, also known as the Muraripukur Conspiracy or Manicktolla Bomb Conspiracy, was a significant criminal trial in India in 1908, involving several Indian nationalists.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: When was the All Bengal Students Conference held in the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions.explanation: 1928. All Bengal Students Conference - It was organized in response to the expulsion of students from Kolkata colleges for "unruly conduct" and the subsequent student protests. The conference led to the formation of the All-Bengal Students Association to unite and organize students across the region.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In 1927, where was the conference against colonial oppression and imperialism, in which Jawaharlal Nehru participated on behalf of Indian National Congress, held?
questions.explanation: Brussels. Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru became General Secretary of the All India Congress Committee in 1923. In 1926, he toured several countries, including Belgium, where he attended the Congress of Oppressed Nationalities in 1927. He also participated in the 10th anniversary of the October Revolution in Moscow. At the 1927 Madras Congress, Nehru advocated for full independence.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Women’s Indian Association (WIA): 1. The Women’s Indian Association was founded in 1917 at Adyar, Chennai by Annie Besant. 2. It was the first women’s organization in India to create an awakening among women and prepare them for public service. Which of the above statements is/are true?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2 are true. Women’s Indian Association, a heritage welfare organization of the women by the women for the women. It was formed on 8th May 1917 at Adyar, Chennai by Annie Besent. It was the first organization to create an overall awakening among women and to train them to shoulder their responsibility in public services.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following national leaders of India inaugurated the first Akhil Bhartiya Kalidas Samman Samaroh held in Ujjain in 1958?
questions.explanation: Rajendra Prasad. The Akhil Bharatiya Kalidas Samaroh is an annual cultural festival held in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, since 1958, celebrating the works of poet Kalidasa.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): Siraj-ud-Daulah became the Nawab of Bengal after the death of Alivardi Khan in 1756. Reason (R): His accession was peaceful and faced no opposition from the British East India Company.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false. Following Alivardi Khan's death in 1756, Sirajuddaulah became Nawab of Bengal but faced conflict with the British, who aimed to install a puppet ruler.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: On which of the following dates did the British Empire transfer its powers to the Constituent Assembly in India?
questions.explanation: 15th August. India gained independence from British rule on August 15, 1947, ending nearly two centuries of colonial control. The transfer of power also led to the partition, creating India and Pakistan.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following has authored the play ‘Nil Darpan’ ?
questions.explanation: Dinabandhu Mitra. Nil Darpan is a Bengali-language play written in 1858-59 by Dinabandhu Mitra, depicting the oppression of indigo farmers by British planters in Bengal. His other works include ‘Nabin Tapasvini’, ‘Biye Pagla Budo’, ‘Sadhabar Ekadashi’, and ‘Kamale Kamini’. Other authors and their works : Sarojini Naidu - ‘The Golden Threshold’, ‘The Bird of Time’. Chittaranjan Das - ‘India for Indians’, ‘Freedom Through Disobedience’.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters of India is the author of the book, 'The Indian Struggle' ?
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose. His Books : An Indian Pilgrim, Jaruri Kichu Lekha, Famous Speeches and Letters of Subhas Chandra Bose.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following books is INCORRECTLY paired with its respective author?

options.c: The Discovery of India – Subhash Chandra Bose
options.d: Why I am an Atheist – Bhagat Singh

questions.answer_text: The Discovery of India – Subhash Chandra Bose
questions.explanation: ‘’The Discovery of India’’ is a book by Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the following institutes with their respective founders of British India. Institutes Their respective founders a. Asiatic Society of Bengal i. Warren Hastings b. Sanskrit College of Benaras ii. Lord Wellesley c. Fort William College iii. Jonathan Duncan d. Calcutta Madrasa iv. Sir William Jones
questions.explanation: A-iv, B-iii, C-ii, D-i.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Khurda Uprising of 1817: 1. The Khurda Revolt of 1817, also called the Paika Rebellion, took place in Odisha. 2. It was led by Bakshi Jagabandhu against the British East India Company. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. The Khurda Revolt of 1817 was an armed uprising against the British, sparked by the rapid and disruptive changes introduced by the East India Company, which agitated the local population. This revolt also impacted other districts of Odisha, such as Cuttack. It is also known as the Paika Rebellion or Paika Bidroha, and it was led by Bakshi Jagabandhu.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Where was the Hindu College established in the year 1791?
questions.explanation: Benaras. The Hindu College was founded by Jonathan Duncan, a British officer, and Raja Rameshwar Singh, the Maharaja of Banaras. The college was originally known as the Sanskrit College, and it was dedicated to the study of Sanskrit language and literature. In 1958, the Sanskrit College became a university and was renamed Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1974. Raja Ram Mohan Roy established the Hindu College in Calcutta in 1817, which is now known as Presidency University, Kolkata.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): B. R. Ambedkar founded the Independent Labour Party in 1936. Reason (R): He later became the first Law Minister of Independent India and the chief architect of the Indian Constitution.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: BR Ambedkar was an Indian jurist and social reformer who served as the first Minister of Law and Justice and was the chief architect of the Constitution of India. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1990. Organizations and Founders: Swatantra Shramik Party (B.R. Ambedkar), Swarajya Party (Motilal Nehru and Chittaranjan Das), Muslim League (Agha Khan & Salimullah), Indian National Congress (A.O.Hume).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: When was the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) established?
questions.explanation: 1920. All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) was formed in Bombay. The AITUC was a broad-based organisation involving diverse ideologies. The main ideological groups were the communists led by S.A. Dange and M.N. Roy, the moderates led by M. Joshi and V.V. Giri and the nationalists which involved people like Lala Lajpat Rai and Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who founded the Theosophical Society in New York in 1875?

options.a: Naoroji Furdunji and Satyendra Nath Bose
options.b: Baba Dayal Das and Madan Lal
options.d: Madame HP Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott

questions.answer_text: Madame HP Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott
questions.explanation: Madame HP Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott. The Theosophical Society, emphasized the study of ancient Hindu, Buddhist, and Zoroastrian philosophies. It advocated for universal brotherhood based on principles from the Upanishads and Vedas. Annie Besant joined the society in 1889 and first came to India on 16 November 1893. Its headquarters in India was established in Adyar, Madras (now Chennai). Ramabai Ranade and G. K. Devadhar were both founders of the Poona Seva Sadan.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: What gave a major impetus to the cotton textile industry in India after Independence?

options.b: Export of raw cotton to England

questions.explanation: Swadeshi movement. The Swadeshi movement, led by Gandhiji, aimed to promote self-sufficiency by boycotting British goods and encouraging Indian-made products. India's first cotton mill, the Bombay Spinning and Weaving Company, was established in Mumbai on July 7, 1854. The world’s first cotton mill, the Upper Priory Cotton Mill, was founded by Lewis Paul and John Wyatt in Birmingham, England, in 1741.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Jyotirao Phule: 1. He wrote Gulamgiri in 1873, which criticized the caste system. 2. He founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in the same year to promote social equality. 3. Gulamgiri was originally written in Hindi and later translated into Marathi. 4. Jyotirao Phule, along with his wife Savitribai Phule, worked for women’s education in Poona. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2 and 4 only. Gulamgiri (Marathi Language), also known as Slavery, summarizes the sufferings of lower-caste people and is written in Marathi. Phule formed the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873. He, together with his wife Savitribai Phule, opened a girls' school in Poona.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In his ‘Drain of Wealth’ argument, who among the following stated that Britain was completely draining India?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji - He was known as the "Grand Old Man of India”. He introduced thе 'drain thеory' in his rеnownеd book "Povеrty and thе Un-British Rulе in India”.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who is the author of the Indian national anthem?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore. He wrote the Indian national anthem, "Jana Gana Mana" in Bengali in 1911, and it was officially adopted as the national anthem of India on January 24, 1950.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Match the following Commissions/Agreements with their outcomes: List I (Commissions/Agree ments) List II (Outcomes) A. Radcliffe Boundary Commission 1. Creation of IMF & World Bank B. Gandhi-Irwin Pact 2. Agreement between Mahatma Gandhi and Lord Irwin C. Hilton Young Commission 3. Recommended establishment of the Reserve Bank of India D. Bretton Woods Conference 4. Drew boundary line between India and Pakistan
questions.explanation: A–4, B–2, C–3, D–1. The "Radcliffe Line" became the border between India and Pakistan the partition of India on 17 August 1947. The Border Commission headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe. Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931 - 32) was an agreement between Mahatma Gandhi and Lord Irwin. The Hilton Young Commission (1926) recommended the establishment of the 'Reserve Bank of India'. The Bretton Woods Committee (BWC in 1944) created two organizations - the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which British colonel is remembered as the Butcher of Amritsar for his role in the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in 1919 ?
questions.explanation: Reginald Dyer. The Jallianwala Bagh massacre (Amritsar massacre) took place on April 13, 1919 (spring festival of Baisakhi) in Punjab. It happened under the rule of Lt. Governor of Punjab, Michael O’Dwyer, and viceroy of India, Lord Chelmsford. People gathered there to protest against the Rowlatt Act and arrests of pro-Indian independence leaders Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satya Pal.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Vasco da Gama, who discovered the sea route from Europe to India, belonged to which nation?
questions.explanation: Portugal. Vasco da Gama arrived in India at Calicut (Kozhikode) in 1498 AD during the reign of the Zamorin, a Hindu ruler. This event marked the discovery of the sea route from Europe to India. He reached India by sea via the "Cape of Good Hope". Francisco de Almeida was appointed as the first Portuguese governor in India. His policy is known for implementing the "Policy of Blue Water," which aimed to establish Portuguese dominance in maritime trade.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Tattvabodhini Patrika promoted the study of India’s past in which language?
questions.explanation: Bengali. Tattvabodhini Patrika was a Bengali monthly that started publishing from Calcutta (now Kolkata) in 1843 as a mouthpiece of Debendranath Tagore's Tattvabodhini Sabha.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following stated in 1902, India was not ruled for its benefit, but rather for the benefit of its conquerors?
questions.explanation: Annie Besant first came to India on 16 November 1893. She joined the Theosophical Society in May 1889 and founded a weekly newspaper, Commonweal, in January 1914 for her political work. Other personalities and their quotes: Bal Gangadhar Tilak - Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it. Lala Lajpat Rai - The shots that hit me are the last nails to the coffin of British rule in India.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Sanskrit College at Benaras was founded by ________.
questions.explanation: Jonathan Duncan. The Sanskrit College at Varanasi was established in 1791. The Hindu College (now Presidency University) in Kolkata was founded in 1817.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): India Gate, also known as the All-India War Memorial, was designed by Edwin Lutyens. Reason (R): The foundation stone of India Gate was laid by Lord Mountbatten in 1947.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false. Other buildings designed by him: Rashtrapati Bhavan, India Gate, The Cenotaph Whitehall (London). The Old Parliament of India was also designed by Herbert Baker and Lutyens. The foundation stone of India Gate was laid by His Royal Highness, the Duke of Connaught in 1921.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the political guru of Subhash Chandra Bose?
questions.explanation: Chittaranjan Das (Deshbandhu).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The name of the Brahmin priest who later came to be known as Ramakrishna Paramahansa is:
questions.explanation: Gadadhar Chattopadhyay.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: When did the Drafting Committee publish the first draft of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: February 1948. Drafting Committee: Formation – 29 August 1947, Chairman – Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, Total Members – 7.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The All India Forward Bloc was founded by_______in 1939 after resigning from the Congress Presidentship
questions.explanation: Subhash Chandra Bose. All India Forward Bloc was a Political Party formed on May 3, 1939 in Makur Unnao, Uttar Pradesh. Its formation was announced in Calcutta.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Assertion (A): Satyendra Nath Tagore was the first Indian to qualify for the Covenanted Civil Service in 1863. Reason (R): The Indian Services Act, 1861, passed during Lord Curzon’s viceroyalty, reserved certain posts for covenanted civil servants.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false. Indian Services Act, 1861 reserved certain positions for covenanted civil servants. It was enacted in 1861 during Lord Canning's Viceroyalty. Charles Cornwallis is known as ‘the father of Civil services in India’.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Hindu Mahasabha was founded as a response to muslim fundamentalism in which year?
questions.explanation: 1915. Hindu Mahasabha (Founder - Madan Mohan Malaviya) First All India Hindu Mahasabha Conference - Haridwar (1915). In 1930, it emerged as a distinct party under the leadership of Vinayak Damodar Savarkar. Prominent Leaders - Lala Lajpat Rai, Navin Chandra Rai, Radha Mohan Das Agarwal, Chandroji Angre, Mahant Avaidyanath.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following said that "English education has enslaved us" ?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi. Muhammad Iqbal - He wrote the famous song 'Saare jahan se achha', also known for giving birth to the 'idea of Pakistan'. Muhammad Ali Jinnah was a barrister, politician and the founder of Pakistan. Raja Ram Mohan Roy was a religious and social reformer, known as the 'Father of Modern India' or 'Father of the Bengal Renaissance'.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In 1921-22, farmers of the Malabar seacoast of Kerala undertook a great uprising, which is known as the __ .
questions.explanation: Moplah uprising - Led by Variyamkunnath Kunjahammed Haji, against the British and the Hindu landlords; Wagon tragedy - Moplah prisoners died of suffocation during transportation in a closed freight wagon.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following social reformers of British India is known as Lokhitwadi ?
questions.explanation: Gopal Hari Deshmukh. Balshastri Jambhekar (Father of Marathi Journalism) - He started the very first newspaper, ‘Darpan’, and revolutionized the journalism system in Maharashtra.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following founded the Asiatic Society in 1784 in Calcutta?
questions.explanation: William Jones. Asiatic Society - It was started with the goal of promoting oriental studies. Jonathan Duncan - He started Sanskrit College (1791) at Varanasi to study Hindu Law and Philosophy. He was the Governor of Bombay.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Social Service League was founded in Bombay by:
questions.explanation: Narayan Malhar Joshi - He was an Indian trade union leader, Founded social service league (1911). He started the All India Trade Union Congress (1920). He was the general secretary of AITUC. Manabendra Nath Roy - leader of India’s communists until the independence of India in 1947.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. At the time of India’s Independence in 1947, the literacy rate was about 20 percent. 2. The first census of Independent India was conducted in 1951. 3. Conduct of census in India is a Union subject under Article 246 of the Constitution. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: 2 and 3 only. The population census, a Union subject under Article 246 of the Indian Constitution, conducted its first census of Independent India in 1951, listed as serial number 69 in the seventh schedule. This census revealed the population of the country to be 36, 10, 88, 090.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: What was the title given to the late Sarojini Naidu?
questions.explanation: Nightingale of India (Bharat Kokila). This title was given to Sarojini Naidu by Mahatma Gandhi. Notable Works - The Golden Threshold, The Broken Wing.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Deccan Riots of 1875 took place in ______ .
questions.explanation: Maharashtra. Deccan Riots: Began at - Supa village (Poona) in 1875. The farmers’ main motive was to destroy the account books of the moneylenders and they also socially boycotted the moneylenders. The movement was supported by the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (co-founded by M G Ranade).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Editor of a Marathi newspaper "Kesari” was .
questions.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Bengal in 1770: 1. In 1770, Bengal and Bihar faced a massive earthquake that destroyed most villages. 2. The British government spent ₹50,000 on rebuilding houses for the affected population. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Neither 1 nor 2. 1770 Bengal Famine - It affected Bengal and Bihar. Relief - Attempts to prevent export and hoard or monopolize grain; 15,000 was spent on the import of food grains.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Tribal leader Birsa was associated with which tribe?
questions.explanation: Munda. Birsa Munda was a tribal reformer, religious leader, and freedom fighter. 15 November - Birsa Munda’s birth anniversary (Jharkhand carved out of Bihar on 15th November 2000).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Dr. B.R Ambedkar was associated with which of the following communities?
questions.explanation: Mahar. It is listed as the Scheduled Caste in India. Dr. B.R Ambedkar - Architect of Indian

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which freedom fighter of British India is widely regarded as the "father of the two-nation theory" ?
questions.explanation: Syed Ahmed Khan was the founder of Aligarh Muslim University and a forward looking Islamist reformer. Mohammed Ali Jinnah - First governor - general (1947–48) of Pakistan.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was a Roman Catholic missionary who worked in Bengal for the majority of his/her life?
questions.explanation: Mother Teresa (from Macedonia) - Nobel Peace Prize (1979), founded the Missionaries of Charity. Saint Bernadette - French saint whose visions led to the founding of the Marian shrine of Lourdes.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: When did Indigo revolt, a peasant movement, start in India?
questions.explanation: 1859 (March). The Indigo Rebellion (Neel Bidroh) started in Bengal and was a revolt by the farmers against British planters who had forced them to grow indigo under terms that were greatly unfavorable to the farmers.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Paris Indian Society was an Indian nationalist organisation founded in ______.
questions.explanation: 1905 at Paris under the patronage of Madam Bhikaji Cama, Munchershah Burjorji Godrej and S. R. Rana. It was a branch of the Indian Home Rule Society which was established in London in 1905. Bhikaji Cama's important publication is 'Vande Mataram' (1909).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Shyamji Krishna Verma and India House: 1. India House in London was established by Shyamji Krishna Verma in 1909. 2. He never founded the Indian Home Rule Society. 3. He became the first President of the Bombay Arya Samaj. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 3 only. Shyamji Krishna Verma founded the Indian Home Rule Society and The Indian Sociologist (Journal) in London. He became the first President of Bombay Arya Samaj.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Identify the freedom fighter who, as a child, hated going to school and found it suffocating and oppressive.
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore. Rabindranath Tagore: Santiniketan (1901), Nobel Prize in Literature (1913, Gitanjali), composed Jana Gana Mana (India’s National Anthem) and Amar Shonar Bangla (Bangladesh’s National Anthem). Other Works: Manasi (1890) [The Ideal One], Sonar Tari (1894) [The Golden Boat], Gitimalya (1914) [Wreath of Songs], and Balaka (1916) [The Flight of Cranes].

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The claim for ‘swarajya’ or self-government within the British Empire, on the model of self-governing colonies like Australia and Canada, was put forward from the Congress platform in 1905 by:
questions.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale (Diamond of India) was Political Guru of Gandhi, Congress President (1905), established Servants of India Society in 1905, English Newspaper (The Hitavada), founded The Ranade Institute of Economics (1905), ‘Dharmatma Gokhale’ (Writer - Mahatma Gandhi).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Bhoodan Yojana (Land Gift) movement: 1. The Bhoodan Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1931. 2. It was first started at Sevagram in Maharashtra. 3. The movement aimed to provide free education to rural children. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: None of the above. Acharya Vinoba Bhave in 1951, the Bhoodan Movement (first started in Andhra Pradesh) was initiated at Pochampally village (Telangana). The Bhoodan movement attempted to persuade wealthy landowners to voluntarily give a percentage of their land to landless people.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The first President of the All India Trade Union Congress was _________.
questions.explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai. All India Trade Union Congress, AITUC (created on October 31, 1920 in Bombay) is the first Central Trade Union of India and the second largest trade union federation in India after the Indian National Trade union Congress. In India, Trade Unions in India are registered under the Trade Union Act (1926).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Dadabhai Naoroji: 1. He was the first Indian to become the Governor-General of India. 2. He was the first Indian to be selected to the British House of Commons on a Liberal Party ticket. 3. He was the founder of the Arya Samaj movement. 4. He was the first Indian to be appointed as the Vice-President of the Council of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 2 only. Dadabhai Naoroji was known as India Gladstone. The first attempt to calculate National Income of India was made by him. He was the first Asian (Indian) member of the British Parliament. He coined the name “Indian National Congress” (INC).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following Indian freedom fighters was fondly called Gandhi Buri (Old Lady Gandhi) for her dedication towards Gandhian principles?
questions.explanation: Matangini Hazra. Matangini Hazra was an Indian revolutionary and social activist who participated in the Indian independence movement.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Avadh Kisan Sabha was set up in the year ______.
questions.explanation: 1920. Oudh Kisan Sabha (Oudh Farmers Association) was an association formed by Baba Ram Chandra. He was a trade unionist who organized the farmers of Oudh and led the first protest against the landlords.

questions.subject: History
