Other related articles include: Article 90 - Specifies the conditions for the vacation, resignation, and removal of the Deputy Chairman of the Council of States. Article 91- Grants the Deputy Chairman or another designated person the power to perform the duties of the Chairman in their absence.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding provisions of the Indian Constitution: 1. Article 177 provides the Advocate-General of a state the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of the State Legislature, though without a right to vote. 2. Article 183 deals with the resignation, vacation, and removal of the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘The Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the state’ ?
questions.explanation: Article 164(2). Article 164(1) - The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor, while other Ministers are appointed on the Chief Minister's advice, and they hold office at the Governor's pleasure. Article 164(3) - Before assuming office, a Minister must take the oaths of office and secrecy administered by the Governor, as specified in the Third Schedule. Article 164(4) - A Minister who is not a member of the State Legislature for six consecutive months will cease to hold office at the end of that period.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding amendment of the Indian Constitution: i. Article 368 in Part XX of the Constitution specifies the procedure for amending the Constitution. ii. In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court ruled that Parliament cannot amend those provisions which form the ‘basic structure’ of the Constitution. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Both i and ii.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions about the salaries and allowances of members of the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council of a state?
questions.explanation: Article 195. Important Articles in Part VI (The States): Article 168 - Constitution of Legislatures in States. Article 169 - Abolition or creation of Legislative Councils in States. Article 170 - Composition of the Legislative Assemblies. Article 194 - Powers, privileges, etc., of the Houses of Legislatures and of the members and committees thereof. Article 199 - Definition of “Money Bills”.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that a person may be appointed as the Governor of two or more states?
questions.explanation: Article 153. The Seventh Amendment Act, 1956, amended Article 153 to allow a governor to oversee two or more states. Other important articles : Article 150 - Form of Accounts of The Union and of The States. Article 151 - The audit reports of the Union and State by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. Article 152 - States about the Definition of state.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution states that “There shall be a High Court for each state” ?
questions.explanation: Article 214. Other important Articles: Article 215 - Every High Court shall be a court of record and shall have all the powers of such a court including the power to punish for contempt of itself. Article 217 - Appointment and conditions of the office of a Judge of a High Court. Article 245 - Parliament may make laws for the whole or any part of the territory of India. Article 275 - provides for the grants from the Union to certain States.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘All the executive action of the Government of a state shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the Governor’ ?
questions.explanation: Article 166(1). Other important Articles: Article 163(1) - There shall be a Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at the head to aid and advise the Governor in the exercise of his functions. Article 164(1) - The Chief Minister shall be appointed by the Governor and the other Ministers shall be appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister. Article 165(1) - The Governor of each State shall appoint a person who is qualified to be appointed a Judge of a High Court to be Advocate-General for the State.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding provisions of the Indian Constitution: 1. Article 173 mentions the qualifications for membership of the State Legislature. 2. A person must be at least 25 years old for the Legislative Assembly and 30 years old for the Legislative Council. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. The person must be at least 25 years old for a seat in the Legislative Assembly and at least 30 years old for a seat in the Legislative Council. Other important Articles : Article 171 - The total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State shall not exceed one-third of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that State. Article 179 - Vacation and resignation of, and removal from, the offices of Speaker and Deputy Speaker. Article 180 - Power of the Deputy Speaker to perform the duties of Speaker.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: What Article of the Indian Constitution provides that the State Governor has the authority to reserve a bill for the consideration of the President.
questions.explanation: Article 200. The Governor may also return the Bill with a message requesting reconsideration by the House or Houses. Article 201 - It states that when a Bill is reserved for the consideration of the President, the President may assent to or withhold assent from the Bill. Article 190 - A person cannot be a member of both houses of a state legislature. Article 181 - The Speaker or the Deputy Speaker not to preside while a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration. Article 267 - Contingency Fund.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding provisions of the Indian Constitution: 1. Article 112 provides for the annual financial statement of the Government of India, to be laid before each House of Parliament every year. 2. Article 120 defines “Money Bills” while Article 116 deals with the annual financial statement. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Article 112 - The President shall cause, in respect of each financial year, to be laid before each House of Parliament a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for that year, which is in this Part referred to as "the annual financial Statement". Other important Articles: Article 110 - Definition of "Money Bills". Article 116 - Votes on account, votes of credit and exceptional grants. Article 120 - Language to be used in Parliament.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: ________ of the Indian Constitution sets qualifications for being a member of Lok Sabha.
questions.explanation: Article 84 outlines the qualifications for being a member of the Lok Sabha. A person must: Be an Indian citizen; Take an oath or affirmation before an authorized person appointed by the Election Commission; Be at least 25 years old; Meet any other qualifications set by the Parliament of India. Article 74 : Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President. Article 64 : The Vice-President to be ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha). Article 76 : It is to the appointment and responsibilities of the Attorney-General for India.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution are related to the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
questions.explanation: Article 148-151. The CAG handles the audit of the accounts of the Union and State governments. Article 148: Establishes the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. Article 149: Duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General. Article 150: Form of accounts of the Union and of the States. Article 151: Mandates the presentation of audit reports by the Comptroller and Auditor General to the President of India, which are then laid before Parliament.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP): 1. Article 37 makes it clear that the Directive Principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply them in making laws. 2. Directive Principles of State Policy in Part IV of the Constitution were directly borrowed from the U.S. Constitution. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) in Part IV of the Indian Constitution are based on the Irish Constitution, which in turn was based on the Spanish Constitution.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution: 1. Medical education, protection of wildlife, and population control are included in the Concurrent List. 2. Artificial habitats are also included in the Concurrent List. Which of the above statements is/are incorrect?
questions.explanation: 2 only. The Parliament and state legislatures can both make laws on matters listed under the Concurrent List. As of now, the list includes 52 subjects (originally 47). Some Subjects in Concurrent list: Bankruptcy and insolvency, Forests, Factories, Boilers, Electricity, Newspapers, books and printing presses.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: In respect of Arunachal Pradesh, the Governor has special responsibility under ________ of the Constitution of India with respect to law and order and in discharge of his functions in relation thereto.
questions.explanation: Article 371 H. Under Article 359, during a national emergency, the President can suspend the right to move courts for Fundamental Rights enforcement, except for Articles 20 and 21. Article 380, which once addressed the President of India, was omitted by the Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act of 1976. Article 361 provides protection to the President, Governors, and Rajpramukhs from being held accountable in courts for actions taken while performing their duties.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Schedules of the Indian Constitution: i. The Third Schedule contains the forms of oaths and affirmations for constitutional offices, including Judges of the Supreme Court. ii. The Second Schedule contains provisions regarding the emoluments, allowances, and privileges of certain constitutional authorities. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both i and ii. The Third Schedule of the Indian Constitution outlines the forms of oaths and affirmations for various constitutional offices : President, Vice-President, Union and State Ministers, Parliament and state legislature candidates, Judges, Comptroller and Auditor General. First Schedule : Names of the States and Union Territories, Second Schedule : Provisions for the emoluments, allowances, privileges of certain constitutional authorities, and Fourth Schedule : Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha and union territories.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘In the performance of his/her duties, the Attorney - General for India shall have the right of audience in all the courts in the territory of India’ ?
questions.explanation: Article 76(3). Article 76 of the Indian Constitution addresses the Attorney General of India. Under Article 76(1), the President of India appoints the Attorney General. Article 76(2) states that it is the duty of the Attorney General to provide legal advice to the Government of India and perform other legal duties. Article 76(4) specifies that the Attorney General holds office at the pleasure of the President and receives remuneration as determined by the President.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Match the following subject matters with their concerned Articles. a b 1. Superintendence, direction and control of elections to be Vested in an Election commission. (A) Article 329 2. Power of parliament to make provision with respect to election to legislature. (B) Article 324 3. Bar of interference by courts in electoral matters (C) Article 327
questions.explanation: 1-B, 2-C, 3-A. Article 325 - No person to be ineligible for inclusion in, or to claim to be included in a special, electoral roll on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex. Article 328 - Power of Legislature of a State to make provision with respect to elections to such Legislature.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India mentions that “there shall be a Public Service Commission for the Union and a Public Service Commission for each State” ?
questions.explanation: Article 315 (1). Article 315 (2) - Two or more States may agree that there shall be one Public Service Commission for that group of States. Article 315 (3) - Any such law as aforesaid may contain such incidental and consequential provisions as may be necessary or desirable for giving effect to the purposes of the law. Article 315 (4) - UPSC can, if requested by a state government, conduct examinations and interviews to select candidates for state government jobs.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides that the Governor appoints the Chief Minister and later, the Chief Minister recommends the appointment of ministers to the Governor?
questions.explanation: Article 164. Other Appointments by Governor: State Election Commissioner (Article 243 K), Vice-Chancellors of the universities in the state (University Grants Commission (UGC) Regulations, 2018), Advocate General for the State (Article 165) etc. Article 163 - Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor of the State.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament to restrict or abrogate the fundamental rights of the members of the armed forces, paramilitary forces, police forces, intelligence agencies and analogous forces ?
questions.explanation: Article 33. Fundamental rights are included in Part III (Article 12-35) of the Constitution. It is described as the Magna Carta of India. Article 35 - Power to make laws to give effect to certain specified fundamental rights shall vest only in the Parliament and not in the state legislatures.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: As per Article 361 of the Constitution of India, who among the following shall NOT be answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of his/her office?
questions.explanation: Governor. Article 361 - The President, or the Governor or Rajpramukh of a State, shall not be answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of his office or for any act done or purporting to be done by him in the exercise and performance.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding provisions of the Indian Constitution: A. The Tenth Schedule contains provisions for disqualification of legislators on the ground of defection, introduced by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985. B. The Ninth Schedule, added by the First Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951, contains laws that are immune from judicial review. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both A and B.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that all the authorities— civil and judicial— in the territory of India shall act in aid of the Supreme Court ?
questions.explanation: Article 144. Article 142: Enforcement of decrees and orders of the Supreme Court and orders as to discovery, etc. Article 141: The law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Article 149 of the Constitution deals with ___________ .

options.a: the qualifications required for the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
options.b: the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
options.c: the term of office of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
options.d: the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India

questions.answer_text: the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
questions.explanation: Part V (Chapter V) of the Indian Constitution (Articles 148-151) deals with the Comptroller and Auditor-General (CAG). Article 148: This article deals with the appointment, oath, tenure and removal of CAG of India. There are no specific qualifications required to become the CAG of India. The President of India appoints the CAG through a warrant under their hand and seal. The CAG serves a term of 6 years or until the age of 65, whichever comes first.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about Article 129 of the Constitution of India ?

options.a: It provides for the Supreme Court to give advisory opinions to the President.
options.b: It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of original jurisdiction
options.c: It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of record.
options.d: It provides for the Supreme Court to be the highest court of appeal.

questions.answer_text: It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of record.
questions.explanation: Article 143 - Power of the President to consult the Supreme Court. Article 132 - Appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in appeals from High Courts in certain cases. Articles 133 and 134 grant the Supreme Court appellate jurisdiction in civil and criminal matters from High Courts.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Schedules of the Indian Constitution : A. The Constitution of India contains 12 Schedules in total. B. The Eleventh Schedule relates to the Panchayati Raj institutions, while the Twelfth Schedule relates to Municipalities. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both A and B. 12 Schedules in Indian Constitution: First - List of States and UT; Second - Emoluments, allowances, and privileges; Third - Oath and affirmation ; Fourth - Seat allocation of the Rajya Sabha; Fifth - Administration of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes; Sixth - Administration of Tribal Areas in the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram; Seventh - Union list, State list and the concurrent list; Eight - List of recognized languages; Ninth - Land reforms and regulations; Tenth - Anti defection law; Eleventh - Panchayati Raj and Twelfth - Municipalities.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Clause of Article 19 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the 'right to move freely throughout the territory of India' ?
questions.explanation: Clause (d). Article 19 - Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc. Other clauses of Article 19(1): Clause (a) grants the freedom of speech and expression; Clause (b) grants the right to assemble peaceably and without arms; Clause (c) grants the right to form associations, unions, or co-operative societies; Clause (d) grants the right to move freely throughout the territory of India; Clause (e) grants the right to reside and settle in any part of the territory of India; Clause (g) grants the right to practise any profession or to carry on any occupation, trade, or business.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Articles of the Constitution of India deal with the Union and its territory ?
questions.explanation: Articles 1-4. Article 1- Name and territory of the Union; Article 2 - Admission or Establishment of New States; Article 3 - Formation of New States and alteration of areas, Boundaries or Names of existing States; Article 4 : Laws made under articles 2 and 3 to provide for the amendment of the first and the fourth schedules and supplemental, incidental and consequential matters.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: In India which of the following is a Gandhian principle of Directive Principles of State Policy ?

options.d: To provide equal pay for equal work

questions.explanation: To organise village panchayat. Article based on Gandhian principles: 40 - Organise village panchayats. 43 - Living wage, etc., for workers. 43B - To promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control of cooperative societies. 46 - promote educational and economic interests of the weaker sections. 47 - To improve public health. 48 - To prohibit the slaughter of cows, calves and other milch. Other Groups - Socialist Principle - Article (38, 39, 41, 42, 43, 43A, 47). Liberal - Intellectual Principle - Article (44, 45, 48, 48A, 49, 50, 51).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following Articles says that double jeopardy which says that “no person shall be prosecuted or punished for the same offence more than once?
questions.explanation: Article 20 (2). Article 21 - Protection of life and personal liberty. Article 19 (1) - The right to freedom of speech and expression. Article 22 - Protection Against Arrest and Detention in Certain Cases. Article 22(2) - A person who is arrested and detained must be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Under which Article of the Directive Principles of State Policy, a working woman on maternity leave, must receive all maternity benefits from the employer?
questions.explanation: Article 42. Directive Principles of State Policies are non-justiciable rights (which means that they cannot be enforced by a Court of Law). Article 43 - The State shall endeavour to secure all workers a living wage and a decent standard of life. Article 44 - Uniform civil code for the citizens.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: 'The state shall endeavour to secure to all workers a living wage and a decent standard of life'. Which of the following is correct about the given statement in the context of India?

options.a: It is mentioned in the 43rd Article of the Constitution.
options.b: It is mentioned in the 44th Article of Constitution.
options.c: This is a Gandhian principle of Directive Principles of State Policy.
options.d: This is a liberal principle of Directive Principles of State Policy.

questions.answer_text: It is mentioned in the 43rd Article of the Constitution.
questions.explanation: Article 43 (Living wage, etc., for workers). Directives based on Liberal-Intellectual Principles: Article 44, Article 45, Article 48, Article 48A, Article 49, Article 50, Article 51.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Co-operative Societies in the Indian Constitution: A. questions.explanation: Both A and B.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: The government is bound to ensure observance of social welfare and labour laws enacted to secure for workmen a life compatible with human dignity, under ___________ of the Indian Constitution.
questions.explanation: Article 21. Article 15 - Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth. Article 19: Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of Speech, etc. Article 17 - Abolition of Untouchability.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Right to move to the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights: 1. Article 32 of the Indian Constitution provides the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. 2. Article 30 of the Indian Constitution is also related to the Right to move the Supreme Court. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) - The ‘Heart and Soul of the Constitution’ by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. Article 30 - Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Poshan Abhiyaan is a programme to achieve nutritional status of children from 0 to 6 years. Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for raising the nutrition level?
questions.explanation: Article 47 - Duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living and to improve public health comes under Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36-51 under Part-IV).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution has the idea that 'No child below the age of fourteen years shall be employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment?
questions.explanation: Article 24. Article 22 - Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases. Article 19 - Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: KA Najeeb Vs Union of India case deals with violation of rights under_____
questions.explanation: Article 21 (Protection of life and personal liberty). Important Cases related to Article 21: A.K Gopalan vs the State of Madras 1950 : The Supreme court has taken a narrow interpretation of Article 21 in this case. Maneka Gandhi vs. Union of India, 1978: In this case, the SC overruled its judgement of the Gopalan Case by taking a wider interpretation of Article 21.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Constitution of India: A. Provisions of the Union Executive are contained in Part V of the Constitution. B. Provisions of Fundamental Rights are also contained in Part V. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: A only. Other parts of constitution: Part III - Fundamental Rights (Article 12 to 35), Part IV - Directive Principle of State Policy (Article - 36 to 51), Part VI - The States (Article 152 to 237).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Fundamental duties were not placed in Part III of the Indian Constitution because Part III is_________.
questions.explanation: Justiciable. Part III Article (12-35): Fundamental Rights. Fundamental duties (Part IVA Article 51A) added by the 42nd Amendment Act (1976). These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by a court of law.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for a bicameral Parliament of India?
questions.explanation: Article 79 :- Constitution of Parliament - There shall be a Parliament of the Union consisting of the President and two Houses known as the Council of States (Rajya Sabha, Article 80) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha, Article 81). Article 49 - Protection of monuments and places and objects of national importance. Article 59 - Conditions of the President's office.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: As per Article 172 (2)_______of a State shall NOT be subject to dissolution.
questions.explanation: Legislative Council (Saasana Mandali) - It is the upper house in those states of India that have a bicameral state legislature. Six States have a Legislative Council: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Article 323 of the Indian Constitution deals with __________ .

options.d: power to extend functions of Public Services Commissions

questions.explanation: reports of Public Services Commissions. Articles 315 to 323 (Part XIV) of the Constitution of India establish the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (SPSC). The UPSC Chairman is appointed by the President for a term of six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to review its own judgements or orders ?
questions.explanation: Article 137. Article 138 - Enlargement of the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court. Article 135 - Jurisdiction and powers of the Federal Court under existing law to be exercisable by the Supreme Court. Article 136 - Special leave to appeal by the Supreme Court.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding provisions of the Indian Constitution: 1. Article 247 empowers the Parliament to establish additional courts for better administration of laws made by it. 2. Article 248 deals with residuary powers of legislation. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2 are correct.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the removal and suspension of a member of the Public Service Commission?
questions.explanation: Article 317. Part XIV (Articles 315 to 323) - Establishment of UPSC for Union and Public Service Commission for each state. Article 320 - Functions of Public Service Commissions. Article 315 - Public Service Commissions for the Union and for the States.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding provisions of the Indian Constitution : I. Article 317 deals with the removal and suspension of a member of the Public Service Commission. II. Article 320 mentions the functions of Public Service Commissions. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?

options.c: Both I and II are correct

questions.answer_text: Both I and II are correct
questions.explanation: Both I and II are correct. Part XIV (Articles 315 to 323) - Establishment of UPSC for Union and Public Service Commission for each state. Article 320 - Functions of Public Service Commissions. Article 315 - Public Service Commissions for the Union and for the States.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Constitution: I. Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) deals with the organisation, composition and powers of the State Legislature. II. Article 171 specifies the composition of the Legislative Councils in States. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: II only is correct. Part VI Article (152 to 237). Article 168 Constitution of Legislatures in States. Article 169 deals with abolition or creation of Legislative Councils in states. Article 170 - Composition of the Legislative Assemblies. Article 171 - Composition of the legislative Councils. Article 172 - Duration of State Legislatures.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides that there shall be a Legislative Assembly for the National Capital Territory of Delhi?
questions.explanation: Article 239AA. The 69th Amendment Act (1991) - A special status to the Union Territory of Delhi by designing it as the National Capital Territory of Delhi. Brahm Prakash was the first chief minister of Delhi.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which among the following is a subject of Union Lists in the Constitution of India ?
questions.explanation: Extradition.The 7th Schedule of the Indian Constitution consists of three lists: Union List: 100 items (e.g., Defence, Army, International Relations). State List: 61 items (e.g., Local Government, Public Health, Prisons). Concurrent List: 52 items (e.g., Education, Forest, Trade Unions).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Provisions related to the seat of the "Supreme Court of India" is mentioned in which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 130. The Federal Court of India was established on 1 October 1937. After Independence, the Federal Court was replaced as the Supreme Court of India (28 January 1950). Other related Articles : Article 124: Establishment and Constitution of Supreme Court. Article 129: Supreme Court to be a Court of Record. Article 131: Original Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court. Article 132: Appellate Jurisdiction of Supreme Court in appeals from High Court in certain cases.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Part XVI of the Indian constitution deals with ___________ .

options.b: Special provisions related to certain classes
options.d: Special provisions related to municipal corporation

questions.answer_text: Special provisions related to certain classes
questions.explanation: Special provisions related to certain classes (Article 330 to 342A). Article 330 - Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the House of the People. Part XV (Article 324-329): Elections. Part XX (Article 368): Amendment of the Constitution. Part IXA (Article 243P-243ZG): The Municipalities.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian constitution provides for the National commission for Scheduled Castes ?
questions.explanation: Article 338. National commission for Scheduled Castes is a constitutional body.Other Commissions - National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (Article 338A inserted by the 89th Amendment Act 2003) and National Commission for Backward Classes (Article 338B). Article 343 - Official language of the Union. Article 344 - Commission and Committee of Parliament on Official Language. Article 337 - Special provisions in terms of educational grants/subsidies provided to the Anglo-Indian population of India.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the provisions of the Indian Constitution: I. Provisions related to Municipalities are mentioned under Part IXA. II. Provisions related to Municipalities are mentioned under Part XII. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: I only is correct. The Municipalities (Urban Local Governments) is a system of Democratic Decentralisation. It was added through the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992. Part VII - Repealed by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment Act, 1956). Part V - Provisions for the functioning of the Union Government. Part XII - Laws pertaining to Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits for Republic of India.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian constitution mentions that it is duty of the Union government to protect States against external aggression and internal disturbance?
questions.explanation: Article 355. Other Articles - Article 353 - States about the Effect of the proclamation of emergency. Article 356 - States about the Provision in case of failure of constitutional machinery in the state (president rule). Article 358 - It deals with the suspension of fundamental rights guaranteed under Article 19 of the constitution.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (CAG): I. Article 151 of the Constitution deals with CAG audit reports. II. Article 150 of the Constitution deals with CAG audit reports. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: I only is correct. Part V: The Union, Chapter V : Comptroller and Auditor - General (CAG) of India (Article 148 - 151). Article 150: Form of accounts of the Union and of the States. Article 149: Duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General. Article 148: Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

questions.question: Central Bureau of Intelligence and Investigation comes under which list of the seventh schedule of the Indian constitution ?
questions.explanation: Union list (100) - Defence, Army, International Relations, Ports, Railways, Census, Communication, Central Bureau of Investigation etc. State list (61) - Public order, Police, Public health and sanitation, Hospitals and dispensaries, Agriculture, State Public Service Commission, etc. Concurrent list (52) - Education, Forest, Trade unions, population control and family planning, Marriage, Adoption, etc. Seventh schedule under Article 246 of the constitution deals with the division of powers between the union and the states.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Part VII of the Indian Constitution: I. Part VII was related to the States in Part B of the First Schedule. II. Part VII was related to the reservation of Anglo-Indians in Parliament. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: I only is correct. States in part B of the first schedule. Provision relating to property - constitutional right under Part XII, Article 300A (Added by 44th Amendment Act, 1978). The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2019 abolished the reservation of seats for Anglo-Indians in the Parliament and State Legislatures of India in January 2020. The amendment also extended reservations for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes for up to ten years.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: The Indian parliament has power to impose restrictions on trade, commerce and intercourse through which Article of the Indian constitution?

Article 304: Restrictions on trade, commerce and intercourse among States. Article 303: Restrictions on the legislative powers of the Union and of the States with regard to trade and commerce. Article 300A: Persons not to be deprived of property save by authority of law.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding powers of the Governor: I. Article 213 states that the Governor has the power to promulgate ordinances during the recess of the State Legislature. II. Article 214 states that the Governor has the power to promulgate ordinances during the recess of the State Legislature. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: I only is correct. Article 214 mandates that every state in India must have its own High Court. Exceptions – Parliament may establish a common High Court for two or more states and union territories under Article 231. Example: Punjab & Haryana share the same High Court at Chandigarh. Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh share the Guwahati High Court.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution does India mention that business in Parliament shall be transacted in Hindi or English?
questions.explanation: Article 120. Article 121 - Restriction on discussion in Parliament. Article 122 - Courts not to inquire into proceedings of Parliament. Article 119 - Regulation by law of procedure in Parliament in relation to financial business.

questions.question: Which Article of Indian constitution is related with the Special provisions with respect to the State of Sikkim?

Article 371 A - Nagaland (13th Amendment Act, 1962). 371 B - Assam (22nd Amendment Act, 1969). 371 C - Manipur (27th Amendment Act, 1971). 371 D - Andhra Pradesh and Telangana (32nd. Amendment Act, 1973). 371 E - To establish Central University in Andhra Pradesh. 371 G - Mizoram (53rd. Amendment Act, 1986). 371 H - Arunachal Pradesh (55th Amendment Act, 1986). 371 I - Goa.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding appointment of judges in India: I. Article 127 deals with the appointment of ad-hoc judges to the Supreme Court. II. Article 126 deals with the appointment of ad-hoc judges to the Supreme Court. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: I only is correct. Article 126: Appointment of acting Chief Justice of India. Article 128: Attendance of retired judges at sitting of the Supreme Court. Article 125: talks about the financial privileges and allowances that are defined for the judges of the Supreme Court.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the Sessions of the Parliament?
questions.explanation: Article 85 - Sessions of Parliament, prorogation, and dissolution. A session is a period during which a House meets almost every day uninterruptedly to manage the business. Article 90 - Vacation and resignation of (and removal from) the office of Deputy Chairman. Article 101- Vacation of seats in Parliament.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Articles of Parliament in the Indian Constitution: I. Chapter II of Part V (Articles 79–122) deals with the Articles of Parliament. questions.explanation: I only is correct. Part V - The Union of Indian Constitution Chapter II deals with the Articles of Parliament . Chapter I (The Executive; Articles 52 to 78); Chapter III: Legislative powers of the President; Article 123); Chapter IV (The Union Judiciary; Articles 124 - 147). Chapter V (Comptroller and Auditor - General of India (CAG); Articles 148 to 151).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: The Article of the Indian Constitution that deals with all the executive powers of the Governor is ____
questions.explanation: Article 154- Executive power of Governor. Article 150 - Form of accounts of the Union and of the States. Article 157 - Qualifications for appointment as Governor. Article 156 - Term of office of Governor.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC): I. Part XIV of the Indian Constitution provides for the Union Public Service Commission. II. Part X of the Indian Constitution provides for the Union Public Service Commission. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: I only is correct. Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is an independent constitutional body. The provisions regarding the composition of UPSC, the appointment, and removal of its members, and the powers and functions of UPSC are provided in Part XIV of the Indian Constitution under Article 315 to Article 323.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the National Commission for Backward Classes: I. Article 338B(1) states that there shall be a Commission for socially and educationally backward classes, called the National Commission for Backward Classes. II. Article 243S(1) states that there shall be a Commission for socially and educationally backward classes. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: I only is correct. Article 243S(1) - There shall be constituted Wards Committees, consisting of one or more wards, within the territorial area of a Municipality having a population of three lakhs or more.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the official language of the Union: I. Article 343(1) states that Hindi in Devanagari script shall be the official language of the Union. II. Article 343(2) states that Hindi in Devanagari script shall be the official language of the Union. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: I only is correct. Article 343(2) -The Constitution adopted in 1950 stipulated that English and Hindi would be used for the Union's official business for a period of fifteen years. Article 354 deals with the application of provisions related to the distribution of revenues while a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the GST Council in India: I. Article 279A provides for the creation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council. II. Article 246A provides for the creation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: I only is correct. Article 279A empowers the president to constitute a joint forum of the central and states namely, Goods and Services Tax Council. The GST Council is a constitutional body for making recommendations to the union and state government on issues related to Goods and Service Tax.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: According to which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India shall a Money Bill NOT be introduced in the Council of States ?
questions.explanation: Article 109. Rajya Sabha (Council of States), the upper house of the Parliament of India. A money bill is a specific type of financial legislation that exclusively deals with matters related to taxes, government revenues, or expenditures.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: As per Article ______ of the Constitution of India, English is the official language for all the high courts in the country.
questions.explanation: Article 348 (1). 329(a) the validity of any law relating to the delimitation of constituencies or the allotment of seats to such constituencies, made or purporting to be made under Article 327 or Article 328, shall not be called in question in any court

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding secretarial staff for the Houses of Parliament: I. Article 98 provides for a separate secretarial staff for each House of the Parliament. II. Article 99 specifies the oath or affirmation that members of Parliament must take before sitting and voting in the House Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both I and II are correct.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following was a major effect of the 42nd Constitutional Amendment?

options.a: It abolished the Directive Principles of State Policy.
options.b: It increased the tenure of the Lok Sabha and introduced Fundamental Duties
options.c: It introduced Fundamental Rights for citizens.
options.d: It reduced the term of the Lok Sabha to four years

questions.answer_text: It increased the tenure of the Lok Sabha and introduced Fundamental Duties
questions.explanation: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, often called the “Mini-Constitution,” extended the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies’ term from 5 to 6 years (later reverted to 5 by the 44th Amendment 1978) and added a new part (Part IVA) introducing Fundamental Duties of citizens. This amendment was enacted during the Emergency. It also amended the Preamble, adding the words "Socialist," "Secular," and "Integrity" to the description of India.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which constitutional amendment is known as the "Mini Constitution" ?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment. It was enacted in 1976 during the Emergency by the Indira Gandhi government. Key changes included adding "socialist," "secular," and "integrity" to the Preamble, establishing Fundamental Duties for citizens, and transferring several subjects from the State List to the Concurrent List, increasing central power. It also extended the term of the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies from five to six years and modified emergency provisions, including granting the President authority to deploy central forces in states.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act made the Right to Education a Fundamental Right in India?
questions.explanation: 86th Amendment Act, 2002. The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 made elementary education a Fundamental Right by inserting Article 21A, which mandates the State to provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years. It also modified Article 45 (Directive Principles) and added Article 51A(k) as a Fundamental Duty, requiring parents/guardians to provide educational opportunities to children. 44th Amendment Act, 1978 – Reversed several provisions of the 42nd Amendment and removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights. 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 – Known as the “Mini-Constitution”, it introduced Fundamental Duties, added “Socialist” and “Secular” to the Preamble, and shifted Education from the State List to the Concurrent List (but did not make it a Fundamental Right). 97th Amendment Act, 2011 – Gave constitutional status and protection to co-operative societies.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: What major reform does Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam bring?
questions.explanation: Digitization of evidence. The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 modernizes the Indian legal system by allowing digital recording, storage, and submission of evidence in courts. This reform aims to increase efficiency, reduce delays, and ensure secure handling of documents and witness statements. By embracing technology, the act facilitates faster judicial processes and enhances transparency, marking a significant step toward digitization in India’s justice delivery system.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which act replaces the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973?
questions.explanation: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita. In 2023, India introduced three new criminal laws to replace colonial-era laws: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 → Replaces the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 → Replaces the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973. Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023 → Replaces the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. Thus, the CrPC 1973 has been replaced by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: As per the Constitution (Ninety - First Amendment) Act, 2003, the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall NOT exceed:

options.a: 20% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
options.b: 15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
options.c: 10% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
options.d: 25% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha

questions.answer_text: 15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
questions.explanation: 91st Amendment Act 2003: The total number of ministers in the Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, cannot exceed 15% of the total number of members in the Lok Sabha. The total number of ministers in a State Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, cannot exceed 15% of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that State.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Part IV A of the Indian Constitution was inserted in the Indian Constitution through______ Constitutional Amendment Act.
questions.explanation: 42nd. The fundamental duties were incorporated in Part IV-A of the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. Initially, there were 10 duties, but an additional duty was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, bringing the total to 11 duties.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution: 1. Part IV-A was inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. 2. Initially, 10 Fundamental Duties were included in Part IV-A. 3. The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 added one more Fundamental Duty, raising the total to 11. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2 and 3. All three statements are correct: the 42nd Amendment introduced Fundamental Duties (based on Swaran Singh Committee’s recommendations), originally 10 in number, and the 86th Amendment added the duty related to education of children, making them 11.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: ____________ Directive principles of State Policy were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.
questions.explanation: Four. questions.subject: Polity

questions.explanation: 2 only. Article 21 asserts that no person shall be deprived of their life except according to the procedure established by law. This means that every individual has the right to live, and their life cannot be taken away except in accordance with the prescribed legal procedures. It is a part of Fundamental rights (Part III). It can be amended only by a special majority in both houses of Parliament by two-thirds of members present and voting.

Article 56 - Term of office of President.

questions.question: On 7 November 2022, the Supreme Court of India upheld the reservations for the weaker sections (EWS). Which of the following amendments brought this reservation in the first place ?

questions.subject: Polity

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Constitution (Fifth Amendment Act), 1955 amended Article 3, which deals with the formation of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states. 2. Article 45, dealing with early childhood care and education, was amended later by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Article 3 deals with the formation of new states and the alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states. Article 45 was amended by the Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act of 2002. The amendment changed the subject matter of Article 45 and made elementary education a fundamental right under Article 21.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A, making the Right to Education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years. 2. The 85th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 provided for promotion with consequential seniority for SC/ST government employees. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Eighty-sixth Amendment Act, 2002, made the Right to Education a fundamental right for children aged 6-14 by adding Article 21A in Part III of the Constitution. The 87th Amendment Act, 2003 involved readjusting electoral constituencies based on the 2001 census. The 85th Amendment Act, 2002 provided for promotion with consequential seniority for government employees from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: The 42nd Amendment of the Indian Constitution (1976) states that India is a/an ______ nation.
questions.explanation: secular. The term means that all the religions in India get equal respect, protection and support from the state. The Preamble was amended only once by the 42nd Amendment Act to add ‘Socialist’, ‘Secular’ and Integrity terms.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 mandated a 3-tier Panchayati Raj system for all states having a population above 20 lakh. 2. The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee first recommended the three-tier structure consisting of Zilla Parishad, Panchayat Samiti, and Gram Panchayat. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992, enacted by the Narasimha Rao government and effective from April 24, 1993, aimed to strengthen local self-governance by establishing democracy at the grassroots level. Part IX of the Constitution outlines the Panchayati Raj system, with Rajasthan implementing it first in Nagaur district on October 2, 1959. The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee recommended a three-tier structure: Zilla Parishad (district level), Panchayat Samiti (block level), and Gram Panchayat (village level).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: In which year did the 44th Amendment remove the right to property from the list of fundamental rights?
questions.explanation: 1978. The right to property was listed under Article 31 before its deletion. At present the right to property is listed under Article 300A as a legal right.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which among the following is INCORRECT about the salient features of the 73rd Amendment Act ?

options.a: The Act corresponds to Part III of the Constitution of India.
options.b: The Act gives a Constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj Institutions.
options.c: The Act has added the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution of India.
options.d: It contains 29 functional items of the Panchayats and deals with Article 243 to 243(O).

questions.answer_text: The Act corresponds to Part III of the Constitution of India.
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment Act - It was enacted in 1992 and came into force from April 1993. It added Part IX (Article 243 - 243O) to the constitution. It was enacted to implement the Directive Principles of State Policy under Article 40 on the recommendation of L.M. Singhvi Committee.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. As per Article 368, the Indian Constitution provides for two types of amendment procedures. 2. Certain amendments require not only a special majority in Parliament but also ratification by at least half of the state legislatures. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Article 368 (Part XX) grants Parliament the power to amend the Constitution. Amendments require either (1) a special majority or (2) a special majority with ratification by at least half of the state legislatures by a simple majority. The amendment procedure is inspired by the South African Constitution.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, which provides for the more effective prevention of certain unlawful activities of individuals and associations dealing with terrorist activities, was first put into effect in India in the year.
questions.explanation: 1967. Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act - Its main objective is dealing with activities directed against the integrity and sovereignty of India. It assigns absolute power to the central government and provides for death penalty and life imprisonment of culprits. Related acts - Armed Forces Special Powers Act (AFSPA) 1958; Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002; The National Investigation Agency Act, 2008; The Anti - Hijacking Act, 2016.

questions.subject: Polity

Purpose of establishment of family court - To promote conciliation and secure speedy settlement of disputes relating to marriage and family affairs and for related matters. This bill was passed by Lok Sabha on 26th July 2022. This bill has granted statutory cover to already established family courts in Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. questions.explanation: 2014. The States Reorganisation Act (1956), under the provisions of Part I (Article 3). The first state formed on the linguistic basis is Andhra Pradesh (1 October 1953). Formation of other states: Gujarat and Maharashtra (1960), Karnataka (1956), Nagaland (1963), Haryana (1966), Sikkim (1975).

Directive Principles of State Policy: Part IV of the Constitution of India (Article 36–51). It was borrowed from the Irish Constitution. questions.question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendments incorporated Dadra and Nagar Haveli in the Union of India as a Union Territory ?

The 12th Amendment (1962) incorporated Goa, Daman, and Diu as the eighth Union Territory, while the 14th Amendment (1962) included Pondicherry as the ninth. questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India amended Article 19 and inserted provisions fully securing the constitutional validity of zamindari abolition laws in general and certain specified State Acts in particular?
questions.explanation: The First Amendment (1951) introduced provisions for advancing socially and educationally backward classes, SCs, and STs, added the Ninth Schedule to secure zamindari abolition laws, and allowed reasonable restrictions on freedom of speech (Article 19) by adding grounds such as public order, friendly relations with foreign states, and incitement to an offence. It also upheld the state’s right to nationalise businesses without violating the right to trade.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Arrange the following Fundamental Rights in the order they are listed in the Indian Constitution: 1. Right to Constitutional Remedies 2. Right to Freedom 3. Right against Exploitation 4. Right to Equality
questions.explanation: 4-2-3-1. In the Indian Constitution, Fundamental Rights are arranged systematically. First comes the Right to Equality (Articles 14–18), followed by the Right to Freedom (Articles 19–22). Next is the Right against Exploitation (Articles 23–24), and finally the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32). This order reflects the logical flow from equality and freedom, to protection against exploitation, and finally the mechanism to enforce these rights.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Arrange the following Fundamental Rights in the order of their appearance in the Constitution : SSC Stenographer 8/08/2025 (Shift 3) 1. Right to Freedom 2. Right to Equality 3. Right to Freedom of Religion 4. Right against Exploitation
questions.explanation: 2-1-4-3. The Fundamental Rights (Part III, Articles 12–35) of the Constitution appear in the following order : Right to Equality – Articles 14 to 18, Right to Freedom – Articles 19 to 22, Right against Exploitation – Articles 23 to 24, Right to Freedom of Religion – Articles 25 to 28.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following duties is specified as the 10th Fundamental Duty in the Indian Constitution?

options.a: To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity
options.b: To provide opportunities for education to his child or as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years
options.c: To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom
options.d: To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform

questions.answer_text: To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity
questions.explanation: The idea of Fundamental Duties is inspired from the Constitution of Russia. These were incorporated in Part IV-A (Article 51A) of the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. Originally 10 in number. The 86th Amendment Act of 2002 added another duty (Article 51A(k)) related to providing educational opportunities for children between the ages of 6 and 14.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution: 1. Fundamental Duties are enforceable by law and justiciable in courts. 2. Fundamental Duties are inspired by the erstwhile USSR Constitution. 3. Fundamental Duties aim to promote national spirit and strengthen unity. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 2 and 3 only. Fundamental Duties (Article 51A, Part IV-A) were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, 1976 based on the USSR model. They are non-justiciable, i.e., not enforceable in courts, but they serve as moral obligations to promote patriotism, discipline, and unity among citizens.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Right of a prisoner to speedy trial will be categorised in which of the following Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: Right to Life. Speedy trial is an inalienable right under Article 21 of the constitution and hence no person shall be deprived of his life and liberty without the procedure of law and the procedure of law must be 'fair', 'reasonable', and 'just'.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding writ jurisdiction in India: 1. Only the Supreme Court can issue writs under Article 32. 2. High Courts are empowered to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights as well as for other purposes under Article 226. 3. The Constitution of India recognizes five types of writs – Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Certiorari, Prohibition, and Quo Warranto. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 2 and 3 only. Article 32 provides the right to constitutional remedies through the Supreme Court, but not exclusively—since High Courts under Article 226 enjoy even wider writ jurisdiction, covering both Fundamental Rights and legal rights. The five writs form the backbone of judicial review, ensuring checks on executive and legislative excesses.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution prohibits providing of any religious instruction in the educational institutions maintained by the State?
questions.explanation: Article 28. Other Important Articles of Fundamental Rights (Part III, Articles 12-35) : Article 29 - Protects the cultural and educational rights of minorities in India. Article 30 - The Rights of Minorities to establish and administer educational institutions. Article 31 (Right to Property) - The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 repealed it and made it a constitutional right under Article 300A.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution: 1. Fundamental Duties are enumerated in Article 51A of the Constitution. 2. They were originally ten in number, added through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. 3. The eleventh Fundamental Duty was inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2 and 3. Fundamental Duties, found in Article 51A (Part IV-A), were introduced by the 42nd Amendment (1976) on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. Initially ten in number, they were expanded to eleven by the 86th Amendment (2002), making it the duty of parents/guardians to provide opportunities for education to children between 6–14 years.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: A student, on his school assignment, is taking a session on how to make compost at home for using it at a park. Which fundamental duty is he performing ?

options.a: To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity
options.b: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
options.c: To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry
options.d: To protect and improve the natural environment

questions.answer_text: To protect and improve the natural environment
questions.explanation: Fundamental Duty (Part IVA - Article 51A). Related Article: Article 51A(g) - To protect and improve the natural environment. Article 51A (h): To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform; Article 51A(i): To safeguard public property and to abjure violence; Article 51A(j): To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following duties has been NOT prescribed by the Indian Constitution as Fundamental Duties? 1. To defend the country 2. To pay income tax 3. To cast the vote in election 4. To safeguard the public property
questions.explanation: 2 and 3 both. Fundamental duties were incorporated into the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. Article 51-A (d) states the duty to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so, while Article 51-A (i) emphasises the duty to safeguard public property and abjure violence.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which fundamental duty applies on you when you see a few school students, on their educational trip to Humayun’s tomb, writing their names on the walls?

options.b: To defend the country and render national service
options.c: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
options.d: To protect and improve the natural environment

questions.explanation: To safeguard public property. Article 51A —It shall be the duty of every citizen of India—(a) to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem; (b) to cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom; (c) to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India; (d) to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding suspension of Fundamental Rights during an emergency: 1. Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency on the grounds of war or external aggression. 2. Articles 14, 19, and 22 can be suspended during such an emergency. 3. Article 32, which gives the right to move the Supreme Court, can never be suspended under any circumstances. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. While Articles 20 and 21 (protection in criminal convictions & right to life and personal liberty) cannot be suspended even during an emergency, Articles 14, 19, and 22 may be curtailed. However, Article 32 can be suspended under Article 359 during a National Emergency, which means citizens cannot directly approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which fundamental duty applies to you when you see your college friends start fighting with the canteen person when he passes a few anti-religious statements?

options.a: To promote harmony and spirit of brotherhood
options.b: To value and preserve the rich heritage
options.c: To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry
options.d: To protect and improve our natural environment

questions.answer_text: To promote harmony and spirit of brotherhood
questions.explanation: This fundamental duty encourages citizens to maintain harmony and foster a spirit of brotherhood among all people, transcending religious, linguistic, or regional differences. It applies in situations where religious sentiments might cause conflicts.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding Fundamental Rights?

options.a: Fundamental Rights can be enforced by Law.
options.b: Fundamental rights are derived from the Britain Constitution.
options.c: The Fundamental Rights are mentioned in the constitution from article 12 to 35.

questions.answer_text: Fundamental rights are derived from the Britain Constitution.
questions.explanation: Fundamental Rights is derived from the Constitution of the USA. Enshrined in Part III (Article 12 to 35) of the Indian Constitution.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: If a 12-year-old is found to be working in a factory manufacturing carpets, which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India will be violated?
questions.explanation: Article 24 - “No child below the age of fourteen years shall be employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment”. Other Articles: Article 23 - Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour. Article 25 - Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion. Article 26 - Freedom to manage religious affairs.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: In which part of the Constitution will you find the six broad categories of Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: Part III (Articles 12 to 35). Six broad categories of Fundamental Rights : Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22), Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24), Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28), Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29-30), Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Writ of Mandamus in the Indian Constitution: 1. The Writ of Mandamus compels a public authority to perform a duty it is bound to do. 2. It is available under the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32 and 226). 3. It is classified under the Right to Equality in the Constitution. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. The Writ of Mandamus is issued to direct a public authority to discharge its legal duty and is part of the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32 & 226), not the Right to Equality. It ensures accountability of state authorities and was borrowed from the English common law tradition.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Article 20 of the Indian Constitution: 1. Clause (2) of Article 20 embodies the doctrine of Double Jeopardy. 2. Double Jeopardy means that no person shall be prosecuted and punished more than once for the same offence. 3. The doctrine of Double Jeopardy is contained in Article 20(3) of the Constitution. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. Article 20 provides protection in criminal cases: Clause (1) bars retrospective criminal laws, Clause (2) incorporates the doctrine of Double Jeopardy, and Clause (3) grants protection against self-incrimination. Double Jeopardy ensures that no individual faces repeated punishment for the same offence, reflecting the principle of fairness in criminal justice.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Article 20 of the Constitution of India is related to _____.

options.a: equality of opportunities in matters of public employment
options.b: protection in respect of conviction for offenses

questions.answer_text: protection in respect of conviction for offenses
questions.explanation: Article 20 provides three key protections: Ex-Post Facto Laws: No punishment for acts not punishable at the time they were committed, nor penalties exceeding those in force. Self-Incrimination: Individuals cannot be compelled to confess or make self-harming statements; includes the right to remain silent. Double Jeopardy: No one can be punished twice for the same offense.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution states that ‘It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.’?
questions.explanation: 51 A (e). Fundamental Duties, outlined in Part IVA, Article 51A of the Indian Constitution, include: Abiding by the Constitution and respecting its ideals, as well as the National Flag and National Anthem. Cherishing and following the noble ideals that inspired India's struggle for freedom. Upholding and protecting the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India. Defending the country and serving the nation when required.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Right to Constitutional Remedies: 1. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) as the “Heart and Soul of the Constitution.” 2. Article 32 empowers citizens to directly approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. 3. The Right to Constitutional Remedies was called the “Soul of the Constitution” by Jawaharlal Nehru during the Constituent Assembly debates. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. Article 32 ensures the enforcement of Fundamental Rights through writs like Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto. Dr. Ambedkar emphasized its importance by calling it the “Heart and Soul of the Constitution”, as without it, Fundamental Rights would remain theoretical. The Supreme Court has also upheld Article 32 as a basic feature of the Constitution.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Certiorari comes under the:
questions.explanation: right to constitutional remedies. Certiorari is a writ issued by the Supreme Court or a High Court to review the decision or action of a lower court or tribunal. Article 32 of the Indian Constitution is a fundamental right that guarantees the right to constitutional remedies. This right allows individuals to seek redressal from the judiciary when their fundamental rights are violated.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution: 1. Ten Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. 2. They were included in Part IV-A of the Constitution under Article 51A. 3. The Swaran Singh Committee recommended the incorporation of Fundamental Duties. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2 and 3. The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added 10 Fundamental Duties in Article 51A (Part IV-A), based on the Swaran Singh Committee’s recommendations. Later, the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 introduced the 11th duty related to education for children aged 6–14 years.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) is/are INCORRECT vis-à-vis Fundamental Duties? 1) The 44th amendment Act introduced Fundamental duties in the Constitution. 2) Fundamental Duties were expanded by the 86th amendment act. 3) Article 51A (a) entails respect for its ideals and institutions, national flag and the national anthem. 4) Fundamental Duty obliges parents to provide opportunities for education to their child between 6-14 years of age.
questions.explanation: 1. The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1978 was enacted to undo many changes made by the 42nd Amendment during the Emergency in India. Key provisions include restoring judicial review, protecting civil liberties, and ensuring that the right to property is no longer a fundamental right but a legal right.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: A. The Swarna Singh Committee recommended 8 fundamental duties. B. Fundamental Duties were incorporated by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. Which of the following is correct?

options.a: Both A and B are correct
options.d: Both A and B are incorrect

questions.answer_text: Both A and B are correct
questions.explanation: Both A and B are correct. The Swarna Singh Committee recommended 8 fundamental duties, which were incorporated in Part IV-A of the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, inspired by the USSR

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: A ________ is issued to prevent an inferior court or tribunal from exceeding its jurisdiction, which is not legally vested, or acting without jurisdiction or acting against the principles of natural justice.
questions.explanation: Writ of prohibition. The Supreme Court and High Courts in India have the power to issue the writs under Article 32 (Supreme Court) and Article 226 (High Courts) of the Constitution, respectively. The Constitution of India provides for five types of writs: Habeas Corpus (To have the body), Mandamus (We Command), Prohibition (To forbid), Certiorari (To be certified), and Quo Warranto (By what authority).
