questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: A housemaid gets her 12-year-old daughter to help in her work as a house cleaner at a residential colony instead of sending her to school. Which fundamental duty is violated by the housemaid ?

options.a: To provide opportunities for education to his/her child
options.b: To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood
options.c: To defend the country and render national service
options.d: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence

questions.answer_text: To provide opportunities for education to his/her child
questions.explanation: To provide opportunities for education to his/her child. Fundamental duty (Part IV-A, Article 51-A) incorporated by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. It mandates that parents should provide educational opportunities for their children between the ages of six and fourteen years (added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: A. Citizens are not discriminated against on the basis of religion, caste, sex, race or place of birth under the Right to Equality. B. Articles 19 to 22 of the Constitution collectively provide for the Right to Equality. Which of the following is correct?

options.a: Both A and B are correct
options.d: Both A and B are incorrect

questions.explanation: Only A is correct. The Right to Equality is guaranteed under Articles 14-18, not Articles 19-22. The Fundamental Rights (Part III, Articles 12-35). Right to equality (Articles 14-18). Article 14: Equality before the law. Article 15: Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. Article 16: Equality of opportunity in public employment. Article 17: Abolition of untouchability. Article 18: Prohibition of titles, except for military or academic distinctions.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Article 32 of the Constitution provides the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. 2. Article 19 of the Constitution deals with the legal enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1 is correct. Article 32, called the "heart and soul" of the Constitution (Dr. Ambedkar), provides the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights through writs. Article 19, on the other hand, guarantees specific freedoms like speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession, but it is not about legal enforcement.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following Fundamental Rights has been deleted from the original list of fundamental rights provided in the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: Right to property. It was deleted by the 44th Constitutional amendment act 1978 from the list of Fundamental Rights (FR) and was listed under Article 300A as a legal right in Part XII.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following Fundamental Rights is available for Indians as well as foreigners?

options.a: Right to protection of language, script and culture of minorities
options.b: Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment
options.c: Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions

questions.explanation: Right to elementary education. Fundamental rights available to both citizens and foreigners (except enemy aliens) include: Article 14, Article 20, Article 21, Article 21A, Article 22, Article 23, Article 24, Article 25, Article 26, Article 27, and Article 28. Fundamental Rights Available Only to Citizens of India: Article 15, Article 16, Article 19, Article 29, and Article 30.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: All historical monuments have signages with instructions that public should not write on the walls. To which fundamental duty does the given statement belong?

options.a: To defend the country and render national service
options.b: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
options.d: To promote harmony and spirit of common brotherhood

questions.answer_text: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
questions.explanation: Fundamental Duties outline the responsibilities of every citizen of India. These duties include: (a) to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem; (c) to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India; (f) to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture. Article 49 - Protection of monuments and places and objects of national importance.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in fundamental duties provided under the Indian Constitution ?
questions.explanation: To join Defence forces. The Fundamental Duties, listed in Part IVA (Article 51A) of the Indian Constitution, were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976 based on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendations. Initially there were 10 fundamental duties, and by the 86th Amendment of 2002 one more fundamental duty (to provide right to education to all children of the age of 6 to 14 years) was added.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which writ literally means 'what is your authority’ ?
questions.explanation: Quo-Warranto. The Supreme Court and High Courts in India have the power to issue writs under Article 32 and Article 226 of the Constitution, respectively. Five types of writs - Habeas Corpus (To have the body); Mandamus (We Command); Prohibition (To forbid); Certiorari (To be certified).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: The original constitution did NOT mention any fundamental duty because:

options.a: initially fundamental duties were not expected to be performed
options.b: initially fundamental duties were punishable as per the constitution
options.c: it was expected that the citizens of the country would perform their duties willingly
options.d: it was expected that the citizens of the country would perform their duties forcefully

questions.answer_text: it was expected that the citizens of the country would perform their duties willingly
questions.explanation: The fundamental duties were incorporated in Part IV-A of our constitution through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. At present, there are eleven fundamental duties under article 51 A of the

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental duty of an Indian citizen?

options.a: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
options.b: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
options.d: To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture

questions.explanation: To vote in public elections. The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added 10 Fundamental Duties to the Indian Constitution, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. The 86th Amendment Act of 2002 introduced the 11th Fundamental Duty, requiring parents or guardians to provide educational opportunities to children aged 6 to 14. These duties are outlined in Article 51A, under Part IV-A.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Article 18 of the Indian Constitution deals with the abolition of titles except military and academic distinctions. 2. Article 24 of the Indian Constitution prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour. Which of the following is correct ?
questions.explanation: Only 1 is correct. Article 18 provides for abolition of titles, ensuring no State-conferred titles except military or academic distinctions. Article 24, however, prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines, and hazardous work — not traffic in human beings (which is covered under Article 23).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Article 21 is related to which of the following fundamental rights?

options.b: Protection of Language, Culture of Minorities
options.c: Protection of Life and Personal Liberty

questions.answer_text: Protection of Life and Personal Liberty
questions.explanation: Protection of Life and Personal Liberty. Fundamental Rights (Part III) : Right to Equality (Article 14 - 18), Right to Freedom (Article 19 - 22), Right against Exploitation (23 - 24), Right to Freedom of Religion (Article 25 - 28), Cultural and Educational Rights (Article 29 - 30), Article 31 (now repealed) - Saving of Certain Laws related to property rights, Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: If a person who is arrested, is NOT produced before the Magistrate within 24 hours from the time of arrest, he will be entitled to be released on the writ of ________.
questions.explanation: Habeas Corpus. The Supreme Court and High Courts in India have the power to issue writs under Article 32 and Article 226 of the Constitution, respectively. Five types of writs - Habeas Corpus (To have the body); Mandamus (We Command); Prohibition (To forbid); Certiorari (To be certified) and Quo Warranto (By what authority).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Article 14 guarantees the Right to Equality before the Law and the Right to Equal Protection of the Laws. 2. Articles 15, 16, and 17 are also part of the Right to Equality under the Constitution of India. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2 are correct. Article 14 guarantees equality before law and equal protection of laws, while Articles 15–17 prohibit discrimination, ensure equality of opportunity in public employment, and abolish untouchability. Together with Article 18 (abolition of titles), these form the Right to Equality under the Constitution.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Article 26(c) of the Indian Constitution grants every religious denomination the right to own and acquire movable and immovable property. 2. Article 26(b) gives the right to own and acquire property to religious denominations. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1 is correct. Article 26(c) specifically provides the right to own and acquire movable and immovable property for religious denominations. Article 26(b), however, deals with the right of denominations to manage their own affairs in matters of religion, not property.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once’?
questions.explanation: Article 20(2). This clause is known as the doctrine of "double jeopardy," which ensures that no individual is tried twice for the same crime. Other clauses: Article 20(1) : This provision ensures that a person cannot be convicted of any offense which was not in force at the time. Article 20(3) ensures that no person accused of an offense shall be compelled to be a witness against themselves.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Committee had suggested a penalty or punishment for the non - performance of Fundamental Duties ?
questions.explanation: Swaran Singh Committee. The Swaran Singh Committee recommended that the duty to pay taxes to be included in the fundamental duties. The committee also recommended that the legislatures should prescribe a law for imposing a penalty for violation of the duties. But these recommendations were not included in Article 51A.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution clarifies that policies like 'reservation' is not a violation of the right to equality ?
questions.explanation: Article 16 (4). Article 15 (2) - No citizen shall, on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth, be subject to any disability, liability, restriction or condition with regard to. Article 21 - Protection of life and personal liberty.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: What is the purpose of the Cultural and Educational Rights?

options.b: To protect the language, culture, and religion of the minority communities

questions.answer_text: To protect the language, culture, and religion of the minority communities
questions.explanation: Cultural and Educational Right (Article 29 - 30) : Article 29 - Guarantees the Protection of Interests of Minorities. Article 30 - Guarantees the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following is enforceable by the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Fundamental Rights (Part III, Articles 12-35).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE about the right to freedom of religion mentioned in the Indian Constitution ?

options.a: It provides freedom to manage religious affairs.
options.c: It is mentioned in Articles 25 to 28.
options.d: It mentions that the state has its own religion.

questions.answer_text: It mentions that the state has its own religion.
questions.explanation: The Right to Freedom of Religion (Fundamental Right under Part III) - Article 25 - Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion. Article 26 - Freedom to manage religious affairs. Article 27 - Freedom as to payment of taxes for promotion of any particular religion. Article 28 - Freedom as to attendance at religious instruction or religious worship in certain educational institutions.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which statement is FALSE regarding fundamental rights mentioned in the Indian Constitution ?

options.a: Only Article 20 and 21 can be suspended during emergency
options.c: Some fundamental rights are negative in nature

questions.answer_text: Only Article 20 and 21 can be suspended during emergency
questions.explanation: 44th Amendment Act, 1978 limits the scope of Article 359 (suspension of the enforcement of the rights conferred by Part III during emergencies). All fundamental rights except articles 20 and 21 can be suspended only on the basis of National Emergency (Article 352).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: The celebration of Christmas, Eid and Holi in school is an example of making children learn fundamental duties as well. Which of the following fundamental duties advocates about this type of ideals ?

options.a: To defend the country and render national service
options.c: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
options.d: To promote harmony and spirit of common brotherhood

questions.answer_text: To promote harmony and spirit of common brotherhood
questions.explanation: Fundamental Duties: Part IV-A of the Indian constitution in Article 51A. Article 51A(e) refers to the duty of every citizen to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India. '

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: What is the aim of fundamental rights mentioned in the Indian Constitution ?
questions.explanation: To establish political democracy. The fundamental rights in the Indian Constitution aim to build a democratic society by safeguarding individual liberty, equality, and protection against discrimination based on race, caste, sex, religion, or birthplace.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Fundamental duties are ______ and not enforceable by law but are taken into account by the courts while adjudicating any matter.
questions.explanation: Statutory. Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Article 51A):- Adopted from the Constitution of Russia (erstwhile Soviet Union). Fundamental duties - Non - justiciable in nature.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Fundamental Duty to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India is mentioned in Article 51A(c). 2. Article 51A(d) of the Constitution mentions the duty to uphold sovereignty, unity and integrity of India. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1 is correct. The duty to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India is provided under Article 51A(c). Article 51A(d), on the other hand, refers to the duty to defend the country and render national service when called upon, not sovereignty and unity.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: The central bank of India or Reserve Bank of India was created before Independence, in the year 1934. The recommendation to create a central bank was made by a commission called:
questions.explanation: Hilton Young Commission. It is also known as the Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, was established in 1926. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is India's central bank and regulatory body overseeing the Indian banking system. It manages the control, issuance, and supply of the Indian rupee. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established on April 1, 1935, in accordance with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The P.K. Thungon Committee (1989) recommended constitutional recognition for local government bodies along with provisions for regular elections, specific functions, and financial support. 2. The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) studied the Panchayati Raj system and suggested a two-tier structure instead of the three-tier system recommended earlier. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2 are correct. The P. K. Thungon Committee (1989) recommended constitutional recognition for Panchayati Raj with elections and financial backing, while the Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) suggested replacing the three-tier Panchayat system with a two-tier system for better functioning.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following commissions/committees identified the existence of legal provisions for implementation of some of the Fundamental Duties?
questions.explanation: Justice Verma Committee. The committee was set up in 1999. It identified the existence of following legal provisions - Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act (1971), Protection of Civil Right Act (1955), Representation of People Act (1951), Wildlife Protection Act (1972) and Forest Conservation Act (1980).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following committees had recommended the inclusion of a chapter on the Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India and stressed that the citizens should become conscious that, in addition to the enjoyment of rights, they also have certain duties to perform ?
questions.explanation: Swaran Singh Committee (1976) originally recommended eight Fundamental Duties under Article 51A of the Indian Constitution. However, at the time of incorporation, ten duties were added to Part IV-A by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. Initially, there were 10 duties, and one more was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, making a total of 11 duties.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Dutt Committee was associated with the Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry. 2. The Gadgil Committee was constituted to review the industrial licensing system under the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1 is correct. The Dutt Committee examined issues related to industrial licensing policy. The Gadgil Committee, however, was not related to licensing policy; it studied ecological and developmental concerns of the Western Ghats.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: In November 2022, the Supreme Court upheld the 10% reservation of EWS quota. This EWS reservation was granted on the basis of recommendations from which of the following commissions ?
questions.explanation: Sinho commission: Constituted in 2005, and submitted its report in 2010. In 2019, the Cabinet decided to amend the Constitution (103rd Amendment) to provide reservation to EWS. Sarkaria Commission (1983) - Reviewed center-state relations. Kelkar Commission (1953) - Also known as the First Backward Classes Commission. Mandal Commission (1979) - The Second Socially and Educationally Backward Classes Commission.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following persons was appointed Chairman of the Second National Judicial Pay Commission ?
questions.explanation: Justice PV Reddi. The second National judicial Pay Commission was formed in 2017 due to the supreme court’s order in the all India judges association case, under article 32, i.e., constitutional remedies. Justice Verma Committee was constituted to recommend amendments to the Criminal Law so as to provide for quicker trial and enhanced punishment for criminals accused of committing sexual assault against women. The Committee submitted its report on January 23, 2013.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Motilal Nehru Report (1928) and the Tej Bahadur Sapru Report (1945) are associated with Fundamental Rights. 2. The Sarkaria Commission Report is also associated with Fundamental Rights. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1 is correct. The Motilal Nehru Report and Tej Bahadur Sapru Report discussed Fundamental Rights and political safeguards. The Sarkaria Commission Report (1983), however, was related to Centre–State relations, not Fundamental Rights.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Sarkaria Commission (1983) recommended that the appointment of Governors should be non-partisan. 2. The Fazal Ali Commission (1953) recommended that Governors should be appointed on a non-partisan basis. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1 is correct. The Sarkaria Commission (1983), set up to review Centre–State relations, suggested that Governors should be appointed in a non-partisan manner. The Fazal Ali Commission (1953), however, was related to State Reorganisation, not to the role or appointment of Governors.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Constitution Review Commission chaired by______recommended some initiatives to be taken by the government for successful implementation of Fundamental Duties.
questions.explanation: MN Venkatachaliah Commission was set up by Government resolution in 2000 to Review the Working of the Constitution. He got Padma Vibhushan In 2004. Justice U.C.Banerjee headed the Commission report on Godhra incident.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Mandal Commission (1979) recommended 27% reservation for OBC candidates in Central government jobs and public sector undertakings. 2. The Kothari Commission recommended 27% reservation for OBC candidates in all levels of government services. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1 is correct. The Mandal Commission (1979), headed by B.P. Mandal recommended 27% reservation for OBCs in Central government jobs and PSUs. The Kothari Commission (1964–66), however, dealt with educational reforms, not reservations in government services.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following bodies has the power to create new All-India Services common to both the Union and the States?

options.a: The President of India by issuing an executive order.
options.b: The Union Cabinet by a simple majority.
options.c: The Prime Minister with the consent of all Chief Ministers.
options.d: The Parliament, provided the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a special majority.

questions.answer_text: The Parliament, provided the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a special majority.
questions.explanation: Under Article 312 of the Indian Constitution, Parliament has the power to create new All-India Services (like IAS, IPS, IFS) if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a special majority (two-thirds of members present and voting) declaring that it is necessary in the national interest. Once such a resolution is passed, Parliament can enact a law to create the new service. The President or Prime Minister alone cannot create such services, and the Union Cabinet’s decision is not sufficient without parliamentary approval.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: According to the Constitution of India, what is the quorum required to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament?

options.a: One-third of the total number of members of the House.
options.b: Fifty members in the Lok Sabha and twenty-five members in the Rajya Sabha.
options.c: One-tenth of the total number of members of the House.
options.d: One-fourth of the total number of members of the House.

questions.answer_text: One-tenth of the total number of members of the House.
questions.explanation: One-tenth of the total number of members of the House. Article 100(3) of the Indian Constitution states that the quorum to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament is one-tenth of the total number of members of that House. If at any time there is no quorum, the presiding officer (Speaker in Lok Sabha or Chairman in Rajya Sabha) must either adjourn the House or suspend the meeting until a quorum is present. This provision ensures that parliamentary decisions are not taken without minimum representation.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha (House of the People) as stipulated by the Constitution is:
questions.explanation: 552 members. Composition of Lok Sabha: The Lok Sabha consists of members who are directly elected by the people of India. The elections are based on Universal Adult Suffrage, meaning every citizen of India aged 18 or above has the right to vote. The Constitution allows a maximum of 550 members in Lok Sabha: 530 from the States and 20 from the Union Territories. At present, Lok Sabha has 543 elected members. The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, passed in 2020, abolished the provision of reserved seats for the Anglo-Indian community in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: What is the role of the Speaker in case of a tied vote in the Lok Sabha election ?

options.d: Refers the decision to the President

questions.explanation: Votes to break the tie. In the Lok Sabha, the Speaker normally does not vote during divisions to maintain neutrality. However, in case of a tie, the Speaker uses the casting vote under Article 100 of the Constitution to resolve the deadlock. This vote is exercised only to maintain the status quo and not to favour any side. The provision ensures smooth legislative functioning and prevents paralysis in decision-making. Famous instances of casting votes have been rare, reflecting the Speaker’s role as an impartial presiding officer.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which body has the power to amend the Union and State power distribution under the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Parliament. The power to amend the Indian Constitution lies solely with Parliament under Article 368, especially for matters like the Seventh Schedule on Union–State powers. Such amendments need a special majority in both Houses and, for federal subjects, ratification by at least half of the state legislatures. The Supreme Court cannot amend but can review amendments under the Basic Structure doctrine. The Lok Sabha alone cannot amend; approval of the Rajya Sabha and in some cases states is mandatory.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: The power to legislate on 'Residuary Subjects' (matters not enumerated in any of the three Lists) rests exclusively with:
questions.explanation: Parliament. Under the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution, legislative subjects are divided into: Union List – Parliament’s exclusive power. State List – State legislatures’ exclusive power. Concurrent List – Both Parliament and State legislatures can make laws. However, certain subjects may not fall under any of these lists. These are called Residuary Subjects. According to Article 248 and Entry 97 of the Union List, the Parliament has exclusive power to make laws on residuary matters, including the power to impose taxes not mentioned in State or Concurrent Lists.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements : 1. The Parliament is the legislative organ of the Union Government of India. 2. The Executive is the legislative organ of the Union Government of India. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1 is correct. The Parliament is the legislative organ of the Union Government and consists of the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and the President. The Executive is a separate organ that implements the laws made by the legislature.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a device of parliamentary proceedings?
questions.explanation: Full-day discussion. In parliamentary proceedings, there are various devices used to facilitate discussions and manage time effectively. These include: Half-an-hour discussion - A device used to discuss matters of urgent public importance. It usually lasts for 30 minutes. Zero-hour discussion - A device where members can raise issues without prior notice, typically after the Question Hour, which allows for unscheduled discussions. Two-hour (short) discussion - This is also a formal discussion where specific issues are debated for two hours.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Parliament has the power to regulate the right of citizenship in India under Article 11. 2. The President has the power to regulate the right of citizenship in India under Article 11. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1 is correct. Article 11 empowers Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law. The President has no such power; citizenship provisions are dealt with under Part II (Articles 5–11) of the Constitution.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: The parliamentary standing committees have a tenure of _____ years.
questions.explanation: one. Parliamentary committees are of two types—Standing Committees and Ad Hoc Committees. Standing Committees are permanent and function on a continuous basis. In contrast, Ad Hoc Committees are temporary and cease to exist once they complete the task assigned to them. Examples - The Joint Committee on Bofors Contract and the Joint Committee on Fertilizer Pricing.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following statements are correct regarding State Legislatures? A. Notwithstanding anything in part XVII, but subject to the provisions of Article 348, business in the Legislature of a State shall be transacted in the official language or languages of the State or in Hindi or in English. B. The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly or Chairman of the Legislative Council can permit any member to speak in his mother tongue. C. Only the Supreme Court is entitled to inquire into the proceedings of the StateLegislature.
questions.explanation: A and B only. State Legislature is mentioned in Chapter III of Part VI (The States) of the Indian Constitution. Related Articles: Article 178 - The Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly. Article 179 - Vacation and resignation of, and removal from, the offices of Speaker and Deputy Speaker. Article 180 - Power of the Deputy Speaker or other person to perform the duties of the office of, or to act as, Speaker.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Council was abolished in 2019 through the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act. 2. The Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Council was abolished in 2020 through the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1 is correct. The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 abolished the Legislative Council in 2019 and bifurcated the state into two Union Territories – Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. Statement 2 is incorrect because the abolition did not happen in 2020.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Meghalaya has two Lok Sabha seats, namely Shillong and Tura. 2. Meghalaya has one Rajya Sabha seat. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2 are correct. Meghalaya elects 2 MPs to the Lok Sabha (Shillong and Tura) and 1 MP to the Rajya Sabha; Additionally, Meghalaya has 60 legislative assembly seats. Other states and their Lok Sabha seats: Manipur (2), Nagaland (1), Mizoram (1), Assam (14), Arunachal Pradesh (2), Tripura (2), Sikkim (1).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Who was the first speaker of the Lok Sabha after India’s Independence?
questions.explanation: Ganesh V Mavalankar was the Chairman of the Committee on the Functions of the Constituent Assembly of India. Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar has been conferred the title of 'Father of Lok Sabha' by Jawaharlal Nehru. M. A. Ayyangar was the first deputy speaker of the Lok Sabha. Meira Kumar was the first woman speaker of Lok Sabha (2009 - 2014).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected for a term of how many years ?
questions.explanation: 6 years. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution. However, one-third of its members retire every two years. The Vice-President of India serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. The House has a maximum of 250 members, with 238 elected members from states and union territories, and 12 nominated by the President.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Who elects the Presiding Officer (the speaker) in the State legislature?
questions.explanation: Members of Vidhan Sabha. There is a Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) in every State. It represents the people of the State. The members of Vidhan Sabha are directly elected by people on the basis of universal adult franchise. The Speaker presides over the meetings of the House and conducts its proceedings. He maintains order in the House, allows the members to ask questions and speak. Article 178 - The Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: The First hour of a sitting of the House allotted for asking and answering of questions is called as __________ .
questions.explanation: Question hour. Censure motion - A motion to express disapproval of the conduct of the government or a minister. Zero hour - The first hour of a sitting of the House, when MPs can raise matters of urgent public importance without notice. Privilege motion - A motion to protect the privileges of the House or its members.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: A money bill under Article 111 of the Constitution of India, presented to the President for assent, has to be endorsed by a Certificate of the ________signed by him/her that it is a money bill.

options.a: Secretary General of the Lok Sabha
options.b: Secretary General of the Rajya Sabha
options.d: Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: Speaker of the Lok Sabha. Articles related to Money Bill: Article 107 - Provisions as to introduction and passing of Bills. Article 108 - Joint sitting of both Houses in certain cases. Article 109 - Special procedure in respect of Money Bills. Article 110 - Definition of “Money Bills”. Article 197 - Restriction on powers of Legislative Council as to Bills other than Money Bills.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: After how many days of absence from Parliament without permission will a Member of Parliament be disqualified?
questions.explanation: 60 days. Disqualifications of Members of parliament : Article 101 - Vacation of seats. Article 102 - Disqualifications for membership. Article 103 - Decision on questions as to disqualifications of members. Article 104 - Penalty for sitting and voting before making oath or affirmation under article 99 or when not qualified or when disqualified.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: What is the bicameral legislature of the Indian Constitution ?

options.a: It is a legislative body with four houses.
options.b: It is a legislative body with two houses.
options.c: It is a legislative body with one house.
options.d: It is a legislative body with three houses.

questions.answer_text: It is a legislative body with two houses.
questions.explanation: The bicameral legislature of the Indian Constitution refers to a legislative body with two houses: the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States). Lok Sabha: The lower house, consisting of directly elected members. Rajya Sabha: The upper house, consisting of representatives elected by the members of the state legislative assemblies and by members of the Lok Sabha, along with nominated members.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: What is the most powerful weapon that enables the Parliament to ensure executive accountability ?
questions.explanation: The no-confidence motion. It moved in the Lok Sabha (and not in the Rajya Sabha) to test the confidence of the government. It needs the support of 50 members to be admitted. Other ways to ensure executive accountability: Question-hour, zero hour, calling attention motion, adjournment motion, censure motion, and other discussions.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: What is the maximum time gap between two sessions of the State Legislature ?
questions.explanation: Six months. Article 174 (1) - The Governor shall from time to time summon the House or each House of the State Legislature to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit. Article 85 (1) of the Constitution empowers the President to summon and prorogue either house of Parliament or to dissolve the Lok Sabha. Three types of Sessions in the Parliament of India: Budget session (February - May), Monsoon session (July - September) and Winter session (November - December) are held in a calendar year.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched regarding the terminology used in the Parliament? A. Appropriation Bill - A Money Bill passed for providing for the withdrawal or appropriation from and out of the Consolidated Fund of India B. Demand for Grants - Earmarking of budgetary allocation for meeting only planned expenditure of a Ministry/Department C. Short Duration Discussion - For raising a discussion on a matter of urgent public importance for which a notice has to be given by a Member and supported by 50 Members.
questions.explanation: A only. Demand for Grants is the form in which estimates of expenditure from the Consolidated Fund (included in the annual financial statement and required to be voted upon in the Lok Sabha) are submitted in pursuance of Article 113 of the Constitution. Short Duration Discussion is a procedural device to enable members to raise discussion on matters of urgent public importance without a formal motion on a matter of urgent public importance. The Speaker can allot two days in a week for such discussions.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following can make provisions for Ancillary powers of the Supreme Court ?
questions.explanation: Parliament of India. Ancillary powers of the Supreme Court (Article 140): The Parliament, through legislation, can grant the Supreme Court additional powers that are in line with the Constitution's provisions. These extra powers should help the Court better fulfill its constitutional jurisdiction. President of India : Articles 52 - 62 (Part V), Parliament of India : Articles 79-122 (Part V), Supreme Court : Articles 124-147 (Part V).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: In India, during a meeting of the Legislative Assembly or Council, if there is no quorum, it shall be the duty of the ________ to adjourn the House or suspend the meeting.
questions.explanation: Speaker/Chairman. Article 100 - Voting in Houses, power of Houses to act notwithstanding vacancies and quorum. Quorum - It refers to the number of members that must be present for a house meeting to take place. Article 189 (3) - The quorum to constitute a meeting of the state legislature shall be ten members or one-tenth of the total number of members of the house whichever is greater.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: A Money Bill should be returned to the Lok Sabha within ___ days by Rajya Sabha, either with recommendations or without recommendations.
questions.explanation: 14. Money Bill (Article 110) - It is involved with tax collection, public expense bills, and other significant costs associated with running the government. Money Bill Types - Financial Bill and Appropriation Bill. The Speaker has the authority to determine whether or not a specific bill is a money bill.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Archana wishes to contest for Lok Sabha elections in India. What is the maximum limit of constituencies that can she contest ?
questions.explanation: Two. Candidates were allowed to contest more than Two seats until 1996. As per, Section 33 (7) of the RPA (Representation of the People Act) 1951, one candidate can contest from a maximum of two constituencies. Section 70 bars candidates from representing two constituencies in the Lok Sabha/state, which means candidates have to vacate one seat in case of winning both the seats.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a kind of question related to Indian Parliamentary Proceedings ?
questions.explanation: Long Notice Question. Starred Questions are those for which an oral answer is expected. Non-starred questions are those for which a written reply is expected. Short notice questions are those which are asked on matters of urgent public importance and can be asked on a shorter notice, less than 10 days.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following is called 'the temple of the country's democracy' ?
questions.explanation: Parliament (Article 79) consists of the President (Article 52), Council of States (Article 80 - Rajya Sabha) and House of the People (Article 81 - Lok Sabha).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: The state legislative assembly has a strength of ____, with exceptions for smaller states.
questions.explanation: 60 and 500 members. However an exception may be granted in the states of Goa, Sikkim, Mizoram, and the union territory of Puducherry which have fewer than 60 members. Maximum seats (Uttar Pradesh; 403) and least number of seats (Puducherry; 30).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: According to the Indian Constitution, the House of People shall consist of not more than ______ members to represent the Union territories.
questions.explanation: Twenty. The Lok Sabha is composed of representatives of people chosen by direct election on the basis of adult suffrage. The maximum strength of the House envisaged by the Constitution is now 550 (530 members to represent States, 20 to represent Union Territories)

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: How many organs of government are there according to the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Three Organs: the Legislature consists of the President and two Houses, known as Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and House of the People (Lok Sabha), the Executive consists of the President, the Vice-President, and the Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister as the head to aid and advise the President. and the Judiciary consists of the Supreme Court, High Court, District Court or Subordinate Court.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: __________ is a motion moved by a member to cut short the debate on a matter before the House.
questions.explanation: ‘Closure Motion’. No Confidence Motion’ also called as Motion of No Confidence: A Vote of No Confidence is a formal proposal in Lok Sabha to evoke a decision of the house.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of parliamentary government in India?

options.a: Membership of the ministers in the legislature,
options.c: Presence of nominal and real executives
options.d: Collective responsibility of the executive to the legislature

questions.explanation: Undissolvable lower house. Features of Parliamentary Government : Nominal and Real Executives, Double Membership, Collective Responsibility, Secrecy of procedure, Prime Ministerial Leadership, Majority Party Rule, Bicameral Legislature, Political Homogeneity, No fixed term.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding forms of government: A. An alliance formed by political parties after elections when no party secures a clear majority is called a coalition government. B. Appropriation refers to setting aside money for a specific purpose, prorogation is the termination of a House session by the President, and allegiance is a tie that binds an individual to an institution or person. Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both A and B. A coalition government is formed when parties join hands to achieve a majority, while appropriation, prorogation, and allegiance have distinct meanings unrelated to forming government alliances.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: The period between prorogation of Parliament and re-assembly in a new session is called______.
questions.explanation: Recess. An adjournment suspends the work in a sitting for a specified time, which may be hours, days or weeks. A dissolution ends the very life of the existing House, and a new House is constituted after general elections are held. Cut motion is a power given to the members of the Lok Sabha that enables its members to oppose any demand in a Finance Bill proposed by a government

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: In the absence of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha, who presides over the joint sitting of the two houses of Parliament?

options.b: Any senior member of Rajya Sabha
options.d: Any senior member of Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha. Article 93 - The Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People . Article 95 - Power of the Deputy Speaker or other person to perform the duties of the office of, or to act as, Speaker. Article 96 - The Speaker or the Deputy Speaker not to preside while a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: The salary and allowances of leaders of opposition in parliament are governed by the Act passed for the first time by the parliament in the year ______.
questions.explanation: 1977. Second Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the provisions in relation to allowances, privileges, emoluments of : The President of India, Governors of Indian States, Speaker of Lok Sabha & Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha etc. The leader of the largest Opposition party having not less than one-tenth of the seats of the total strength of the House is recognized as the leader of the Opposition in that House opposition cabinet. President, Vice President and Prime Minister

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: The Vice-President of India is part of which branch of the government ?
questions.explanation: Both Executive and Legislative. The Vice-President of India is part of the Executive as he is the second highest constitutional authority after the President. At the same time, he is also part of the Legislature, since he is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States). Thus, the Vice-President has a dual role, functioning in both the Executive and Legislative branches of the government.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Which body is responsible for resolving disputes related to the election of the President of India?
questions.explanation: Supreme Court. Article 71 of the Indian Constitution provides that all doubts and disputes regarding the election of the President (and Vice-President) shall be inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court, whose decision is final. The decision of the Supreme Court in such matters is final and cannot be challenged in any other court. Under Article 71(2), if a President’s election is declared void, all acts done before the verdict remain valid to ensure continuity.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Which of the following statements is true in relation to the enforcement of President's Rule ?

options.a: The Governor's recommendation can lead to dismissal of a State government, even if it enjoys a majority.
options.b: It can be extended indefinitely with the consent of the Prime Minister.
options.c: The President cannot impose President's Rule unless the Supreme Court permits.
options.d: President's Rule can be declared without Parliament's approval.

questions.answer_text: The Governor's recommendation can lead to dismissal of a State government, even if it enjoys a majority.
questions.explanation: President’s Rule is imposed under Article 356 of the Constitution when the President is satisfied that the government of a state cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution. The Governor’s report is the usual basis for recommending President’s Rule, though the President may act otherwise too. Historically, it has often been misused to dismiss state governments even when they had majority support (e.g., S.R. Bommai case, 1994).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a condition for the President’s office in India?

options.a: He shall not be entitled, without payment of rent, to use his official residence
options.b: He shall not be a member of either House of the Parliament.
options.c: The allowances shall not be diminished during his term of office.
options.d: He shall not hold any office of profit.

questions.answer_text: He shall not be entitled, without payment of rent, to use his official residence
questions.explanation: Article 59 of the Constitution of India outlines the conditions for the office of the President of India. Article 59 (3) - The President shall be entitled without payment of rent to the use of his official residences and shall be also entitled to such emoluments, allowances and privileges as may be determined by Parliament by law.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India expressly provides that the President is eligible for re-election?
questions.explanation: Article 57. Important articles related to the President of India : Article 52 - The President of India. Article 53 - Executive power of the Union. Article 54 - Election of President. Article 55 - Manner of election of President. Article 56 - Term of office of President. Article 58 - Qualifications for election as President. Article 59 - Conditions of President’s office. Article 60 - Oath or affirmation by the President.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: In the state legislative assembly, the Money bill can be introduced with the prior permission of __________.
questions.explanation: Governor. Money Bills in State Legislatures : A Money Bill is a special type of financial bill that deals with matters like taxation, borrowing, or expenditure from the state's Consolidated Fund. Article 198 of the Constitution of India deals with the special procedure for money bills in state legislatures. Article 148 : Provision for the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) by the President.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: As per article 123, the ordinance making power is the most important legislative power of ____________.
questions.explanation: President. Article 123 of the Indian Constitution allows the President to issue ordinances when Parliament is not in session, with approval required within six weeks of reassembly. The maximum life of an ordinance is six months and six weeks. Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed issued the most ordinances in India. Article 213 : Power of Governor to promulgate Ordinances during recess of Legislature.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides that ‘there shall be a Vice President of India’ ?
questions.explanation: Article 63. The Vice President of India is the second-highest constitutional office in India, after the President. Important Articles related to Vice President: Article 64 - The Vice-President to be ex officio Chairman of the Council of States. Article 65 - The Vice-President to act as President or to discharge his functions during casual vacancies in the office, or during the absence, of President.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: The ________ of every state unfurls the flag in its capital on the Republic Day.
questions.explanation: Governor is the constitutional head of a state in India, appointed by the President. They represent the central government at the state level. Article 153 - Governors of States.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Which of the following Articles states that the Prime Minister should be appointed by the President ?
questions.explanation: Article 75. Article 62 - Time of holding the election to fill the vacancy in the office of President and the term of office of the person elected to fill the casual vacancy. Article 66 - Election of Vice-President. Article 71 - Matters relating to, or connected with, the election of a President or Vice-President.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Which of the following is the most controversial Article in the Indian Constitution, which provides for President’s rule in any state?
questions.explanation: Article 356. Other Articles : Article 352 - Proclamation of Emergency. Article 358 - Suspension of provisions of article 19 during emergencies. Article 360 - Provisions as to financial emergency.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Who is considered the highest law officer of the state in India?
questions.explanation: Advocate general. It is a Constitutional post and its authority is mentioned in article 165 of the Indian Constitution. Appointment: The Governor of each State shall appoint a person qualified to be a High Court Judge as the Advocate-General for the State. Term and Remuneration: The Advocate-General holds office at the pleasure of the Governor and receives remuneration as determined by the Governor.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Which Article deals with the election of the President ?
questions.explanation: Article 54 - The President shall be elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of: (a) the elected members of both Houses of Parliament; and (b) the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: As per article 158, the Governor shall NOT be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State specified in ___________ Schedule.
questions.explanation: First. If a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any such State be appointed Governor, he shall be deemed to have vacated his seat in that House on the date on which he enters upon his office as Governor. First Schedule - The list of names of states and union territories and their extent and territorial jurisdictions.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with the election of the Vice President?
questions.explanation: Part V (Article 52- 151). Article 66 - Election of Vice President. The Vice-President shall be elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and the voting at such election shall be by secret ballot.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Who among the following was the shortest-serving Prime Minister of India?
questions.explanation: Gulzarilal Nanda was an Indian politician and economist specializing in labor issues. He served as the Acting Prime Minister of India twice, for 13 days each, following the deaths of Jawaharlal Nehru in 1964 and Lal Bahadur Shastri in 1966. Chandra Shekhar, known as Jananayak, was Prime Minister from 10 November 1990 to 21 June 1991. Chaudhuri Charan Singh briefly served as Prime Minister from 1979 to 1980. Atal Bihari Vajpayee, an Indian politician and poet, was Prime Minister first for 13 days in 1996, then for 13 months from 1998 to 1999, and finally for a full term from 1999 to 2004.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: In case the President is satisfied with the Governor’s report, he may declare President’s Rule under Article 356 but such proclamation is initially for a period of ________.
questions.explanation: Six months. Article 356 allows the President to issue a proclamation if a state's government cannot function according to the Constitution. The President can act based on the governor's report or independently. This proclamation must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within two months. It can be extended for a maximum of three years, with parliamentary approval every six months.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Among the following, which is not a qualification for membership in the Vidhan Sabha

options.a: Not hold any office of profit
options.b: Have attained the age of 25 Years

questions.explanation: Knowledge of Politics. The Legislative Assembly, also known as the Vidhan Sabha, consists of a maximum of 500 members and a minimum of 60. Its tenure is five years, but the Governor can dissolve it before the completion of the period.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: The minimum strength of the Council of Ministers in a state as per the Indian Constitution is ________ .
questions.explanation: 12 persons. As per the Constitution (91st Amendment) Act, 2003, clause 1A was inserted into Article 164, which states: "The total number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, in the Council of Ministers of a State shall not exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Legislative Assembly of that State."

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Who has the power to prorogue the House or either House of State Legislature from time to time ?
questions.explanation: Governor. According to Article 174 (1) The Governor shall from time to time summon the House or each House of the Legislature of the State to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit, but six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session. Article 174 (2): The Governor may from time to time—(a) prorogue the House or either House; (b) dissolve the Legislative Assembly.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Which option is NOT correct in case of appointment of a Governor ?

options.b: Cannot hold any office of profit during his tenure

questions.explanation: Appointed for six years. Governors in India are appointed by the President under Article 155 of the Constitution, with a tenure of five years. However, they serve at the President's pleasure and can be removed at any time.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: On whose advice does the Governor appoint the ministers ?
questions.explanation: Chief Minister. According to Article 164, the Governor appoints the Chief Minister, who in turn advises the Governor on appointing other Ministers. The Ministers hold office at the pleasure of the Governor.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Who unfurls the flag at Rajpath on the Republic Day?
questions.explanation: The President of India takes the salute from various units of the Army, Navy, Air force, Para-military, and Police forces during the parade. This ceremony commemorates the adoption of the country's Constitution on January 26, 1950. The Prime Minister of India, on the other hand, hoists the national flag on Independence Day at the Red Fort.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: The Governor’s emoluments are decided by the:
questions.explanation: Parliament. The Governor (Part VI, Article 153 -167) serves as a titular or constitutional head and acts as the agent of the central government. The Governor of State is appointed by the President. Article 158 (4) - The emoluments and allowances of the Governor cannot be diminished during his term of office. Article 158(3A) - When the same person is appointed as the Governor of two or more States, the emoluments and allowances payable to him are shared by the States.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: The ministers in the state hold office during the pleasure of the:
questions.explanation: Governor. Under Article 164 (1) The Chief Minister shall be appointed by the Governor and the other Ministers shall be appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister, and the Ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the Governor.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: In which year did Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan assume office as the first Vice-President of India ?
questions.explanation: 1952. Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan served as first vice president of India from 1952 to 1962 and the second president of India from 1962 to 1967. He received Bharat Ratna in 1954. Teachers' Day is celebrated on September 5 in India to honor him.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘The President shall, notwithstanding the expiration of his/her term, continue to hold office until his successor enters upon his/her office’?
questions.explanation: Article 56. The President shall hold office for a term of five years. The President may, by writing under his hand addressed to the Vice-President, resign his office. Other important Articles: Article 61 - Procedure for impeaching the President of India. Article 58 - Qualifications for election as a President of India. Article 50 - The separation of the judiciary from the executive.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that an election to fill a vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of office of the President shall be completed before the expiration of the term?
questions.explanation: Article 62. This article also covers the scenario where a vacancy arises due to the President's death, resignation, or removal, requiring the election to be held within six months. Other articles: Article 59: Conditions of President’s office. Article 61: Procedure for impeachment of the President. Article 60: Oath or affirmation by the President.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Who was the second vice - President of India?
questions.explanation: Dr Zakir Hussain (1962 -1967) - He was the third President of India from 1967-1969, and the first Indian President to die in office in 1969. He was awarded Bharat Ratna in 1963. First five vice presidents of India : First - Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1952-1962). Third - Sh. V.V. Giri (1967-1969). Fourth - Sh. Gopal Swarup Pathak (1969-1974). Fifth - Sh. B.D.Jatti (1974-1979).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Article 112 provides for the annual financial statement at the Union level. 2. Article 202 provides for the annual financial statement at the State level, which is laid before the Legislature by the Governor. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Article 112 relates to the Union Budget presented by the President, while Article 202 relates to the State Budget presented by the Governor.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: When the President of India keeps a bill (except money bill and constitutional amendment bill) pending for an indefinite period, it is called______.
questions.explanation: Pocket veto of the President. Veto Power of the President of India is guided by Article 111. Three types of Veto Power: Absolute veto, Suspensive veto and Pocket veto. Absolute Veto: It refers to the power of the President to withhold his assent to a bill passed by the Parliament. The bill then ends and does not become an act. Suspensive Veto: The President uses a suspensive veto when he returns the bill to the Indian Parliament for its reconsideration.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: The Governor of an Indian state before entering upon his office takes an oath or affirmation before ____________.

options.a: the Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to the State
options.c: the Chief Minister of the concerned state

questions.answer_text: the Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to the State
questions.explanation: Article 159 - Oath or affirmation to the Governor by the Chief Justice of the High Court and in his Absence, senior most Judge of that Court available. Article 155 - The Governor of a State shall be appointed by the President. Article 153 - Governors of States.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: What is the duty of the Chief Minister, as mentioned under Article 167 of the Indian Constitution?

options.a: Communication of all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor.
options.b: Appointment and removal of Council of the Ministers.
options.c: Appointment of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.
options.d: Appointment of Advocate General of the state in consultation with Attorney general.

questions.answer_text: Communication of all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor.
questions.explanation: Article 167 imposes on the Chief Minister the responsibility of keeping the Governor informed of all decisions made by the Council of Ministers concerning administration and legislation. Article 178 - It deals with the corresponding position for Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of a state.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Who among the following served the shortest tenure as the Prime Minister of India ?
questions.explanation: Chandra Shekhar. Shri Gulzari Lal Nanda (11 January 1966 - 24 January 1966 and 27 May 1964 - 9 June 1964) served the shortest tenure as PM. H D Deva Gowda (June 1, 1996 - April 21, 1997) - 11th Prime Minister of India. V. P. Singh (December 2, 1989 - November 10, 1990) - 7th Prime Minister of India. Chandra Shekhar (10 November 1990 and 21 June 1991) - 8th Prime Minister of India. The longest-serving prime minister was Jawaharlal Nehru, (16 years and 286 days).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Inter-State Council: 1. It is established under Article 263 of the Constitution. 2. It is chaired by the Prime Minister of India. 3. It consists of four Cabinet Ministers of the Union Council of Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister. 4. Chief Ministers of all States are its members. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2 and 4 only. Inter-State Council is a constitutional body under Article 263, established by the President to promote coordination between Centre and States. It is chaired by the Prime Minister and includes Chief Ministers of all States/UTs with legislatures, Administrators of UTs without legislatures, and Governors of States under President’s Rule. Additionally, six Union Cabinet Ministers are nominated by the Prime Minister as members.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Who appoints the Chief Justice of India ?
questions.explanation: President. Article 124 (2) - Vests power on the President to appoint every Judge of the Supreme Court including the Chief Justice of India. Article 124 - States the establishment of the Supreme Court. Article 124 (3) - Qualification of Supreme court Judge.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the qualifications for the appointment of a Governor in India: A. A person must be a citizen of India and must have completed 35 years of age. B. The minimum age required to contest for the Lok Sabha election is 30 years. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: A only. Article 157 - Qualifications for appointment as Governor (must be a citizen of India and must have completed 35 years of age). Article 153 - Governors of States. Article 154 - Executive power of State. Article 155 - Appointment of Governor. Article 58 - The presidential candidate must complete the age of 35 years. Article 84 (b) - the minimum age for Lok Sabha election shall be 25 years, not 30, hence Statement B is incorrect.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Who administers the Union Territories of India?
questions.explanation: President. The administrator appointed by the President runs the administration on the behalf of the President. Part - VIII (Union Territories), Article 239 (Administration of Union territories). Article 239A (Creation of local legislatures or council of ministers or both for certain Union territories. Example (Pondicherry). Article 239AA (Special provisions with respect to Delhi).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Which of the following statements are correct regarding the benefits of the retired President of India? A. The former President of India will also be entitled to a monthly pension of ₹2.5 lakh. B. He/She is entitled to a secretarial staff comprising a private secretary, a personal assistant, an additional private secretary, two peons, and office expenses up to ₹1 lakh per annum. C. He/She is also entitled to free highest-class travel anywhere in India, accompanied by one person, by rail, air, or steamer.
questions.explanation: A, B and C. The President {Article (52-62)} of India is the head of state of the Republic of India. First President - Rajendra Prasad (held office for two terms, longest serving president of India).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Who among the following Presidents of India was also the deputy chairman of the Planning Commission?
questions.explanation: Dr. Pranab Mukherjee (13th president). Other positions he hold were Minister of Finance (2009 - 2012), Minister of Defence (2004 - 2006), Minister of External Affairs (2006 - 2009), 15th Leader of the Lok Sabha (2004 – 2012), Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission (1991 - 1996), 14th Leader of the Rajya Sabha (1980 – 1984), Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha (2004 - 2012), and Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha (1969 - 1981). V.V Giri (4th President), K.R Narayan (10th president). Ramaswamy Venkataraman (8th president).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Vice President of India is INCORRECT?

options.a: Members of State legislatures do not take part in his elections.
options.b: He acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
options.c: The Vice President is elected for five years.
options.d: He can be removed from his office by the President approved through a resolution passed by the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

questions.answer_text: He can be removed from his office by the President approved through a resolution passed by the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
questions.explanation: Vice president of India: The vice president is elected for five years. Minimum age: 35. He acts as the ex-officio chairman of the Rajya sabha. In the electoral college for Vice President, both elected and nominated members of both the Houses of Parliament take part.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: The emoluments and allowances of the President and other expenditure relating to his office is charged on the ______ of India.
questions.explanation: Consolidated Funds - Article 266(1). Three types of funds of the Central Government – Consolidated Fund of India - Revenues received by the government and expenses made by it, excluding the exceptional items. Contingency Fund of India (Article 267) - the emergency fund for the nation and Public Accounts of India (Article 266(2) - those funds that are received on behalf of the Government of India.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Which is NOT correct about the powers of the Chief Minister?

options.b: He presides over the meetings of the Council of Ministers.
options.c: When he resigns or dies, it has no effect in the functioning of the council of ministers.
options.d: The Governor appoints ministers on His recommendations.

questions.answer_text: When he resigns or dies, it has no effect in the functioning of the council of ministers.
questions.explanation: The Governor appoints the Chief Minister and other Ministers (Article 164). The Chief Minister is the head of the State Council of Ministers and the real executive head of state government. Article 167 (Chief Minister acts as a link between Governor and state council of ministers).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Who among the following is NOT appointed by the President of India?

options.b: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

questions.explanation: Solicitor General of India (the second - highest law officer of the country) is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC). Attorney Generals of India (Article 76). Comptroller and Auditor General of India (Article 148).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: Who among the following was the third Vice - President of India?
questions.explanation: V. V. Giri. Vice Presidents of India - 1st Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, 2nd￾Zakir Hussain, 4th Gopal Swarup Pathak, 5th B D Jatti. 14th- Jagdeep Dhankhan.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.chapter_name: President, Vice President and Prime Minister
questions.question: The election of the next Vice - President is to be held within _____ of the expiry of the term of office of the outgoing Vice - President.
questions.explanation: 60 days. Article 66 of the Constitution of India states the manner of election of the vice president.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Who among the following is the final interpreter of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court of India. The Supreme Court of India, as the apex judicial body, holds the ultimate power to interpret the Constitution and exercise Judicial Review over laws and executive actions of both the Centre and States. Its decisions are final and binding, unless changed by a Constitutional amendment or a larger bench. The President, as head of the executive, can seek the Court’s advice under Article 143. The Prime Minister functions as the real executive authority, while the Parliament holds supreme legislative powers, including amendments under Article 368.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, what is the punishment for mob lynching?
questions.explanation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, which replaces the Indian Penal Code, has introduced a specific provision to deal with the crime of mob lynching. Section 103(2) of the BNS addresses this offense. It states that when a group of five or more individuals, acting in concert, commits murder on the grounds of race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief, or any other similar ground, each member of that group shall be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to a fine. This provision was specifically created to provide a stringent and clear punishment for hate crimes committed by mobs.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct in the context of constitutional interpretation and judicial doctrine?

options.a: The Constitution of India clearly defines the term "basic structure" under Article 368.
options.b: The Judiciary rejected the idea of spirit-based interpretation and strictly follows the written text.
options.c: The "basic structure" doctrine was brought into existence by the Supreme Court to protect the fundamental features of the Constitution.
options.d: The Parliament can propose amendments that repeal judicial principles without limitation.
