questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding drainage patterns in India: 1. Radial drainage pattern is formed when rivers discharge their waters into a central depression or lake, as in Loktak Lake (Manipur). 2. Centripetal drainage pattern is formed when rivers originate from a hill and flow in all directions, as in the case of Narmada. Which of the above statements are incorrect?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. The drainage system formed when rivers discharge their waters from all directions in a lake or depression, as in the case of Loktak Lake in Manipur, is called Centripetal. Radial drainage pattern: When the rivers originate from a hill and flow in all directions. Example - Narmada.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In which of the following districts is Baira Siul Dam located ?
questions.explanation: Chamba. The Baira Siul hydroelectric plant is an operational hydroelectric power facility located in Chaurah, Himachal Pradesh. It is a type of Earthen / Gravity & Masonry dam. Length: 160m and Height: 53m. River: Baira + Bhaled + Siul / Ravi. Other dam of Himachal Pradesh and district: Pandoh Dam and Bassi Dam (Mandi), Kol Dam and Bhakra dam (Bilaspur), Karchham-Wangtoo Dam (Kinnaur), Chamera Dam (Chamba), Parbati Dam (mandi).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Choose the correct statement about the peninsular rivers. A. The Narmada rises in the Malwa plateau. B. The Godavari rises from the slopes of the Western Ghats near Nashik. C. The Mahanadi rises in the highlands of Chhattisgarh. D. The Krishna rises from a spring near Mahabaleshwar.
questions.explanation: Only B, C and D. The Narmada River rises from the Amarkantak Plateau in Anuppur district in Madhya Pradesh. The Peninsular drainage system : It is older than the Himalayan river. These rivers are characterised by fixed course, absence of meanders and non-perennial flow of water. Most of the major rivers (except Narmada and Tapi which flow east to west) flow from west to east. The Chambal, the Sind, the Betwa, the Ken, the Son, originating in the northern part of the Peninsula belong to the Ganga river system.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding India’s water treaties with its neighbours: 1. The Farakka Treaty (1996), signed with Bangladesh, relates to the sharing of Ganga waters. 2. The Mahakali Treaty (1996) was signed between India and Pakistan. Which of the above statements is incorrect?
questions.explanation: 2 only. Farakka water -sharing treaty - It was signed by then PM H. D. Deve Gowda (India) and PM Sheikh Hasina Wajed (Bangladesh). India’s treaty with its Neighbours: Nepal Treaty - Mahakali treaty (1996), and Pakistan - Indus Waters Treaty (1960).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about River Ganga ?

options.a: River Ganga flows from the Himalayas all the way to the Bay of Bengal.
options.b: River Ganga in India is more than 2500 km long and is the most populated river basin in the world.
options.c: River Ganga and its river basin support lots of wonderful wildlife, particularly river dolphins, otters, freshwater turtles, and gharials.
options.d: The water level of River Ganga never depends on monsoon and climatic condition of the Himalaya.

questions.answer_text: The water level of River Ganga never depends on monsoon and climatic condition of the Himalaya.
questions.explanation: The Ganga river depends on the rains brought by the southwesterly monsoon winds from July to October as well as on the flow from melting Himalayan snow. The Wildlife Institute of India conducted a survey revealing that 49% of the Ganga River has high biodiversity.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In which district of Uttarakhand does the Ramganga river originate from the Doodhatoli ranges?
questions.explanation: Pauri Garhwal. The Ramganga is a smaller river that begins near Gairsain in the Garhwal mountains. It changes direction to the southwest after crossing the Shiwalik and enters the plains of Uttar Pradesh near Najibabad. It eventually joins the Ganga near Kannauj.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Trishulganga is a stream of the river:
questions.explanation: Gandak. It comprises two streams, namely Kaligandak and Trishulganga. It rises in the Nepal Himalayas between the Dhaulagiri and Mount Everest.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The drainage basin of the Godavari river is present in which of the following states of India ?

options.a: Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu
options.b: Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, and Odisha
options.c: Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Kamataka, and Tamil Nadu
options.d: Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Odisha

questions.answer_text: Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, and Odisha
questions.explanation: Godavari River (Dakshin Ganga) - Second longest river in India after the Ganges River. Origin - Trimbakeshwar near Nashik in Maharashtra. It has the largest Peninsular River system and falls into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Identify the dam that is located in South India.
questions.explanation: Mettur dam: Built on Kaveri river and located at Mettur, Salem District (Tamil Nadu). Gandhi Sagar dam - Built on Chambal River and located in the Mandsaur district (Madhya Pradesh). Tilaiya dam - Constructed by Damodar Valley Corporation across Barakar River, in Koderma district (Jharkhand).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which east-flowing river basin covers the states of Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Orissa and has a drainage area of 39,033 sq km ?
questions.explanation: Brahmani river (second largest river in Odisha): It is formed by the confluence of the Shankh and Koel rivers, both join at Veda Vyasa near Rourkela (Odisha). Baitarani: It originates from Gonasika hills and drains into the Bay of Bengal. Nagavali (Langulya): It rises in the Eastern Ghats. Sarada: Originated from Kalapani in the Himalayas and flows along Nepal's western border with India and joins Ghaghra River.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which ports belong to the western coast of India ?

options.a: Kandla port, Mormugao port, Kochi port
options.b: Kandla port, Mormugao port, Chennai port
options.c: Kandla port, Mormugao port, Kolkata port
options.d: Kandla port, Haldia port, Kochi port

questions.answer_text: Kandla port, Mormugao port, Kochi port
questions.explanation: Ports in India: West Coast - Mumbai, Jawaharlal Nehru (Maharashtra), New Mangalore (Karnataka). East Coast - V. O. Chidambaranar formerly Tuticorin, Ennore, Chennai Port (Tamil Nadu), Paradip (Orissa), Kolkata, Haldia (West Bengal), Port Blair, Haddo (Andaman and Nicobar Islands).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Dihang and Lohit are rivers in which of the following regions?
questions.explanation: Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. Dihang River - The Brahmaputra rises in Tibet, where it is known as Tsangpo and crosses over into India in Arunachal Pradesh under the name of Dihang. Lohit River - It originates in eastern Tibet, in the Zayal Chu range and surges through Arunachal Pradesh for 200 km, before emptying into the Brahmaputra river in the plains of Assam.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding major ports of India: 1. Kandla Port (Deendayal Port), located in the Gulf of Kutch (Gujarat), was developed in the 1950s after Independence to ease pressure on the Mumbai Port. 2. Visakhapatnam Port was developed after Independence to replace Karachi Port, which went to Pakistan during partition. Which of the above statements is incorrect?
questions.explanation: 2 only. Visakhapatnam Port, also known as Vizag Port, is a major Indian port located on the east coast, in Andhra Pradesh. It's a natural harbor and one of India's 12 major ports, serving as a key gateway for cargo and trade, particularly for the eastern coast of India.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which river basin originates from the Western Ghats range of Karnataka state and has many tributaries such as the Noyyal, Kabini, Arkavathi and Amaravati?
questions.explanation: Kaveri river basin falls in 3 States (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala) and a Union Territory (Puducherry). It originates in the foothills of Western Ghats at Talakaveri. Tributaries - Shimsha, Hemavati, Bhavani, Lokapavani.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The Jog Falls, one of the highest waterfalls in India is the cataract of which river?
questions.explanation: Sharavati - It originates at a place called Ambutheertha in the Thirthahalli taluk (Karnataka). Tungabhadra River is formed by the confluence of the Tunga River and the Bhadra River, The two rivers originate in Mudigere Taluk of Chikmagalur District (Karnataka).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: With a stretch of about 724 km, which river is one of the most important rivers of peninsular India ?
questions.explanation: Tapi River - It flows through the states of Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat. The river originates in the Satpura Mountains in Madhya Pradesh and flows westwards before emptying into the Arabian Sea.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which river originates from the southern part of Devarayanadurga hill in Tumkur district, and flows for about 221 km before joining Kaveri?
questions.explanation: Shimsha River (a tributary of the river Kaveri). Shimsha has a waterfall at Shimshapura in Malavalli Taluk (Mandya district, Karnataka). Devarayanadurga is a small hill station located in the Indian state of Karnataka. Girna River - It originates near Kem Peak in western ghats of Maharashtra and is a tributary of Tapti river. Ghataprabha River - Right bank tributary of the Krishna River. Waghur River - It originates near Ajanta in the Aurangabad district of Maharashtra.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following lakes is the longest in India?
questions.explanation: Vembanad lake (Kerala) : Length 83.72 km and Width 14.48 km. It is connected to the Arabian Sea. The lake is known for its backwaters (a network of canals and waterways). Kanjia Lake - Odisha. Ansupa Lake - Odisha.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which river from the following flows through a rift valley?
questions.explanation: Tapi. Rift valley : It is a lowland region that forms where Earth’s tectonic plates move apart. Famous rift valleys : Great Rift Valley (East Africa), East Rift Valley or Hualien - Taitung (Taiwan), Baikal Rift Valley (Southern Siberia).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Beas River: 1. The Beas River, a tributary of the Indus, originates near the Rohtang Pass at an altitude of about 4,000 meters. 2. Its ancient name was Vipasha. Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Tributaries of the Beas river : Parbati, Banganga, Tirthan, Suketi, Sainj, Gaj, Chakki and Uhaul.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which is the biggest tributary of the upper Brahmaputra that originates in the Tibetan Himalayas and winds its way into India through Arunachal Pradesh ?
questions.explanation: Subansiri. Tributaries of Brahmaputra River: Ronganadi, Dikrong, Buroi, Borgong, Jiabharali, Dhansiri (North), Puthimari, Manas, Beki, Sonkosh are the main tributaries on the North while the Noadehing, Buridehing, Desang, Dikhow, Bhogdoi, Dhansiri (South), Kopilli, Kulsi, Krishnai, Dhdhnoi, Jinjiran are the main tributaries on the South.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following rivers originates near Sihawa in Raipur district of Chhattisgarh, flows through Odisha, and eventually empties into the Bay of Bengal ?
questions.explanation: Mahanadi - The largest river of Odisha state. Krishna River originates near Mahabaleshwar in the Satara district of Maharashtra. It flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Assertion (A): Rajasthan is not a part of the Tapi River Basin. Reason (R): The Tapi River originates in the Satpura range (Betul district, Madhya Pradesh) and flows westward through Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat before draining into the Arabian Sea.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. Tapti River - A river in central India that flows westwards before draining into the Arabian Sea. Origin - In Satpura range in the Gawilgarh hills of the northern part of the Deccan Plateau (In Betul district, Madhya Pradesh). The Tapi river is known as the 'Gateway of International trade' as it conducts much international trade.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is not a freshwater lake in India?
questions.explanation: Pulicat Lake (Andhra Pradesh) is the second largest brackish water lagoon in India, (after Chilika Lake, Odisha).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which state ranks first with a total length of 31.2 thousand km of rivers and canals, which is about 17% of the total length of rivers and canals in the country?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh - Fourth largest state according to area and 1st state in population. Longest canal in India - Indira Gandhi Canal, Longest river - Ganga River (2525 km), Origin - Gangotri. Longest canal of Uttar Pradesh - Sharda Canal.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Tila, Seti and Beri are the tributaries of :
questions.explanation: Ghaghara. It originates in the glaciers of Mapchachungo and a major left - bank tributary of the Ganges River. Its Tributaries: The left bank tributaries - Bheri, Sarju, Kuwana, Rapti, Chhoti Gandak and the right bank tributaries - Seti, Dahawar, Sarda, Budhi Ganga.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the name of the branch of river Godavari that joins the Bay of Bengal flowing through the Yanam enclave of the union territory of Puducherry?
questions.explanation: Gautami. The Godavari basin extends over states of Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Odisha in addition to smaller parts in Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka and Union territory of Puducherry. Projects - Polavaram Irrigation Project, Kaleshwaram, Sadarmat Anicut, Inchampalli, Sriram Sagar.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding types of waterfalls: 1. A cataract is a waterfall with an enormous volume of water. 2. In a cascade waterfall, water descends vertically, losing all contact with the bedrock. 3. In a horsetail waterfall, water descends in distinctly separate flows. 4. In a punchbowl waterfall, water maintains continuous contact with the bedrock. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Types of Waterfalls: Horsetail - Descending water maintains some contact with bedrock. Plunge - Water descends vertically, losing contact with the bedrock surface. Block - Water descends from a relatively wide stream or river. Multi-step - A series of waterfalls one after another of roughly the same size each with its own sunken plunge pool. Segmented - Distinctly separate flows of water form as it descends. Cascade - Water descends a series of rock steps. Punchbowl - Water descends in a constricted form and then spreads out in a wider pool.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following rivers does NOT flow in Kerala State?
questions.explanation: Penner - It rises in Nandi Hills in Chikballapur District of Karnataka and falls into the Bay of Bengal. Bharathapuzha (Ponnani) river is Kerala's second longest West Flowing River, draining into the Arabian Sea.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A long, winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel is known as:
questions.explanation: Esker. These are ridges made of sands and gravels, deposited by glacial meltwater flowing through tunnels within and underneath glaciers, or through meltwater channels on top of glaciers. Other depositional landforms: Drumlins are smooth oval shaped ridge -like features composed mainly of glacial till with some masses of gravel and sand.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding dams in India: 1. Almatti Dam of Karnataka is built over the Krishna River. 2. Mullaperiyar Dam of Kerala is built over the Kaveri River. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1. Other dams on Krishna river - Achakdani (Maharashtra), Achler (Maharashtra). Mullaperiyar is on the Periyar River. River (Dams) : Kaveri {Alalur (Karnataka), Amaravathi, (Tamil Nadu)}.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding large dams? I. They have social problems because they displace a large number of peasants and tribals without adequate compensation or rehabilitation. II. They have Environmental problems because they contribute enormously to deforestation and the loss of biological diversity.
questions.explanation: Both I and II. Advantages of Dams - Irrigation, tourist attraction, flood control, hydro power generation, etc. Disadvantages of dams - High construction cost, unbalanced sedimentation, deforestation, ecological imbalance, endangered aquatic life etc.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Indian rivers: 1. The Banas River originates from the Khamnor Hills of the Aravalli Range in Rajasthan and is a tributary of the Chambal River. 2. The Tapi River originates from the Satpura Range in Rajasthan. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1. Tapi originates from Satpura ranges in Madhya Pradesh. The Banas river originates from the Khamnor hills of the Aravali range. It is a tributary of the Chambal River. It is also known as “Van ki Asha”. Length of Banas: 512 km. Tributaries: Kothari, Dai, Dheel, Menali etc.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Jabalpur is located on the banks of which of the following rivers?
questions.explanation: Narmada (Reva River, 1312 km): India’s 5th longest and largest west-flowing river, running through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is not an important river of Malwa plateau?
questions.explanation: Mahanadi. Rivers of Malwa plateau - Mahi River, Ken river, Shipra River, Chambal River, Betwa River.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Ganga– Brahmaputra basin: 1. The region of the Ganga– Brahmaputra basin lies between 10°N to 30°N latitudes. 2. The Brahmaputra originates from Mount Kailash peak in Nepal. Which of the above statements is/are incorrect?
questions.explanation: Only 2. The Brahmaputra originates in the north of the Himalayas near Mansarovar Lake in the Purang district of Tibet (Known as Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet), (other names : Siang/Dihang River) India, and Bangladesh (Jamuna River). The Delta formed by Ganga Brahmaputra is Sunderban Delta (largest delta in the world).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Kadana Dam of Gujarat is built over which of the following rivers?
questions.explanation: Mahi River. Indian Rivers and Dams: Sabarmati River - Dharoi Dam (Gujarat). Tapti River - Hatnur Dam (Maharashtra), Ukai Dam (Gujarat), Girna Dam (Maharashtra), Dahigam Weir (Maharashtra). Krishna River - Nagarjuna sagar Dam (Telangana). Manjira River - Singur Dam and Nizam Sagar dam (Telangana). Banas River - Bisalpur Dam (Rajasthan).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following rivers forms the Dhuandhar falls?
questions.explanation: Narmada. The Dhuandhar Falls is located in the Jabalpur district of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which among the following lakes connects the twin cities of Hyderabad and Secunderabad?
questions.explanation: Hussain Sagar: A heart - shaped lake in Hyderabad, Telangana, built by Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah; Fed by the River Musi. Salim Ali lake - Aurangabad, Kanwar lake - Bihar, Periyar lake - Kerala.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In which state of India is Tawa dam located?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh - Indra Sagar dam, largest in state (Narmada river), Gandhisagar Dam (Chambal River), Bargi Dam (Narmada River). Uttar Pradesh - Rihand dam also known as Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar. Haryana - Kaushalya Dam (Yamuna River), Anangpur Dam (Hakra River). Gujarat - Sardar Sarovar Dam (Narmada River). Rajasthan - Rana Pratap Sagar (Chambal river).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following arrangements of rivers from North to South in India: 1. Indus → Chenab → Ravi → Beas → Satluj 2. Satluj → Ravi → Indus → Chenab → Beas 3. Indus → Ravi → Beas → Chenab → Satluj 4. Satluj → Indus → Chenab → Ravi → Beas Which of the above arrangements is correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1. Indus (Sindhu) river - Source (Lake Manasarovar), Satluj (Lake Rakshastal in Tibet), Ravi (Multhan tehsil of Kangra district of Himachal Pradesh), Chenab (Baralacha Pass in Himachal Pradesh) etc.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which state in India is the source of river Ghaggar?
questions.explanation: Himachal Pradesh (Shivalik hills). It flows through Punjab, Haryana and then into Rajasthan. It flows only during the monsoon season. It is known as Hakra river in Pakistan. The main tributaries of the Ghaggar are the Kaushalya river, Markanda, Sarsuti, Tangri and Chautang.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: India and Sri Lanka are joined by a group of islets forming ______.
questions.explanation: Adam's Bridge (Rama Setu), is a chain of limestone shoals, between Pamban Island (Rameswaram Island), Tamil Nadu, India, and Mannar Island, Sri Lanka. Mahatma Gandhi Setu (Bihar), Sisseri River Bridge (Arunachal Pradesh), Bhupen Hazarika bridge (Connects Assam and Arunachal Pradesh).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Pushkar lake is situated in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Ajmer. Freshwater Lakes in Rajasthan: Ajmer - Ana Sagar Lake, Lake Foy Sagar; Alwar - Siliserh Lake; Banswara - Anand Sagar Lake and Dailab Lake; Bundi - Jait Sagar Lake, Kanak Sagar Lake, and Nawar Sagar Lake; Dungarpur - Gaib Sagar Lake; Jaisalmer - Gadsisar Lake; Jodhpur - Balsamand Lake, Kailana Lake; Kota - Kishore Sagar Lake; Rajsamand - Rajsamand Lake; Udaipur - Doodh Talai, Fateh Sagar Lake, Jaisamand Lake, Udai Sagar Lake, and Pichola Lake.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the meaning of the term Moraine?

options.b: Material transported and deposited by glacier
options.c: Valley with vertical sides and wide floor

questions.answer_text: Material transported and deposited by glacier
questions.explanation: A moraine is material left behind by a moving glacier. This material is usually soil and rock. Moraines are divided into four main categories: lateral moraines, medial moraines, supraglacial moraines, and terminal moraines.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following ports is known as ‘Diamond Harbour’?
questions.explanation: Kolkata Port (Haldia seaport) is the only riverine Major Port situated on the Hugli river in West Bengal. Cochin Port or Kochi port lies on two islands in the Vembanadu Lake; Willingdon Island and Vallarpadam and is important for the export of spices and salt.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements about lakes of India: Statement I: Wular Lake in Jammu & Kashmir, one of Asia’s largest freshwater lakes, is of tectonic origin and is fed by the Jhelum River. Statement II: Dal Lake in Jammu & Kashmir is also of tectonic origin. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only I. Wular Lake, located in Jammu and Kashmir, is South Asia’s largest freshwater lake. Formed by tectonic activity, it is fed by the Jhelum River and Madhumati stream. In 1990, it was designated a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance. Dal Lake, located in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir’s summer capital, is an urban lake and the union territory’s second largest. It is popularly known as the "Lake of Flowers," "Jewel in the Crown of Kashmir," or "Srinagar’s Jewel."

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Tsomgo Lake is a glacial lake located in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Sikkim. Tsongmo Lake (Changu Lake) remains frozen during the winter season. It is revered as a holy lake by the people of Sikkim.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The Ganga plain extends between two rivers?
questions.explanation: Ghaggar and Teesta. Six Physiographic Divisions of India - 1. The Himalayan Mountains 2. The Northern Plains 3. The Peninsular Plateau 4. The Indian Desert 5. The Coastal Plains 6. The Islands. The Western part of the Northern Plain is referred to as the Punjab Plains. Brahmaputra plain lies in the state of Assam.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which river basin covers an area of 65,145 𝑘𝑚 , of which about 80% lies in 2 Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: Tapi Basin is situated in the northern part of the Deccan Plateau. Nearly 80% of the basin lies in the State of Maharashtra.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which state does the Brahmaputra river enter when it takes a U turn at Namcha Barwa?
questions.explanation: Arunachal Pradesh. The catchment area of the Brahmaputra (Tsangpo) river falls in four countries (Tibet, Bhutan, India, and Bangladesh).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which river basin covers an area of 8,60,000 𝑘𝑚 and is spread across 11 2 Indian states?
questions.explanation: Ganga Basin - 11 States. Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, West Bengal, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Delhi. Indus Basin - Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Jammu & Kashmir. Brahmaputra Basin - Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, West Bengal, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Sikkim.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which river rises near Mhow in the Malwa plateau of Madhya Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Chambal. Varuna River (Tributary of Ganga River originates in Phulpur in the Prayagraj district). Betwa River (originates from Hoshangabad, Vindhya Range, Madhya Pradesh.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In ancient times, which river was also known as 'Pooni' in Tamil which is the fourth largest river flowing in the southeast direction through the states of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu ?
questions.explanation: Kaveri River. It is a sacred river in southern India. It rises on Brahmagiri Hill of the Western Ghats in southwestern Karnataka state and drains into the Bay of Bengal through Pondicherry.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The Hundru Fall lies along the course of which of the following rivers?
questions.explanation: Subarnarekha. It is located in Ranchi District. Rajrappa waterfalls occur at the confluence of River Bhairavi and river Damodar.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: River Ken is one of the major rivers of the Bundelkhand region of central India and flows through two states, Madhya Pradesh and ______.
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh. River Ken It is a tributary of the Yamuna. The important tributaries of Ken - Alona, Bearma, Sonar, Mirhasan, Shyamari, Banne, Kutri, Urmil, Kail and Chandrawal.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following rivers form Kunchikal waterfall in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Varahi. Kunchikal Falls is located in Nidagodu village near Masthikatte in Shimoga district of state Karnataka. It cascades down rocky boulders and the total height of fall is 455 meters.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Indus River: Statement I: The Indus was called Vitasta by the Iranians and Greeks about 2500 years ago. Statement II: The term Vipasa is the Sanskrit origin of the word "Hindos". Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Neither I nor II. The river Indus was called Hindos by the Iranians and the Greeks about 2500 years ago. The word is derived from the Sanskrit word "Sindhu'', which means "river".

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: On which of the following rivers is Pakistan constructing a dam named Diamer Basha' dam?
questions.explanation: Indus. It is located between Kohistan district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Diamer district in Gilgit Baltistan, Pakistan administered Kashmir.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following waterfalls is in the state of Goa?
questions.explanation: Dudhsagar Falls is a four-tiered waterfall on the Mandovi River. Duduma Falls lies on the border of Koraput (Odisha) and Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh). Gokak Falls is on the Ghataprabha River in Belagavi, Karnataka. Shivasamudram Falls is located in Chamarajanagar and Mandya districts, Karnataka.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is the largest west flowing river in Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Luni River originates in the Pushkar valley, Aravalli Range, flows through the Thar Desert, and ends in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following states has the largest catchment area of Godavari Basin?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra. Banganga, Kadva, Shivana, Purna, Kadam, Pranahita, Indravati, Taliperu, Sabari, Nasardi, Pravara, Sindphana, Manjira, Manair, Kinnerasani are tributaries of Godavari river.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Muhuri River: Statement I: The Muhuri River is a transnational river between India and Bangladesh. Statement II: The Muhuri River originates in Tripura and later merges with the Feni River before draining into the Bay of Bengal. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both I and II.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In which Indian state is the 'Bhushi Lake' located?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra. Popular Lakes in Maharashtra - Upvan Lake, Vihar Lake, Powai Lake, Rankala Lake, Panshet Lake, Ganesh Lake, Venna Lake, Lonar Lake.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which Indian state is the source of the rivers Brahmani, Kharkai and Subarnarekha?
questions.explanation: Jharkhand. Other rivers in Jharkhand - Sone, Barakar, Damodar, Ajay, South Koel, Shankh, and North Koel river.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Gurdwara Patalpuri Sahib is located on the bank of river ______.
questions.explanation: Sutlej. Gurdwara Patalpuri Sahib located in Rupnagar district of Punjab. Guru Hargobind Ji in 1644 as well as Guru Har Rai Ji in 1661 were cremated here.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a tributary of the river Brahmaputra that flows through Bhutan?
questions.explanation: Wang Chhu River. Bhutan has four major rivers, named Drangme Chhu, Mo Chhu, Wang Chhu and Torsa Chhu. The Brahmaputra is one of the largest rivers of the Indian Subcontinent.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In which of the following states is Anchar Lake located?
questions.explanation: Jammu and Kashmir. It is located near the Soura area in the city of Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir. The lake is connected with the famous Dal Lake.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Yerla, Warna and Dindi are tributaries of the ______ river system.
questions.explanation: Krishna.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding hydrological units: Statement I: A watershed is a natural geo-hydrological unit of land that collects water and drains it through a common point by a system of streams. Statement II: Watersheds are classified based on their area — Macro (>50,000 ha), Sub-watershed (10,000–50,000 ha), Milli (1,000–10,000 ha), Micro (100–1,000 ha), and Mini (1–100 ha). Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both I and II. A watershed, also known as a drainage basin or catchment area, is an area of land where all the surface water from rain, snowmelt, etc., converges and drains into a single point, such as a river, lake, or other body of water.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A channel of a canal where water flows under the influence of gravity is called ______.
questions.explanation: flow channel. It is the flow of water induced by the effect of gravity. The surface of the flowing liquid is at atmospheric pressure and free to air. The example of open channel flow includes flow in canal, river, etc.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: On which river is Peacock Island located?
questions.explanation: Brahmaputra. Peacock Island or Umananda Island is the smallest inhabited river island in the middle of river Brahmaputra, flowing through the city of Guwahati. Its name derives from Assamese Uma. It is also known as Bhasmachal.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is Uttarakhand’s first gravity dam?
questions.explanation: Song dam which is to be built on the foothills of Mussoorie on the Song river to meet the water shortage of the state during the summers.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the rivers of Nepal: Statement I: The Karnali River, also called Ghaghara, originates on the Tibetan Plateau near Lake Manasarovar. Statement II: The Seti River is the longest river of Nepal. Which of the above statements is/are incorrect?
questions.explanation: Only II. The Karnali River is the longest river of Nepal. The river cuts through the Himalayas in Nepal and eventually joins the Sharda River at Brahmaghat in India, becoming the Ghaghara River

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which type of dam is a temporary dam constructed to exclude water from the specific area?
questions.explanation: coffer. It is built to permit damming, diversion, or dewatering and construction of a permanent structure in a dry area. A detention dam is built to catch surface runoff and stream water flow to regulate the water flow in areas below the dam. Detention dams are commonly used to reduce the damage caused by flooding or to manage the flow rate through a channel.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Suryadhar lake is located in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Uttarakhand. Famous Lakes in Uttarakhand - Auli Artificial Lake, Baraadsar Lake, Bedni Kund , Bhalu Dam, Bhimtal Lake, Bhulla Tal, Bisurital, Brahmatal Trek etc.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In which of the following states is the Sirki Waterfall located?
questions.explanation: Arunachal Pradesh. Other Waterfalls - The Nuranang Waterfall, the Bap Teng Kang Waterfall.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Rain is liquid ______.
questions.explanation: Precipitation is any product of the condensation of atmospheric water vapor that falls under gravitational pull from clouds. The main forms of precipitation include drizzling, rain, sleet, snow, ice pellets, graupel and hail.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following dams is located in Jharkhand?
questions.explanation: Maithon dam is on the river Barakar in the district Dhanbad of Jharkhand. It has an underground power station, the first of its own kind in the whole of SouthEast Asia.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Assertion (A): The mouth of the Indus River lies to the north of the Tropic of Cancer. Reason (R): The rivers Mahanadi, Krishna, and Godavari lie to the south of the Tropic of Cancer.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A. The Tropic of Cancer is an imaginary line on the Earth's surface, located at approximately 23.5 degrees North latitude. In India, the Tropic of Cancer passes through eight states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What kind of depositional landforms are formed when streams flowing from higher levels break into foot slope plains of low gradient?
questions.explanation: Alluvial fans. A point bar is a depositional feature made of alluvium that accumulates on the inside bend of streams and rivers below the slip-off slope. An alluvial fan is a triangle-shaped deposit of gravel, sand, and even smaller pieces of sediment, such as silt

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Where is the Baglihar Dam located?
questions.explanation: Jammu and Kashmir. Baglihar dam is a run-of-the-river power project on the Chenab river. Important Dams - Kadana Dam (Gujarat), Chamera Dam (Himachal Pradesh), Singur Dam (Telangana).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following has the highest salinity?
questions.explanation: Lake Van. Being the largest lake in Turkey, it has the highest salinity (330%). As a saline soda lake fed by small streams, it is one of the few endorheic lakes over 3,000 square kilometers. High salinity usually prevents it from freezing, despite high altitude and winter temperatures below 0 °C (32 °F).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements about river landforms: 1. A river in its middle course is capable of forming meanders due to both erosion and deposition. 2. Landforms such as V-shaped valleys and waterfalls are typically associated with the upper course of a river. Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. A meander is a U-shaped bend in a river formed by erosion and deposition. A V-shaped valley is created by river erosion. A waterfall is where water drops vertically over a ledge. A delta forms at a river's mouth where it meets the sea or ocean.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: As of 2021, which is the world's largest drainage basin with an area of about 70,00,000 km2 ?
questions.explanation: Amazon basin. The Amazon Basin, formed by numerous tributaries, drains parts of Brazil, Peru, Bolivia, Ecuador, Colombia, and a small section of Venezuela. It lies directly on the equator and experiences a hot, humid climate year-round, with both day and night feeling equally warm and sticky. High rainfall, high temperature, and high humidity are the features of the basin.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is the largest artificial lake of Asia?
questions.explanation: Bhopal Lake, also known as Bhojtal, was created in the 11th century by King Bhoja of the Paramara dynasty. It is situated in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, and is constructed on Kolans river. Lakes in Madhya Pradesh: Sangram Sagar, Shahpura lake. Dal Lake - It is often referred to as Srinagar's Jewel, is a freshwater lake located in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which river originates south of the equator and flows north through north-eastern Africa to drain into the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.explanation: Nile River. Its length is about 6,695 kilometers (4,160 miles). The Nile basin is huge and includes parts of Tanzania, Burundi, Rwanda, Congo (Kinshasa), Kenya. Other important rivers of the world : Lena River : Origin - Baikal range, Drains - Laptev Sea. Amazon River : Origin - Andes Mountains, Drains - Atlantic Ocean. Congo River (cross the equator twice) : Origin - Africa Rift, Drains - Atlantic Ocean.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.chapter_name: Minerals and Energy Resources in India
questions.question: Name the state which is the largest producer of lignite coal ?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu. Coal is a vital mineral in India, mainly used for thermal power generation and iron smelting. It is found in Gondwana and Tertiary deposits, with about 80% being non-coking bituminous coal. Major Gondwana coalfields lie in the Damodar Valley, with Jharia being the largest and Raniganj the second. Important coal mining centres include Singrauli, Korba, Talcher, Chanda–Wardha, and Singareni, while Tertiary coal is found in Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, and Nagaland. Lignite deposits occur in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Gujarat, and Jammu & Kashmir.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.chapter_name: Minerals and Energy Resources in India
questions.question: Name the major coal producing region located in Telangana state?
questions.explanation: Singareni Coalfield. These coal reserves are located in the Pranhita -Godavari Valley and are managed by The Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL), a government-owned coal mining company. This coalfield is a crucial source of coal for the power plants and other industries in Southern India. Major coalfields in India: Raniganj Coalfield (West Bengal), Talcher Coalfield (Odisha), Jharia (Jharkhand), Korba (Chhattisgarh).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.chapter_name: Minerals and Energy Resources in India
questions.question: Which of the following river valleys is NOT known for coal deposits in India ?
questions.explanation: Satluj. The Satluj originates in the 'Raksas tal' near Mansarovar at an altitude of 4,555 m in Tibet where it is known as Langchen Khambab. Satluj, is the longest of the five rivers that flow through the historic crossroads region of Punjab in northern India and Pakistan. The Damodar Valley is particularly rich in coal and is known as the "Ruhr of India" because of its similarities to the coal-rich Ruhr region of Germany.

questions.subject: Geography

questions.question: Match the following mineral deposits with their respective states: List – I (Mineral Deposits/Regions) List – II (States) (a) Panchpatmali (Bauxite) 1. Madhya Pradesh (b) Balaghat (Manganese) 2.Odisha (c) Khetri (Copper) 3.Andhra Pradesh (d) Nellore Belt (Mica) 4.Rajasthan
questions.explanation: a-2, b-1, c-4, d-3. Panchpatmali deposits in Koraput district are the most important bauxite deposits in the state. Important Mines deposit in India: Balaghat mines (Madhya Pradesh), Khetri mines (Rajasthan), Maikal hills (Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh), Nellore mica belt (Andhra Pradesh), Kudremukh mines (Karnataka).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.chapter_name: Minerals and Energy Resources in India
questions.question: Which of the following is a precious mineral?
questions.explanation: Platinum. It is used in hard disk drives, thermocouples, optical fibers, LCDs, turbine blades, and spark plugs. Hematite: A common iron ore used in iron production. Platinum-based drugs cisplatin, carboplatin, and oxaliplatin are widely used for chemotherapeutic eradication of cancer. Mica: A group of silicate minerals used in various industrial applications, including electronics and construction. Bauxite: The primary ore of aluminum.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.chapter_name: Minerals and Energy Resources in India
questions.question: Which type of coal is found in Damodar valley?
questions.explanation: Bituminous is a type of coal with a carbon content ranging from 60% to 80% and a relatively low moisture content, making it highly efficient for energy production. It has a high calorific value. The Damodar Valley, located in the states of Jharkhand and West Bengal in eastern India, is renowned for its extensive bituminous coal deposits. This region is part of the Jharia and Raniganj coalfields, which are significant contributors to India's coal production.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.chapter_name: Minerals and Energy Resources in India
questions.question: Which of the following is an inosilicate amphibole mineral used in highway construction and as railroad ballast?
questions.explanation: Hornblende: It is an inosilicate amphibole mineral. Uses: Highway construction: As an aggregate for road bases and surfaces. Railroad ballast: To provide drainage and stability under railroad tracks.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.chapter_name: Minerals and Energy Resources in India
questions.question: Which coal is low-grade, brown and soft with high moisture content?
questions.explanation: Lignite. Bituminous: Medium-grade, black, and less moisture content than lignite, used for electricity, industrial, and domestic purposes. Anthracite: High-grade, hard, black, and very low moisture content, used for residential heating and industrial processes. Tamil Nadu is the largest producer of lignite in India.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.chapter_name: Minerals and Energy Resources in India
questions.question: Match the following renewable sources of energy with their producing regions in India correctly. Renewable source of energy Regions in India 1. Tidal energy a. Gulf of Khambhat 2. Wind energy b. Nagercoil 3. Geo Thermal energy c. Puga valley
questions.explanation: 1-a, 2-b, 3-c. Renewable energy comes from natural sources that are regenerated more quickly than they are used up. They are natural and self-replenishing, and usually have a low￾or zero-carbon footprint. Examples of renewable energy sources include wind power, solar power, bioenergy (organic matter burned as a fuel) and hydroelectric.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.chapter_name: Minerals and Energy Resources in India
questions.question: The district of Shivamogga that is famous for its Iron-Ore and Manganese mineral is located in which state of India?
questions.explanation: Karnataka. Other famous mines in India: Panna and Bunder Project - Madhya Pradesh. West Singhbhum, Pahadia, Kunderkocha and Parasi - Jharkhand. Bailadila iron ore and Dalli-Rajhara - Chhattisgarh. Ratnagiri - Maharashtra. Sundergarh, Joda, Keonjhar and Jajpur - Odisha.

questions.subject: Geography

questions.subject: Geography
questions.chapter_name: Minerals and Energy Resources in India
questions.question: Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh states are rich with ____________ material deposits.
questions.explanation: Coal. Jharkhand - 40% of the country's total mineral resources are available here. It produces coking coal, uranium, and pyrite. Jharkhand ranks 1st in the production of coal, mica, kyanite, and copper in India. Major coal fields include Jharia, Bokaro, Karanpura, Hutar, Auranga, Daltonganj, Deoghar, and Rajmahal. Chhattisgarh: A leading producer of coal, dolomite, bauxite, and iron ore. Major coal-producing areas include Korea, Korba, Raigarh, and Sarguja districts.

questions.subject: Geography

questions.question: The Salal Project, also called the Salal Hydroelectric Power Station, is on which river?

The beneficiary states are Uttar Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Himachal Pradesh, Chandigarh & Rajasthan. Important hydel power stations and the rivers on which they are located: Bhakra Nangal (Sutlej River), Gandhi Sagar Dam (Chambal River), and Nagarjuna Sagar Dam (Krishna River).

questions.subject: Geography

questions.question: Which of the following agencies is responsible for the operation and maintenance of the Hazira- Vijaypur￾Jagdishpur pipeline?
questions.explanation: Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) is India's first cross-country natural gas pipeline commissioned in 1987-88 with compressor stations at Hazira, Jhabua (Madhya Pradesh), Vijaipur (Madhya Pradesh) and Auraiya (Uttar Pradesh). questions.subject: Geography

questions.subject: Geography

questions.question: What are the main energy sources for earth's internal heat engine?

options.a: Radiogenic heat and oceanic tide heat
options.b: Heat from volcanoes and solar heat
options.c: Solar heat and oceanic tide heat

An Export Processing Zone (EPZ) is a customs area that allows import of machinery and raw materials for manufacturing export goods without payment of duty. 3. Farakka is also an Export Processing Zone in West Bengal. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. Farakka is known for its barrage, not an EPZ.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Given below are the Assertion and Reason, choose the correct options regarding both the statements. Assertion (A): Seasonal agricultural practices, such as stubble burning, have no significant impact on AQI levels in India. Reason (R): Stubble burning is a controlled practice that doesn't release substantial pollutants into the atmosphere.

options.a: A is true, but R is false.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: Both A and R are false.
options.d: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are false.
questions.explanation: Both A and R are false. Seasonal stubble burning in North India is a major cause of severe air pollution, raising AQI to hazardous levels. This uncontrolled practice releases large amounts of PM2.5, PM10, carbon monoxide, and toxic gases into the

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: High honey yield and gentle behaviour in bees for commercial beekeeping can be achieved through one of the following methods:

options.a: Using wild bee species with aggressive defence traits
options.b: Frequently relocating hives to prevent bees from settling
options.c: Avoiding bee farms and relying solely on natural honey collection
options.d: Introducing Italian bees that collect more honey and remain in hives longer

questions.answer_text: Introducing Italian bees that collect more honey and remain in hives longer
questions.explanation: Italian bees (Apis mellifera ligustica) are preferred in commercial apiculture because they are gentle in nature, highly productive, and stay longer in hives. They gather more nectar compared to indigenous species, making them suitable for large-scale honey production. Unlike wild or aggressive species, they are easier to manage, ensuring higher yield and safer beekeeping practices.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Match the columns: Column A (Cropping Season) Column B (Major Crops - Shuffled) A. Kharif (June-September) 1. Vegetables, Fruits , Fodder B. Rabi (October-March) 2. Rice, Cotton, Bajra, Maize, Jowar, Tur C. Zaid (April-June) 3. Wheat, Gram, Rapeseeds and Mustard, Barley
questions.explanation: A-2, B-3, C-1. Kharif Crops (Monsoon season: June–Sept). Sown with onset of monsoon, harvested in autumn. Examples: Rice, Cotton, Bajra, Maize, Jowar, Tur (Pigeon pea). Rabi Crops (Winter season: Oct–March). Sown in winter, harvested in spring. Examples: Wheat, Gram, Rapeseed, Mustard, Barley. Zaid Crops (Summer season: April–June). Short-season crops grown between Rabi and Kharif. Examples: Vegetables, Fruits (melon, cucumber), Fodder.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Match the local names of shifting agriculture with the states where they are practiced: List I (Local Name) List II (State/Region) a. Penda 1. Odisha b. Bringa 2. Andhra Pradesh c. Dahiya 3. Madhya Pradesh d. Jhumming 4. North-Eastern region
questions.explanation: a-2, b-1, c-3, d-4. In India, shifting agriculture is called ‘Bewar’ or ‘Dahiya’ in Madhya Pradesh, ‘Podu’ or ‘Penda’ in Andhra Pradesh, ‘Pama Dabi’ or ‘Koman’ or ‘Bringa’ in Odisha, ‘Kumari’ in Western Ghats, ‘Valre’ or ‘Waltre’ in South-eastern Rajasthan, ‘Khil’ in the Himalayan belt, ‘Kuruwa’ in Jharkhand, and‘Jhumming’ in the North-eastern region.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The term 'Aus', 'Aman' and 'Boro' are associated with which crop in India?
questions.explanation: Paddy is basically a tropical crop. 'Aus', 'Aman' and 'Boro' are grown in states like Assam, West Bengal, and Odisha throughout the year. Aus: Sown in the summer, along with pre-monsoonal rains, and harvested in the autumn. Aman: Sown in the monsoon and harvested in the winter. Boro: Sown in the winter and harvested in the summer.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which type of tea in large amount is exported from India to importing countries?
questions.explanation: Black tea. India is the world's second largest tea producer after China. The types of tea exported through India are: Black tea, Regular tea, Green tea, Herbal tea, Masala tea, and Lemon tea. The majority of the tea exported out of India is black tea which makes up about 96% of the total exports.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The people of Himachal Pradesh make channels to bring water from a glacier or rainwater to villages for the function of mainly irrigation. These channels are locally known as:
questions.explanation: Guls or Kuls. In hill and mountainous regions, people built diversion channels like the ‘guls’ or ‘kuls’ of the Western Himalayas for agriculture. Water harvesting system: ‘Rooftop rain water harvesting’ was commonly practised to store drinking water, particularly in Rajasthan. In arid and semi-arid regions, agricultural fields were converted into rain fed storage structures that allowed the water to stand and moisten the soil like the ‘khadins’ in Jaisalmer and ‘Johads’ in other parts of Rajasthan. Roof top rain water harvesting is the most common practice in Shillong, Meghalaya.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following states is the biggest producer of Pulses?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh. Based on the production estimates for the year 2022-23, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Rajasthan are the top three pulses producing states in the country. India is the largest producer of pulses in the world.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines the green revolution?

options.a: It is a new strategy in agriculture to produce food grains, especially wheat and rice.
options.b: It is a new strategy to increase the share of the forest.
options.c: It is a new strategy to use green colour for all purposes.
options.d: It is a new strategy to use only herbal products.

questions.answer_text: It is a new strategy in agriculture to produce food grains, especially wheat and rice.
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution, starting in the 1960s, aimed to achieve food security and reduce food imports, particularly in India. It involved the introduction of high-yielding variety seeds, mechanized farming, improved irrigation, and the use of pesticides and fertilizers.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: According to the Agricultural and Processed food products Export Development Authority (APEDA) 2020-2021, which state of India has the first rank in grapes production?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra. APEDA was established in 1986, operates under the Ministry of Commerce and Trade to promote the export of agricultural and processed food products.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The green revolution technology resulted in an increase in production of cereal production from 72.4 million tons in 1965-66 to ________ million tons in 1978-79.
questions.explanation: 131.9. The cereal production was increased due to three factors: (i) Increase in net area under cultivation; (ii) Growing two or more crops in a year on the same piece of land; and (iii) Use of HYV seeds.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Second Green Revolution Cell: 1. The headquarters of the Second Green Revolution (SGR) Cell is located at ICAR–Research Complex for Eastern Region (RCER), Patna. 2. The benefits of the first Green Revolution were mainly confined to the eastern region of India. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. The Second Green Revolution (SGR) Cell was created by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare, Government of India to improve agricultural productivity and livelihood in the Eastern region of India because the benefits of first Green Revolution were mainly confined to north-western states of Haryana, Punjab and western Uttar Pradesh.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the aims of National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) of India is/are correct? 1. To make agriculture more productive. 2. To make agriculture more sustainable. 3. To promote organic farming.
questions.explanation: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) has been made operational from the year 2014-15 which aims at making agriculture more productive, sustainable, remunerative and climate resilient by promoting location specific integrated /composite farming systems; soil and moisture conservation measures; comprehensive soil health management; efficient water management practices and mainstreaming rainfed technologies.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What was a significant negative environmental impact of the Green Revolution?
questions.explanation: Soil degradation. The Green Revolution caused soil fertility loss through the use of chemical fertilizers. Chemical fertilizers also kill bacteria and other microorganisms in the soil. Green Revolution also led to groundwater depletion due to extensive tubewell irrigation, impacting long-term environmental resources.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: How was the growth in all food grains after the Green Revolution?
questions.explanation: Disproportionate. Larger farmers with more resources were able to afford the necessary inputs, like high-yield variety (HYV) seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation, and thus reaped greater benefits. Smaller farmers often lacked access to these resources and faced higher risks, as the HYV crops were more vulnerable to pests, potentially causing severe losses. About 65 percent of the country’s population continued to be employed in agriculture even as late as 1990.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What was the main objective of the Second Green Revolution in India?

options.a: Ensuring food security in the western states
options.c: Focusing on holistic development in agriculture
options.d: Increasing the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides

questions.answer_text: Focusing on holistic development in agriculture
questions.explanation: In the second phase of the green revolution (mid-1970s to mid-1980s), the HYV technology spread to a larger number of states and benefited more variety of crops. The spread of green revolution technology enabled India to achieve self-sufficiency in food grains.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following movements created regional disparities between large and small farmers in India?
questions.explanation: Green revolution in India started with the aim of increasing India's agricultural production to make India self-sufficient in food grains.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct? I. The first green revolution led to over-exploitation of natural resources. II. The second Green Revolution was more focused on Southern India. III. The second green revolution ensured in achieving sustainable livelihood security.
questions.explanation: I and III. The Second Green Revolution focuses on sustainable agriculture in eastern India, rainfed areas, and small farmers, promoting climate￾resilient practices and livelihood security.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What action was taken by the government to celebrate the achievement of the Green Revolution in agriculture?

options.a: Released a regular salary for the farmers
options.b: Distributed free food to all the people
options.d: Distributed green vegetables to the people

questions.explanation: Green Revolution : The term was first used by William Gaud, with Norman Borlaug recognized as its global father and M.S. Swaminathan was the father of the Green Revolution in India. India adopted a new agricultural strategy, boosting wheat and rice production. In July 1968, Prime Minister Indira Gandhi commemorated its success by releasing a special stamp titled "Wheat Revolution."

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the economic justification for subsidies in the agriculture sector?

options.a: It is mostly used to provide benefits for rich farmers.
options.b: It is a part of government expenditure in the service sector.
options.c: It is an incentive to provide the benefits of advanced technology and decrease the cost of production.
options.d: It is used to provide benefits for capital goods producers in agriculture.

questions.answer_text: It is an incentive to provide the benefits of advanced technology and decrease the cost of production.
questions.explanation: Agricultural subsidies support food security and development by helping farmers boost production, improve food availability, and reduce poverty. Input subsidies lower costs, incentivize adoption, increase productivity, and stimulate economic growth.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In West Bengal, how many rice crops are grown in a year?
questions.explanation: Three. In states like Assam, West Bengal, and Odisha, three paddy crops are grown annually: Aus, Aman, and Boro.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In the given main characteristics of farming which is NOT a characteristic of the Indian commercial farming?
questions.explanation: Slash and burn farming is a form of shifting agriculture where natural vegetation is cut down and burned to clear the land for cultivation. In commercial farming, higher doses of modern inputs are used to obtain higher productivity. The degree of commercialization in agriculture varies from one region to another. For example, rice is a commercial crop in Haryana and Punjab, but in Odisha, it is a subsistence crop.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following types of crops are sown after the end of the monsoon season?
questions.explanation: Rabi crops. It is an agricultural crop that is sown in the winter and harvested in the spring.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the consequences of the Green Revolution?

options.b: Rising prices and a shift in the mode of payment of agricultural workers from payment in cash to payment in kind (grain)
options.d: The rich grew richer and many of the poor stagnated or grew poorer

questions.answer_text: Rising prices and a shift in the mode of payment of agricultural workers from payment in cash to payment in kind (grain)
questions.explanation: Impact of Green Revolution : Positive - Increase in production and productivity of food grains, reduction in hunger, and technological advancements in agriculture. Negative - Decline in Soil fertility, High production costs, Regional disparities.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Match the following names of primitive forms of cultivation in different states correctly. States Name of Primitive form of cultivation 1. Madhya Pradesh a. Penda 2. Andhra Pradesh b. Bewar 3. Odisha c. Kuruwa 4. Jharkhand d. Bringa

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Match the items in List I with those in List II. List I List II i. Blue revolution a. Oilseeds ii. Yellow revolution b. Overall horticulture iii. Round revolution c. Fish iv. Golden revolution d. Potato
questions.explanation: i-c, ii-a, iii -d, iv-b. Agricultural Revolutions in India: Green Revolution - To increase agricultural productivity, White Revolution - Milk production, Black Revolution - Petroleum products, Brown Revolution - Leather / Cocoa / Non-Conventional Products, Golden Fiber Revolution - Jute Production, Silver Revolution - Egg Production / Poultry Production, Red Revolution - Meat Production / Tomato Production.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following types of crops are sown at the beginning of the monsoon season?
questions.explanation: Kharif crops. These crops are typically planted during June to September and harvested in the post-monsoon season (October to November). Examples of Kharif crops include rice, maize, cotton, and sorghum. Rabi crops are sown after the monsoon season, usually in the winter months (October to December), and harvested in the spring (March to May). Zaid crops are grown in the intervening period between Kharif and Rabi seasons, typically in the summer months (March to June).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following statement/s about the Green Revolution is/are CORRECT? I. India became self-sufficient with the introduction of the Green Revolution. II. The Green Revolution led to loss of nutrients in the soil from farming the same crop over and over again. III. The Green Revolution led to depletion of fresh ground water.
questions.explanation: I, II and III. The Green Revolution resulted in a great increase in production of food grains (especially wheat and rice) due to the introduction into developing countries of new, high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds. The green revolution enabled the government to procure sufficient amounts of food grains to build a stock which could be used in times of food shortage.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following statements are true about the positive impact of the Green Revolution (GR) on yield levels in India? I. During the post GR period, the yield of rice grew at a much faster rate than that of wheat. II. GR technology had penetrated more in wheat crop than in the rice crop. III. During post GR period, the area under rice achieved a relatively slow growth when compared to the area under wheat.
questions.explanation: Only ii and iii. The Green Revolution technology had a greater impact on wheat crops than on rice crops. Important Crops in the Revolution: Main crops were - Wheat, Rice, Jowar, Bajra and Maize. Non-food grains were excluded from the ambit of the new strategy. Wheat remained the mainstay of the Green Revolution for years. Mankombu Sambasivan Swaminathan is known as the "Father of India's Green Revolution" for his work to increase food production and alleviate world hunger.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of these is NOT true of the second phase of the green revolution?

options.a: It was adopted by farmers living in dry and semi-arid regions of India.
options.b: It was launched in areas with a significant shift from dry to wet (irrigated) cultivation.
options.c: It covered the period of the 1960s and 1970s.
options.d: It covered the period of the 1980s.

questions.answer_text: It covered the period of the 1960s and 1970s.
questions.explanation: The use of HYV seeds was restricted to the more affluent states such as Punjab, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu in the 1st Phase(Mid 1960s to mid-1970s). In the second phase of the green revolution (mid-1970s to mid-1980s), the HYV technology spread to a larger number of states and benefited more variety of crops.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Who among the following is NOT associated with the Green Revolution?
questions.explanation: P Chidambaram. Green Revolution: Initiated by - Norman Borlaug (1960s). He is known as the ‘Father of Green Revolution’ in world. He received the Nobel prize (1970) for developing High yielding varieties (HYVs) of wheat. M.S. Swaminathan (Father of Green Revolution in India). The Green revolution came under the third five year plan (1961-66). Chidambaram Subramaniam was an Indian politician and agricultural scientist who played a crucial role in India's Green Revolution. Award - Bharat Ratna (1998).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Identify the crop which is grown in Kharif cropping season in Northern States of India.
questions.explanation: Rice. Kharif is sown during the rainy season, typically from June to September in India. Examples include paddy, maize, soybean, groundnut, and cotton. Rabi grows in the winter season, from October to March. Examples include wheat, gram, peas, mustard, and linseed. In between the rabi and the kharif seasons, there is a short season during the summer months known as the Zaid season. Examples are watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In which of the following ways were farmers encouraged to begin to use high yielding variety seeds ?

options.a: Farmers’ children were given free education in government colleges and universities.
options.b: Agricultural labourers were paid wages directly by the government.
options.c: Farmers were given monetary support in cash to cultivate food grains.
options.d: The government provided seeds and other inputs at prices lower than those prevailing in the market.

questions.answer_text: The government provided seeds and other inputs at prices lower than those prevailing in the market.
questions.explanation: Farmers were encouraged to use high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds during the Green Revolution through various forms of support from the government. The government made HYV seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, and irrigation systems available at subsidized prices, meaning they were cheaper than market rates. This helped reduce the financial burden on farmers and incentivized them to adopt new agricultural technologies. HYV seeds are resistant to insects and diseases and are known for their high yields.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an agro-based industry?
questions.explanation: Fertiliser. Agro-based industries depend on agricultural raw materials, producing mainly consumer goods. Major industries include cotton, jute, textiles, and edible oil. India's first sugar mill was established in Pratappur, Uttar Pradesh, in 1903. The Sugar Cane Act of 1934 allowed state governments to set the minimum price for sugarcane.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true with regard to the Green Revolution?

options.a: Cultivation became more intensive in nature.
options.b: In its second phase, there was a shift to from dry to wet (irrigated) cultivation in dry and semi-arid regions of India.
options.c: Cultivation became more extensive in nature.
options.d: There was change in the cropping pattern and types of crops grown in its second phase.

questions.answer_text: Cultivation became more extensive in nature.
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution did not focus on expanding the area under cultivation but rather on making the existing land more productive (intensive cultivation), using modern inputs and technology.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which crops are benefitted from the temperate cyclones arising from the Mediterranean Sea that cause rainfall in Punjab?
questions.explanation: Rabi crops. Temperate cyclones cause rainfall in Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and western Uttar Pradesh. The precipitation is in the form of snowfall in the lower Himalayas. It is this snow that sustains the flow of water in the Himalayan rivers during the summer months. The precipitation goes on decreasing from west to east in the plains and from north to south in the mountains.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In July 1968, Indira Gandhi, the then Prime Minister of India, officially recorded impressive strides of the Green Revolution in agriculture by releasing a special stamp entitled _________ .
questions.explanation: Wheat Revolution (Part of Green Revolution) was initiated under the Third Five Year Plan (1961-66) by introducing high-yielding varieties of seeds of rice and wheat.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following reasons can be attributed to the excessive pressure on agricultural land in India? A. Right of inheritance B. Size of unprofitable land holding C. Division of land D. Multiple cropping
questions.explanation: A, B and C. Reasons that cause pressure on Agriculture: The right of inheritance, Division of land, Rising population, Use of Excessive Chemical Fertilizer, Salinization of soil, Desertification, Urbanisation, Waterlogging, Climate Change, Droughts, Pollution etc.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following countries is related with high yielding variety seeds that are used as part of Green Revolution policies in India?
questions.explanation: Mexico. Green Revolution - A period that began in the 1960s during which agriculture in India was converted into a modern industrial system by the adoption of technology (The use of high yielding variety (HYV) seeds, mechanised farm tools, irrigation facilities, pesticides, and fertilizers).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding rice varieties in India: 1. IR8, also called Miracle Rice, was first harvested in 1967 and helped India overcome a massive famine. 2. Golden Rice, developed in 1998, is genetically modified to contain pro-vitamin A. 3. PETA is the high-yielding semi-dwarf rice variety developed by the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) in 1967. Which of the above statements is/are incorrect?
questions.explanation: 2 and 3 only. IR8 is a high-yielding semi-dwarf rice variety developed by the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI). Golden rice: A transgenic rice having a gene for carotene. It was first introduced in 1999 by Ingo Potrykus and Peter Beyer. It contains pro-vitamin A which upon ingestion is converted to vitamin A in the human body.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: For Kharif crops, the temperature required for farming is above 25 degrees Celsius with high humidity and annual rainfall above ________ cm.
questions.explanation: 100. Kharif crops are sown during the monsoon season, which lasts from June to September in India.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Green Revolution in India: 1. Punjab was the most transformed state due to the Green Revolution. 2. The Green Revolution had maximum impact in Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh. 3. The eastern region, including Assam, Bihar, West Bengal, and Odisha, was the most benefitted from the Green Revolution. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. Statement 3 is incorrect because the eastern region had minimal impact, not maximum, from the Green Revolution.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The agricultural land below the main canal water level forms the ______.
questions.explanation: command area. Lift system - Water is lifted from lower level to higher level with the help of pumps and other equipment. Flow system - The type of irrigation in which water is available at a higher level to enable supply to the land by gravity flow. Warabandi - It is a system of rotation of supply of water according to a predetermined schedule as per area and crop needs specifying the day, time and duration of supply to each holding to ensure equitable water distribution among farmers of an outlet command.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: _______ land is suitable for regular cropping.
questions.explanation: Arable land is the land under temporary crops, temporary meadows for mowing or for pasture, land under market or kitchen gardens, and temporary fallow. It is capable of being ploughed and used to grow crops. Barren land - Land that normally cannot be brought under cultivation with the available technology. Marginal land - Land that has little or no agricultural Value.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which group of crops belong to fibre crops and are produced on a large scale in India ?
questions.explanation: Jute and Hemp. Jute is known as Golden Fibre. It grows well on well-drained fertile soils in the floodplains. MajorJute producing states (West Bengal, Bihar, Assam, Odisha and Meghalaya).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following crops is the only genetically modified (GM) crop approved for commercial cultivation in India?
questions.explanation: Bt Cotton. GM crops : These are derived from plants whose genes are artificially modified, usually by inserting genetic material from another organism. India approved the release of Bt cotton (Cry 1 AC) for commercial cultivation in 2002 - Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu. The best known variety of GM rice is golden rice.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Extensive cultivation refers to farming on large farms with moderately low inputs of labour and capital. 2. Hybrid cultivation is the practice of cultivating crops only on small plots of land with no use of hybrid seeds. Which of the above statements is/are incorrect?
questions.explanation: 2 only. Hybrid cultivation - It involves the use of hybrid seed varieties (created by crossbreeding two or more genetically distinct plants). Example - Wheat - Sonalika and Kalyan Sona, Rice - Jaya and Ratna.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following crops is classified as fine grain?
questions.explanation: Wheat. India produces a variety of cereals, which are classified into fine grains (rice, wheat) and coarse grains (jowar, bajra, maize, ragi, etc.).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is the most suitable application of rainwater harvesting?
questions.explanation: Irrigation. Rainwater harvesting is the process of collecting, storing, and purifying rainwater from rooftops, parks, roads, and open grounds. It is used for drinking, domestic needs, livestock, small irrigation, and replenishing groundwater levels.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is meant by subsistence agriculture ?

options.a: Agricultural output is sufficient for the country.
options.d: Agriculturists produce primarily for the market.

questions.explanation: Types of Subsistence Farming : Primitive subsistence farming or shifting cultivation (oldest form of agriculture) - It happens on a self-sufficient basis, and farmers raise food according to their family’s needs. The trees are cut down and burnt and the cleared land is cultivated. Other names: Shifting cultivation or slash and burn cultivation. Intensive subsistence farming - The farmer cultivates a small plot of land using simple tools and more. More than one crop is cultivated during a year.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following states of India still uses the ancient bamboo drip irrigation method?
questions.explanation: Meghalaya. Bamboo drip irrigation system is tapping stream and spring water by using bamboo pipes.
