questions.explanation: Subtropical high pressure belts (Horse latitude) extend 30° N and 30° S. It is formed because the warm air rising from the equator moves towards the tropics in both hemispheres. Equatorial Low - Pressure belt extends from 0 to 5° North and South. The subpolar low pressure belt extends around latitudes 60° to 70° North and South. High Pressure belts are located at 70°- 90° North and South latitudes. There are majorly seven Pressure Belts on the surface of Earth i.e., the Equatorial Low, two Subtropical Highs, two Subpolar Lows, and two Polar Highs.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: When the grains of sand are very fine and light , the wind can carry it over a very long distance . When such sand is deposited in large areas, it is called_____.
questions.explanation: Loess. It is a clastic, predominantly silt-sized sediment that is formed by the accumulation of wind - blown dust.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the main reasons for the excessive cold in north India during the cold weather season and identify which of the statements are correct. 1. States like Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan, being far away from the moderating influence of sea, experience continental climate. 2. The snowfall in the nearby Himalayan ranges creates a cold wave situation. 3. Around February, the cold winds coming from the Caspian Sea and Turkmenistan bring a cold wave along with frost and fog over the northwestern parts of India.
questions.explanation: 1, 2 and 3. Coastal areas have moderate temperatures because the land absorbs and radiates heat much faster than sea. So, during the day cool air from the sea rushes towards the land and during the night cool air from the land rushes towards the sea.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Low annual range of temperature and high annual rainfall are characteristics of a _________.
questions.explanation: Tropical Humid Climate: Low range of temperature, Rainfall exceeds evapotranspiration for at least 270 days in a year, between Tropic of Cancer and Capricorn.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following codes signify Cold Climate with Dry Winters according to Koeppen’s classification?
questions.explanation: Dw. Koeppen recognised six major climatic groups based on seasonal precipitation and temperature patterns. The six main groups are A (tropical), B (arid), C (temperate), D (continental), E (polar) and H (highland).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The cold snow forest climate is found largely in the continental region in the Northern Hemisphere between _______ northern latitudes in Europe, Asia and North America
questions.explanation: 40°-70°. India has a tropical climate because of the Himalayan

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In early November, the low Pressure conditions shift over the Bay of Bengal. This transfer is related to cyclonic low pressure, which originates over ________.
questions.explanation: Andaman Sea (Burma sea in Thai) is a body of water to the southeast of the Bay of Bengal, south of Myanmar, west of Thailand and east of the Andaman Islands; it is a part of the Indian Ocean.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Name the port that is privately owned by the Adani Group?
questions.explanation: Mundra Port, Gujarat. Mundra Port, located in Gujarat, is India’s largest private commercial port, owned and operated by the Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ) under the Adani Group. It handles bulk, container, and liquid cargo, and has emerged as a key hub for India’s international trade, unlike other government-owned major ports.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement from the following.

options.a: The development of the cotton textile industry in Britain led to the decline of Indian textile producers.
options.b: Cotton clothes made in England had driven Indian clothes out of the markets of Europe and America in the beginning of the 20th century.
options.c: The Sale and Devang communities of South India were famous for weaving.
options.d: The first cotton textile mill in India was established in Bombay in 1854.

questions.answer_text: Cotton clothes made in England had driven Indian clothes out of the markets of Europe and America in the beginning of the 20th century.
questions.explanation: By the beginning of the 20th century, India was not competing in European and American markets because British policies had already eliminated Indian textile exports to these regions by the 19th century. The decline of Indian textiles in international markets occurred much earlier, during the late 18th and 19th centuries, following the Industrial Revolution in Britain.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Identify the oldest iron and steel company of India from the following options.
questions.explanation: Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO): Founded by Jamsetji Tata and Dorabji Tata in 1907, It is located in Jamshedpur (Jharkhand). Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Plant: Founded in 1923, this plant is situated in Bhadravathi (Karnataka), and specializes in the production of pig iron and steel. Indian Iron and Steel Company (IISCO): Established in 1918, IISCO is an integrated steel plant located in Burnpur (West Bengal) and is part of Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Identify the group of districts that are NOT an example of industrial districts of India.
questions.explanation: Alwar and Bhiwani. Cuttack (Odisha) is known for textile and handicraft industries, especially the silver filigree (Tarakasi) work. Kota (Rajasthan) is famous for its engineering and chemical industries. Kanpur is a significant industrial hub, historically known for its leather and textile industries. It is sometimes called the "Manchester of the East." Agra is widely known for its tourism, but it also has industries related to leather goods, footwear, and marble stone carving. Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh) is known for ordnance factories, defense-related industries, and manufacturing units. Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh) is a major industrial center with industries like electrical goods, chemicals, and the famous Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements about industries in India: Statement I: BHEL (Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited) is a public sector industry established in 1964, headquartered in New Delhi. Statement II: Reliance, Tata, and Adani Groups are public sector industries. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only I. Reliance Industries Limited is an Indian multinational company based in Mumbai, Maharashtra. It was founded by Dhirubhai Ambani. The Tata Group is one of India's oldest and largest business conglomerates. It was founded in 1868 by Jamsetji Tata. The Adani Group is an Indian multinational conglomerate based in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. It was founded in 1988 by Gautam Adani.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a major industrial region of India?

India has several industrial regions like Mumbai￾Pune cluster, Bangalore-Tamil Nadu region, Hugli region, Ahmedabad -Baroda region, Chottanagpur industrial belt, Vishakhapatnam-Guntur belt, Gurgaon -Delhi-Meerut region and the Kollam -Thiruvanathapuram industrial cluster.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Where was the first successful textile mill established in India?
questions.explanation: Mumbai. The first successful textile mill in India was the Bombay Spinning and Weaving Company, established in 1854 in Bombay (now Mumbai) by Cowasjee Nanabhoy Davar, a Parsi businessman and banker. Located in Tardeo, Bombay, it began production in 1856.

Surat - It is an important silk weaving center of India and is famous for silk brocades. Rajkot - It is popular for traditional and folk silver jewelry. Palitana - Known for making bronze sculptures. Ahmedabad (Manchester of India) - Famous for cotton textile works. The first cotton textile mill was started in 1861.

questions.subject: Geography

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which group of states was concentrated in the cotton production in the early years to develop textile industry?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra and Gujarat. Cotton is a tropical crop and it is raised in India as a Kharif crop. Climatic condition - Temperatures between 21 degrees Celsius and 30 degrees Celsius. It grows best in Black soil. India grows both short staple (Indian) cotton as well as long staple (American) cotton called ‘narma’ in north-western parts of the country.

questions.question: Where was the first cement plant located in India in the year 1904 ?
questions.explanation: Chennai. South India Industries Limited in Madras, made an initiative to manufacture Portland cement. India entered into the Cement Era in 1914, when the Indian Cement Company Ltd. started manufacturing Cement in Porbandar in Gujarat.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider the following statements about oilfields in India: Statement I: Digboi and Naharkatiya oilfields are located in Assam. It is located in Tinsukia district, Assam. Naharkatiya Oilfield : Discovered in 1953, with oil production starting in 1954. It is located in Dibrugarh district, Assam. Other Oil Refineries in Assam - Noonmati Refinery, Numaligarh Refinery, and Bongaigaon Refinery. Kosamba, Lunej, Mehsana, Nawagam, Ankleshwar and Kalol are oil-producing regions located in Gujarat.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following cities is called the Silicon Valley of India due to its prominence in the IT industry ?

questions.subject: Geography

questions.explanation: Hindustan Copper Limited. It is a public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Mines. The company was incorporated on 9th November 1967, under the Companies Act, 1956. Headquarters - Kolkata.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding gold mines in India: 1. The Kolar region of Karnataka is famous for its gold fields and is also called the “Golden City of India.” 2. Hutti Gold Mines is located in Jharkhand, is among the largest gold producers in India. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only I. Kolar - Golden City of India. It is popularly known as the land of Silk, Milk, Mango, Gold. Other Gold mines - Hutti Gold Mines (Karnataka), Lava Gold Mines (Jharkhand), Sonbhadra Mine (Uttar Pradesh), Parasi (Jharkhand), Dadam (Haryana).

questions.subject: Geography

questions.explanation: Odisha. Aluminum smelting plants - Korba, Alupuram, Renukoot, Mettur, Hirakud, Angul, Jharsuguda and Faridabad. Aluminium Companies in India - Hindustan Aluminium Company (Mumbai, Maharashtra), Vedanta Limited (Jharsuguda, Odisha), Sacheta Metals (Mumbai, Maharashtra).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following industries is its own major consumer in India?
questions.explanation: Chemical. India is the 6th largest producer of chemicals in the world and 3rd in Asia. Also the fourth-largest producer of agrochemicals after the United States, Japan and China.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which city in India is known as the ‘Detroit of India’ due to its automobile industry?
questions.explanation: Chennai - It is contributing more than 40% of the country's auto parts and vehicles. The World's major automotive giants that operate in Chennai are TVS, Ashok Leyland, Royal Enfield, TI Cycle, TAFE, Hyundai, Mitsubishi etc.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The Kudremukh Mines are located in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Karnataka. Kudremukh Mines is an iron ore mine located in the Bellary, Chitradurga, Chikkamagaluru, Tumkur belt. Other Iron ore mines : Chhattisgarh - Rowghat Mines, Bailadila. Odisha - Balda Block, Joda East, Gorumahisani, Jajang Rungta. Madhya Pradesh - Agaria Iron Ore mine.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: In which of the following regions in India are there high-grade iron ore deposits?
questions.explanation: Northern Odisha. The iron ore mines are located near the coal fields in the northeastern plateau region. Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Goa, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu account for approximately 95% of total iron ore reserves. Iron Ore and Percentage of iron : Magnetite - 72 %, Hematite - 60-70 %, Limonite - 40 to 60%, Siderite - 48 %.

options.a: The Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Limited

Steel plants built in India during the Second Five Year Plan (FYP): Durgapur Steel Plant (West Bengal - Britain Cooperation), Bhilai Steel Plant (Chattisgarh - USSR Cooperation).

questions.subject: Geography

questions.explanation: The Muri Alumina Plant - Situated near Chota Muri at Swarnarekha River in Ranchi (Jharkhand). It was commissioned in 1948. Its capacity is 450 Kilo tonne per annum (present). The Mettur Plant, Tamil Nadu. Damanjodi - Located in the Koraput district (Odisha), famous for discovery of bauxite mines and setting up of NALCO (National Aluminium Company Limited).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: With respect to value addition in the textile industry, knitting is followed by which procedure?
questions.explanation: Dyeing and finishing. In the textile industry, the process begins with fiber production, followed by spinning to create yarn, and then knitting or weaving to form fabric. Next comes dyeing, printing, and finishing to enhance the fabric, and finally, garment manufacturing, involving cutting and sewing. Thus, the step following knitting is dyeing and finishing.
