Infrastructure is defined as the basic physical systems of a business, region, or nation and often involves the production of public goods or production processes. Examples - Transportation systems, Communication networks, Sewage, Water, and School systems etc.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements about India’s industrial production in 1991–92 : 1. Industrial production recorded a positive growth rate of 0.6%. 2. The mining and manufacturing sectors performed exceptionally well, boosting industrial growth. 3. The high growth rate reflected strong economic performance during that period.
questions.explanation: 1 only. In 1991–92, industrial production barely grew at 0.6%, largely due to poor performance in mining and manufacturing, reflecting the economic challenges of that time.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: When a person is NOT paying anything for public goods, this is known as ________.
questions.explanation: Free rider. In the context of public goods, a free rider is able to use or enjoy the benefits of the public good without contributing to its cost. This is possible because of the nature of public goods, which are typically non-excludable. Example: Using public parks without paying for them.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of these is not the reason why ‘final’ goods are called so?

options.a: They are meant for final use.
options.b: They are the last to be consumed.
options.c: They will not pass through any more stages of production.
options.d: They are not processed or transformed further.

questions.answer_text: They are the last to be consumed.
questions.explanation: Final goods are products that are meant for direct consumption or investment and will not undergo any further stages of production or transformation. These goods reach the ultimate user, either households (consumers) or firms (producers). Consumption Goods: Goods used by households for direct satisfaction of wants. Examples: Television, Ready -to-eat foods, Medicines, Clothes, Automobiles. Capital Goods: Goods used by producers for producing other goods and services, but not meant for direct consumption. Examples: Machines, Tools, Buildings, Equipment.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of durable goods?

options.a: They are capable of repetitive use.
options.b: They are not extinguished by immediate consumption.
options.c: They are meant for repetitive purchases.
options.d: They have a relatively long life.

questions.answer_text: They are meant for repetitive purchases.
questions.explanation: Durable goods (Consumer durables) : Those products that are used repeatedly over a period of time. The life of these products is high and the price paid to possess these products are also high. Example - Refrigerators, air conditioners, tools, computers, televisions, jewellery, home and office furnishings. Non - Durable goods : These goods have a shelf life of less than three years and many can be recycled. Example - Milk, vegetables, meat, fruit, paperboard, magazines.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements about sectors of the Indian economy : 1. Hotels and restaurants are part of the tertiary (service) sector. 2. Mining and quarrying are part of the tertiary sector. 3. Electricity production is a component of the primary sector.
questions.explanation: 1 only. The tertiary sector provides services to other sectors and includes hotels, restaurants, trade, transport, communication, banking, education, health, tourism, and insurance. Mining and quarrying fall under the primary sector, while electricity production belongs to the secondary sector.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the New Industrial Policy of 1991 : 1. It abolished industrial licensing for most industries in India. 2. It allowed Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) up to 51% in selected sectors. 3. It strengthened the control of the MRTP Act over big business houses. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. The new Industrial Policy of 1991 actually diluted MRTP controls, instead of strengthening them.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: How many industries were listed in Schedule A of Industrial Policy, 1956 ?
questions.explanation: 17. The 1956 policy divided the industries into 3 categories based on management. Schedule A Industries: It consisted of 17 industrial areas which were under the Central Government. Schedule B Industries : It consisted of 12 industries that were left to the state government to follow up with the private sector that includes compulsory licensing provisions. Schedule C Industries: It consisted of those industries which were left out of Schedule A and B and were with the private sectors and subject to licensing and regulation under the IDR Act.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following can be considered as an example of flow variable? (i) Production of rice (ii) Import of cloth (iii) Change in capital
questions.explanation: All of (i), (ii) and (iii). Flow variable - A quantified variable that is measured over a specified period of time. It is time bounded and expressed as per unit of time. Examples - Income, expenditure, depreciation, production, consumption, exports, rent, profit, interest. Stock variable - A quantity which is measurable at a particular point of time. Examples - Capital, wealth, foreign debts, loan.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In migration the factors which cause people to leave their place of residence or origin are called ________.
questions.explanation: Push factors. These are the factors that drive people away from their place of origin, such as war, political instability, or economic hardship. Pull factors are the factors that attract people to a new place, such as better economic opportunities, better education, or a more favourable climate.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Macroeconomics deals with which of the following studies? I. Reasons behind the unemployment of resources. II. Determination of total output.
questions.explanation: Both I and II. Macroeconomics looks at the economy as a whole and studies aggregate phenomena such as overall economic output (e.g. GDP), unemployment rates, inflation, and national income.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: A free - market economy is a crucial aspect of _______ .
questions.explanation: Capitalism is an economic system where the means of production are privately owned and organized to make profits. In a capitalist economy, the government has a limited role, and the free market determines the supply, demand, and prices of products.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Name the two states in which land reform was successful ?
questions.explanation: West Bengal and Kerala. The Kumarappan committee (1949) was appointed to study and recommend comprehensive land reform measures for independent India. Land reforms refer to change in the ownership of landholdings through abolishment of intermediaries and to make the tillers the owners of land. Land Reforms consisted of four elements : The Abolition of the Intermediaries, Tenancy Reforms, Fixing Ceilings on Landholdings and Consolidation of Landholdings.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Aid or Auxiliary to Trade : 1. Production is considered an auxiliary to trade. 2. Buying and selling are auxiliaries to trade. 3. Warehousing is an auxiliary to trade. 4. Transport, banking, insurance, and advertising are also examples of auxiliaries to trade. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 3 and 4 only. Production, buying, and selling are not auxiliaries to trade; they are direct business/economic activities. Auxiliaries are supportive services like warehousing, transport, banking, insurance, and advertising.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948, which of the following was NOT the monopoly of the Central Government ?
questions.explanation: Iron and Steel. Industrial Policy Resolution (1948) declared the Indian economy as a Mixed Economy. Four categories: The exclusive monopoly of central government (arms and ammunitions, production of atomic energy, and management of railways); New undertakings were undertaken only by the state (coal, iron and steel, aircraft manufacturing, shipbuilding, telegraph, telephone, etc.); Industries to be regulated by the government (Industries of basic importance); Open to private enterprises, individuals, and cooperatives (remaining).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the emigration of a significant proportion of a country’s highly skilled, highly educated professional population to other countries offering better economic and social opportunities called ?
questions.explanation: Brain Drain is the movement of highly skilled and educated people to a country where they can work in better conditions and earn more money.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the given example : 1. Cotton used in making clothes is classified as an intermediate good. 2. Intermediate goods are used to produce final goods and are sold between industries. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Intermediate goods, like cotton for clothes, wheat for bread, or steel for automobiles, are not consumed directly but used in production. Other goods types : Giffen goods (demand rises with price), capital goods (machinery / equipment used in production), and inferior goods (demand falls as income rises).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: People like small farmers and seasonal workers who regularly move in and out of poverty are categorised as___.
questions.explanation: Churning poor. Churning poor : Their poverty status changes depending on external circumstances such as harvest seasons or job availability. Occasionally poor : People fall into poverty rarely or due to specific, temporary reasons (e.g., a sudden illness or economic downturn). Always poor : People live in chronic poverty and remain poor regardless of external conditions. Usually poor : People who are poor most of the time but may occasionally rise above the poverty line.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: 'Income and employment theory' is the other name for which branch of Economics?
questions.explanation: Macroeconomics, as a separate branch of economics, emerged after the British economist John Maynard Keynes published his celebrated book “The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money” in 1936. It focuses on the aggregate changes in the economy such as unemployment, growth rate, gross domestic product, and inflation.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Microeconomics : 1. It studies the behaviour of individual decision-making units such as consumers, firms, and resource owners. 2. It deals with concepts like wages, rent, interest, and profit. 3. It focuses on the overall national income, employment, and general price level. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. The focus on the overall national income, employment, and general price level belongs to Macroeconomics, not Microeconomics. Microeconomics is a branch of economics that studies the behaviour of individuals and firms in making decisions regarding the allocation of scarce resources and the interactions among these individuals and firms. The concepts of wages, rent, interest and profit are studied under Microeconomics.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: At higher levels of development, which sector of the economy contributes less to the GDP ?
questions.explanation: Agriculture sector: As countries develop, their economies shift from agriculture to industry, and later, to services, reducing agriculture's share in GDP while boosting industry and services. Agriculture has lower productivity growth, so technological advances lead to fewer workers needed for food production, allowing labor to shift to higher-value jobs.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In 2011–12, what percentage of Indian workforce was engaged in secondary sector?
questions.explanation: 24.3%. Trends in Employment Pattern (Sector-wise) in 2011–12 : Primary sector (48.9%), Secondary sector (24.3%), and Service sector (26.8%). Status-wise : Self-employed (52%), Regular Salaried Employees (18%), and Casual Wage Labourers (30%).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Match the column with their descriptions: Column A (Laws) Column B (Descriptions) A. Law of Demand 1. After a certain point, increasing input leads to declining marginal product. B. Law of Diminishing Marginal Product 2. Demand and price move in opposite directions when income increases C. Law of Variable Proportions 3. Marginal product initially rises with input usage, then falls.
questions.explanation: A-2, B-1, C-3. Law of Demand : States that when the price of a good increases, its demand decreases (inverse relationship between price and demand). Law of Diminishing Marginal Product : After a certain point, adding more of a variable factor (like labor) to a fixed factor (like land) leads to a decline in marginal product. Law of Variable Proportions : Marginal product first increases with additional input, reaches a maximum, and then decreases.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility states that as a consumer consumes more and more units of a commodity:

options.a: Marginal utility derived from each additional unit decreases.
options.b: Total utility increases at an increasing rate.

questions.answer_text: Marginal utility derived from each additional unit decreases.
questions.explanation: Marginal utility derived from each additional unit decreases. The ‘Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility’ (DMU) is a fundamental concept in economics given by Hermann Heinrich Gossen (also called Gossen’s First Law). It states that as a consumer consumes successive units of the same commodity, the extra satisfaction (marginal utility) obtained from each additional unit goes on diminishing. Example: Eating one apple gives high satisfaction, the second gives slightly less, the third even less, and so on. Eventually, utility may even become zero or negative. Key points: ‘Total Utility (TU)’ increases but at a diminishing rate until it reaches a maximum. After that, Marginal Utility (MU) becomes zero (point of satiety). Beyond this, MU can become negative, reducing total utility.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: According to the law of demand, the consumer's demand for a good must be ______.

options.a: directly related to the supply of the good
options.b: inversely related to the price of the good
options.c: directly related to the price of the good
options.d: inversely related to the supply of the good

questions.answer_text: inversely related to the price of the good
questions.explanation: The law of demand and supply given by Adam Smith. Law of demand : An economic principle explaining the negative correlation between the price of a good or service and its demand. If all other factors remain the same, when the price of a good or service increases, the quantity of demand decreases, and vice versa.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The relationship between interest rate and demand for money is direct. 2. The relationship between interest rate and demand for money is inverse.
questions.explanation: Only 2 is true. Interest rate and demand for money have an inverse relationship, meaning that demand for money decreases as interest rates increase, and increases as interest rates decrease.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: A country allows its currency to fluctuate freely in the international market. The value of its currency rises when exports are high and falls when imports exceed exports. The government does not intervene in determining the exchange rate. Which type of exchange rate system is being followed?
questions.explanation: Floating exchange rate. In a floating exchange rate system, the value of the currency is determined purely by demand and supply in the foreign exchange (forex) market. The government does not intervene, unlike in a fixed or managed system. Currency appreciation occurs when exports exceed imports, and depreciation occurs when imports exceed exports.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What happens in case of market equilibrium : (A) Market demand = market supply (B) There is no excess supply in the market
questions.explanation: Both (A) and (B). Market equilibrium is a market state where the supply in the market is equal to the demand in the market. The equilibrium price is the price of a good or service when the supply of it is equal to the demand for it in the market.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Money supply is a _____ concept.
questions.explanation: stock. The total stock of money in circulation among the public at a particular point of time is called money supply. RBI publishes figures for four alternative measures of money supply : M1, M2, M3 and M4.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: As compared to monopolistic competition, the demand curve in a monopoly is :
questions.explanation: less elastic. In a monopoly, there is only one seller and no close substitutes for the product. Because of this, the demand curve is less elastic than in monopolistic competition, where there are many sellers and close substitutes for the product.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Assertion (A): Competitive behaviour and competitive market structure are inversely related. Reason (R): In a perfectly competitive market, firms cannot influence prices, but in monopoly, firms compete aggressively.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false. Competitive behaviour and competitive market structure are inversely related, but in monopoly firms do not compete aggressively, they rather face no competition.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: If ex ante aggregate demand and ex ante aggregate supply are plotted together in a graphical diagram, then at which point equilibrium will be reached?

options.a: Where ex ante aggregate demand is equal to ex ante aggregate supply
options.b: Where ex ante aggregate demand is zero
options.c: Where ex ante aggregate demand is less than ex ante aggregate supply
options.d: Where ex ante aggregate demand is more than ex ante aggregate supply

questions.answer_text: Where ex ante aggregate demand is equal to ex ante aggregate supply
questions.explanation: The aggregate demand / aggregate supply model is a model that shows what determines total supply or total demand for the economy and how total demand and total supply interact at the macroeconomic level. Aggregate supply is the total quantity of output firms will produce and sell, in other words, the real GDP. Aggregate demand is the amount of total spending on domestic goods and services in an economy. Equilibrium point is E and equilibrium level of income is OY1

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Assertion (A): If price elasticity of demand is less than one, demand is inelastic. Reason (R): Consumers are relatively less responsive to price changes in inelastic demand.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Price Elasticity of Demand is a measurement of the change in the consumption of a product in relation to a change in its price. If price elasticity is greater than 1 then the good is elastic, if less than 1 then it is inelastic, if the price elasticity is infinite then a good is perfectly elastic, and If the good's price elasticity is 0 then it is perfectly inelastic.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The simultaneous shifts of both the demand curve and the supply curve can happen in which of the following ways ? I. Supply curve shifts leftward and demand curve shifts rightward. II. Both supply and demand curves shift leftwards. III. Supply curve shifts rightward and demand curve shifts leftward.
questions.explanation: I, II and III. When both curves shift rightward, the equilibrium quantity increases, but the equilibrium price may increase, decrease or remain unchanged. When Both curves shift towards the left, the equilibrium quantity decreases but the equilibrium price may increase, decrease or remain the same. When demand curve shifts right and supply curve to the left, the equilibrium price increases but the equilibrium quantity may increase, decrease or remain the same. All depending on the magnitude of shift in the two curves. Cost, Production, Consumption and Market

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which curve is typically U-shaped due to the law of variable proportions?
questions.explanation: Average Variable Cost Curve. The U-shape of the Average Variable Cost (AVC) curve is a direct consequence of the Law of Variable Proportions (also known as the Law of Diminishing Marginal Returns). This law describes the relationship between inputs and outputs in the short run when at least one factor of production is fixed (e.g., a factory). (1) Initially (Downward slope): Adding more variable inputs (like labor) to fixed capital increases efficiency due to specialization and better utilization, so productivity rises and AVC falls. (2) Eventually (Upward slope): Beyond a point, diminishing returns set in as fixed factors get overused; extra workers add less output, lowering productivity and causing AVC to rise. Thus, AVC first decreases, reaches a minimum, and then increases, forming the U-shaped curve.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: A factory purchases machinery worth ₹50 lakh. At the end of the year, depreciation is ₹5 lakh. What is the Net Investment made by the firm?
questions.explanation: ₹45 lakh. Net Investment is calculated by subtracting depreciation from the gross investment (the total amount spent on new capital assets). In this case, the calculation is ₹50 lakh (Gross Investment) - ₹5 lakh (Depreciation), which equals ₹45 lakh.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following reflects the 'what to produce' decision in economics?

options.a: Choosing between capital and consumer goods
options.b: Increasing taxes to raise government revenue

questions.answer_text: Choosing between capital and consumer goods
questions.explanation: Choosing between capital and consumer goods. In economics, societies face three central problems due to scarcity of resources: What to produce? → Refers to the decision of allocating limited resources among different goods and services. For example, producing capital goods (machines, infrastructure) vs. consumer goods (food, clothes). How to produce? → Refers to the choice of production technique (labour-intensive vs. capital-intensive methods). For whom to produce? → Refers to distribution of goods and services among different sections of society.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In cost theory, the usual shape of the ____ curve is a rectangular hyperbola.
questions.explanation: average fixed cost (AFC) curve is typically a rectangular hyperbola, which means it has a downward-sloping shape. As output increases, the average fixed cost decreases, but the rate of decrease slows down. Average fixed cost (AFC) equals total fixed cost (TFC) divided by output (Q) : AFC = . 𝑇𝐹𝐶 𝑄

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Trade liberalisation has helped India improve its _________ in industries with medium-to-high technology content.
questions.explanation: Comparative advantage. It argues that countries can benefit from trading with each other by focusing on making the things they are best at making, while buying the things they are not as good at making from other countries. Theory of Comparative Advantage given by David Ricardo in 1817. Trade liberalization - The removal or reduction of barriers, such as tariffs and quotas, to encourage free and open exchange of goods and services between nations for economic growth.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Factor cost represents the total cost incurred on factors of production. 2. Factor cost is also called input cost. 3. Factor cost excludes wages, rent, and raw material costs.
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 are true. The actual cost incurred on goods and services produced by industries and firms. Factor costs include all the costs of the factors of production to produce a given product in an economy. It includes the costs of land, labour, capital and raw material, transportation etc.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Import substitution strategy is commonly called ________.
questions.explanation: Inward Looking Trade Strategy - Trade and Economic policy that advocates replacing foreign imports with domestic production. Example - Instead of importing vehicles made in a foreign country, industries would be encouraged to produce them in India itself.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: A car manufacturing company purchases tyres from another firm to use in assembling cars. These tyres are not sold directly to consumers but are used up in the production process. In economic terms, these tyres are considered:
questions.explanation: Intermediate goods. The materials that a firm buys from another firm which are completely used up in the process of production. Consumer durable goods can be used repeatedly and have a long life. An item that is meant for final use and will not pass through any more stages of production or transformations is called a final good.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Commercialisation of agriculture is an indication of _________ .
questions.explanation: Marketable surplus - Difference between the total output produced by a farmer and his self consumption from that output. Producer surplus - Total amount that a producer benefits from producing and selling a quantity of a good at the market price.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Assertion (A): The rural poverty line in 1979 was set at ₹49.09 per capita per month. Reason (R): Rural poverty estimation was linked to a calorie norm of 2400 calories per person per day.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: 1979 Planning Commission task force on poverty estimation suggested a minimum calorie consumption of 2400 calories for rural areas (with a consumption expenditure of 49.1 Rs per capita per month) and 2100 calories for urban areas (with a consumption expenditure of Rs 56.64 per capita per month). Some committees for poverty line - Lakdawala Committee (submitted report in 1993), Tendulkar Committee (2009), Rangarajan Committee (2014).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The production function can be expressed as_________ (where L is labour and C is capital and Q is the maximum output that can be produced)
questions.explanation: Q = f(L,C). Production function refers to the functional relationship between the quantity of a good produced (output) and factors of production (inputs). Mathematically, such a basic relationship between inputs and outputs may be expressed as: Q = f( L, C, N ). Where Q = Quantity of output, L = Labour, C = Capital, N = Land.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The consumption of fixed capital is also known as _________.
questions.explanation: depreciation - Means loss of fixed assets overtime due to wear and tear. Fixed capital consists of assets that are not consumed or destroyed in the production of a good or service and can be used multiple times.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the marginal utility of a commodity ? I. It is the change in total utility due to consumption of one additional unit of a commodity. II. It diminishes with increase in consumption of the commodity.
questions.explanation: Both I and II. Marginal utility : It is a measure that defines the additional satisfaction a customer receives from one more unit of a product or service. Ordinal utility : It explains that the satisfaction level after consuming any goods or services cannot be scaled in numbers.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Gini index measures inequality in income distribution. 2. A Gini coefficient of 0 means perfect equality. 3. A Gini coefficient of 100 means perfect inequality.
questions.explanation: 1, 2 and 3 are true. Gini coefficient measures inequality in income distribution (0 - perfect equality; 100- perfect inequality). National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation And GDP

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: According to Keynesian theory, during recession, what should the government ideally do?
questions.explanation: Increase spending and cut taxes. Keynesian theory suggests that recessions occur due to insufficient demand. To revive the economy, governments should adopt expansionary fiscal policies—raising public spending and reducing taxes. This boosts aggregate demand, creates jobs, and stimulates production. Increasing interest rates or reducing spending would worsen recession, while promoting imports does not directly address demand deficiency.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Which of the following sectors contributes the most to India's GDP?
questions.explanation: The services sector contributes the largest share to India’s GDP, accounting for over 50% of the total. It includes industries like IT, finance, education, healthcare, and tourism. While agriculture and manufacturing are vital for employment and growth, the services sector leads in economic value generation.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Identify the correct interpretation of Gross National Product (GNP).

options.b: Income earned by Indians at home and abroad
options.c: Income earned by Indians only within India
options.d: Income earned by residents and non-residents within India

questions.answer_text: Income earned by Indians at home and abroad
questions.explanation: Income earned by Indians at home and abroad. Gross National Product (GNP): Refers to the total market value of all final goods and services produced in a year by the nationals of a country. It includes income earned within the country (domestic production) plus income earned by nationals abroad, but excludes income earned by foreigners within the country. GDP (Gross Domestic Product): Income earned within the country’s borders, regardless of nationality. GNP vs GDP Formula: GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: What trend is reflected by increasing share of urban people in non-manual tertiary occupations?
questions.explanation: Emerging service economy. The rising share of urban populations in non-manual tertiary jobs (IT, finance, healthcare, education, etc.) indicates the structural shift of India’s economy towards a service-led growth model. A shift of the workforce into these white-collar service jobs signifies that the economy is maturing beyond its traditional reliance on agriculture (primary sector) and manufacturing (secondary sector) and is now being increasingly driven by services.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Consider the emphasis placed on the public sector in India's industrial development strategy between 1947 and 1990. What was a key rationale behind giving the public sector a dominant role during this period?

options.a: There was a lack of demand for industrial goods in the domestic market, necessitating government intervention.
options.b: Public sector industries were inherently more efficient than private sector ones.
options.c: The private sector had sufficient capital and technological expertise to drive industrialization in all key sectors.
options.d: The public sector was seen as a tool for achieving social goals, promoting balanced regional development, and controlling strategic industries.

questions.answer_text: The public sector was seen as a tool for achieving social goals, promoting balanced regional development, and controlling strategic industries.
questions.explanation: After independence, India adopted a mixed economy model where the public sector was given a dominant role in industrialization. The rationale included: Lack of capital and technology in the private sector to invest in heavy industries like steel, power, and defense. Strategic industries (e.g., defense, railways, atomic energy) were kept under state control for national security. Social goals such as reducing regional imbalances, creating employment, and ensuring equitable growth were prioritized. Implementation of the Mahalanobis Model (Second Five-Year Plan, 1956) emphasized heavy industries through the public sector.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: In what way did fiscal discipline reforms affect center-state financial relations post-1991?

options.b: States had to adhere to fiscal targets
options.c: Increased state autonomy in tax policy

questions.answer_text: States had to adhere to fiscal targets
questions.explanation: After the 1991 economic reforms, India adopted policies of fiscal consolidation and discipline to reduce fiscal deficits and ensure macroeconomic stability. One major step was the implementation of Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Acts at both the central and state levels. States were encouraged (and later mandated) to maintain fiscal deficit and debt targets. Central assistance and borrowing limits became linked to adherence to fiscal discipline, thereby reshaping center-state financial relations. This limited the fiscal profligacy of states, but also reduced their flexibility in spending. (a) Reduced tax sharing – Incorrect; post-1991, tax devolution was guided more by Finance Commissions, not directly reduced by fiscal reforms. (c) Increased state autonomy in tax policy – Incorrect; taxation powers remained largely constitutionally defined. (d) Centralized control over agriculture pricing – Incorrect; agricultural pricing is influenced by MSP policies, not fiscal discipline reforms.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Calculate the revenue receipts from the following information. Revenue deficit= 2.80% of GDP Revenue expenditure= 10.80% of GDP
questions.explanation: 8.00. To calculate the Revenue Receipts, we need to use the given information about the Revenue Deficit and Revenue Expenditure as percentages of GDP. Formula for Revenue Deficit: Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts Given: Revenue Deficit = 2.80% of GDP Revenue Expenditure = 10.80% of GDP Now, We can set up an equation: 2.80% = 10.80% - Revenue Receipts To find Revenue Receipts: Revenue Receipts = 10.80% - 2.80% = 8.00%

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: A start-up receives ₹1 crore from an angel investor, but the fair market value of shares is estimated only at ₹60 lakhs. The difference of ₹40 lakhs may be taxed under which section of the Income Tax Act?
questions.explanation: Section 56 (2) (vii b). The concept of Angel tax was introduced in the union budget 2012, to curb money laundering of funds in the India economy. ‘Angel Tax’ refers to section 56 (2) (vii b) of the Indian Income Tax Act, 1961, wherein the Income Tax Authorities are challenging additional taxes from Start-up Companies who have received financial support from Indian Angel Investors at a valuation higher than what can be ascertained for an early stage start-up venture. Angel investors are wealthy individuals who invest in business ventures and provide capital for startups that need quick funding.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: The CSO adopted the concept of Gross Value Added in ___________ .
questions.explanation: January 2015. Central Statistics Office (CSO) : The CSO is a government agency under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme implementation. The CSO replaced GDP at factor cost with GVA at basic prices to better estimate economic activity. It follows the United Nation's System of National Accounts (SNA). As per the SNA, GVA is defined as the value of output minus the value of intermediate consumption and is a measure of the contribution to growth made by an individual producer, industry or sector.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: In the context of a consumption function for an economy, if MPC = 0.6, then what is the likely value of MPS?
questions.explanation: 0.4. The Marginal Propensity to Save (MPS) is related to the Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC) by the equation: MPC + MPS = 1. Given that MPC = 0.6, we can find MPS as follows: MPS = 1− MPC = 1−0.6 = 0.4.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Match the concepts in column A with their respective descriptions in column B. Column A Column B a. Devaluation 1. decline in the market rate of exchange b. Depreciation 2. contraction of home currency c. Deflation 3. foreign exchange rationing d. Exchange control 4. contraction of imports 5. official reduction in external value of the currency
questions.explanation: a-5, b-1, c-2, d-3. Devaluation refers to the intentional downward adjustment of a country's currency value relative to another currency or standard. Depreciation, on the other hand, allows a business to allocate the cost of a tangible asset over its useful life for accounting and tax purposes. Deflation occurs when prices decrease over time, contrasting with inflation, which signifies rising prices. Exchange controls are governmental restrictions placed on the buying and selling of currencies.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Assertion (A): Personal income tax is a non-tax revenue source for the government. Reason (R): Non-tax revenue includes receipts like fees, fines, and interest.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation: A is false, but R is true. Non-tax revenue refers to income generated by the government through sources other than taxes. Examples of non-tax revenue include : Fees - Licence fees, registration fees, tuition fees, etc. Fines - Penalties imposed for violating laws or regulations. Interest receipts - Interest earned on government investments or loans. Dividends - Earnings from government - owned companies. Grants - Receipts from international organisations or foreign governments.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: If GNP is 16% higher than the last year and the rate of inflation is 9%, production in the economy has grown by:
questions.explanation: 7%. To determine the real growth in production, we need to adjust the increase in Gross National Product (GNP) for inflation. The real growth rate can be approximated by subtracting the inflation rate from the nominal growth rate. Real Growth Rate = Nominal Growth Rate - Inflation Rate (16% - 9% = 7%).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: What is net investment ?

options.a: Sum of all the investments in a country

questions.explanation: Gross investment - depreciation. Net Investment: It refers to the actual addition to the capital stock of a country or business, accounting for the depreciation of existing assets. Gross Investment: This is the total expenditure on new assets, including new buildings, machinery, equipment, and inventory.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: By adding depreciation to NDP, we get :
questions.explanation: GDP. Net Domestic Product at factor cost (NDP at FC) is the income earned by the factors in the form of wages, profits, rent, interest etc. NDP (Net Domestic Product) at FC (Factor Cost) = GDP (Gross Domestic product) at FC minus Depreciation. Gross Domestic Product - Final monetary value of the goods and services produced within the country during a specific period of time. It is released by the National Statistical Office (NSO).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Identify the sequence of implementation of the following taxes. I. Land revenue II. Sales tax III. MODVAT IV. Service tax
questions.explanation: I, II, III, IV. Land revenue is the oldest form of taxation in India, it was prevalent even before the British era. Sales tax was introduced in India through the Central Sales Tax (CST) Act, 1956. The Modified Value Added Tax (MODVAT) was introduced in India in 1986 to streamline the indirect tax system. Service Tax was introduced in India in 1994 by Chapter V of the Finance Act, 1994.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Which of the following options best describes the primary cause of the per capita income decline?

options.d: Decline in the gross domestic product

questions.explanation: Increase in the population growth. Per capita income is calculated by dividing a country's total income (GDP) by its population. If the population grows rapidly while the economy (GDP) doesn't grow at the same pace, the per capita income decreases because the same amount of wealth is distributed among a larger number of people.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Assertion (A): The financial year in India runs from 1 April to 31 March. Reason (R): This system was adopted to align with the British system of accounting.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, R is false.
options.d: A is false, R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Both A and R are true, and R explains A. A financial year, also known as a fiscal year, is a 12-month period used by governments, businesses, and organizations for accounting and financial reporting purposes.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: If a household’s income or consumption is below the minimum level required for subsistence, it is classified as :
questions.explanation: Below Poverty Line (BPL). Poverty Estimation in India : It is based on the income or consumption levels and if the income or consumption falls below a given minimum level, then the household is said to be Below the Poverty Line (BPL).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct formula for calculating NNP ?
questions.explanation: NNP = GNP – Depreciation. Net National Product (NNP) - Total value of finished goods and services produced by a country's citizens overseas and domestically, minus depreciation. Gross National Product (GNP) is Gross Domestic Product (GDP) plus net factor income from abroad. Depreciation is an annual decrease in the price of a capital goods over a year due to wear and tear and some other reasons.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: _____ at Market Price refers to the sum total of factor incomes earned by residents of a country during an accounting year including net indirect taxes.
questions.explanation: Net National Product (NNP). It is at Factor Cost, also known as national income. When calculated at factor cost, the NNP includes the sum of wages, rents, interests, and profits distributed in an economy but excludes indirect taxes while including subsidies. Thus, it reflects the income earned through the productive activities of the country's normal residents.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Which cost is considered for calculating the national income in India?
questions.explanation: Factor cost refers to the cost of factors of production such as labor, capital, and entrepreneurship. Market cost : The cost of a product or service in the market, influenced by supply and demand. Sunk cost : A cost that has already been incurred and cannot be changed or avoided.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Price control and rationing are direct control measures to check _____.
questions.explanation: Inflation:Inflation refers to the general rise in the price levels of goods and services over time. When inflation becomes excessive, it can reduce the purchasing power of consumers and destabilise the economy. To control inflation, governments use various fiscal policies : Price control and rationing, Reduction in Public Spending, Increase in Taxes, and Subsidy Cuts.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Calculate personal income (in ₹ crore) from the given data. Particulars ₹ (in crore) Private income 1800 Net retained earnings of private enterprises 500 Corporation tax 250
questions.explanation: 2050. Personal Income = Private Income + Net Retained Earnings of Private Enterprises − (Corporation Tax) Now applying the formula : Personal Income = 1800 + 500 − (250) Personal Income = 2300 - 250 Personal Income = ₹ 2050 crore

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Wealth tax and gift tax are classified as “Paper Taxes”. 2. Paper taxes are easy to administer and yield high revenue. 3. These taxes are called “paper” because they are difficult to enforce. Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1 and 3. Wealth tax and gift tax are often called paper taxes because they are difficult to enforce and frequently evaded. Wealth Tax : Hard to assess the true value of assets, as people hide wealth through offshore accounts or other means. Gift Tax : Easily avoided by transferring assets in ways that don’t trigger the tax. These taxes exist on paper but are challenging to implement effectively.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: National income at constant prices means:

options.a: income estimated at current year prices
options.b: income estimated at base year prices
options.c: income estimated for next year prices
options.d: income estimated at any year prices

questions.answer_text: income estimated at base year prices
questions.explanation: income estimated at base year prices. Net National Product at factor cost is called National Income. National income = NDP at factor cost + net factor income from abroad. National Income at Constant Prices refers to the measurement of a country’s total income while adjusting for inflation. This is done by using prices from a base year (2011-12) as a reference, rather than the prices prevailing during the current year.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: If tax rate decreases with increase in taxable base, then this type of taxation is called:
questions.explanation: regressive. Progressive tax - A tax that takes a larger percentage of income from high-income groups than from low-income groups. Proportional tax - A tax that takes the same percentage of income from all income groups. Vertical equity - The concept that people in different income groups should pay different rates of taxes or different percentages of their incomes as taxes.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Which of the following options represents the total income earned by individuals from all the sources before deduction of personal income taxes?
questions.explanation: Personal income. National income - The total value of all the final services and goods produced in an economy during a specific period of time. Gross income - Total income earned by an individual on a paycheck before taxes and other deductions. Disposable income - Personal income minus Taxes.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Expenditure of the government on health facilities, education and fixed-asset acquisition is termed as ____ .
questions.explanation: Capital expenditure: It involves the spending of government funds on the acquisition of assets that have long-term value and contribute to the overall development of the country. Example - Construction of school and Buildings. Revenue expenditure: It refers to the government's spending on day-to-day operational costs and current expenses such as salaries, wages, interest payments, and subsidies.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in inventory investment when calculating national income ?

options.a: Change in sales during the year
options.b: Change in stock of semi-finished goods
options.c: Change in stock of raw material
options.d: Change in stock of finished goods

questions.answer_text: Change in sales during the year
questions.explanation: Change in sales during the year. The stock of unsold finished goods, or semi-finished goods, or raw materials which a firm carries from one year to the next is called inventory. Inventories are treated as capital. Its addition to the stock of capital of a firm is known as investment.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Calculate the GDP at factor cost given in the following data. GDP at market price = 600 crores Consumption of fixed capital = 100 crores Indirect taxes = 200 crores Subsidies = 50 crores
questions.explanation: 450 crores. GDP at factor cost = GDP at market price + Subsidies - Indirect Tax. GDP at factor cost = 600 + 50 - 200 GDP at factor cost = 450

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Assessment of the country’s GDP growth, external balance and fiscal balance are presented in which part of the budget document?
questions.explanation: The Macro-Economic Framework Statement, was presented to Parliament as per the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003. The FRBM instructs the government to make an assessment of the growth prospects of the economy with specific underlying assumptions.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct formula for calculating Net Indirect Taxes ?
questions.explanation: Indirect Taxes - Subsidies. Net Indirect Taxes : Taxes that are levied on services and products and are collected by the seller. Examples - Sales tax, Value-added tax (VAT), Excise tax, Customs duty, Service tax. Subsidies : Financial assistance provided by the government to reduce the cost of certain goods or services for consumers.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a non-debt capital receipt in the government budget ?
questions.explanation: Non-debt capital receipts : Those money receipts which are received by the government from the sale of old assets. It refers to the incoming cash flows and not treated as liabilities of the government. Example: Recovery of loans and advances, disinvestment, and issue of bonus shares.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Assertion (A): A Balanced Budget is always considered ideal in public finance. Reason (R): Because it ensures that government expenditure equals revenue.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Balanced Budget is an ideal approach to achieve a balanced economy and maintain fiscal discipline. Surplus Budget - When income or revenue exceeds expenditures. Deficit Budget - When government expenses exceed revenue.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Which of the following statements (s) is true ? A. Higher inflation means lower real GDP, ceteris paribus B. Price Index is 200 if nominal GDP and real GDP are the same
questions.explanation: Only A. Real GDP : An inflation -adjusted measure that reflects the value of all goods and services produced by an economy in a given year. Real GDP is expressed in base-year prices. Nominal GDP is the GDP given in current prices, without adjustment for inflation. Real GDP = (Nominal GDP / Price Index) x 100. If nominal GDP and real GDP are the same, the price index equals 100, not 200.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Usually, the reduction in the taxes will have _____multiplier effect compared to an increase in government spending on aggregate demand.
questions.explanation: Smaller. Aggregate demand is a term used in macroeconomics to describe the total demand for goods produced domestically, including consumer goods, services, and capital goods. Formula :- AD = C + I + G + (X - M), AD = Aggregate demand, C = Consumption, I = Investment, G = Government spending, X = Total exports, M = Total imports.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Which of the following is correct regarding NNP at FC? 1. It is also known as National Income. 2. It is derived by adding NFIA (Net Factor Income from Abroad) to Net Domestic Product (NDP) at factor cost (FC). 3. It includes indirect taxes but excludes subsidies.
questions.explanation: Only 1 and 2. Net Domestic Product (NDP) at factor cost (FC) is the income earned by the factors in the form of wages, profits, rent, interest, etc., within the domestic territory of a country. NDP at FC = NDP at Market Price - Indirect Cases + Subsidies.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: According to David Ricardo, during a high deficit situation taxation and borrowings are _________ means of spending.
questions.explanation: Equivalent. Ricardian equivalence is an economic theory that says that financing government spending out of current taxes or future taxes (and current deficits) will have equivalent effects on the overall economy. This means that attempts to stimulate an economy by increasing debt-financed government spending will not be effective because investors and consumers understand that the debt will eventually have to be paid for in the form of future taxes.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Which of the following is an objective of the Government Budget? A) GDP Growth B) Reallocation of Resources C) Balanced Regional Growth
questions.explanation: All - A, B and C.The objective of the Government Budget is to outline the government's revenue and expenditure for a specific period, to achieve various economic and social goals.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Which of the following items is NOT a part of the non-plan revenue expenditure of the government budget ?

options.d: Central assistance for states and union territories

questions.answer_text: Central assistance for states and union territories
questions.explanation: The distinction between Plan and Non-Plan expenditure was abolished in 2016 on the recommendation of C. R. Rangarajan Committee. Non-Plan Revenue Expenditure refers to the recurring expenses incurred by the government that are not associated with any specific development plan or project. Examples include Interest Payments, Salaries and Wages, Subsidies, Pensions, Defense Revenue Expenditure, Other Administrative Expenses, etc.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: ________ is the income of the Government, which arises out of the property left by the people without a legal heir.
questions.explanation: Escheat. Felony - Felonies are the most serious offences that a person or corporation can commit against another. Moot - Unsettled, open to argument or debatable. Lien - A legal claim or legal right which is made against the assets that are held as collaterals for satisfying a debt.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: The stabilisation function of the government budget mainly includes ____.

options.b: intervention to expand or reduce the demand
options.d: distribution of income in society in a fair way

questions.answer_text: intervention to expand or reduce the demand
questions.explanation: Stabilisation policy seeks to limit erratic swings in the economy's total output (measured by the Gross domestic product), Controlling surges in inflation or deflation. Two forms : Expansionary policy - Government moves to lower taxes or increase spending to boost the economy. Contractionary policy - When the Government increases taxes or reduces spending to slow the economy and reduce inflation.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: In the estimation of national income, which of the following items will be subtracted from NNP at market price?

options.b: Net product taxes and net production taxes

questions.explanation: Net indirect taxes: Net National Product (NNP) at factor cost is also known as national income. NNP at Factor Cost = NNP at Market Price — Net Indirect Taxes. Thus, Net Indirect Taxes must be subtracted from NNP at Market Price to arrive at National Income (NNP at Factor Cost).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Proportional taxes would help to reduce the autonomous expenditure multiplier because _____________ .

options.b: MPC does not have any role in it

questions.explanation: Taxes reduce the MPC. MPC (marginal propensity to consume) - It is the change in consumption per unit change in income. Proportional taxes take a constant fraction of income as tax, reducing the disposable income available for consumption. Since households have less disposable income after taxes, the amount they consume from additional income decreases. Thus, the autonomous expenditure multiplier will reduce.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: CBIC stands for ________.

options.a: Central Bureau of Investigation and Committee
options.b: Central Board on Issues Related to Caste
options.c: Central Board of Information and Communication
options.d: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs

questions.answer_text: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
questions.explanation: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (erstwhile Central Board of Excise and Customs). It is one of the Boards constituted under the statute the Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963 and is subordinate to the Department of Revenue under the Ministry of Finance. It deals with the tasks of formulation of policy concerning levy and collection of customs, central excise duties, Central Goods & Services Tax (CGST) and Integrated GST (IGST).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Zero-Based Budgeting (ZBB) differs from traditional budgeting because:

options.b: It continues past allocations without review.
options.c: It requires justification for all expenses in each new period.

questions.answer_text: It requires justification for all expenses in each new period.
questions.explanation: Zero-Based Budgeting (ZBB) was first introduced in the U.S. by Peter Pyhrr. In India, it was first adopted in the Department of Science and Technology in 1983, and formally by the Government in 1986 during the Seventh Five-Year Plan. Maharashtra was the first Indian state to implement ZBB.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Match List I with List II and choose your answer from the code below: List - I List - II i. Service tax a. Capital receipt ii. Interest receipt b. Revenue expenditure iii. Sale of shares of PSUs c. Non-tax revenue iv. Salaries and pension d. Tax revenue
questions.explanation: i-d, ii-c, iii-a, iv-b. Tax revenue: Income tax, corporate tax, customs duties, VAT, etc. Non-tax revenue: Interest on loans provided by the government, dividends from public sector enterprises, fees for services, etc. Capital receipt: Borrowing from the public, sale of government assets, disinvestment of shares in PSUs, etc. Revenue expenditure: Spending on government salaries, pensions, subsidies, interest payments on loans, etc.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Operating Surplus: 1. It includes rent, interest, and profit. 2. It includes wages and salaries paid to workers. Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1. Operating Surplus : It is a concept used in national accounts statistics which refers to the measure of surplus accruing from production of the output before deducting property income from it like profits, rent, and interest. It is a component of value added and gross domestic product.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: What is the basic difference in the aggregates at market price and factor cost ?
questions.explanation: Net indirect taxes. Factor cost - The total cost of all the factors of production in manufacturing a good, which does not account for the subsidies received and taxes paid.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Identify the correct match. A. Pension to retired government employees - Revenue Receipt B. Purchase of Machinery in Railways - Capital Expenditure
questions.explanation: Only B. Capital expenditure : Expenditure that either creates an asset or reduces the liability of the government. Example: Purchases of property, equipment, land, computers, furniture, and software.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Exports of mangoes by India is a part of _____ method of measurement of its national income.
questions.explanation: Expenditure. This method adds up Consumer spending, Investment, Government expenditure, and Net exports. Formula (Expenditure method for national income): C + I + G + (X - M), where C = Consumer spending, I = Investment, G = Government spending, X = Exports and M = Imports.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Assertion (A): India adopted Gender-Responsive Budgeting (GRB) in 2005-06. Reason (R): GRB ensures equitable allocation of public funds for only women.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, R is false
options.d: A is false, R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, R is false
questions.explanation: A is true, R is false. Gender-Responsive Budgeting does not mean allocating funds only for women. Instead, it is a tool for analyzing a government's budget to understand its impact on all genders.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: ____is an item for which both, GST and central excise duty are applicable in India.
questions.explanation: Tobacco and tobacco products. GST (Goods and Services Tax) : Implemented - 1st July 2017. Amendment - 101st Amendment Act, 2016. Article - 279 A. The primary GST slabs for any regular taxpayers are presently pegged at 0% (nil-rated), 5%, 12%, 18% & 28%. However, petroleum products, alcoholic drinks, and electricity are not taxed under GST and instead are taxed separately by the individual state governments.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: While computing Net Economic Welfare (NEW), which of the following items is subtracted from GNP ?

options.b: Adjustments for congestion of urban life

questions.answer_text: Adjustments for congestion of urban life
questions.explanation: Net Economic Welfare (NEW) : It is a broader concept than Gross National Product (GNP) to measure economic welfare. NEW = GNP + Value of Housewives Services + Value of leisure – Expenditure on defence – Cost of Environment Degradation.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts is _________.
questions.explanation: Revenue deficit refers to the excess of revenue expenditure over revenue income in a financial year. Budget Deficit = Total Expenditures by the government – Total Income of the government.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: The value of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of India is published by PIB in ______.
questions.explanation: Indian Rupee. The GDP of India is typically measured and published in Indian Rupees, as it is the official currency of the country.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: ______ is a tax system that collects a greater share of income from those with high incomes than from those with lower incomes.
questions.explanation: Progressive tax is a tax system that collects a greater share of income from those with high incomes than from those with lower incomes. Payroll tax can be defined as the tax that is withheld, charged, or levied on the payroll of the employer.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of taxes and their types is/are correctly matched? 1. Income Tax – Direct Tax 2. Goods and Services Tax (GST) – Indirect Tax 3. Custom Duty – Indirect Tax 4. Wealth Tax – Direct Tax
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 and 4. Income Tax — Direct (paid by individual, cannot be shifted). GST — Indirect (added to price, can be shifted to consumers). Custom Duty — Indirect (levied on imports, paid by importer but passed on via price). Wealth Tax — Direct (paid by the owner of wealth).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: GDP deflator = _______ .
questions.explanation: (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100. The GDP deflator also known as implicit price deflator is an indicator of inflation. This helps in measuring the actual increase in GDP.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: In which union budget was India's first sovereign wealth fund named 'National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF)' announced ?
questions.explanation: 2015-16. NIIF is a government-backed entity established to provide long-term capital to the country’s infrastructure sector. Headquarter - Mumbai. The Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs in the Finance Ministry is the nodal body responsible for preparing the Budget.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: A company pays ₹10,000 as wages, ₹5,000 as rent, ₹3,000 as interest, and ₹2,000 as pension. Which of the following is NOT a factor payment?
questions.explanation: Pension. Factor payments : It is the sum total of remunerations earned by the four factors of production. Rent is paid for land. Wages are paid for labour. Interest is paid for capital. Profit is the payment for entrepreneurship.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: In national income accounting, GVA stands for
questions.explanation: Gross value added (GVA) - A significant macroeconomic indicator that measures the value of goods and services produced in an economy, after deducting the cost of inputs and raw materials used in the production process. Gross Value Added = GDP + subsidies on products - taxes on products.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Duties levied on goods produced within the country are _______.
questions.explanation: Excise taxes. Custom duties - It is a tax collected on imports and exports by the customs authorities of a country. Anti - dumping duty is a tariff imposed on imports manufactured in foreign countries that are priced below the fair market value of similar goods in the domestic market.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: If the value of gross fiscal deficit will be more than net interest liabilities, the value of gross primary deficit will be ___________ .
questions.explanation: Positive. Gross primary Deficit = Gross fiscal Deficit - Net interest liabilities. Deficit - The amount by which the spending done in a budget surpasses the earnings.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: When was the Direct Tax Code Bill introduced in the Parliament of India?
questions.explanation: 2010. Direct tax: It is directly paid to the authority imposing the tax. It is levied on taxable income earned by individuals and corporate entities. Example - Income tax, real property tax, personal property tax, and taxes on assets, corporation tax, gift tax, inheritance tax.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: The subject of the Study of Macroeconomics is based on which principle?
questions.explanation: The principle of National Income. Macroeconomics - It explains how the economy as a whole operates and how aggregate demand and supply are used to generate the level of national income and employment.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Which of the following organisations of the Government of India has been reporting the GDP at factor cost and at market prices?
questions.explanation: National Statistical Office. It also compiles the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) and all-India Economic Censuses. It conducts nationwide sample surveys to gather data on employment, consumer expenditure, housing conditions, environment, literacy, health, nutrition, and family welfare. The National Sample Survey Office (NSSO, founded in 1950) is merged with the Central Statistical Office (CSO, founded in 1951) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation to form the National Statistical Office (NSO) in 2019.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Assertion (A): Proportional income tax acts as an automatic stabiliser in the economy. Reason (R): It adjusts disposable income automatically, limiting extreme fluctuations in consumer spending.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, R is false
options.d: A is false, R is true

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: The proportional income tax acts as an automatic stabiliser – a shock absorber because it makes disposable income, and thus consumer spending, less sensitive to fluctuations in GDP. When GDP rises, income taxes reduce disposable income, limiting excessive spending. During recession, income falls less sharply, and consumption does not drop as much as it did, because tax liability has been fixed.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Who among the following headed the National Income Committee?
questions.explanation: PC Mahalanobis (chairman of Indian Statistical Institute). The National Income Committee (NIC) (1949) calculated the National Income of India and compiled statistics. Members of NIC : VKRV Rao and DR Gadgil.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: The difference between a farmer's output over and above his on-farm consumption is known as ______.
questions.explanation: Marketable Surplus. Consumer surplus occurs when the price consumers pay for a product or service is less than the price they are willing to pay. Domestic consumption products and services that are bought and used in the country that makes them.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: In 1950-51, what percentage of GDP of India was contributed by the industrial sector ?
questions.explanation: 13%. In 1950-51, the Agriculture sector contributed 59% to India’s GDP, and the Service sector contributed 28% to India’s GDP.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Which of the following commodities are exempted from GST ?
questions.explanation: Alcohol for human consumption. Other Goods not covered under Goods and Services Tax (GST) : Petrol, high-speed diesel, aviation turbine fuel, crude oil, Electricity, and Natural Gas.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: GDP that takes into account the costs in terms of environmental pollution and exploitation of natural resources is called __________.
questions.explanation: green GDP. The Green Gross Domestic Product is an indicator of economic growth with environmental factors taken into consideration along with the standard GDP of a country.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Which of the given statements about the Union Budget is/are true? a) Vote on Account deals only with the expenditure side of the government budget. b) Vote on Account and Interim Budget are not the same. c) An Interim Budget gives a complete financial statement, similar to a full budget.
questions.explanation: Budget (Annual financial statement, Article 112) is a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the government in a financial year (1st April - 31st March). A vote-on-account is Parliament's approval to the Centre for withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India for a specified expenditure to be incurred for a particular period. The Union Budget 2021-22, presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, was India's first paperless budget.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: Which of the following angles of the flow of factor payments forms the basis to estimate the national income?
questions.explanation: Income distribution angle National income is the sum of all the factor income (Wage, Rent, Interest, Profit) that is generated during a production year.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
