questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct ? I. Only marketed goods are considered while estimating Gross Domestic Product (GDP). II. The work done by a woman at her home is outside the purview of Gross Domestic Product. III. In estimating GDP, only final goods and services are considered.
questions.explanation: I, II and III. GDP is the value of all final goods and services produced within a country during a particular year. Unpaid domestic work, like cooking or caregiving at home, is valuable but not included in GDP because it is not traded in markets.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: National Income, Inflation, Budget, Taxation and GDP
questions.question: According to the Output Method, GDP is calculated as:

options.a: GDP at Constant Prices – Taxes + Subsidies
options.d: GDP at Constant Prices + Taxes – Subsidies

questions.answer_text: GDP at Constant Prices – Taxes + Subsidies
questions.explanation: GDP at Constant Prices – Taxes + Subsidies. The output method is also known as the value-added method. Money Banking and Financial Institutions

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What was the recommendation regarding entry of foreign banks in India?

options.a: Allow foreign banks to operate freely
options.b: Restrict foreign banks to urban areas
options.d: Encourage foreign banks to expand operations in India

questions.answer_text: Encourage foreign banks to expand operations in India
questions.explanation: Recommendations for foreign bank entry in India evolved to allow operation through wholly-owned subsidiaries (WOS) or branches, with the RBI mandating a move to the WOS model for fundamentally significant banks to ensure better supervision and a level playing field with domestic institutions.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct? Statement I: A bank's main liability is the deposits it holds. Statement II: Open Market Operations involve buying and selling government bonds. Statement III: The Bank Rate is the rate at which RBI lends to commercial banks.

options.b: I, II and III all three statements are correct
options.c: Only Statements I and II are correct
options.d: Only Statements II and III are correct

questions.answer_text: I, II and III all three statements are correct
questions.explanation: I, II and III all three statements are correct. A bank’s main liability is deposits, while the RBI controls liquidity through Open Market Operations (buying and selling government bonds). The Bank Rate refers to the rate at which RBI lends long-term funds to commercial banks. The Repo Rate is for short-term borrowing and requires the banks to provide collateral (government securities). The Bank Rate, on the other hand, is for longer-term borrowing and does not require collateral.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016?

options.c: To simplify the process of resolving financial distress in businesses
options.d: To provide protection for startups from financial harassment

questions.answer_text: To simplify the process of resolving financial distress in businesses
questions.explanation: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016 was enacted to provide a time-bound and efficient mechanism for resolving insolvency and bankruptcy cases of companies, partnership firms, and individuals. It aims to improve the ease of doing business, protect creditors’ interests, and ensure quicker recovery of debt.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Arrange the following RBI Governors in the correct chronological order of their tenure (from earliest to latest): 1. Dr. Y. V. Reddy 2. Dr. D. Subbarao 3. Dr. Urjit R. Patel 4. Shri Sanjay Malhotra
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3, 4. Dr. Y. V. Reddy served as RBI Governor from 2003 to 2008, followed by Dr. D. Subbarao (2008–2013). After him, Dr. Urjit R. Patel held office from 2016 to 2018. Shri Sanjay Malhotra has been mentioned here, but he is not an RBI Governor; he is a senior IAS officer currently serving as Finance Secretary.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What significant institutional development emerged from banking reforms after 1991 to regulate financial stability?
questions.explanation: Board for Financial Supervision (BFS). After the 1991 economic reforms, the need for stronger banking regulation was recognized. In 1994, the Board for Financial Supervision (BFS) was set up under the RBI to oversee banks, financial institutions, and NBFCs, ensuring prudential norms and financial stability. NABARD supports rural credit, SAT deals with securities disputes, and MSME Credit Bureau is not a post-1991 creation.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What was the recommendation of the Narasimham Committee-II regarding public sector banks ?

options.a: Reduce lending by public sector banks
options.b: Increase government ownership in public sector banks
options.c: Merge and consolidate public sector banks

questions.answer_text: Merge and consolidate public sector banks
questions.explanation: Narasimham Committee-II (1998). This was the second committee on banking sector reforms, chaired by M. Narasimham. Main recommendations included: Merger & consolidation of strong banks to create globally competitive banks. Reduction of government stake in public sector banks to 33%. Establishment of Asset Reconstruction Fund for tackling NPAs. Greater autonomy and professionalism in PSBs. Strengthening of prudential norms.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which policy reform targeted improving competitiveness and efficiency of the banking system after 1991?

options.a: Introduction of prudential norms and CRAR
options.b: Limiting foreign entry into retail banking

questions.answer_text: Introduction of prudential norms and CRAR
questions.explanation: Following the 1991 economic liberalization, the Narasimham Committee recommended these reforms to align the Indian banking system with international standards. Prudential norms (like income recognition and asset classification) and the Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) forced banks to improve their financial health and risk management, thereby boosting their overall efficiency and competitiveness.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is a key responsibility of IRDAI?

options.a: Protecting the interests of insurance policyholders
options.c: Managing disinvestment in public sector enterprises

questions.answer_text: Protecting the interests of insurance policyholders
questions.explanation: Protecting the interests of insurance policyholders. IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India) is the statutory body regulating insurance and reinsurance industries in India, established under the IRDA Act, 1999. Its primary functions include: Protecting the interests of policyholders.Regulating, promoting, and ensuring orderly growth of the insurance sector. Framing regulations for insurance companies, agents, and intermediaries.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is referred to as ‘Near Money’ ?
questions.explanation: National savings deposits. 'Near money' refers to assets that are not in the form of cash but can easily be converted into cash or used for transactions. National savings deposits are considered 'near money' because they can be quickly converted into cash, similar to liquid assets, though they are not immediately spendable like currency notes or coins.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements : 1. Shri Mahila SEWA Sahakari Bank was established in 1974. 2. The founder of SEWA was Ela Bhatt. 3. The headquarters of SEWA is in Mumbai. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. Self-Employed Women's Association (SEWA), meaning "service" in several Indian languages, is a trade union based in Ahmedabad. Headquarters - Ahmedabad, Founder - Ela Bhatt.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: ________is an industry association and self-regulatory organisation (SRO) whose primary objective is to work towards the robust development of the microfinance sector.
questions.explanation: Microfinance Institutions Network (MFIN) was established in 2009. In 2014, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) recognized MFIN as a Self-Regulatory Organization (SRO) for the NBFC-MFI, making MFIN the first industry association to be accorded recognition as an SRO by the RBI.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Assertion (A): Self-Help Groups (SHGs) have improved the economic status of rural women. Reason (R): SHGs provide collateral-free loans and promote income-generating activities.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Self-Help Groups are informal associations of people who choose to come together to find ways to improve their living conditions. They help the poor and marginalized by building skills for employment and income generation. SHGs also provide loans without requiring collateral.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is a component of the SHG-bank linkage program in India?

options.a: Microfinance institutions providing loans directly to SHGs
options.b: Banks providing loans to individual members of SHGs
options.c: Non-governmental organisations providing capacity building training to SHGs
options.d: State government providing subsidies to SHGs for credit

questions.answer_text: Banks providing loans to individual members of SHGs
questions.explanation: The SHG-BL Project was launched by NABARD in 1992-93, has now become the largest microfinance programme in the world. The SHG-Bank Linkage Model involves banks (Commercial, Rural, and Cooperative) directly lending to SHGs, which manage and guarantee loans for members.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: If assets of a bank are greater than liabilities, it will be recorded as:
questions.explanation: net worth. The amount by which the value of the assets exceed the liabilities is the net worth (equity) of the business. The net worth reflects the amount of ownership of the business by the owners. The formula for computing net worth is : Assets - Liabilities = Net Worth.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is Fisher's equation of exchange?
questions.explanation: MV = PT. Fisher Equation states that the nominal interest rate is equal to the sum of the real interest rate plus inflation. It lies at the heart of the Quantity Theory of Money. MV = PT, where M = Money Supply, V = Velocity of circulation, P = Price Level, and T = Transactions.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The Working Group under the chairmanship of_______in the year_______ proposed a new intermediate monetary aggregate to be referred to as NM2.
questions.explanation: Dr. YV Reddy; 1998. NM2 (Narrow Money 2) measures the money supply in an economy, including currency, demand deposits, and time deposits. It indicates liquidity and helps guide monetary policy and economic regulation. Central banks, such as the RBI, use NM2 to control inflation and manage economic growth, reflecting broader money supply aspects for policy decisions.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The term ‘Microfinancing’ was first used in the 1970s during the development of Grameen Bank of Bangladesh, which was founded by _____.
questions.explanation: Muhammad Yunus. Muhammad Yunus is a Bangladeshi economist, entrepreneur, politician, and civil society leader. He is the founder of modern micro finance. He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006 for founding the Grameen Bank and pioneering microcredit and microfinance.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is issued by commercial banks at a discount on face value?
questions.explanation: Certificates of deposits are unsecured, negotiable, short-term instruments in bearer form, issued by commercial banks and development financial institutions. Commercial papers - It is issued by large companies for short-term funding at lower interest rates, with maturities of 15 days to one year. Treasury bills - They are short-term government securities maturing in less than one year.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the primary aim of Regional Rural Banks in India ?
questions.explanation: Development of rural economy. The Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) : Established in 1975 under the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976 on the recommendations of the Narsimham Committee. The first RRB was Prathama Bank, with its head office in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh. In India, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) oversees the entire banking system, while NABARD supervises rural financial institutions, including RRBs under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Assertion (A) : The Reserve Bank of India’s Central Office was initially established in Kolkata. Reason (R) : Kolkata was the capital of India in 1935.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true but R is false.
options.d: A is false but R is true.

questions.answer_text: A is true but R is false.
questions.explanation: A is true but R is false. The Reserve Bank of India was established on April 1, 1935, and its Central Office was initially located in Kolkata (then Calcutta). It was later permanently moved to Mumbai in 1937. Kolkata was not the capital of India in 1935. The decision to shift the capital of British India from Kolkata to Delhi was announced by King George V in December 1911. The new capital, New Delhi, was formally inaugurated in 1931.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In 2000-01, NABARD instituted Micro Finance Development Fund with a corpus of ________.
questions.explanation: ₹100 crores. The Micro Finance Development Fund was established to support and promote the microfinance sector in India. The fund aimed to support microfinance institutions and promote self-help groups (SHGs) across India. NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) established on 12 July 1982.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Open Market Operations (OMO) : 1. OMOs are conducted by the Ministry of Finance. 2. OMOs are used to control money supply and liquidity. 3. RBI sells government securities to absorb liquidity. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 2 & 3 only. The purchase and sale of government securities (G-Sec) is entrusted to the Central bank on behalf of the Government.Open market operations (OMOs) are a key tool used by central banks to control the money supply and interest rates in an economy. To increase the money supply, RBI purchases G-sec from the market and to reduce the money supply, RBI sells G-Sec in the market.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Rotating Savings and Credit Association (ROSCA) was introduced by Shirley Ardener in the year ________.
questions.explanation: 1964. ROSCA is an alternative financial vehicle in which a group of individuals fills the role of an informal financial institution.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following banks is in charge of India’s banking and monetary system?
questions.explanation: RBI. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central authority responsible for regulating the circulation of the Indian rupee, monetary policy, and the banking system within the Indian economy.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Selling of bonds by the RBI will cause money supply to __________.

options.b: No relationship exists between selling bonds and money supply

questions.explanation: Decrease. Open Market Operations (OMOs) refer to the buying and selling of government securities by RBI to regulate the short-term money supply. If RBI wants to induce liquidity or more funds in the system, it will buy government securities and inject funds into the system. If RBI wants to reduce liquidity or money supply, it will sell securities and suck funds from the system.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: If the value / percentage of the cash reserve ratio falls, then the value of money multiplier ________.
questions.explanation: rises. The money multiplier is inversely related to the cash reserve ratio (CRR). If the CRR falls, banks are required to keep a smaller percentage of their deposits as reserves. This means they can lend out more money, which increases the overall money supply. An increase in a cash reserve ratio prevents the banks from lending more money and reduces the money multiplier.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Who issued guidelines for the microfinance institutions in India?
questions.explanation: Reserve Bank of India. Microfinance institution - An organisation that offers microloans, microsavings and microinsurance services to low income populations. In India, loans below one lakh rupees are defined as microloans. The RBI defined microfinance as collateral free loans given to households having annual income up to Rs. 3 lakh.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: When RBI decides to decrease the repo rate, money supply will _________.

options.d: initially stay constant and then decrease

questions.explanation: increase. Repo rate : It refers to the rate at which commercial banks borrow money by selling their securities to the Reserve bank of India (RBI) to maintain liquidity, in case of shortage of funds or due to some statutory measures. It is one of the main tools of RBI to keep inflation under control. If Repo Rate increases then money supply will decrease.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: For providing a non-microfinance loan to a low-income household, there is a limit of ____on monthly loan repayment obligations of a household as a percentage of monthly household income.
questions.explanation: 50%. This limit is set by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to protect low-income households from over-indebtedness.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What distinguishes a bank from other financial institutions?
questions.explanation: Accepting deposits. Accepting deposits is the primary function of banks that sets them apart from other financial institutions. Banks accept deposits from the public, provide safe-keeping for these funds, and allow depositors to withdraw their money on demand. Lending and Borrowing is also a function of Banks but it is also performed by other financial institutions such as Non-Banking financial institutions (NBFC), Microfinance companies, Self-Help groups, investment firms, etc.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: ________ is an instrument under the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) at which RBI lends to commercial banks.
questions.explanation: Repo rate. Reverse repo rate - The rate at which the central bank of a country borrows money from commercial banks. Bank rate - It is a rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) provides the loan to commercial banks without keeping any security. Cash reserve ratio - The percentage of a bank's total deposits that it needs to maintain as liquid cash.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The maximum limit on microfinance loans for NBFCs other than NBFC-MFIs is _________.
questions.explanation: 25% of the total assets. The Reserve Bank of India has increased the maximum limit on microfinance loans given by NBFCs that are not qualified as NBFC-MFIs to 25% from 10% earlier. RBI has also given a breather to NBFC-MFIs by reducing the minimum requirement of microfinance loans of total loan assets to 75 % from 85% earlier, in sync with the harmonisation of microfinance regulation for all lenders.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In the concept of money supply, M4 refers to ________.

options.d: M1+ time deposits of the public with banks

questions.explanation: M3+ total post office deposits. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) releases data for four different metrics representing money supply, namely M1, M2, M3, and M4. M2 = M1 + Savings deposits with Post Office savings banks. M3 = M1 + Net time deposits of commercial banks.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Identify the correct statement in the context of money supply i) Money supply refers to the total volume of money held by public at a particular point of time ii) Money supply is a flow concept iii) M1 is the most liquid measure of money supply
questions.explanation: Only (i) and (iii). The money supply is the entire stock of currency and other liquid instruments in a country's economy as of a particular time. M1, M2, M3, M4 is the measure of money supply. M1 is the most liquid and makes transactions the easiest, while M4 is the least liquid. M1, M2 - Narrow Money. M3, M4 - Broad Money.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is a function performed by commercial banks in India?
questions.explanation: Credit creation - Process by which commercial banks create new money by lending to businesses and individuals. Other functions of Commercial banks : Accepting deposits, Providing loans, Facilitating payments, etc. The function of Reserve bank of India includes, Issue of currency, Banking facilities to the government, Credit control, Managing foreign exchange, Issuing banking licenses.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following best describes a Micro Finance Institution (MFI)?

options.a: A financial institution lending only to corporates
options.b: A non-banking institution lending to poor and low-income households without collateral
options.d: A cooperative society registered with SEBI

questions.answer_text: A non-banking institution lending to poor and low-income households without collateral
questions.explanation: Non-Banking Financial Company - Micro Finance Institution (NBFC-MFI) : A type of financial institution that provides financial services, including microloans and other financial products, to low-income and economically vulnerable individuals, especially in rural and underserved areas. The regulator of Micro Finance in India is the Reserve Bank of India.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following microfinance institutions was established in India at the time of independence ?
questions.explanation: Rural Cooperatives. Bandhan Bank became the first microfinance company to get a bank licence in 2014. Grameen Bank - It was the brainchild of Nobel Laureate Prof. Muhammad Yunus in Bangladesh in the 1970s.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the difference between a debit card and a credit card ?

options.a: Debit cards are used for online transactions, while credit cards are used for in-person purchases.
options.b: Credit cards require a PIN, while debit cards require a signature.
options.c: Debit cards withdraw money directly from a bank account, while credit cards allow borrowing up to a certain limit.
options.d: Debit cards have higher interest rates than credit cards.

questions.answer_text: Debit cards withdraw money directly from a bank account, while credit cards allow borrowing up to a certain limit.
questions.explanation: Debit cards (Plastic Money) and credit cards look nearly identical, and both can give a fast and convenient way to pay - no matter whether you’re paying in person, online or over the phone.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement about money :

options.a: Money acts as a medium of exchange.
options.d: Money acts as a store of value.

questions.explanation: Perishability - A characteristic of products and services that do not allow for the product or service to be stored for sale at a future date. Money - Any object that is generally accepted as payment for goods and services and repayment of debts in a given country or socio-economic context.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following options is not an example of small savings?
questions.explanation: Mutual Funds - A mutual fund is a type of investment vehicle consisting of a portfolio of stocks, bonds, or other securities. The mutual funds in India are regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). The Government of India set up the first mutual fund by an Act of Parliament in 1963.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is a dimension related to the sustainability of microfinance institutions in India?
questions.explanation: Dependency on donor funding. Sustainability of microfinance institutions (MFIs) refers to their ability to operate independently and efficiently in the long term without relying on external financial aid or donor funding. If an MFI heavily depends on donor funding, its operations and growth become uncertain once the donor funds dry up. Hence, reducing this dependency is crucial for the sustainability of MFIs in India.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the main role of commercial banks in the economy?

options.a: To promote economic growth and development

questions.answer_text: To promote economic growth and development
questions.explanation: Other functions of commercial Banks : Accepting Deposits (Savings, Currents, Fixed), Lend money to people and businesses, Provide Locker to Customers, Deals with foreign exchanges etc. Commercial Banks are regulated by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) under Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the main function of money in an economy ?
questions.explanation: To facilitate exchange. Primary functions of money : Medium of exchange, measure of value. Secondary Functions / Derivative functions : Store of value, deferred payment, Transfer of Value / Purchasing Power.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the meaning of the term 'Collateral' in banking ?

options.d: An asset pledged as security for a loan

questions.answer_text: An asset pledged as security for a loan
questions.explanation: Collateral is an asset that the borrower owns (such as land, building, vehicle, livestocks, deposits with banks) and uses this as a guarantee to a lender until the loan is repaid. If the borrower fails to repay the loan, the lender has the right to sell the asset or collateral to obtain payment. Property such as land titles, deposits with banks, livestock are some common examples of collateral used for borrowing.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the purpose of a savings account?
questions.explanation: Earning interest on deposits : It is paid by a bank or financial institutions to account holders who have deposited with them.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a microfinance institution (MFI) in India?
questions.explanation: Bandhan Bank. Microfinance companies in India - Annapurna Finance (2009), Asirvad Microfinance (2007), Bandhan Financial Services (1995), Fusion Microfinance (2010), Cashpor Micro Credit (2002).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the main source of income for commercial banks?

options.d: Interest earned on loans and advances

questions.answer_text: Interest earned on loans and advances
questions.explanation: The commercial bank is a financial institution whose purpose is to accept deposits from people and provide loans and other facilities. Banks collect deposits from customers and pay interest on these savings. Similarly, they charge interest when providing loans to borrowers. The primary source of a bank's income is the difference between the interest earned on loans and the interest paid on deposits. Typically, banks charge higher interest rates on loans than what they offer on deposits, creating a profit margin.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What does the term 'Overdraft' mean in banking?

options.a: The process of transferring funds between bank accounts
options.b: The maximum withdrawal limit from an ATM

questions.explanation: Short-term financing facility. Bank overdraft is a type of financial instrument that is provided to some customers by the bank in the form of an extended credit facility, which comes into effect once the main balance of the account reaches zero. It is mainly used for covering short term cash requirements.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Who said the following ? "Money is what money does."
questions.explanation: Prof. Walker - American economist. Famous quotes in economics: Adam Smith - "Economics is the science of wealth", Alexander Hamilton - "A national debt, if it is not excessive, will be to us a national blessing" , Gita Gopinath - “Any policy maker’s tool kit must have enough room for fiscal policies because they are of paramount importance”.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the main purpose of a bank statement ?

options.b: To transfer funds to another account
options.d: To have locker facility in the bank

questions.explanation: A bank statement is a summary provided by a bank that shows all the transactions in a customer’s account over a specific period. Its main purpose is to help customers : Track their income and expenses (deposits, withdrawals, transfers, and payments); Check their account balance and verify transactions; Monitor for any unauthorised or fraudulent activity.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Women SHG member appointed as a banking agent is called _________ .
questions.explanation: Bank Sakhi. Qualification for Bank Sakhi : A woman SHG member for at least 12 months; Preferably in the age group of 22-45 years; Preferably a literate person with a Minimum 10th/8th standard pass (Good in writing and reading skills;) Representative of the community but not the bank. Whenever members of SHG visit the bank to deposit/ withdraw money, the bank Sakhi should help the SHGs in Filling transaction slips/ bank challans; and In accounting of cash – segregation by denomination.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In 2014, Bandhan Financial Services, microlender with Headquarters at ____, was granted in-principal approval by RBI to start a universal bank
questions.explanation: Kolkata. Bandhan Finance Service : Established - 2001. Founder - Chandra Shekhar Ghosh.Banks and their headquarters : Jana Small Finance Bank (Bengaluru), Ujjivan Small Finance Bank (Bengaluru), Equitas Small Finance Bank (Chennai), AU Small Finance Bank (Jaipur), Suryoday Small Finance Bank (Navi Mumbai) etc,.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: When the general interest rate reaches a very low level, which of the following statements will be correct

options.a: Most people will expect the interest rate to rise in the future.
options.b: Most people will prefer to hold bonds.
options.c: Most people will speculate a further decline in the rate of interest.
options.d: Any increase in the money supply will cause the interest rate to fall further

questions.answer_text: Most people will expect the interest rate to rise in the future.
questions.explanation: When interest rates are very low, they are unlikely to fall further and are more likely to rise over time. Historically, low interest rates are seen as temporary, and people anticipate increases in interest rate due to factors like inflation or central bank policies.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: NABARD launched a special pilot project in 2004-05 called ______ mainly to fulfil the credit needs of the small and marginal farmers and tenant farmers.
questions.explanation: JLGs (Joint Liability Groups). Financing of JLGs was introduced as a pilot project in 2004-05 by NABARD in 8 States with the support of 13 RRBs. The scheme was later mainstreamed for the banking system in the year 2006. JLGs are informal groups of 4-10 members who are engaged in similar economic activities and who are willing to jointly undertake to repay the loans taken by the Group from the Banks.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements : I. Fiat money is always legal tender. II. Cheques are not fiat money because they require the payer’s consent. III. All coins and banknotes issued by RBI are examples of fiat money. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: II & III only. Fiat money : Currency issued by the Government that is not backed by a commodity such as Gold. Examples : Paper currency, Coins, and Demand drafts. Legal tender : A type of currency or medium of exchange that can be in the form of a coin or a banknote that is recognized by law as an acceptable means for settling debts or obligations.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Who gave the concept of 'money illusion' for the first time?
questions.explanation: Irving Fisher (American economist) : Term ‘Money Illusion’ first coined by him in his book “Stabilising the Dollar.” Money illusion is the belief that money has a fixed value and the effects of inflation are ignored. The concept of money illusion was popularised by John Maynard Keynes. Adam Smith was a Scottish economist who wrote the book "The Wealth of Nations". Dennis Robertson was a British economist known for his work on monetary economics and his contributions to Keynesian economics.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Due to which of the following reasons can money be differentiated from other physical assets that can perform the function of store of value?
questions.explanation: Money is easy to store. Three main functions of money : Primary function - Money is used as a medium of exchange and it is the measure of value. Secondary function - It is the standard of deferred payments, the transfer, and the store of value. Contingent function - The distribution of national income, maximum profit to the producers, and maximum satisfaction to the consumers, basis of credit and liquidity.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In which year did RBI introduce the regulatory framework for microfinance loans?
questions.explanation: 2022. Regulatory Framework for Microfinance Loans 2022 : There is no requirement of treating all members of the household as borrowers of a loan which can be provided to an individual member; All collateral-free loans to individual/s belonging to low-income households, i.e., households having annual income up to ₹3,00,000 are treated as microfinance loans; Limit of 50 per cent on monthly loan repayment obligations of a household as a percentage of monthly household income.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In any economy, the income velocity of the hoarded money (idle) by the public is equal to ______
questions.explanation: Zero. The velocity of money - It measures the number of times that the average unit of currency is used to purchase goods and services within a given time period. Formula (The velocity of money) : V = PQ / M. Where, V = Velocity of Money, PQ = Represents the GDP (Nominal Gross Domestic Product), M = Money Supply. Hoarded money - It is not used to purchase goods and services, so the income velocity of hoarded money is zero.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding liquidity trap? i. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely inelastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly elastic. ii. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely elastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly inelastic. iii. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely elastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly elastic. iv. It is the point where speculative demand for money and the liquidity preference curves are not related.

options.d: Only Statements i and ii are correct

questions.explanation: Liquidity Trap : A situation in which prevailing market interest rates are so low that an increase in money supply has no effect on interest rates. A liquidity preference curve is a demand curve for money because a household's or business's value of liquidity is the same as its demand for cash.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which statement best explains the difference between commercial banks and microfinance institutions in terms of products?

options.a: Both offer credit cards to all customers
options.b: MFIs focus on microloans and savings for low-income groups, while banks offer advanced products like credit cards
options.c: Banks are only for the rich, MFIs are only for the poor
options.d: MFIs issue debit cards but not loans

questions.answer_text: MFIs focus on microloans and savings for low-income groups, while banks offer advanced products like credit cards
questions.explanation: Credit cards are used to borrow money with the agreement to pay back the borrowed money with the interest.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Under the current regulatory framework, what is the maximum tenure of a microfinance loan in India?
questions.explanation: 36 months. Microfinance loans are financing options that help people with low or no regular income gather funds to meet their financial requirements. Top Microfinance Companies in India - Equitas Small Finance, ESAF Microfinance and Investments, Fusion Microfinance, Annapurna Microfinance.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In 1987, an Action Research Programme was launched by NABARD with______based on which a pilot project for linking 500 SHGS with banks was launched.
questions.explanation: MYRADA (Mysore Resettlement and Development Agency) : Founded in 1968. Other Associations of NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) - Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) by Government of India (1995-96), Warehouse Infrastructure Fund (WIF) in 2013-14, Designed Kisan Credit Card Scheme (KCC) 1998, Launched E-Shakti for digitisation of Self Help Groups SHGs in 2015.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the given statements is/are correct with respect to NAFED? i. NAFED is registered under the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act. ii. It was set up with the objective of promoting Cooperative marketing of agricultural produce to benefit farmers. iii. It was established in 1956.
questions.explanation: NAFED (National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India): Founded - 2 October 1958 and registered under Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act 2002, Headquarters - New Delhi. Objective - To organise, promote and develop marketing, processing, and storage of agricultural, horticultural and forest produce.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: With regard to the Currency Deposit Ratio (CDR), all of the following is true, EXCEPT:

options.a: It depends on seasonal pattern of expenditure.
options.c: During festive season the CDR typically declines.
options.d: It reflects people's preference for liquidity.

questions.answer_text: During festive season the CDR typically declines.
questions.explanation: The currency Deposit Ratio (CDR) - The ratio of money held by the public in currency to that they hold in bank deposits. CDR = CU/DD. For example - CDR increases during the festive season as people convert deposits to cash balance for meeting extra expenditure during such periods. Factors affecting CDR - Interest rates, Inflation, Economics conditions, Banking regulations.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In which year did RBI accord approval to Equitas Holdings to launch a small finance bank?
questions.explanation: 2016. Reserve Bank of India (RBI) - India's central bank and regulatory body responsible for regulation of the Indian banking system. It is also known as the 'lender of the last resort”. Function - To operate the currency and credit system in India. First Governor - Osborne Smith.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: How many digits does the MMID code of any commercial bank have?
questions.explanation: 7. Mobile Money Identifier (MMID) Code : Each mobile banking account has a unique MMID allotted to the user by the bank itself. The first four digits - Unique identification number of the bank offering IMPS (Immediate Payment Service). Every bank account has only one MMID. Along with the mobile number, MMID identifies a bank account. Different MMID can be linked to the same Mobile Number.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In which of the following economic accounts are transfer payments included ?
questions.explanation: Government account. Transfer payment : It is a redistribution of income and wealth by means of the government making a payment, without goods or services being received in return. Example: Social security benefits, state pension, unemployment benefits, civil service benefits, survivor benefits, public health services.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The net worth of any bank is equal to_________.
questions.explanation: (Reserves + Loans) - Liabilities. Bank Assets - Anything that the bank owns. Example: Loans given to bank customers, Deposits made to the central bank. Bank liabilities - Anything that the bank owes to someone else. Example: Loans taken from the central bank, Interest paid to customers for savings and fixed deposits.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is the most problematic and primary difficulty of barter exchanges as against money-based exchanges?

options.a: Bartered exchanges involve difficulty in preserving value.
options.b: Barter exchanges may result in an incorrect valuation of the goods transacted.
options.c: Barter exchanges may be imperfectly divisible.
options.d: Barter exchanges require a double coincidence of wants.

questions.answer_text: Barter exchanges require a double coincidence of wants.
questions.explanation: Barter System - An act of trading goods or services between two or more parties without the use of money. Drawbacks of the Barter system: Lack of Common Measure of Value, Problems in Storing Wealth, and Division of Certain Products is not possible. Advantages of Barter system: suitable in international trade, No real concentration of power No overexploitation of Natural Resources, Proper division of labour.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: 'BFSI' stands for Banking, Financial Services and _________ in India. It is a broad term for industries that offer financial products and services.
questions.explanation: Insurance. BFSI is the industry's umbrella term for companies that provide a range of such financial products or services.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Why does increasing the bank rate discourage credit in the economy?

options.b: Because borrowing from RBI becomes costlier for commercial banks.
options.d: Because it reduces currency in circulation directly.

questions.answer_text: Because borrowing from RBI becomes costlier for commercial banks.
questions.explanation: When the RBI increases the bank rate, borrowing from RBI becomes costlier for commercial banks, which discourages lending and reduces credit flow in the economy. Bank rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) lends money to commercial banks without any security or collateral.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following committees was constituted to study the issues and concerns in the Micro Finance Institution in 2010?
questions.explanation: Malegam Committee. The Sub-Committee was under the chairmanship of Y.H. Malegam. Ghosh Committee (1991) - It inquired into the various aspects of frauds and malpractices in the bank and to make recommendations to reduce such instances. Sivaraman Committee (1979) - Recommended the establishment of NABARD. Khan Committee (1997) - Examined the financial system's effectiveness for the small-scale sector and the role of primary dealers.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements: A. ₹10,000 note was first issued in 1938. B. It was demonetized in 1946 and again in 1978. C. The Indian Rupee symbol (₹) was designed by Udaya Kumar. D. The Rupee symbol was adopted by the Government of India in 2005. Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: A, B and C only. ₹10,000 note was printed in 1938 and demonetized in January 1946 and again introduced in 1954 and demonetized in 1978. On November 8, 2016 : Rs 500, Rs 1000 notes were demonetised. Currency notes have 15 languages on the panel which appear on the reverse of the note. The symbol (₹) of Indian Rupee was accepted by the Government of India on 15th July 2010. The symbol of Indian Rupee is designed by Udaya Kumar.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: For a bank, the main liability is the__________.
questions.explanation: Deposits - money held in a bank account or with another financial institution that requires a transfer from one party to another.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In India, credit creation is done by: A) Ministry of Finance B) Reserve Bank of India C) Commercial Banks
questions.explanation: Credit creation - A process where a bank uses a part of its customers' deposits to offer loans to other individuals and businesses. Commercial banks create credit by advancing loans and purchasing securities.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which law of economics states "Bad money drives out good money" ?
questions.explanation: Gresham's Law. It is a principle in economics named after Sir Thomas Gresham, an English financier, which states that when there are two forms of money in circulation, people tend to hoard or use the better-quality money and spend or circulate the lower-quality money. Baxter's law (also known as the Bell doctrine) is a law of economics that describes how a monopoly in a regulated industry can extend into, and dominate, a non - regulated industry.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which among the following is the oldest joint stock bank in India?
questions.explanation: Allahabad Bank (1865). The first variety of joint-stock banks was the Bank of Bombay, established in 1720 (Bombay). Yes Bank: Founded - 2004 (Mumbai), Founder- Rana Kapoor, Ashok Kapoor. Punjab National Bank : Founded - 1894, Founder - Dyal Singh Majithia.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Money multiplier uses which of the following monetary instruments for its calculation?
questions.explanation: Cash reserve ratio - The percentage of total deposits a bank must have in cash to operate risk-free. The Reserve Bank of India decides the amount and is kept with them for financial security.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Assertion (A): Banks cannot lend below the Base Rate. Reason (R): RBI fixes the base rate uniformly for all banks.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false. The Base Rate was introduced in 2010 as the minimum lending rate below which banks were not allowed to lend (except in certain cases like loans to farmers or government schemes). However, the RBI does not fix a uniform base rate. Instead, each bank determines its own base rate, based on cost of funds, margin, and operating expenses.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which among the following was set up in 1956 by the Indian government by nationalising all the existing private sector life insurance companies?
questions.explanation: Life Insurance Corporation of India - A government-owned insurance and investment firm in India. Established - 1 September 1956, Headquartered - Mumbai. United India Insurance Company Limited - Established - 18 February 1938 and Nationalised in 1972, Headquarters - Chennai (Tamil Nadu). General Insurance Corporation of India - Incorporated on 22 November 1972 under Companies Act, 1956. Headquarters - Mumbai. New India Assurance Company Limited - Founded by Sir Dorabji Tata in 1919, and Nationalised in 1973, Headquarters - Mumbai.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) is regulated by ____.
questions.explanation: Reserve Bank of India (RBI). SIDBI was set up in 1990 under an Act of Parliament as an All India financial institution (AIFI).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Α _______ account is one which is maintained by an Indian Bank in the foreign countries, usually in the currency of that country for the purpose of carrying out transactions there.
questions.explanation: NOSTRO. VOSTRO: An account that domestic banks hold for foreign banks in the former's domestic currency. LIBOR : London Inter-Bank Offered Rate. It is a benchmark interest rate at which major global banks lend to one another in the international interbank market for short-term loans. MIBOR : Mumbai Interbank Offered Rate. It is the overnight lending offered rate for Indian commercial banks.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The National Payments Corporation of India was set up under the provisions of which act?
questions.explanation: Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 : It is an Act to provide for the regulation and supervision of payment systems in India and to designate the Reserve Bank of India as the authority for that purpose and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. National Payments Corporation of India - Founded in 2008. Industrial Finance Corporation of India - Founded in 1948.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Bankruptcy is a legal declaration of inability to repay debts. 2. In India, bankruptcy and insolvency matters are governed under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016. 3. Credit crunch refers to reduction in credit availability even without change in interest rates. 4. Bancassurance means banks directly lending to insurance companies. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect – Bancassurance means selling of insurance products through banks, not lending.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: A type of loan that allows borrowers to make low payments in the initial phases but repayment of the balance amount in lump sum at maturity is known as ________.
questions.explanation: Balloon mortgage. Types of mortgage: Simple Mortgage, Mortgage by Conditional Sale, English Mortgage, Fixed - Rate Mortgage, Usufructuary Mortgage, Anomalous Mortgage, Reverse Mortgage, Equitable Mortgage. The Income - Sensitive Repayment Plan is available to low-income borrowers who have Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) Program loans. A payday loan is a type of short-term borrowing where a lender will extend high-interest credit based on income.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: _______ became the first bank to get Reserve Bank of India's approval for rupee trade.
questions.explanation: UCO bank (United Commercial Bank): One of the nationalised banks in India under the ownership of the Ministry of Finance, Government of India. Headquarters : Kolkata; Founded : 6 January 1943, Kolkata; Founder : Ghanshyam Das Birla. Axis Bank : Founded: 1993, in Ahmedabad; Headquarters: Mumbai. ICICI Bank (Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India) : Founded: 1994, in Vadodara, Headquarters: Mumbai.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: A bank that has a paid-up capital of and above qualifies for the schedule bank category as listed in the RBI Act 1934.
questions.explanation: Rs 5 lakhs. The Reserve Bank of India, established (1 April 1935) by RBI Act 1934. It regulates all Indian banks. It is also known as the bank of banks.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India introduced a comprehensive regulatory framework for NBFC-MFI on __________.
questions.explanation: 2 December 2011. Capital adequacy ratio for a NBFC-MFI is 15% of the aggregate risk weighted assets.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Assertion (A): A Balance Sheet reports assets, liabilities, and shareholder equity. Reason (R) : It is used to show the company’s financial performance over a period of time.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false. The Balance Sheet shows a company’s financial position (assets, liabilities, and shareholder equity) at a specific point in time. Financial performance over a period of time is shown by the Income Statement (Profit & Loss Statement), not the Balance Sheet.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: If marginal propensity to consume is denoted by c, then government expenditure multiplier can be expressed as _______.
questions.explanation: Expenditure Multiplier = 1 1 − 𝑐 The expenditure multiplier shows what impact a change in autonomous spending will have on total spending and aggregate demand in the economy.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: ______are those where a monthly installment is deposited in the accounts every month.
questions.explanation: Recurring Deposit is the savings through regular monthly deposits of a fixed sum over a period. A Savings bank deposit is held at a financial institution that provides principal security and a modest interest rate.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: ______is the currency in the hands of the public plus commercial bank reserves, also called ‘high-powered money’.
questions.explanation: Monetary base (M0) is the total amount of a currency that is either in general circulation in the hands of the public or in the form of commercial bank deposits held in the central bank's reserves.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Open Market Operations conducted by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) are of ______ types.
questions.explanation: two. Open market operations refer to central bank purchases or sales of government securities in order to expand or contract money in the banking system and influence interest rates. Two Types - Outright Purchase is permanent and involves the outright selling or buying of government securities. Repurchase Agreement is a form of short-term borrowing for dealers in government securities.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The _______ and ______ determine the corridor for the daily movement in the weighted average call money rate.

options.b: Marginal standing facility, Reverse repo rate

questions.answer_text: Marginal standing facility, Reverse repo rate
questions.explanation: Marginal standing facility (MSF), Reverse repo rate. MSF is a penal rate (above the repo rate) at which banks can borrow money from RBI when they are completely exhausted of all borrowing assistance.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Why is the study of Money Supply important for the economy ?

options.a: It helps in measuring black money
options.b: It is used to formulate monetary policy and control inflation
options.c: It shows the profitability of banks

questions.answer_text: It is used to formulate monetary policy and control inflation
questions.explanation: Money Supply refers to the total stock of money (currency + deposits) available in the economy at a given time. It is a key indicator for the RBI while framing monetary policy. Changes in money supply directly impact inflation, interest rates, credit flow, and economic growth. Hence, studying money supply helps the RBI control inflation and stabilize the economy.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Commercial banks keep their deposits with RBI. These deposits are called ______.
questions.explanation: Reserves. A liability is something a person or company owes, usually a sum of money. A loan is a form of debt incurred by an individual or other entity. An inheritance is a financial term describing the assets passed down to individuals after someone dies.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: At a Regional Rural Bank, the share of the Government of India is______.
questions.explanation: 50%. Sponsored bank share is 35%, and state Government share is 15%. Regional Rural Bank was founded on 2nd October 1975. Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) are government owned scheduled commercial banks. Scheduled banks are banks that are listed in the 2nd schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which one of these organisations issues one rupee currency notes and coins in India?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Finance issues coins (under the coinage Act 2011) and the one rupee note (bears the signatures of the Finance Secretary), while other notes are printed by the Reserve bank of India (which bears the signatures of the RBI governor). The Coinage Act, 2011, allows issue of coins up to the denomination of ₹ 1000 in India.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements about NBFC–MFIs : 1. NBFC–MFIs cannot charge interest rates beyond the ceiling prescribed by RBI. 2. The maximum variance permitted for individual loans between the minimum and maximum interest rate is 4%. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. NBFC–MFIs are regulated by the RBI to ensure fair lending practices for small borrowers. They cannot charge interest rates above the ceiling prescribed by RBI from time to time. The difference (variance) between the minimum and maximum interest rates charged to individual borrowers by an NBFC–MFI cannot exceed 4%. These norms protect borrowers (especially low-income groups) from exploitation and ensure transparency in microfinance lending.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following has been designated as the self-regulatory organisation for Micro finance institutions in India?
questions.explanation: Sa-Dhan (Association of Community Development Finance Institutions) is designated as the self-regulatory organisation for Microfinance institutions in India.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following was the first development bank in India?
questions.explanation: Industrial Finance Corporation of India founded on 1st July 1948. National Housing Bank was founded on 9th July 1988. Export Import Bank of India was founded in March 1982. Industrial Development Bank of India was founded on 1st July 1964.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The Regional Rural Banks were established on the recommendations of the ______ on Rural Credit.
questions.explanation: ‘Narasimham Committee’. ‘Rekhi Committee’ - A Tribunal should be set up to deal with problems between taxpayers and tax collectors. ‘Kelkar committee’ was set up to study and evaluate the extant public-private partnership (PPP) model in India.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The Central Board of Directors of the RBI (Reserve Bank of India) is appointed/nominated for a period of _____ years.
questions.explanation: four. RBI is India's central bank and regulatory body under the jurisdiction of Ministry of Finance. It is responsible for the issue and supply of the Indian rupee and the regulation of the Indian banking system.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In which of the following years did the Reserve Bank of India liberalise the licensing policy for Urban Co-operative Banks?
questions.explanation: 1993. It was a significant step aimed at expanding the reach of banking services in urban and semi-urban areas.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Assertion (A): The Central Government can issue directions to the RBI under Section 7 of the RBI Act. Reason (R): RBI is a department under the Ministry of Finance.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: Section 7 of the RBI Act, 1934 empowers the Central Government to issue directions to the RBI in matters of public interest, after consultation with the RBI Governor. RBI is a statutory body established under the RBI Act, 1934.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The 'Clean Note Policy' was announced by the Reserve Bank of India in the year ______.
questions.explanation: 1999. The objective of the Reserve Bank's Clean Note Policy is to give the citizens good quality currency notes and coins while the soiled notes are withdrawn out of circulation.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In which year was the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) established in India?
questions.explanation: 1992 . Securities Appellate Tribunal was mainly established to hear an appeal against the order passed by the SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) or by an adjudicating officer under the SEBI Act, 1992.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In which year was the State Bank of India created following the passage of the Imperial Bank of India into state ownership ?
questions.explanation: 1955. The State Bank of India - Headquarters - State Bank Bhawan, Nariman Point, Mumbai.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India also acted as the central bank for _______ till April 1947.
questions.explanation: Central bank for Burma. Burma (Myanmar) seceded from the Indian Union in 1937 but the Reserve Bank continued to act as the Central Bank for Burma till the Japanese Occupation of Burma and later up to 1947.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: ________ is the money which is accepted as a medium of exchange because of the trust between the payer and the payee.
questions.explanation: Fiduciary money. Credit money refers to a future monetary claim against an individual who has used the credit facility to buy goods and services. Full-bodied money refers to any unit of money, whose intrinsic value and face value are equal. Navratna /Maharatna/PSUs

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Match the column:| Column A (Status Category) Column B (Public Sector Enterprise) A. Maharatna 1. Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited B. Navratna 2. Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation C. Miniratna 3. Steel Authority of India Limited

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following public sector enterprises falls under the status ‘Maharatna’ ?
questions.explanation: Maharatna Company : Steel Authority of India Limited, Bharat Heavy Electricals, Bharat Petroleum Corporation, Coal India, GAIL India, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation, Indian Oil Corporation, NTPC, Oil & Natural Gas Corporation, Power Finance Corporation, Power Grid Corporation of India, Rural Electrification Corporation, Oil India.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched ?
questions.explanation: Airport Authority of India – Navratna. The government has divided all the Public Sector Undertakings mainly in three categories namely Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna. Airport Authority of India is a Miniratna.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of public sector industry in India?
questions.explanation: Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited. The public sector is the part of the economy that is owned and managed by the government, including government-controlled enterprises. BHEL is a government-owned company that specializes in manufacturing electrical equipment. It was established in 1964. Other PSUs: Steel Authority of India Ltd (SAIL), ONGC, and OIL etc.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of private sector industry in India?
questions.explanation: Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO). Jamsetji Tata founded TISCO on August 26, 1907 in Jamshedpur, Jharkhand. Headquarters - Mumbai (Maharashtra). In 2005, TISCO changed its name to Tata Steel Ltd.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Correctly match the following. Type of Industries Name of Company 1. Public sector a. Tata Iron and Steel Company 2. Private sector b. Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited 3. Joint sector c. Oil India Ltd
questions.explanation: 1-b, 2-a, 3-с. Public sector companies are owned by the government like NTPC Limited, Power Grid Corporation of India, Steel Authority of India Limited etc. Private sector companies are owned by individuals or private groups like Infosys, Wipro, etc. Joint sector industries are owned and operated by the state and individuals or a group of individuals. Maruti Udyog Limited is the example of the joint sector industry.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is a joint sector industry in India ?
questions.explanation: Oil India Limited (OIL). OIL (Maharatna Company) is a state-owned enterprise of the Government of India, under the administrative control of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. It was incorporated in 1959. Headquarters - Noida. National Aluminium Company Limited (NALCO) established in 1981. Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) founded by Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata and established by Sir Dorabji Tata in 1907 in Jamshedpur. Dabur was founded by Dr. SK Burman in 1884.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Identify which of the following statements are correct. 1. Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL) was incorporated on 9 November 1967. 2. The Khetri Copper Complex (KCC) is located in Rajasthan. 3. The headquarters of Mineral Exploration Consultancy Ltd. is located in Jaipur.
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL) - a public sector undertaking (under the administrative control of the Ministry of Mines). Headquarters - Kolkata. The headquarters of Mineral Exploration Consultancy Ltd. is located in Nagpur.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: ONGC _____ is a subsidiary of the Indian public sector enterprise, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation.
questions.explanation: Videsh. ONGC Videsh is a subsidiary of the Indian public sector enterprise, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation and it is working globally for the energy security of India. International Organizations

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What role did the WTO membership (1995) play in India's post-reform globalization strategy?

options.b: Deepened India's integration into global trade

questions.answer_text: Deepened India's integration into global trade
questions.explanation: India’s decision to become a founding member of the WTO in 1995 was a key step in its post-1991 economic reforms. By joining, India accepted global trade rules requiring lower tariffs, removal of non-tariff barriers, and market liberalization, marking a shift from protectionism. In return, India gained predictable access to global markets, boosting both imports and exports. This move also encouraged foreign investment and strengthened India’s integration into the global economy.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following institutions conducts the survey on employment and unemployment?

options.b: National Institution of Economic and Social Research
options.c: National Council of Applied Economic Research

questions.explanation: National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO). It is the largest independent organisation since 1950 in the country for conducting the socio-economic survey.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The analysis of the interrelationship between the economy and the environment in the economic environmental accounting system was put forward by______ .
questions.explanation: United Nations Statistical Office. The System of Environmental Economic Accounting (SEEA) - A statistical system that measures the condition of the environment, the contribution of the environment to the economy and the impact of the economy on the environment.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) seeks to ‘Protect, restore and promote sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, sustainably manage forests, combat desertification, and halt and reverse land degradation and halt biodiversity loss’ ?
questions.explanation: SDG 15. SDG 12: Ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns. SDG 7 focuses on global efforts to ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The UN’s Sustainable Development Goal 6 aims to ______.

options.a: ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages
options.b: ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all
options.c: end poverty in all forms everywhere
options.d: take urgent action to combat climate change and its impact

questions.answer_text: ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all
questions.explanation: SDG 1 - end poverty in all forms everywhere. SDG 13 - take urgent action to combat climate change and its impact.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) focuses on:

options.a: Developing industrial clusters in backward regions

questions.explanation: The Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) is an Indian government initiative launched in 2018 by NITI Aayog to transform 112 socio-economically underdeveloped districts into engines of growth and opportunity through data-driven governance, convergence, collaboration, and healthy competition.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The PM-MITRA scheme is focused on which of the following objectives?

options.b: Enhancing textile exports and setting up large textile parks
options.d: Providing smart classrooms in rural schools

questions.answer_text: Enhancing textile exports and setting up large textile parks
questions.explanation: The PM-MITRA scheme (Pradhan Mantri Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel) was launched by the Government of India to establish seven world-class integrated textile parks across the country. Its main aim is to strengthen the textile value chain, from spinning, weaving, processing, dyeing, printing to garment manufacturing, thereby boosting textile exports, employment, and investment. These parks are planned with modern infrastructure, common facilities, and plug-and-play systems to make Indian textiles more competitive globally.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) focuses on:

options.c: Developing industrial clusters in backward regions

questions.explanation: Enhancing development in underdeveloped districts. The Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP), launched in January 2018, seeks to rapidly transform 112 under-developed districts. Its strategy rests on Convergence, Collaboration, and Competition, driven by states and district administrations. Districts are ranked monthly on 49 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) under 5 themes—Health & Nutrition, Education, Agriculture & Water Resources, Financial Inclusion & Skill Development, and Infrastructure.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which government scheme aims to phase out unfit and polluting vehicles from India's roads to reduce emissions and boost automotive industry recycling ?
questions.explanation: Voluntary Vehicle Fleet Modernisation Programme : Launched in 2021, this is also known as the Vehicle Scrappage Policy. It aims to phase out unfit, old, and polluting vehicles, reduce air pollution, and promote the automobile recycling industry. Vehicles failing fitness and emission tests are to be deregistered. The policy introduces fitness testing through Automated Fitness Centres. Personal vehicles older than 20 years and commercial vehicles older than 15 years must undergo fitness checks. Incentives include scrappage value, road tax rebate, and registration fee waiver for new vehicles purchased after scrapping.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

options.a: Mission Shakti - Startup grants for rural men
options.b: PM-AAGY - Railway safety in backward areas

questions.explanation: Swadesh Darshan 2.0 is a central government scheme aimed at developing sustainable and theme-based tourist circuits across India to enhance visitor experiences and promote local economies. Mission Shakti is a women-centric empowerment initiative, PM-AAGY focuses on village development in aspirational districts (not railway safety), and PM-JANMAN is focused on tribal development but not specifically on urban housing.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following statements are correct about the PM MITRA Scheme? 1. It aims to establish integrated large-scale textile parks. 2. It is implemented by the Ministry of Textiles. 3. The scheme promotes synergy among textile value chain segments.
questions.explanation: The PM Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel (PM MITRA) Scheme, launched by the Ministry of Textiles, aims to establish 7 world-class textile parks in India. These parks will integrate the entire textile value chain “from farm to fashion”, helping reduce costs, attract investment (domestic & FDI), boost exports, create jobs, and promote Aatmanirbhar Bharat. Sites of 7 PM MITRA Parks: Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following schemes provides annual income support to farmers directly into their bank accounts?
questions.explanation: PM-KISAN. Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) was launched in February 2019. It provides direct income support of ₹6,000 per year to all eligible farmer families. The amount is transferred in three equal installments of ₹2,000 directly into farmers’ bank accounts through DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer). PM Fasal Bima Yojana - Crop insurance scheme against natural calamities, not direct income support. MGNREGA - Provides guaranteed wage employment (rural job scheme), not income support for farmers specifically. PM Jan Dhan Yojana - A financial inclusion scheme to provide bank accounts, not income support.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is the central objective of Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 scheme?

options.a: Strengthening early childhood care and nutrition delivery systems

questions.answer_text: Strengthening early childhood care and nutrition delivery systems
questions.explanation: Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 is an umbrella scheme launched by the Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD) in 2021–22 by merging: Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS), Poshan Abhiyaan, Scheme for Adolescent Girls (SAG), National Creche Scheme. Its core objective is to: Provide supplementary nutrition to children, pregnant women, and lactating mothers. Strengthen early childhood care, health, and nutrition delivery systems through modernized Anganwadis. Address the problems of malnutrition, stunting, and wasting among children.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What are the three components of the empowerment model in SAPAP of SHGs ?

options.a: Social mobilisation, economic development, and education
options.b: Collective empowerment, capital formation, and poverty eradication
options.c: Public resource allocation, capacity building, and microfinance
options.d: Social mobilisation, capital formation, and capacity building of the poor

questions.answer_text: Social mobilisation, capital formation, and capacity building of the poor
questions.explanation: The SAPAP model of SHG (Self Help Groups) is also known as the International Model. In 1995, SAPAP piloted 20 poor mandals of Andhra Pradesh. The SAPAP model contemplated the process of social mobilization as an institutional mechanism to mobilise the poor into SHGs (Self Help Groups). SAPAP is implemented in collaboration with local NGOs and state governments. This is also a microfinance plus model.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is the main objective of the DWCRA model of SHGs?

options.a: To provide education opportunities for rural children
options.b: To provide housing support for rural families
options.c: To provide self-employment opportunities for rural women
options.d: To provide healthcare services to rural women

questions.answer_text: To provide self-employment opportunities for rural women
questions.explanation: The Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas (DWCRA) scheme, a sub-scheme of IRDP launched in 1982–83, aimed to provide self-employment opportunities to rural women, especially those belonging to BPL families. It is funded jointly by the Centre and States in a 50:50 ratio.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: When was the Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme for Least Developed Countries (LDCs) announced by India?
questions.explanation: 2008. Duty Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) scheme of 2008 : Prime Minister Manmohan Singh announced the DFTP scheme at the India-Africa Forum Summit on April 8, 2008. India became the first developing country to extend this facility to Least Developed Countries (LDCs).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: When was the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana introduced to provide health insurance to people below the poverty line?
questions.explanation: 2008. Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) has been launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment. Objective: To provide protection to BPL households from financial liabilities arising out of health shocks that involve hospitalization. Other related schemes in India aimed at improving healthcare access: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (2018), and National Rural Health mission (2005).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Match the following items. List I List II i. Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya Scheme a. 1994 ii. Mid-Day Meal Scheme b. 2004 iii. The National Accreditation Assessment Council c. 1945 iv. All India Council for Technical Education d. 1995 (a) i (b), ii (d), iii (a), iv (c) (b) i (d), ii

options.d: , ii (c), iii (d), iv (a) (d) i (c), ii (d), iii (b), iv (a)

questions.explanation: i (b), ii (d), iii (a), iv (c). The Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya (KGBV) is a government-run residential school for girls from weaker sections of society. The Mid-Day Meal Scheme (MDM) provides free, nutritious meals to school children across India.
