The National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) accredits higher education institutions, while the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) oversees technical education under the Department of Higher Education.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the primary objective of the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act of 2006 in India ?

options.b: To focus on large-scale industries only
options.c: To increase import tariffs to protect MSMEs
options.d: To promote and facilitate the development of MSMEs

questions.answer_text: To promote and facilitate the development of MSMEs
questions.explanation: Currently, MSMEs (Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises) are defined under the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006. The Act classifies them as micro, small and medium enterprises based on: (i) investment in plant and machinery for enterprises engaged in manufacturing or production of goods, and (ii) investment in equipment for enterprises providing services.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The RBI launched the Lead Bank Scheme (LBS) to mobilise deposits and step-up lending to weaker sections of the economy. When was the scheme launched?
questions.explanation: 1969. The Lead Bank Scheme was introduced on the basis of the recommendations of both the Gadgil Study Group and Banker's Committee (Nariman Committee). It envisages assignment of lead roles to individual banks for the districts allotted to them. The Nariman Committee endorsed the idea of an ‘Area Approach’ in its report (November 1969), that each bank should concentrate on certain districts where it should act as a 'Lead Bank'.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Assertion (A): The SHG–Bank Linkage Programme has become the largest microfinance project in the world. Reason (R): NABARD introduced it in 1992 to promote rural credit through group savings and bank linkage.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: NABARD is a statutory body established in 1982 under the Parliamentary act - National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act, 1981. The Self Help Group – Bank Linkage Programme Project has blossomed into the world's largest microfinance project. Under this programme, banks were allowed to open savings accounts for SHGs.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following government initiatives focuses on skill development to reduce open unemployment among youth in India?

options.b: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)

questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) was launched in 2015 with the objective to deliver skills to the youth of the country through Short Term Training (STT) and Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: ‘NISHTHA’ stands for _________.

options.a: National Initiative for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Assessment
options.b: National Inauguration for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Advancement
options.c: National Initiative for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Advancement
options.d: National Inauguration for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Assessment

questions.answer_text: National Initiative for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Advancement
questions.explanation: NISHTHA was launched on 21st August, 2019 by the Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education to improve learning outcomes at the Elementary level.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are FALSE about the Special Economic Zones (SEZs) of India? i. One of the main objectives of the Zones Act was promotion of exports of goods and services. ii. The Government of India announced the Special Economic Zones (SEZs) Policy in the year 2011. iii. The SEZ Rules provided for different minimum land requirement for different classes of SEZs.
questions.explanation: Only ii. SEZs are to have world class facilities: electricity, water, roads, transport, storage, recreational and educational facilities. Companies who set up production units in the SEZs do not have to pay taxes for an initial period of five years. The SEZ Act was passed in 2005 and came into force along with the SEZ Rules in 2006.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the National Investment and Manufacturing Zones (NIMZs) of India?

options.a: A special purpose vehicle will be constituted to take care of the functioning of NIMZs.
options.b: The state government will provide power connectivity, water and other infrastructural facilities.
options.c: It prescribes a minimum area of 10000 hectares for establishing NIMZs.
options.d: At least 30% of the total land area proposed for the NIMZ is to be utilized for manufacturing units.

questions.answer_text: It prescribes a minimum area of 10000 hectares for establishing NIMZs.
questions.explanation: National Investment and Manufacturing Zones (NIMZs) are special areas in India that aim to attract investments and promote manufacturing. They provide good infrastructure and support for businesses. Focus Areas of NIMZ: To provide a conducive environment for businesses to operate. To attract investment from domestic and foreign companies. Nodal ministry - The Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The government notified the National Manufacturing Policy (NMP) in 2011.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Sukanya Samriddhi Account (SSA) : 1. It was launched in 2015 under the Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao campaign. 2. The maximum deposit allowed in one financial year is ₹1.5 lakh. 3. It can be opened for a girl child until she attains 12 years of age. Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. The Sukanya Samriddhi Account (Girl Child Prosperity Account) is a Government of India-backed savings scheme. The scheme encourages parents to save for the future education and marriage of their daughters. It was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 22 January 2015 as part of the Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao campaign. The minimum deposit is ₹250, and the maximum deposit is ₹1.5 lakh in a financial year. The account can be opened in the name of a girl child until she attains the age of 10 years.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: How much percentage of the capital of MUDRA is contributed by SIDBI?
questions.explanation: 100. The Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA) was set up in 2015, as a wholly owned subsidiary of the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI). MUDRA provides refinancing support to financial institutions for lending to micro and small enterprises. The categorised loans: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh), and Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹20 lakh).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (2005) provides work for how many days?
questions.explanation: 100. The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), passed in September 2005, is a labor law that guarantees the 'Right to Work' and was officially launched on 2 February 2006. Initially proposed by P.V. Narasimha Rao in 1991, its name was changed from NREGA to MGNREGA on 2 October 2009.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The ‘Urban Self Employment Programme’ and the ‘Urban Wage Employment Programme’ are the two special components of which poverty alleviation programme of India?
questions.explanation: The Self-Employment Scheme run by the Central government provides financial and educational benefits to its citizens. It motivates them to be self-employed.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following schemes adopts the One District One Product (ODOP) approach to reap the benefit of scale in terms of procurement of inputs, availing common services and marketing of products?

options.b: Micro and Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP)
options.c: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMF ME)
options.d: Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI)

questions.answer_text: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMF ME)
questions.explanation: PMFME: Launched in 2020. It is a centrally sponsored initiative. It was launched by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) in India under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In which year did the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare of India launch the Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation (WIFS) program to meet the challenge of high prevalence and incidence of anaemia among adolescent girls and boys (56% girls and 30% boys) ?
questions.explanation: 2012. WIFS: Objective - To reduce the prevalence and severity of nutritional anaemia in adolescent population (10-19 years).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: How many cities are covered under the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) scheme?
questions.explanation: 500. AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation) scheme launched on 25th June 2015. Ministry - Housing and Urban Affairs.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: When was the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) launched ?
questions.explanation: 2008. The PMEGP scheme is implemented by Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC). Aim - To provide continuous and sustainable employment.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The government of India launched a new programme called the New India Literacy Programme (NILP) for five years, from FY's ________ to _______ with a budget of ₹1,037.90 crores.
questions.explanation: 2022-23 to 2026-27. New India Literacy Programme (NILP) - Aims to cover a target of 5 crore non-literates in the age group of 15 years and above.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following schemes aims to provide an integrated property validation solution for rural India ?
questions.explanation: SVAMITVA (Survey of Villages Abadi and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas): Launched on April 24, 2020, which is also celebrated as National Panchayat Day.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Twenty Point Programme (TPP) : 1. It was launched in 1975. 2. The programme was revised in 1982, 1986, and 2006. 3. The main objective is to improve urban infrastructure. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. The 3rd statement is incorrect. The primary objective of the Twenty Point Programme is the eradication of poverty and the improvement of the quality of life for the poor and underprivileged, with a significant focus on rural areas.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following options best describes the objective of Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY) Scheme, 2016?

options.a: To provide financial assistance to entrepreneurs
options.b: To provide free healthcare services to the unemployed
options.c: To provide employment opportunities for rural women
options.d: To encourage employers to create new jobs

questions.answer_text: To encourage employers to create new jobs
questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY). Objective - To incentivise employers for creation of employment. Nodal Ministry - Ministry of Labour and Employment.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following programmes of the Government of India aims to provide connectivity to unconnected habitations as part of a poverty reduction strategy?

options.a: Prime Minister Rural Development Fellows Scheme

questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) : Launched by Atal Bihari Vajpayee in 2000. Ministry - Ministry of Rural Development. National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) - Launched in 2011.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the full form of MEDP ?
questions.explanation: National Bank For Agriculture And Rural Development (NABARD) since 2006, has been supporting need-based skill development programmes (MEDPs) for matured SHGs which already have access to finance from Banks.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana is for Indian citizens in the age group of ___________ .
questions.explanation: 18 to 50 years. Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY): Launched: 9 May 2015. It is a life insurance plan that has to be renewed every year, which is provided with the benefits of the insurance plan in case of death due to any reason.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Rural Backyard Piggery Scheme was launched by which state government?
questions.explanation: Meghalaya. The Scheme is aimed to ensure the farmers earn a sustainable livelihood through different livestock farming activities. Launched on - 10th August 2022.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP) was launched in ___ .
questions.explanation: 1995. The Khadi & Village Industries Commission (KVIC) launched the Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP) on 1st April, 1995 for generation of two million jobs under the KVI sector in the rural areas of the country.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Stand Up India scheme aims at supporting entrepreneurship to _________ community of India
questions.explanation: Scheduled caste (SC). Stand Up India scheme: Launched on 5th April 2016 (by the Ministry of Finance), For financing schedule caste, schedule tribe and women Entrepreneur.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: LPG subsidy to domestic consumers under PAHAL Scheme is given by _______.

options.a: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
options.b: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

questions.answer_text: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
questions.explanation: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. PAHAL (Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh) scheme - Direct benefit Transfer for LPG. It was launched on June 1, 2013. The scheme aims to reduce diversion and eliminate duplicate or bogus LPG connections. This scheme is acknowledged as the world's largest cash transfer program (households) by the Guinness Book of World Records.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Under the Atal Pension Yojana, the pension returns are given after the subscriber turns ________ .
questions.explanation: 60. The Atal Pension Yojana (APY) was launched on 09 May 2015. In this Scheme, pensioners would receive the guaranteed minimum monthly pension of Rs 1000 and maximum Rs 5000 at the age of 60 years. The age of the subscriber should be between 18 - 40 years.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The National Family Benefit Scheme was started in August ______ by the Government of India.
questions.explanation: 1995. Launched under the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP). Restricted to BPL families. ₹ 20000/- will be given as a lump sum assistance to such surviving members of the household of the deceased poor, who after local inquiry, is found to be the head of the household.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The UMEED Scheme of Rural Livelihoods Mission is providing help to the aspirations of rural women in the Union Territory, who aspire to become economically independent.
questions.explanation: Jammu and Kashmir. UMEED Scheme - Launched in 2018 and was sponsored by the central government under the Jammu Kashmir State Rural Livelihood Mission (JKSRLM). Aim - To encourage women to be self dependent and self sufficient.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: PM SVANidhi Scheme aims to empower _________ .
questions.explanation: Street Vendors. The PM Street Vendor’s Atma Nirbhar Nidhi Scheme - It was launched on 1st June 2020 is a micro credit scheme for urban street vendors that aims to provide collateral-free working capital loans up to ₹50,000.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Start Up India Scheme which aims at developing an ecosystem that promotes and nurtures entrepreneurship across the country was launched in ____.
questions.explanation: 2016. Start Up India Scheme - Under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) was launched in_________.
questions.explanation: 1999. Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana focused on poverty alleviation by setting up a large number of Micro enterprises in rural areas of our country. It is an employment generation programme in India.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an initiative by the government for development of the microfinance sector in India ?
questions.explanation: Pradhani Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (Launched in 2014 by the Ministry of Finance). Aim - To provide banking facilities to all the families across the country by opening bank accounts for every family.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements: Statement I: The objective of "Growth with Social Justice & Equality" was introduced in the 10th Five-Year Plan. Statement II: The first Five-Year Plan was based on the "Harrod-Domar model". Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.a: Statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct
options.b: Both statements I and II are correct
options.c: Both statements I and II are incorrect
options.d: Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect

questions.answer_text: Statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: The Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997–2002) had the central theme of “Growth with Social Justice and Equality”, aiming to balance rapid growth with equitable distribution of benefits. The Tenth Plan (2002–2007) targeted 8% GDP growth (achieved 7.6%) and focused on reducing poverty with monitorable goals. The First Five-Year Plan (1951–1956), based on the Harrod–Domar model, emphasized savings, investment, and agricultural development to tackle food shortages and inflation. Its targeted growth was 2.1%, but it achieved a much higher 3.6%.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: How did India's trade policy reforms post-1991 impact the import of capital goods?

options.a: Linked capital imports only to foreign companies

questions.explanation: India’s trade policy reforms initiated in 1991 marked a significant shift towards liberalization and globalization. One of the key changes was the relaxation of restrictions on the import of capital goods—such as machinery and equipment used in production. The government reduced import tariffs and eliminated licensing requirements for many items, making it easier and more cost-effective for domestic industries to access modern technology and equipment from abroad. This move was aimed at improving industrial productivity and integrating the Indian economy with global markets.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Read the below statements: Statement I: The Sixth Five-Year Plan aimed at income growth and modernization of technology through various schemes. Statement II: The Third Five-Year Plan failed due to various factors such as wars, rupee devaluation and food crisis. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?

options.a: Both statements I and II are incorrect
options.b: Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect
options.c: Statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct
options.d: Both statements I and II are correct

questions.answer_text: Both statements I and II are correct
questions.explanation: Both statements I and II are correct. The Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980–85) focused on achieving economic growth, modernization of technology, reducing poverty, and strengthening infrastructure. It emphasized income growth, modernization, and poverty eradication through schemes like Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP). The Third Five-Year Plan (1961–66) targeted self-reliance and agriculture development, but it failed mainly because of the Sino-India war of 1962, Indo-Pak war of 1965, severe droughts (leading to food crisis), and the devaluation of the rupee in 1966.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The Drought Prone Area Programme (DPAP) for providing employment to people in drought prone areas was started by the Government of India during the _______.
questions.explanation: Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969 - 74): Objective - Growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance. It was introduced under the Prime Ministership of Indira Gandhi. The government nationalized 14 major Indian Banks and the Green Revolution boosted agriculture. Implementation of Family Planning Programmes. The target growth rate was 5.7%, but the actual growth rate was 3.3%. Joseph Stalin was the first person to introduce a five year plan in the Soviet Union. India borrowed features of the Five-year plan from the USSR.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Match the Five-Year Plan with its emphasis : Plan Emphasis A. Fifth Plan 1. Poverty alleviation and 'Garibi Hatao' B. Seventh Plan 2. 'Food, work, and productivity' C. Sixth Plan 3. Industrial growth and energy development
questions.explanation: A-1, B-2, C-3. Seventh Plan (1985-90): It focused on accelerating food grain production, increasing employment opportunities, and raising productivity with an emphasis on "food, work, and productivity." It was quite successful, achieving a 6% growth rate, surpassing the target of 5%, especially during a time when the 1980s were trying to overcome the so-called "Hindu Rate of Growth."

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the second five-year plan is INCORRECT ?

options.a: The plan stressed the rapid industrialisation of heavy and basic industries.
options.b: Electricity, Railway, Steel etc. industries were established during the plan.
options.c: The plan was based on the Keynesian Model.
options.d: The socialist pattern of the society was reflected in the plan.

questions.answer_text: The plan was based on the Keynesian Model.
questions.explanation: The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961) was based on the Mahalanobis model, named after Indian statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis. The target growth rate was set at 4.5%, while the actual growth achieved was 4.3%.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The five-year plans for India with their duration are given below. Which of the following is correctly matched? (a) Second five-year plan 1956 - 57 to 1960 - 61 (b) Third five-year plan 1961- 62 to 1965 - 66 (c) Fourth five-year plan 1966 - 67 to 1970 - 71
questions.explanation: Both a and b. The First Five-Year Plan was launched in 1951. The Second Plan (1956-1961), known as the Mahalanobis Plan, had a target growth rate of 4.5% and achieved 4.3%. The Third Plan (1961-1966) aimed to make the economy self-sufficient. Due to the Indo-China war, Indo-Pakistan war, and severe droughts, a "Plan Holiday" was observed from 1966 to 1969. The Fourth Plan (1969-1974), under Indira Gandhi, focused on growth and included Family Planning Programmes.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following statements are true? i. The First Five-Year Plan was based on the PC Mahalanobis model. ii. The First Five-Year Plan laid emphasis on agriculture development. iii. The Five-Year planning model in India was borrowed from Russia.
questions.explanation: Only ii and iii. The First Five-Year Plan (1951 - 1956) was based on the Harrod-Domar model, and focused on sectors like agriculture, price stability, power, and transport to address food shortages and promote economic growth. The Mahalanobis model, focused on industrialization, was introduced in the Second Five-Year Plan (1956 - 1961).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct ?

options.a: The five-year plan focuses mostly on private intervention in the economy.
options.b: The five-year plan always focused on the growth of the tertiary sector.
options.c: The five-year plan permits long-term intervention by the government in the economy.
options.d: A five-year plan always stresses market-oriented activities.

questions.answer_text: The five-year plan permits long-term intervention by the government in the economy.
questions.explanation: The Five Year Plans were formulated, implemented and regulated by a body known as the Planning Commission. The National Development Council (NDC) was the final authority to approve Five Year Plans (FYPs). The Five-Year Plans in India were primarily focused on government intervention, not private intervention, although some plans did encourage private sector participation. It focused on the growth of all sectors depending on the needs of the economy. Five-Year Plans were not always focused on market-oriented activities.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Fifth Five-Year Plan: 1. It was launched in 1974 and ended in 1978. 2. The plan’s main focus was the 'Garibi Hatao' initiative for poverty alleviation. 3. Its targeted growth rate was 6%. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. The Fifth Five-Year Plan was introduced for the period 1974 to 1979. However, the newly elected Morarji Desai government terminated the plan a year ahead of schedule in 1978. The Fifth Five-Year Plan laid significant stress on poverty alleviation (Garibi Hatao), employment generation, and justice. The targeted growth rate for the Fifth Five-Year Plan was 4.4%.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The Harrod Domar model was the main idea behind the ____ Five Year Plan.
questions.explanation: First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) aimed for a growth rate of 2.1% but achieved 3.6%. It focused on agriculture, investing in dams and irrigation, with significant funds allocated for the Bhakra Nangal Dam. Third Five Year Plan (1961-66) aimed to establish India as a self-reliant and self-generating economy.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of these is NOT among the reforms related to agriculture undertaken under the five year plans ?

options.a: Introduction of the policy of land to the tiller'
options.c: Launch of the high yielding variety seed technology

questions.explanation: Formation of Rent Authority Department. The first five-year plan (1951-56) the highest priority was accorded to increase agricultural production.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following years were considered plan holidays in Independent India?
questions.explanation: 1966-1969. This period was a gap between the Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966) and the Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974). During this time, there was no formal five-year plan, and the government focused on annual plans to address the economic challenges faced by the country.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following options is INCORRECT?

options.a: The Planning Commission of India was set up in 1950.
options.b: India borrowed the idea of five-year plans from the former Soviet Union.
options.c: The chairmanship of the Planning Commission of India was given to the Prime Minister.
options.d: Distinguished economists from India and abroad were invited to advise on India's economic development during the first five-year plan period.

questions.answer_text: Distinguished economists from India and abroad were invited to advise on India's economic development during the first five-year plan period.
questions.explanation: India's Five-Year Plans (FYPs) were centralized national economic programs initiated after independence, with the first plan starting in 1951. Influenced by Prime Minister Nehru's socialist vision, the Planning Commission was established in March 1950 to oversee these plans.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Match the integrated steel plants with the foreign countries that helped in their setup : Steel Plant Country A. Bhilai 1. United Kingdom B. Durgapur 2. Soviet Union (USSR) C. Rourkela 3. Germany
questions.explanation: A-2, B-1, C-3. The three steel plants at Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela were established with the help of the Soviet Union (USSR), Britain (United Kingdom) and Germany respectively.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The 10th Five-Year Plan aimed at reducing poverty by :
questions.explanation: 5%. The Tenth Five-Year Plan was from 2002 to 2007, under the leadership of Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Manmohan Singh. Target Growth - 8% and Actual Growth - 7.6%. The first five-year plan in India was launched in 1951 and since then, India has witnessed twelve Five Year Plans.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Assertion (A): Education was not considered one of the four primary explicit goals of Five-Year Plans. Reason (R): The primary goals focused on Growth, Equity, Self-reliance, and Removal of poverty.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: The model of the Indian Economy was premised on the concept of planning based on five year plans from 1951-2017. The Five Year Plans were formulated, implemented and regulated by a body known as the Planning Commission. Plan and Aim/Goal : First Plan (Economic development), Second Plan (Rapid industrialization - heavy & basic industries), Third Plan (‘Self-reliant' and ‘self-generating' economy), Fourth Plan (Growth with stability and progressive achievement of self reliance), Fifth Plan (‘Removal of poverty’ and 'attainment of self reliance').

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which Five Year Plan period saw the initiation of the Hill Area Development Programme?
questions.explanation: Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-1979) was terminated in 1978 by the Morarji Desai government. Key initiatives during this period included the amendment of the Electricity Supply Act (1975), the launch of the Twenty-point Program, the Minimum Needs Programme (MNP), and the Indian National Highway System. The Planning Commission, which formulated and regulated these plans, was established on March 15, 1950, and replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Growth, as envisaged in the five-year plans, refers to :

options.a: increase in the country’s capacity to produce the output of goods and services within the country
options.b: improvement in the state of equity in the country
options.c: improvement in the level of education and primary health in the country
options.d: self-reliance in producing all goods and services it requires, within its geographical boundaries

questions.answer_text: increase in the country’s capacity to produce the output of goods and services within the country
questions.explanation: The goals of the five year plans (FYP) were growth, modernisation, self-reliance and equity. India launched a series of FYP after independence to build its economy and attain development. The FYP was formulated, implemented and regulated by the Planning Commission, and was replaced by a think tank called NITI AAYOG in 2015.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Match the following Prime Ministers of India with the Five - Year Plans they initiated. List - 1 (Prime Ministers) List - 2 (Five-Year Plans) i. Jawaharlal Nehru a) Second Five-Year Plan ii. Manmohan Singh b) Tenth Five-Year Plan iii. Atal Bihari Vajpayee c) Eleventh Five-Year Plan
questions.explanation: i-a, ii-c, iii-b. Five year plans and Prime Ministers and : First (1951-56) - Jawaharlal Nehru. Second (1956-1961) - Jawaharlal Nehru. Third (1961-1966) - Jawaharlal Nehru. Plan Holidays (1966-1969). Fourth (1969-1974) - Indira Gandhi. Rolling Plan (1978-1980). Fifth Plan (1974-79) - Indira Gandhi. Sixth (1980-1985) - Indira Gandhi. Seventh (1985-1990) - Rajiv Gandhi. Annual Plans (1990–1992). Eighth (1992-1997) - P. V. Narasimha Rao. Ninth (1997-2002) - Atal Bihari Vajpayee. Tenth (2002-2007) - Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Manmohan Singh. Eleventh (2007-2012) - Manmohan Singh. Twelfth (2012-2017) - Manmohan Singh and Narendra Modi.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Before the launch of which Five-Year Plan did India introduce structural adjustment policies?
questions.explanation: Eighth Five-Year Plan (1992 - 97) : Target Growth 5.6 %, Actual Growth 6.8%. Introduction of fiscal & economic reforms including liberalisation under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri P V Narasimha Rao. Adoption of Indicative Planning (1st Adopted in France).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The five-year plans in India laid down not only specific objectives to be attained in the five years of a plan, but also what was to be achieved over a period of 20 years. This long-term plan is called a _________ .
questions.explanation: Perspective plan. The Idea of Planning as a process of rebuilding the economy gained prominence in the 1940s-50s. Joseph Stalin was the first person to implement the Five-Year Plan in the Soviet Union in 1928. The model of the Indian Economy was premised on the concept of planning based on five-year plans from 1951-2017.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In which Five-year plan was the following statement quoted? “The urge to bring economic and social change under present conditions comes from the fact of poverty and inequalities in income, wealth and opportunity”.
questions.explanation: First Five year plan (1951- 56) - Its president was Jawaharlal Nehru and Vice-president was Gulzarilal Nanda.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Five-Year Plans during the 2000s: 1. The Tenth Plan aimed to double per capita income in 10 years. 2. The Eleventh Plan’s main theme was “rapid and more inclusive growth”. 3. The global financial crisis occurred during the Eleventh Plan. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2 and 3. Eleventh Five Year Plan (2007-2012) - Under the leadership of Manmohan Singh. Its main theme was “rapid and more inclusive growth”. Tenth Five Year Plan (2002 to 2007) - Under the leadership of Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Manmohan Singh. This plan aimed to double the Per Capita Income of India in the next 10 years. Ninth Plan (1997 - 2002) : This Plan focussed on “Growth With Social Justice & Equality”.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the reasons why the public sector played a dominant role in establishing the Industrial sector in India post - Independence ?

options.a: Poor savings capacity of the public
options.b: To avoid generation of private profit
options.c: Absence of large enough market for output
options.d: Lack of adequate capital with private industrialists

questions.answer_text: To avoid generation of private profit
questions.explanation: In 1950, a Planning Commission was established by the government to formulate and implement effective economic development policies. The "mixed economy" model was embraced, where the State and private sector collaborated to boost production and employment. Indian Economy : Central Problems and Planning

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: Which of the following is a key reason for the decline in the agricultural sector in India after 1991 economic reforms ?

options.a: Rising minimum support prices for all crops
options.b: Greater protection through higher import duties
options.c: Shift toward export-oriented cash crops and reduced public investment
options.d: Increased investment in irrigation and rural infrastructure

questions.answer_text: Shift toward export-oriented cash crops and reduced public investment
questions.explanation: Shift toward export-oriented cash crops and reduced public investment. After 1991 economic reforms (LPG – Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation), India opened its economy to world trade and markets. Agriculture faced decline due to : Shift from food crops to export-oriented cash crops (cotton, sugarcane) — made farmers dependent on global price fluctuations. Reduced public investment in irrigation, rural credit, research, and extension services. Decline in subsidies for fertilizers, electricity, and irrigation. Increased import competition due to WTO agreements. Rising cost of inputs — debt burden on farmers. Agricultural growth became slower compared to industry and services.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: Which Indian state was the first to benefit from the Green Revolution?
questions.explanation: Punjab. The Green Revolution in India, led by M.S. Swaminathan in the 1960s, marked a major shift in agriculture. It introduced high-yielding seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, and irrigation techniques, mainly for wheat and rice. Punjab was the first state to benefit, followed by Haryana and Western Uttar Pradesh.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: How did Second Generation Reforms impact foreign investment in India?

options.b: It had no impact on foreign investment
options.c: It restricted foreign companies from entering India
options.d: It increased foreign investment by improving the investment climate

questions.answer_text: It increased foreign investment by improving the investment climate
questions.explanation: The Second Generation Reforms of the late 1990s and early 2000s emphasized financial liberalization, tax reforms, privatization, and infrastructure development. Building on the 1991 reforms, they created a stable and transparent business environment, improved governance, and eased restrictions. As a result, India attracted higher FDI inflows, technology transfer, and global corporate participation.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: What was the primary impact of the 'License Raj' system on industrial growth in India before 1991 ?

options.a: It created entry barriers, hindered expansion, and fostered inefficiency.
options.b: It led to efficient resource allocation and increased competition.
options.c: It ensured balanced regional development and prevented monopolies.
options.d: It promoted rapid industrial diversification and innovation.

questions.answer_text: It created entry barriers, hindered expansion, and fostered inefficiency.
questions.explanation: The License Raj system in India before 1991 created a restrictive framework of licenses and regulations for industries. Businesses needed government approval for almost every activity, which slowed down growth. This led to inefficiency, corruption, and lack of competition in the economy. Innovation and consumer choice were severely limited under this bureaucratic control. As a result, India’s industrial growth remained sluggish compared to other Asian nations.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: What was the main occupation of the majority of the Indian population during the period immediately after independence (around 1947)?
questions.explanation: Agriculture, immediately after independence, was the backbone of the Indian economy, providing livelihood to nearly 70–75% of the population. Industrialization was still in its early stages, and sectors like information technology and large-scale services were practically non-existent. Most rural families depended on farming, animal husbandry, and related activities for survival, making agriculture the dominant occupation in post-independence India.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: Which key reform in 1991 specifically addressed the inefficiency of public sector enterprises and promoted competition in industrial production?
questions.explanation: Privatization of profit-making PSUs. In the 1991 economic reforms, privatization was a major step to address inefficiencies in public sector enterprises. Many PSUs were overstaffed, uncompetitive, and suffered losses. By allowing disinvestment and reducing the government’s direct control, competition increased and private players entered industrial production. This reform, along with liberalization and globalization, marked a shift towards a market-oriented economy.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: The regulatory framework adopted by India between 1947 and 1990, often referred to as the "License Raj," aimed to direct economic activity. While it had certain intended benefits, what was a significant unintended negative consequence often associated with this system?

options.a: A rapid increase in the quality and global competitiveness of Indian-made goods due to stringent quality control measures
options.b: The fostering of a highly competitive market environment with numerous players in each industry.
options.c: The creation of barriers to entry for new businesses potentially stifling innovation and leading to inefficiencies.
options.d: A significant reduction in corruption and bureaucratic delays in obtaining necessary approvals for economic activities.

questions.answer_text: The creation of barriers to entry for new businesses potentially stifling innovation and leading to inefficiencies.
questions.explanation: The "License Raj" required extensive government permissions to start or expand a business, which created significant hurdles for new entrepreneurs. This system protected established players from competition, leading to monopolies, reduced innovation, and widespread economic inefficiencies as there was little incentive to improve quality or lower costs.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: Which of the following steps promoted the growth of the economy as a whole by stimulating the development of industrial and tertiary sectors?
questions.explanation: Planning. After independence, India adopted a planned economy, which was primarily aimed at boosting industrialization and service sectors. The Five-Year Plans were introduced to guide and stimulate growth in various sectors. These plans included infrastructure development, the establishment of industries, and the expansion of services, all of which contributed to the overall economic growth.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: What is the primary benefit offered to businesses in Special Economic Zones (SEZs) ?
questions.explanation: Tax and duty concessions. The incentives and facilities offered to the units in SEZs for attracting investments into the SEZs, including foreign investment include :- Duty free import/domestic procurement of goods for development, operation and maintenance of SEZ units.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: Which industrial policy marked the beginning of liberalisation in the Indian industry, reducing the restrictions on private companies?
questions.explanation: Industrial Policy 1991. It was introduced as part of the broader economic reforms initiated by the government of P.V. Narasimha Rao, with Dr. Manmohan Singh as the Finance Minister. This policy marked a paradigm shift from the previous regime of licenses, permits, and regulations to a more open and market-oriented economy. Important features included : Abolition of industrial licensing for most industries, Liberalization of foreign technology agreements, and Abolition of the MRTP Act (Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: Which of the following sectors in India faces seasonal unemployment?
questions.explanation: Agriculture. Seasonal unemployment occurs when people are jobless during specific seasons when labor demand is low. It arises from a mismatch between the skills of the workforce and those required for available jobs.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT associated with the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 ?

options.b: A system of licenses for the private sector was introduced.
options.c: It classified industries into three categories.
options.d: It formed the basis of the Third Five Year Plan.

questions.answer_text: It formed the basis of the Third Five Year Plan.
questions.explanation: The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 formed the basis for the Second Five Year Plan, which aimed to build the foundation for a socialist pattern of society. IPR was the first comprehensive statement on India's industrial development.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: Which of the following is more important to promote modernisation and overall prosperity of a country ?
questions.explanation: Stable employment - ensures that a significant portion of the population has a steady income, which drives consumption, improves living standards, and supports economic growth.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: Which of the following options is the most appropriate cause for unemployment in India ?
questions.explanation: Over population leads to a surplus of labor in the job market, often outpacing the availability of jobs, which contributes significantly to unemployment. In India, the estimated Unemployment Rate on usual status for persons of age 15 years and above was 4.2%, 4.1% and 3.2% during 2020-21, 2021-22 and 2022-23, respectively as per the Annual PLFS Reports.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: Which of the following is the socio-economic objective of Industrial Policy Statement 1980 ?

options.b: Consumer protection against high prices and bad quality

questions.explanation: All of the above. Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 : It aimed to accelerate economic growth and promote industrialization for a socialist society, with comprehensive revisions made after the Constitution's adoption. To address new challenges, it was further modified through statements in 1973, 1977, and 1980. Industrial Policy Statement of 1980 : It aimed for higher employment generation, consumer protection, promotion of export-oriented industries, encouragement of small-scale and cottage industries, regional balance and decentralization, and self-reliance through import substitution.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: What were the main obstacles during the industrial development of India at the time of independence?
questions.explanation: Capital investment in industries. At independence, India faced challenges like illiteracy, poverty, low per capita income, industrial backwardness, and unemployment. The government implemented industrial policies that marked a turning point in India's industrial history.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948 mainly categorised the large-scale industries into ________ fragments.
questions.explanation: Four. The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 was India's first major policy document on industries after independence. It was announced by Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee, the then Industry Minister, in the Parliament on April 6, 1948. Four categories: Exclusive monopoly of central government, New undertaking undertaken only by the state, Industries to be regulated by the government, Open to private enterprise, individuals and cooperatives.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: Which of the following was a feature of the Indian economy before the British rule?
questions.explanation: Independent economy. A prosperous economy is a successful system of trade and industry that usually earns a lot. A self-reliant economy is an economy that is less dependent on other countries and does not require aid from outside the country. Economic dependence in the context of a country's economy refers to a situation where a nation heavily relies on another country or countries for its economic growth and development.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of globalisation?

options.b: Restrictions on expansion of public sector

questions.explanation: Liberalisation of import licensing. Globalization is the integration between countries through foreign trade and foreign investments by multinational corporations (MNCs). Peter Sutherland is known as the 'father of globalization'. Globalization in India (1991) was done by Manmohan Singh under leadership of PV Narasimha Rao. The three main pillars of Reform were : Liberalization, Globalization, and Privatization.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: With progressive delicensing of industries as part of liberalisation, which of the following is the industry that is removed from the requirement of license?

options.a: Cigars and cigarettes of tobacco, and manufactured tobacco substitutes

questions.explanation: Coal and lignite. Mineral Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2020 provides that prior approval of the central government will not be required by the state government in granting licenses for coal and lignite. Industries subject to compulsory licensing in India: Tobacco items, Defense aerospace and warships, Hazardous chemicals, Industrial explosives.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: The main worker is a person who works for at least _______ days in a year.
questions.explanation: 183 (or six months). The population of India according to their economic status is divided into three groups, namely; main workers, marginal workers (who work less than 183 days) and non-workers. The proportion of workers (both main and marginal) is only 39.8 percent (2011) leaving a vast majority of about 60 percent as non-workers.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: Which of the following states has the largest net - out migrants ?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh. A net out-migrant state is one where more people migrate out of the state than those that migrate into the state. As of 2011, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar were the largest source of inter-state migrants while Maharashtra and Delhi were the largest receiver states. Around 83 lakh residents of Uttar Pradesh and 63 lakh residents of Bihar had moved either temporarily or permanently to other states. Around 60 lakh people from across India had migrated to Maharashtra by 2011.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: _________ is a state of deprivation that reflects the inability of an individual to satisfy basic needs for a sustained, healthy and reasonably productive living.
questions.explanation: Poverty. Ignorance : This refers to a lack of knowledge, information, or awareness about a particular subject or situation. Bondage : This refers to the condition of being a slave or being in a state of servitude.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: ______ unemployment refers to the time lag between jobs when an individual is searching for a new job or is switching between jobs.
questions.explanation: Frictional. Seasonal Unemployment : Unemployment due to seasonal fluctuations in industries (e.g., winter tourism). Technological Unemployment : Unemployment caused by technological advancements replacing jobs. Structural Unemployment : Long-term unemployment due to fundamental changes in the economy (e.g., industry decline).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: Which of the following types of unemployment arises from a mismatch between the jobs available in the market and the skills of the available workers in the market?
questions.explanation: Structural. Frictional unemployment occurs when workers transition between jobs while searching for new opportunities. Seasonal unemployment happens when workers are jobless during certain seasons, especially in agriculture, tourism, and retail. Disguised unemployment occurs when more workers are employed than needed, leading to reduced productivity, commonly seen in agriculture and family businesses.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: Which of the following was NOT an advantage of privatisation?

options.c: Additional source of revenue for the government

questions.explanation: Privatization generally aims to enhance competition by allowing private entities to enter markets, which can lead to improved efficiency and innovation. The other options listed are commonly recognized advantages of privatization.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: The Suresh Tendulkar committee was formed in 2005 for_________.
questions.explanation: Poverty estimates. Other committees : Sukhamoy Chakravarty Committee (1985) - Examined issues related to monetary policy and economic reforms. Chelliah Committee (1991) - Recommended economic reforms and liberalization policies. Janaki Ballabh Patnaik Committee (2005) - Reviewed the implementation of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA).

questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: What is the percentage of people below the poverty line in India according to Government of India, planning commission 2013 ?
questions.explanation: 21.92%. According to the Planning Commission, the percentage of people below the poverty line in urban areas was 13.7% in 2011-12, while in rural areas it was 25.7%. The current methodology for poverty estimation is based on the recommendations of an Expert Group to Review the Methodology for Estimation of Poverty (Tendulkar Committee) established in 2005.

questions.subject: Economics

questions.explanation: 21.81%. Poverty is measured based on consumer expenditure surveys of the National Sample Survey Organisation. options.a: Large industrial houses availed licences to prevent competition

options.d: Many small private firms appropriated licences

questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct? I. The Family Welfare Program has sought to promote responsible and planned parenthood on a mandatory basis. II. questions.explanation: II only. The Family Welfare Programme (launched in 1952) seeks to promote responsible and planned parenthood through voluntary (not on a mandatory basis) choice of family planning methods.

questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: The poverty line in India is normally estimated ______ by conducting sample surveys.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: The system of MSP (Minimum Support Price) was first introduced for ______ in 1966-67 and later expanded to include other essential food crops.
questions.explanation: Wheat. Minimum Support Price (MSP) is a form of market intervention by the Government of India to insure agricultural producers against any sharp fall in farm prices. Crops covered by MSPs include: 7 types of cereals (paddy, wheat, maize, bajra, jowar, ragi and barley), 5 types of pulses (chana, arhar/tur, urad, moong and masoor), 7 oilseeds (rapeseed-mustard, groundnut, soyabean, sunflower, sesamum, safflower, niger seed), 3 commercial crops (cotton, copra, raw jute,). Fair Remunerative Prices￾Sugarcane.

questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: The national poverty line for 2011-12 was estimated at____ per capita per month for urban areas of India.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: In India, what type of unemployment is created due to lack of employable skills among the educated youths in India?
questions.explanation: Educated unemployment. Structural unemployment - It is a category of unemployment arising from the mismatch between the jobs available in the market and the skills of the available workers in the market. questions.question: Formula to find the unemployment rate is .
questions.explanation: (Unemployed workers/Total labour force) × 100. Statistics on unemployment in India had traditionally been collected, compiled and disseminated once every ten years by the Ministry of Labour and Employment (MLE).

questions.question: Which among the following types of unemployment is also known as the real wage unemployment?
questions.explanation: Classical. Real wage unemployment occurs when wages are set above the equilibrium level causing the supply of labour to be greater than demand.

questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: In pre-independent India, who was the first person to discuss the concept of the poverty line?

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct with respect to the poverty line? I. In India, it is normally estimated after every ten years. II. The proportion of people below the poverty line is not the same for all social groups and economic categories in India.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.chapter_name: Indian Economy: Central Problems and Planning
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of E-Commerce?
questions.explanation: E-Commerce is a business model that lets firms and individuals buy and sell things over the Internet. Disadvantage : chance of fraudulent financial transactions and loss of sensitive financial information. Stock, Debentures and Foreign Trade

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In the context of India's trade policies between 1947 and 1990, what was a common characteristic of the approach towards imports?

options.a: Promoting imports as a way to boost domestic competition.
options.b: Primarily focusing on the import of luxury goods and consumer durables.
options.c: Following a strategy of import substitution to protect domestic industries.
options.d: Encouraging unrestricted import of all goods.

questions.answer_text: Following a strategy of import substitution to protect domestic industries.
questions.explanation: Following a strategy of import substitution to protect domestic industries. In the period 1947–1990, India pursued a development strategy centered on self-reliance. The trade policy emphasized import substitution industrialization (ISI): Imports of consumer goods and non-essential items were restricted. Only capital goods, technology, and essential raw materials were allowed in a controlled manner. High tariffs, quotas, and licensing created a protected domestic market, reducing foreign competition. The aim was to encourage domestic industries to grow by insulating them from international competition.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Read the following statements about Trade Policy Reform: Statement I: Trade policy reform in India involved removing quantitative restrictions on imports and exports. Statement II: Trade policy reform increased import licensing to support domestic manufacturers.

options.a: Both statements I and II are correct
options.b: Both statements I and II are incorrect

questions.explanation: Statement I – Correct. The 1991 Economic Reforms (Liberalization) brought major changes in trade policy. Quantitative restrictions (QRs) on imports/exports were gradually removed. Import licensing was dismantled, tariffs were reduced, and India moved towards a more open economy. Statement II – Incorrect . Instead of increasing import licensing, reforms aimed at abolishing or reducing licensing requirements. The idea was to shift from a protectionist regime to a competitive, liberalized trade environment.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of investment ?

options.b: Money spent on purchasing shares of a company
options.c: Machinery and equipment employed by a firm
options.d: Inventories of raw materials stocked by a firm

questions.answer_text: Money spent on purchasing shares of a company
questions.explanation: Buying shares of a company- It is not deemed an investment as it does not directly enhance productive capacity. Share purchase grants ownership in the company but not in its capital goods, which the company might acquire with share-sale funds.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The country can improve its balance of payments by devaluation when the sum of elasticity of demand for exports and imports is .
questions.explanation: Greater than unity. It is called the Marshall-Lerner condition in economics. If the domestic currency devalues, imports become more expensive, and exports become cheaper due to the change in relative prices. Balance of Payment (BoP) : It is a statement of all transactions made between entities in one country and the rest of the world over a defined period, such as a quarter or a year. Two main accounts in the BoP: Current account - It includes a nation's net trade in goods and services. Capital account - It consists of a nation's transactions in financial instruments and central bank reserves.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The index titled SENSEX of BSE (erstwhile Bombay Stock Exchange) is an index of trading of top ____companies in terms of their volume of trade and their share prices.
questions.explanation: thirty. The full form of SENSEX is the Stock Exchange Sensitive Index. Published on 1 January 1986, the BSE SENSEX is regarded as the pulse of the domestic stock markets in India.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In which year was the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) enacted to replace the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) ?
questions.explanation: 1999. The Parliament has enacted the Foreign Exchange Management Act,1999 to replace the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973. This Act came into force on the 1st day of June, 2000.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Bombay Stock Exchange became the first stock exchange in India to launch commodity derivatives contracts in gold and ______.
questions.explanation: silver. BSE was established in 1875 by cotton merchant Premchand Roychand and is located in Dalal Street, Mumbai. It is the oldest Stock Exchange in Asia. It is the first stock exchange of Asia. The Dutch East India Company (founded in 1602) was the first joint-stock company to get a fixed capital stock.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What challenge does foreign investment often face in India?
questions.explanation: Inconsistent regulatory environment can lead to difficulties in compliance and planning for investors, ultimately affecting their confidence and willingness to invest in the country. Foreign investment refers to when an investor from one country purchases ownership of an asset or business in another country.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the balance of trade of a country?
questions.explanation: Difference between imports and exports. The Balance of Trade (BoT) is the difference between a country's exports and imports over a specific period, typically a year. Conditions of BoT : (i) If exports > imports, the country has a trade surplus (positive balance). (ii) If imports > exports, the country has a trade deficit (negative balance).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is the most traditional mode of entering into the foreign market?

options.d: Setting up fully owned manufacturing facilities

questions.explanation: Exporting involves the sale of domestically produced goods to international buyers. It allows companies to expand their reach with low risk and investment. Exporting can take various forms, including direct sales and online platforms, and is often the first step for businesses seeking to internationalize.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Special Drawing Rights are also known as ________.
questions.explanation: Paper Gold. The SDR (Special Drawing Rights) is an international reserve asset. The SDR is not a currency, but its value is based on a basket of five currencies - the US dollar, the euro, the Chinese renminbi, the Japanese yen, and the British pound sterling. SDR created by the IMF in 1969. The SDR serves as the unit of account of the IMF and other international organizations. Fiscal Policy and Monetary Policy

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the primary objective of a government's fiscal policy ?

options.a: To control the money supply and interest rates.
options.b: To promote international trade and maintain a favorable balance of payments.
options.c: To influence aggregate demand and economic activity through government spending and taxation.
options.d: To regulate the stock market and financial institutions.

questions.answer_text: To influence aggregate demand and economic activity through government spending and taxation.
questions.explanation: The primary objective of a government's fiscal policy is to manage and influence the nation's economy. This is achieved mainly through two instruments: adjusting government spending levels and altering tax rates. The overarching goal is to foster stable and sustainable economic growth by managing aggregate demand. Key aims include stabilizing the economy during fluctuations, promoting long-term growth, and maintaining full employment. Ultimately, fiscal policy is a crucial tool for a government to steer its country's economic direction and achieve macroeconomic stability.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: During the period of 1947-1990, India's trade policy was largely characterized by:

options.a: An inward-looking strategy emphasizing import substitution and protection of domestic industries.
options.b: A policy of free trade with minimal government intervention in international transactions.
options.c: A liberal import policy aimed at providing consumers with a wide range of goods.
options.d: An aggressive export-oriented strategy focused on global competitiveness.

questions.answer_text: An inward-looking strategy emphasizing import substitution and protection of domestic industries.
questions.explanation: After independence, India adopted a planned economic development model with a focus on self-reliance. The trade policy emphasized import substitution – producing goods domestically instead of importing them. High tariffs, quotas, and licensing requirements were imposed to protect domestic industries from foreign competition. This approach limited foreign trade and kept India relatively isolated from the global economy until the 1991 economic reforms, which shifted towards liberalization, privatization, and globalization (LPG).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which indicator in EODB (Ease of doing business) measures the time and cost to resolve commercial disputes?
questions.explanation: Enforcing contracts. In the Ease of Doing Business (EODB) Index, enforcing contracts evaluates the time, procedures, and cost required to resolve a commercial dispute through courts. This indicator highlights the efficiency and reliability of the judicial system in safeguarding business agreements. Effective enforcement reduces risks, builds investor confidence, and strengthens trust in the legal framework. Other indicators deal with permits, electricity, or trade, but contract resolution is exclusively measured under this category.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following was a major criticism of the industrial policy followed in India during 1950-1990?

options.b: Creation of a protected market leading to inefficiency and lack of innovation.

questions.answer_text: Creation of a protected market leading to inefficiency and lack of innovation.
questions.explanation: The industrial policy of 1950–1990 was based on a mixed economy model with heavy state control. It had certain achievements (building a strong industrial base, growth of public sector, self-reliance in some sectors), but it also faced criticisms: The system of industrial licensing (License Raj) restricted private entry and innovation. Heavy protection through tariffs, quotas, and import substitution led to a protected domestic market. Industries had little incentive to improve efficiency or innovate, since competition (both domestic and foreign) was minimal. Public sector monopolies became inefficient and loss-making over time.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What does 'repo rate' refer to in India's monetary policy?

options.b: Rate at which the government borrows from banks
options.c: Rate at which consumers take loans
options.d: Rate at which commercial banks borrow from the RBI

questions.answer_text: Rate at which commercial banks borrow from the RBI
questions.explanation: Rate at which commercial banks borrow from the RBI. Repo rate (Repurchase rate) is the rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) lends short-term money to commercial banks against the collateral of government securities. It is a key instrument of monetary policy used to control liquidity, inflation, and credit availability in the economy. If RBI increases repo rate → borrowing becomes costlier → money supply contracts → inflation controlled. If RBI reduces repo rate → borrowing becomes cheaper → liquidity increases → boosts growth.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following measures can be adopted by the government to reduce revenue deficit?
questions.explanation: Tax reforms. A revenue deficit occurs when a business' sales or government revenue isn't enough to cover its basic operations. The fiscal deficit in the economy will be zero if there is no provision for borrowings in the budget. A budget deficit occurs when expenses exceed revenue, and it can indicate the financial health of a country.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Reserve ratio and money supply have ________ relationship.
questions.explanation: a negative. As the reserve ratio increases, the money supply decreases, and vice versa. The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is the percentage of a bank's Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) that must be maintained as cash reserves with the central bank. Quantitative tools of monetary policy - SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio), Repo rate, Reverse Repo Rate, Bank Rate.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is a selective credit instrument?
questions.explanation: Credit rationing. It means limiting the availability of credit in the market. It is a qualitative measure through which the central bank fixes the credit limit for different business activities in the economy. The variable reserve ratio is a monetary policy tool that central banks use to control credit and the money supply in the economy. It's made up of two components: the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) and the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The Flexible Inflation Targeting Framework (FITF) was introduced in India post the amendment of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Act, 1934 in_______.
questions.explanation: 2016. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Act, 1934, was amended to provide a statutory basis for the Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) framework. FIT is a monetary policy strategy employed by the RBI to maintain inflation within a specified range, allowing for flexibility. This approach enhances stability and transparency in monetary policy decisions.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the main objective of Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBMA), 2003 ?
questions.explanation: To reduce fiscal deficit. The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act is a law enacted by the Government of India in 2003 to ensure fiscal discipline – by setting targets including reduction of fiscal deficits and elimination of revenue deficit. Enacted - 26 August 2003. Introduced by Mr. Yashwant Sinha.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: _____is defined as excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings during a fiscal year.
questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit is the difference between the government’s total expenditure and its total receipts excluding borrowing. The gross fiscal deficit is a key variable in judging the financial health of the public sector and the stability of the economy. Gross Primary Deficit is the fiscal deficit minus interest payments on previous borrowings.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Intervention by the monetary authority of a country in the money market to keep money supply stable against exogenous or sometimes external shocks is called _____.
questions.explanation: Sterilisation. It refers to the actions taken by a monetary authority, such as a central bank, to offset the effects of foreign exchange operations on the domestic money supply. For instance, if a central bank experiences an inflow of foreign exchange, it might conduct an open market sale of government securities to absorb the excess money and maintain the stability of the money supply. This process helps to protect the economy from external shocks and prevent inflationary or deflationary pressures.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the impact of proportional taxes?

options.a: Increases the marginal propensity to consume

questions.explanation: Proportional taxes reduce the autonomous expenditure multiplier because taxes reduce the marginal propensity to consume out of income. Marginal propensity to consume (MPC) is the fraction of additional income that a person or household spends. When taxes increase, disposable income decreases, which in turn reduces the MPC.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is a revenue deficit in the government budget?

options.a: The excess of expenditure over revenue, excluding interest payments on debt
options.b: The excess of expenditure over revenue, including interest payments on debt
options.c: The excess of revenue over expenditure, excluding interest payments on debt
options.d: The excess of revenue over expenditure, including interest payments on debt

questions.answer_text: The excess of expenditure over revenue, including interest payments on debt
questions.explanation: A revenue deficit occurs when revenue falls short of covering day-to-day operational expenses. Revenue expenditure covers the costs of maintaining operations and generating revenue. Interest payments are compensation made by borrowers to lenders for using borrowed money.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The RBI act provides for how many members in RBI Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) ?
questions.explanation: 6. The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (RBI Act) has been amended by the Finance Act, 2016 to provide for a statutory and institutionalized framework for a MPC. MPC (Monetary Policy Committee) members: RBI Governor (chairperson), Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, An officer of the Bank to be nominated by the Central Board, Three persons to be appointed by the central government.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which deficit reflects the borrowing needs of the government?
questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit : The difference between total revenue and total expenditure of the government. Fiscal Deficit = Total expenditure of the government (Capital and Revenue expenditure) – Total income of the government (Revenue receipts + recovery of loans + other receipts).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the change in fiscal deficit if both the primary deficit and interest payments are doubled?
questions.explanation: Increase by 100%. Primary deficit - It is defined as the fiscal deficit of the current year minus interest payments on previous borrowings.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Gross primary deficit is equal to ________.

options.a: difference between gross fiscal deficit and interest payments
options.b: difference between total expenditure and total receipts
options.c: difference between net borrowings and net capital receipts
options.d: difference between revenue deficit and capital expenditure

questions.answer_text: difference between gross fiscal deficit and interest payments
questions.explanation: Gross Primary Deficit is Gross Fiscal Deficit less interest payments.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The general target of the monetary policy is to ensure ___________ . A. price stability in the economy B. greater tax collections for the government C. employment generation in the rural areas
questions.explanation: Only A. Monetary policy - Actions and strategies adopted by a central bank to control the money supply, interest rates, and credit availability in an economy, aiming to achieve stable prices and sustainable economic growth.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: In which year did the Government of India bring FRBM (Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management) Act into effect ?
questions.explanation: 2004-05. The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act 2003 envisages the setting of limits on the Central government’s debt and deficit. The Centre and states are mandated to reduce their fiscal deficit to 3 percent of GDP.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: ______refers to a method adopted by the Central Bank to persuade or convince the commercial banks to advance credit in the economic interest of the country.
