questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an electric cell symbol, what does the shorter and thicker line indicate?
questions.explanation: Negative terminal. The longer, thinner line represents the positive terminal. An electric cell is a device, which converts chemical energy into electrical energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct ?

options.a: Magnetic flux is a vector quantity.
options.b: Two magnetic field lines may intersect.
options.c: The net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero.
options.d: Earth's magnetic poles coincide with the geographic poles.

questions.answer_text: The net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero.
questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines are continuous loops, all closed surfaces have as many magnetic field lines going in as coming out. Hence, the net magnetic flux through a closed surface is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the net electric charge possessed by an electric dipole?
questions.explanation: 0. An electric dipole is a pair of equal and opposite charges, therefore the total charge in an electric dipole will be zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Why does a skilled cricketer move his hands backwards while catching a fast-moving ball?

options.a: To apply a greater opposing force on the ball for a quick stop.
options.b: To reduce the force by increasing the time over which momentum changes.
options.c: To increase the speed of the ball during impact.
options.d: To decrease the weight of the ball using gravity.

questions.answer_text: To reduce the force by increasing the time over which momentum changes.
questions.explanation: This is an application of Newton's Second Law of Motion, specifically the impulse-momentum theorem. The impulse (Force × time) is equal to the change in momentum (mass × change in velocity). When catching the ball, the change in its momentum (from its initial speed to zero) is constant. By moving his hands backward, the cricketer increases the time interval (Δt) over which this change in momentum occurs. Since the force of impact is inversely proportional to this time, increasing the time significantly reduces the average force exerted on the hands, preventing injury and making the catch easier.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Read the following statements carefully: Statement I: A pressure cooker operates by decreasing the pressure inside, which lowers the boiling point of water. Statement II: Food cooks faster in a pressure cooker because the higher pressure allows water to boil at a temperature above 100°C. Statement III: The superheated steam within the cooker increases the rate of heat transfer to the food, leading to faster cooking. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.a: Only II and III are correct
options.b: All I, II, and III are correct
options.c: Only I and II are correct
options.d: Only I and III are correct

questions.answer_text: Only II and III are correct
questions.explanation: Only II and III are correct. Statement I is incorrect because a pressure cooker increases, not decreases, the pressure inside. This is a basic principle of thermodynamics: increased pressure raises the boiling point of water, not lowers it. Statement II is correct — Under high pressure, water boils at temperatures above 100°C (usually around 121°C in a pressure cooker), allowing food to cook faster. Statement III is also correct — The superheated steam (steam at a temperature higher than 100°C) increases the rate of heat transfer to the food, making the cooking process faster and more energy-efficient.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of inertia at rest?

options.a: Falling down backward when a vehicle starts immediately
options.b: Falling down of dust particle while dusting a cloth
options.c: The detachment of leaves/fruits due to shaking
options.d: The sudden application of brakes in a vehicle

questions.answer_text: The sudden application of brakes in a vehicle
questions.explanation: The sudden application of brakes in a vehicle. Newton's First Law of Motion, also known as the law of inertia, states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force. Inertia is the body's resistance to changes in its state. Inertia of rest means a body at rest stays at rest until an external force acts on it. Inertia of motion means a body in motion continues moving until an external force stops it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: Frictional force can act only when there is contact between two surfaces. Statement II: Gravitational force requires direct physical contact to be applied. Options:

options.a: Both statements I and II are true
options.b: Both statements I and II are false
options.c: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
options.d: Statement I is false and Statement II is true

questions.answer_text: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
questions.explanation: Statement I is true because frictional force arises only when two surfaces are in contact with each other. It acts to oppose the motion or tendency of motion between them and is classified as a contact force. In contrast, Statement II is false because the gravitational force is a non-contact force—it can act even at a distance, such as the Earth attracting the Moon or objects falling due to Earth's gravity without touching them.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which metric unit of pressure is approximately equivalent to 0.986923 atm?
questions.explanation: Bar. questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: Galileo studied the motion of objects on inclined planes to understand how forces affect motion. Statement II: He concluded that in the absence of external forces, objects continue to move with constant speed. Statement III: This observation directly supported Newton’s Third Law of Motion. Options:

options.b: Only Statements I and II are correct
options.c: Only Statements II and III are correct

questions.answer_text: Only Statements I and II are correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct because Galileo conducted experiments with objects rolling down inclined planes to study motion. These experiments helped him isolate the effects of friction and gravity. Statement II is also correct; from these observations, Galileo deduced that when no external force acts on an object (such as friction), it continues to move at a constant speed—laying the foundation for Newton’s First Law of Motion, not the Third. Statement III is incorrect because Newton’s Third Law deals with action-reaction forces, not uniform motion.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Assertion (A): The force applied on a body for a very short duration is called impulse. Reason (R): Impulse is the product of pressure and time. Options:

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false.

Pressure relates to force distributed over an area, which is a different physical quantity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which law was developed in the 1600s to describe that any force applied to a confined fluid is transmitted equally in all directions, regardless of the shape of the container?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Post-tensioning is most suitable for which type of structural span?
questions.explanation: long spans. Post tensioning is a technique for reinforcing concrete, in which prestressing steel cables inside plastic ducts are positioned in the forms before the concrete is placed. Pretensioning - The technique in which we are imparting tension in strands before placing the concrete. It is more durable and reliable.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Select the option that is true regarding the following two statements labelled Assertion (A) and Reason (R). (A): An object slips less on a rough surface than a smooth surface. (R): When a surface is rough, frictional force increases.

options.a: Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false.

questions.answer_text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are the true and Reason (R) is a correct explanation of Assertion (A).
questions.explanation: Frictional force is the resistance encountered when two surfaces slide or attempt to slide against each other, resulting from the interaction between their roughness and molecular forces. Formula - F (friction force) = μ (coefficient of friction) × N (normal force). Normal Force - The force that surfaces exert to prevent solid objects from passing through each other.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Find the acceleration (in m/𝑠 ) of a 2 body which accelerates from 5 m/s to 10 m/s in 2 seconds.
questions.explanation: 2.5 m/sec2 . questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Assertion (A): A javelin thrown by an athlete follows a curvilinear path. Reason (R): The motion of the javelin is influenced by both the horizontal velocity and the vertical acceleration due to gravity.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: When a javelin is thrown, it travels in a curved path, known as curvilinear motion. This is because its motion is the result of two simultaneous components: a horizontal velocity (due to the force applied by the athlete) and a vertical motion (caused by gravitational acceleration). The combination of these two motions results in a parabolic trajectory. Therefore, the assertion is true. The reason correctly explains why the javelin follows a curvilinear path, as it is governed by the laws of projectile motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT pair regarding motion and their examples?

options.a: Translatory motion – A ball falling from the cliff
options.b: Periodic motion – Hands of a clock
options.c: Oscillatory motion – Earth moving around the sun
options.d: Rotatory motion – Blades of a fan

questions.answer_text: Oscillatory motion – Earth moving around the sun
questions.explanation: Oscillatory motion involves repeated back - and - forth movement around a fixed point, like a pendulum. Other examples : Oscillatory motion - Pendulum, swing, vibrating string. Periodic motion - Wave motion, planetary orbits. Rotatory motion - Merry-go- round, wheel rotation. Translatory motion - Car moving on a straight road, projectile motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Assertion (A): When two forces act in opposite directions on an object, the net force is the difference between the magnitudes of the two forces. Reason (R): The forces acting in opposite directions partially cancel each other, resulting in a net force equal to their difference.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: When two forces act on an object in opposite directions, they oppose each other. The net force on the object is calculated by subtracting the smaller force from the larger force, because the forces partially cancel each other out. This means the object experiences a net force equal to the difference between the two forces. Hence, the assertion that the net force is the difference between the magnitudes of the forces is true. The reason correctly explains this concept by stating that forces in opposite directions partially cancel, leading to the net force being the difference.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following equations correctly represents the relationship between force, mass, and acceleration?
questions.explanation: F = ma. Newton's second law is often stated as F = ma, which means the force (F) acting on an object is equal to the mass (m) of the object times its acceleration (a). This means the more mass an object has, the more force you need to accelerate it, and the greater the force, the greater the object's acceleration. SI unit of Force = Newtons (N).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: Force can change the direction of a moving object or cause it to start moving. Statement II: Force can increase the mass of an object. Options:

options.a: Both statements I and II are true
options.b: Both statements I and II are false
options.c: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
options.d: Statement I is false and Statement II is true

questions.answer_text: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct because a force can influence the motion of an object in several ways—it can set a stationary object in motion, change the speed of a moving object, or alter its direction. These are well-known effects of force as observed in daily life and explained by Newton’s laws of motion. On the other hand, Statement II is incorrect because force cannot increase or decrease the mass of an object. Mass is an intrinsic property of matter and remains constant regardless of the amount or direction of force applied.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The given equation provides the property of the motion of an object, traversing a circular path. What is 'v' in this equation ? (ac = v²/R)
questions.explanation: Speed. Centripetal acceleration - That is directed towards the center of the circle. It is caused by the change in direction of the velocity vector as the object moves around the circle. Centripetal Acceleration (ac) formula: ac = v 2/r (where v is the speed, r is the radius). Dimensional formula of centripetal acceleration = [ M0L 1T -2 ].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: A centripetal force is responsible for keeping an object moving in a circular path. Statement II: Centripetal force is also known as a center-seeking force.

options.a: Both statements I and II are true
options.b: Both statements I and II are false
options.c: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
options.d: Statement I is false and Statement II is true

questions.answer_text: Both statements I and II are true
questions.explanation: Statement I is true because centripetal force is the force that keeps an object moving in a circular path, always directed toward the center of the circle. It acts perpendicular to the motion of the object, preventing it from flying off in a straight line due to inertia. Statement II is also true because "centripetal" literally means "center-seeking," referring to the direction of the force.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is another name for Newton's first law of motion?
questions.explanation: Law of Inertia. Newton's first law of motion - A body remains in the state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line unless and until an external force acts on it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: Static friction prevents a stationary object from moving when a force is applied. Statement II: Static friction adjusts its magnitude in response to the applied force up to a certain maximum limit. Statement III: Kinetic friction is considered a self-adjusting force because it changes as the object moves. Options:

options.b: Only Statements I and II are correct
options.c: Only Statements II and III are correct

questions.answer_text: Only Statements I and II are correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct because static friction is the force that resists the initial motion of a stationary object. It keeps the object at rest until the applied force exceeds a certain limit. Statement II is also correct—static friction is self-adjusting, meaning it increases proportionally with the applied force up to a maximum threshold (called the limiting friction). Once this limit is crossed, the object begins to move. Statement III, however, is incorrect because kinetic friction (which acts when an object is already moving) has a relatively constant value and does not adjust itself like static friction does.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: Lubricants are substances that help in reducing friction between surfaces in contact. Statement II: Magnets are commonly used to reduce friction between moving mechanical parts.

options.a: Both statements I and II are true
options.b: Both statements I and II are false
options.c: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
options.d: Statement I is false and Statement II is true

questions.answer_text: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
questions.explanation: Statement I is true because lubricants such as oil, grease, or graphite are used between surfaces in contact to reduce friction. They create a thin film that allows smooth movement by minimizing direct contact between surfaces. Statement II is false because magnets are not typically used for reducing mechanical friction in general applications. While magnetic levitation exists in specialized systems (like maglev trains), it's not a standard method in everyday machinery.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A ball possesses 3000 units of momentum. What would be the ball's new momentum if its velocity was doubled?
questions.explanation: 6000 units. We know that Momentum is directly proportional to the object's mass (m) and velocity (v). Momentum (p) = mass (m) × velocity (v). And if velocity is doubled, momentum is also doubled. Hence momentum = 2 × 3000 = 6000 units.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between an object's mass and its inertia?

options.a: Greater the mass, greater the inertia
options.b: Lesser the weight, greater the inertia
options.c: Lesser the mass, greater the inertia
options.d: Greater the mass, lesser the inertia

questions.answer_text: Greater the mass, greater the inertia
questions.explanation: Greater the mass, greater the inertia. As inertia is directly proportional to the mass of the object (I = mr2 ) so Inertia will increase if mass increases. Inertia is defined as a property of matter by which it tries to maintain its state of rest or of uniform motion along a straight line. Types of Inertia include Inertia of Rest, Inertia of Motion and Inertia of direction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What type of motion does an object exhibit when it moves with a constant velocity?
questions.explanation: Uniform motion - When an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, then its motion is called uniform motion. Example - Motion of the blades of a ceiling fan. Non-uniform motion - Objects move with different speeds and do not cover equal distances in equal intervals of time. Example - Speed of train.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Pressure in a liquid is obtained by dividing thrust by which physical quantity?
questions.explanation: Area. Thrust acting per unit area is known as pressure i.e. Pressure = Thrust/Area.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: When a sailor jumps forward, the boat moves backward due to the third law of motion. Statement II: The recoil of a gun when a bullet is fired is an example of Newton’s third law. Statement III: A fielder pulling his hands backward while catching a ball is an example of the third law of motion.

options.b: Only Statements I and II are correct
options.c: Only Statements II and III are correct

questions.answer_text: Only Statements I and II are correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct because when a sailor jumps forward, the boat moves backward—a classic example of Newton’s third law of motion: "For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction." Statement II is also correct; when a gun fires a bullet, the forward motion of the bullet is accompanied by the backward recoil of the gun, another example of Newton’s third law. However, Statement III is incorrect. When a fielder pulls his hands back while catching a ball, it is done to increase the time of impact and reduce the force experienced—this illustrates the concept of impulse and Newton’s second law, not the third.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct order of friction ?
questions.explanation: Static > Sliding > Rolling. Static Friction : A force that hinders the movement of an object moving along the path. Sliding Friction : Resistance created by any two objects when sliding against each other. Rolling Friction : The force resisting the motion of a rolling body on a surface.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which scientific principle accounts for the thrust produced in rockets, jet engines, and even a deflating balloon?
questions.explanation: Newton’s laws of motion. Third Law is often given as an explanation for the generation of thrust (to every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The range of ______ force is of the order of 10−16 m.
questions.explanation: Weak Nuclear Force - Very Short 10-16 m, (Range), 10-13 (Relative Strength). Gravitational Force - Infinite (Range), 10-39 (Relative Strength), Electromagnetic Force - Infinite (Range), 10-2 (Relative strength), Strong Nuclear Force - Short Nuclear size 10-15m (Range), 1(Relative Strength).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following quantities changes with time when an object experiences acceleration?
questions.explanation: Velocity. Acceleration is defined as the rate at which an object changes its velocity. It is a vector quantity. Unit of acceleration is the metre per square second (𝑚/𝑠 ). 2

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If two forces act on an object from opposite directions, then the magnitude of the net force acting on it is the ______ of the magnitudes of the two forces.
questions.explanation: Difference. Net force is the sum total of all the forces which are acting on the body. Forces applied on an object in the same direction add to one another.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which property of sound determines its loudness ?
questions.explanation: Amplitude. The loudness of a sound is determined by the amplitude of its wave. A sound wave with a larger amplitude carries more energy and is perceived as a louder sound, while a wave with a smaller amplitude is perceived as a quieter sound. Wavelength: This is the distance between two consecutive crests or troughs of a wave. It is related to frequency and the speed of sound. Pitch: The pitch of a sound is determined by its frequency, which is the number of waves that pass a point in a certain amount of time. A higher frequency results in a higher pitch, and a lower frequency results in a lower pitch.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Read the following and choose the correct option: Assertion (A): Sound waves travel faster in steel than in air at the same temperature. Reason (R): The particles in solids (like steel) are more closely packed and experience stronger intermolecular forces compared to particles in gases (like air), allowing vibrations to be transmitted more efficiently and rapidly.

options.a: A is false but R is true.
options.b: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.c: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.d: A is true but R is false.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Speed of sound depends on the medium. It travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids, and slowest in gases. In air (gas): sound speed ≈ 343 m/s (at 20°C). In steel (solid): sound speed ≈ 5000–6000 m/s. The reason is correct: particles in solids are more closely packed with stronger intermolecular forces, enabling faster transfer of vibrations compared to gases where molecules are far apart.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: Sound can travel through a vacuum. Statement II: In human beings, the vibration of vocal cords produces sound. Options:

options.c: Statement I is true, but Statement II is false.
options.d: Statement I is false, but Statement II is true.

questions.answer_text: Statement I is false, but Statement II is true.
questions.explanation: Sound requires a medium (like air, water, or solid materials) to propagate, so it cannot travel through a vacuum—making Statement I false. In contrast, in human beings, sound is produced by the vibration of vocal cords, making Statement II true.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The loudness of a sound is directly proportional to which of the following mathematical functions of the amplitude of vibration?
questions.explanation: Square. The loudness of sound is expressed in the units called the Decibel. The symbol of the decibel is dB. The sound pressure level of audible sound ranges from 0 dB through 120 dB.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The branch of physics that deals with the production and propagation of sound waves is known as:
questions.explanation: Acoustics. Optics is the branch of physical science that deals with the properties and phenomena of both visible and invisible light. Photonics is the study of light and other types of radiant energy whose quantum unit is the photon. Astrophysics is a branch of space science that applies the laws of physics and chemistry to seek to understand the universe.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If an object executes 10 oscillations per second, then its frequency in kilohertz is equal to :
questions.explanation: 1 kilohertz = 1000 oscillation per second. 10 oscillation per second = = 0.01 kilohertz. 10 1000

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The sound of thunder is heard much later than the flash of light is visible. What does it represent?

options.a: The speed of sound is much less than the speed of light.
options.b: The speed of sound is three times the speed of light.
options.c: The speed of sound is twice the speed of light.
options.d: The speed of sound is equal to the speed of light.

questions.answer_text: The speed of sound is much less than the speed of light.
questions.explanation: The speed of sound in air is about 346 meters per second. Light travels at a speed of 300,000 km/s (186,000 mi/s) from a stationary source. Time taken by Light - Moon to Earth: 1.3 seconds and Sun to Earth (1 AU) : 8.3 minutes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: How long will a sound wave take to travel 1.5 km, which has a frequency of 5 kHz and wavelength of 6 cm?
questions.explanation: 5 seconds. Given that, Frequency (f) = 5 kHz = 5000 Hz. Wavelength (λ) = 6 cm = 0.06 m. Distance = 1.5 km = 1500 m. The speed (v) of a wave is given by: 𝑣 = frequency × wavelength 𝑣 = 5000 Hz × 0.06 m = 300m/s. The distance to be traveled is 1.5 km = 1500 m. Time = = 𝐷𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑒 𝑆𝑝𝑒𝑒𝑑 1500 𝑚 300𝑚/𝑠 = 5 seconds.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Assertion (A): In a longitudinal wave, the particles of the medium oscillate parallel to the direction of wave propagation. Reason (R): Sound waves in air are examples of longitudinal waves.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: A longitudinal wave is defined as a wave in which the particles of the medium vibrate back and forth parallel to the direction of wave propagation. Sound waves in air are an example of longitudinal waves because the air molecules oscillate in the same direction as the wave travels. Therefore, the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Among the given options, which one causes an echo?

options.b: When sound waves travel through a solid medium
options.c: When sound waves travel through a liquid medium
options.d: When sound waves travel through a vacuum

questions.explanation: When sound is reflected. Echo : The sound is heard more than once because of the time difference between the initial production of the sound waves and their return from the reflecting surface. Applications of echo - Measuring Depth and Height, Measuring Distance, Medical Diagnosis.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: At 25°C, sound travels fastest through which of the following materials?
questions.explanation: Aluminium. Speed of sound (meters/second) in different media at 25 ºC: Aluminium (6420 m/s), Nickel (6040 m/s), Steel (5960 m/s), Iron (5950 m/s), Brass (4700 m/s).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which force governs the motion of planets, stars, and galaxies ?
questions.explanation: Gravitational force. The gravitational force is a universal force that acts between all masses in the universe. It is the weakest among the four fundamental forces, but it has infinite range and dominates at large scales like planets, stars, galaxies, and even the entire universe. This force was explained by Newton’s Law of Gravitation and later refined by Einstein’s General Theory of Relativity, which showed that gravity is due to the curvature of spacetime caused by mass. Other forces (for context) : Nuclear force — Binds protons and neutrons in the nucleus (short-range). Magnetic force — Arises due to motion of charges, limited to smaller scales. Electromagnetic force — Governs interactions between charged particles, also infinite range but usually cancels out at cosmic levels.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to the Law of Periods, the square of a planet's time period is proportional to:

options.a: The square of its distance from the sun
options.b: The cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit
options.c: The square root of its orbital radius
options.d: The product of its mass and orbital speed

questions.answer_text: The cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit
questions.explanation: The cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit. Kepler’s laws of planetary motion state that (a) All planets move in elliptical orbits with the Sun at one of the focal points (b) The radius vector drawn from the Sun to a planet sweeps out equal areas in equal time intervals. This follows from the fact that the force of gravitation on the planet is central and hence angular momentum is conserved. (c) The square of the orbital period of a planet is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of the elliptical orbit of the planet The period T and radius R of the circular orbit of a planet about the Sun are related by T 2 = R 4π 3 2 𝐺𝑀 𝑠 ( )

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following quantities remains conserved when an object moves under the gravitational pull of another object?
questions.explanation: Gravity is a central force, meaning it always acts along the line connecting the two objects, which results in zero torque and thus the conservation of angular momentum. It is also a conservative force, which means the total mechanical energy (the sum of kinetic and potential energy) of the system remains constant, as no energy is lost to non-conservative forces like friction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which law states that the square of the orbital period of a planet is proportional to the cube of the radius of its orbit?
questions.explanation: Kepler's Third Law : The square of the period of revolution of any planet is directly proportional to the third power of the semi-major axis of the elliptical orbit of that planet. Bragg's Law : 2dsin(θ) = nλ, where, d (distance between crystal lattice planes), θ (Angle of incidence), n (Integer), λ is the wavelength of the X-rays. Copernicus’s Law : Proposed a heliocentric system, that the planets orbit around the Sun.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Who among the following was the first to conclude that in vacuum all objects fall with the same acceleration g and reach the ground at the same time?
questions.explanation: Galileo Galilei (father of observational astronomy, modern physics and the scientific method). He is known for observations of the Moon, phases of Venus, moons around Jupiter, sunspots.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the name of the scientific instrument that detected gravitational waves for the first time?
questions.explanation: LIGO (Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory) is a large-scale physics experiment and observatory to detect cosmic gravitational waves and to develop gravitational - wave observations as an astronomical tool.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two masses of 1 kg and 2 kg were dropped from a height of 3.2 metres. Their respective velocities just before touching the ground will be: (Assume acceleration due to gravity g = 10 m/s2 )
questions.explanation: 8 m/s for both. We can calculate the velocities of the two masses just before touching the ground using the equation of motion for free fall: 𝑣 = 2𝑔ℎ Where: v = velocity just before touching the ground g = acceleration due to gravity (10 m/s2 ) h = height from which the masses were dropped (3.2m) For both masses (1 kg and 2 kg), the velocity will be the same because the equation is independent of mass: v= 2✕10✕3. 2 ⇒ 𝑣 = 64 ⇒ 𝑣 = 8 m/s Hence, the velocities of both masses just before touching the ground will be 8 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: The universal law of gravitation explains the motion of the moon around the Earth. Statement II: Tides on Earth are caused by the gravitational pull of distant stars.

options.c: Statement I is true, but Statement II is false.
options.d: Statement I is false, but Statement II is true.

questions.answer_text: Statement I is true, but Statement II is false.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct because the motion of the moon around the Earth is governed by the gravitational force between them, which is accurately described by the universal law of gravitation. This law states that every object in the universe attracts every other object with a force that is directly proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. Statement II, however, is incorrect. Tides on Earth are mainly caused by the gravitational pull of the Moon and, to a lesser extent, the Sun—not by distant stars. The gravitational influence of distant stars on Earth's tides is negligible.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Assertion (A): The unit of acceleration due to gravity (g) is the same as that of acceleration. Reason (R): Acceleration due to gravity is a type of acceleration experienced by a body due to Earth's gravitational pull.

options.a: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
options.b: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
options.c: Assertion is true, but Reason is false.
options.d: Assertion is false, but Reason is true.

questions.answer_text: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
questions.explanation: The assertion is true because the acceleration due to gravity, denoted by g, has the same unit as acceleration, which is metres per second squared (m/s²). This is because gravity causes a change in the velocity of an object, just like any other acceleration. The reason is also correct, as g represents the acceleration experienced by a body under the influence of Earth's gravitational force. Since g is simply a specific type of acceleration, the reasoning directly explains why its unit matches that of acceleration in general.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Match Column A (Denudational Processes) with Column B (Their Driving Forces/Energy): Column A (Denudational Processes) Column B (Their Driving Forces/Energy) A. Weathering 1. Kinetic Energy B. Mass Movement 2. Gravitational / Molecular Stresses /Chemical Actions C. Erosion and Transportation 3. Gravitational Force D. Denudation (overall process) 4. External Forces acting on Earth surface

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which form of energy is exhibited by moving objects such as falling coconuts, speeding cars, rolling stones, and flying aircraft?
questions.explanation: Kinetic Energy - The energy an object has because of its motion. Radiant Energy : Energy of electromagnetic and gravitational radiation. Examples - Produce heat, light, rays. Elastic Energy : Energy stored in an object due to a force that temporarily changes its shape. Example - Compressed spring, archer's stretched bow.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What will be the average kinetic energy per molecule in SI units for an ideal gas at a temperature of 25°C ?
questions.explanation: 6.17 × 10-21 J. Average kinetic energy (KE) = 3 2 𝐾𝑇 Boltzmann constant is = K Temperature (T) = 25 0C Value of degree Celsius to Kelvin = T = 0C + 273 T = 25 + 273 ⇒ T = 298 K The value of Boltzmann constant (K) is 1.38 x 10-23 J/K Average KE = 3 2 𝐾𝑇 Average KE = (1.38 x 10-23 J/K) (298K) 3 2 Average KE = 6.17 x 10-21 J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy. Statement II: The energy stored in a battery is mechanical in nature.

options.c: Statement I is true, but Statement II is false.
options.d: Statement I is false, but Statement II is true.

questions.answer_text: Statement I is true, but Statement II is false.
questions.explanation: Statement I is true because a battery works by converting chemical energy into electrical energy through chemical reactions within its cells. This electrical energy is then used to power various devices. Statement II is false because the energy stored in a battery is not mechanical—it is chemical energy stored in the form of potential energy within chemical compounds.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Assertion (A): The lifting and lowering of an object are examples of oscillatory motion. Reason (R): Oscillatory motion refers to any motion that repeats itself in a regular time interval.

options.a: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
options.b: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
options.c: Assertion is true, but Reason is false.
options.d: Assertion is false, but Reason is true.

questions.answer_text: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
questions.explanation: The assertion is true because the lifting and lowering of an object, such as in an exercise or with a spring, represents oscillatory motion, where the object moves back and forth about a mean position. The reason is also true, as oscillatory motion is defined as a type of motion that repeats itself in a regular time interval, like the swinging of a pendulum or the vibration of a tuning fork. Since the lifting and lowering of an object fits this repetitive pattern, the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following formulas correctly represents the potential difference between two points in an electric circuit?
questions.explanation: V = W/Q . In an electrical circuit, the potential between two points (V) is defined as the amount of work done (W) by an external agent in moving a unit charge (Q) from one point to another.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Hydroelectric power stations generate electricity by using the force of water that falls into the turbines and spins the shaft. By rotating the shaft of the turbine, the potential energy of water is converted into ________ energy.
questions.explanation: Kinetic. In Hydropower plants, a turbine converts the potential energy of water into kinetic energy, the kinetic energy of falling water into mechanical energy and then a generator converts the mechanical energy into electrical energy. Largest Hydroelectric power station in India: Koyna Hydroelectric Project (Maharashtra); First: Sidrapong Hydroelectric Power Station (West Bengal).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Who coined the term "horsepower" to describe the output power of an engine?
questions.explanation: James Watt was a Scottish engineer and inventor. Watt defined one horsepower as the power required to lift 33,000 pounds by one foot in one minute, which is equivalent to about 746 watts. Albert Einstein was a physicist who is best known for his theory of relativity and the famous equation E = mc2 .

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If an object of mass 2 kg is dropped from a height of 10 metres, what will be the ratio of its potential energy and kinetic energy at the height of 5 metres (g = 10 m/sec2 )
questions.explanation: 1 : 1. When the object is dropped from a height of 10 meters, its potential energy (PE) is converted to kinetic energy (KE) as it falls. At the height of 5 meters, the object has lost half of its initial potential energy and has gained an equal amount of kinetic energy. Initial Potential energy (PE) = mgh = 2 kg × 10 m/s² × 10 m = 200 J At 5 meters, Potential energy (PE) = mgh = 2 kg × 10 m/s² × 5 m = 100 J Kinetic energy (KE) = Initial PE - PE = 200 J - 100 J = 100 J Ratio of PE to KE = 100 J : 100 J = 1:1

questions.subject: Physics

questions.subject: Physics

questions.subject: Physics

questions.subject: Physics

questions.explanation: Magnetic resonance imaging is a medical imaging technique used in radiology to form pictures of the anatomy and the physiological processes of the body. questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I : The photoelectric effect provides evidence for the particle nature of light. Statement II : In the photoelectric effect, light ejects electrons from a metal surface only when its intensity is high.

options.c: Statement I is true, but Statement II is false.
options.d: Statement I is false, but Statement II is true.

questions.answer_text: Statement I is true, but Statement II is false.
questions.explanation: Statement I is true because the photoelectric effect—where electrons are ejected from a metal surface when light of a certain frequency shines on it—supports the particle nature of light. It demonstrates that light behaves as if it is made up of discrete packets of energy called photons. Statement II is false because the ejection of electrons depends not on the intensity of light, but on its frequency. Even a very intense light will not cause electron emission if its frequency is below the threshold level.

questions.explanation: Spontaneous Radioactivity. Henri Becquerel shared the prize with Pierre and Marie Curie for their work on this radiation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I : Uranium-235 is commonly used as a fuel in nuclear power plants to generate electricity. Statement II : Uranium-235 undergoes nuclear fission, releasing a large amount of energy.

options.c: Statement I is true, but Statement II is false.
options.d: Statement I is false, but Statement II is true.

questions.explanation: Statement I is true because Uranium-235 is a key fissile isotope used in most nuclear reactors as a fuel to produce electricity. Statement II is also true since Uranium-235 undergoes nuclear fission, a process where its nucleus splits when struck by a neutron, releasing a tremendous amount of energy in the form of heat. This heat is then used to generate steam, which drives turbines to produce electricity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Assertion (A) : Solar energy is the main source of the Earth's internal heat. Reason (R) : Radioactive decay of elements like uranium and thorium releases heat inside the Earth.

options.b: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of Rutherford's experimental observations led him to conclude that the positive charge of an atom is concentrated in a very small region ?

options.a: Electrons were found to orbit the nucleus in specific energy levels.
options.b: A very small fraction of α-particles rebounded almost backwards.
options.c: Most α-particles followed a straight path through the gold foil.
options.d: A small fraction of α-particles were deflected by small angles.

questions.answer_text: A very small fraction of α-particles rebounded almost backwards.
questions.explanation: A very small fraction of α-particles rebounded almost backwards. Rutherford’s gold foil experiment showed that most α-particles passed through the foil, proving that most of the atom is empty space. A few were slightly deflected, indicating a small region with positive charge. Very few rebounded, showing that the mass and positive charge are concentrated in a tiny nucleus. He concluded that electrons revolve around this dense nucleus in circular paths. Thus, Rutherford proposed the nuclear model of the atom with a very small nucleus compared to the whole atom.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Ramjets operate efficiently at hypersonic speeds. 2. Dual Mode Ramjets can work in both subsonic and supersonic modes. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 2 only. Ramjet: A ramjet is an air-breathing jet engine that relies on the vehicle’s forward motion to compress incoming air for combustion, eliminating the need for a rotating compressor. It operates most efficiently at supersonic speeds (around Mach 2–4) but becomes inefficient at hypersonic speeds (above Mach 5) due to excessive heating and drag. Dual-Mode Ramjet (DMRJ): A Dual-Mode Ramjet is a hybrid engine that functions as a ramjet at lower supersonic speeds and transitions into a scramjet (supersonic combustion ramjet) at higher speeds, typically in the Mach 4–8 range. This allows it to efficiently operate in both subsonic combustion mode (ramjet) and supersonic combustion mode (scramjet), bridging the performance gap between the two technologies.

questions.subject: Physics

Therefore, the assertion is correct, but the reason is incorrect.

options.b: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.subject: Physics

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding James Watt and horsepower are correct? questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I : The concept of refractive index explains how light bends when passing through different substances. Statement II : Willebrord Snellius was the first to formally state the law of refraction involving a constant ratio for each substance.

questions.subject: Physics

Therefore, the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I : A wire carrying an electric current can attract or repel another nearby wire that is also carrying electric current. Statement II : This discovery was made by Andre-Marie Ampere, laying the foundation for the science of electromagnetism.

options.b: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.c: Statement I is true, but Statement II is false
options.d: Statement I is false, but Statement II is true

Statement II is also true, as this phenomenon was discovered by French physicist Andre-Marie Ampere in the early 19th century. His experiments laid the groundwork for understanding electromagnetic interactions and led to the formulation of Ampère's Law, which describes the magnetic field generated by electric currents.

questions.subject: Physics

In 1830, American scientist Joseph Henry built the Albany magnet, the world’s most powerful electromagnet at the time, which could lift up to 750 pounds of iron — an extraordinary achievement in early electromagnetism. His advancements also played a crucial role in the invention of the electric telegraph, particularly through his work on long-distance signal transmission using electromagnetic relays. However, Statement III is incorrect — William Gilbert did not invent the electromagnet; he was an earlier scientist known for his pioneering work on magnetism and for coining the term "electricity" in the 1600s, well before electromagnets were understood.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In 1851, who discovered the phenomenon of Eddy currents which flow in closed loops within conductors in planes perpendicular to the magnetic field?
questions.explanation: Leon Foucault also discovered the Gyroscope. Famous scientists and discoveries: Nikola Tesla - AC Power (alternating current), Tesla Coil, Magnifying Transmitter. Albert Einstein - Theory of relativity and the concept of mass-energy equivalence (E = mc2 ).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Michelson–Morley experiment and the aether theory are correct? Statement I : The Michelson–Morley experiment was conducted to detect Earth's motion through the luminiferous aether. Statement II : The experiment provided strong evidence in support of the existence of the aether. Statement III : The failure of the experiment led to the development of Einstein's Special Theory of Relativity.

options.a: Only I and II are correct
options.b: Only II and III are correct
options.c: Only I and III are correct

questions.answer_text: Only I and III are correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct — the Michelson–Morley experiment, conducted in 1887, was specifically designed to detect the motion of the Earth through the hypothetical luminiferous aether, which was believed to be the medium through which light waves travel. Statement II is incorrect because the experiment famously failed to detect any motion through the aether, thereby disproving its existence rather than confirming it. Statement III is correct — this null result played a critical role in physics, leading scientists like Albert Einstein to question the need for aether and ultimately develop the Special Theory of Relativity in 1905, which discarded the concept of aether entirely.

questions.question: As per physicists and their major contributions/discoveries, which of the following pairs is INCORRECT ?

options.b: Louis Victor de Broglie – Wave nature of matter

questions.explanation: Paul Dirac Known for “Dirac equation” related to quantum theory. Physicist Heike Kamerlingh Onnes discovered liquid Helium. Edwin Hubble - Law of Cosmic Expansion. Archimedes - Buoyancy Principle. Heisenberg - Uncertainty Principle.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In the early nineteenth century, who demonstrated that there are fourteen space lattices, or regularly repeating arrangements of points in space, that differ in symmetry and geometry?

Jerome Karle : He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1985, for the direct analysis of crystal structures using X-ray scattering techniques. Charles Frank : known for his work on crystal growth, liquid crystals and on the role of dislocations in crystals.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For which discovery is Hideki Yukawa, Nobel Prize winner in 1949, best known?

Famous Nobel Prize Awardee in Physics : 1945 - Wolfgang Pauli (“for the discovery of the Exclusion Principle, also called the Pauli Principle”); 1944 - Isidor Isaac Rabi (“for his resonance method for recording the magnetic properties of atomic nuclei”) ; 1950 - Cecil Frank Powell (“for his development of the photographic method of studying nuclear processes and his discoveries regarding mesons made with this method”).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which scientist suggested that the magnet must also exert an equal and opposite force on the current-carrying conductor?
questions.explanation: Andre Marie Ampere. He proposed that a current-carrying conductor creates a magnetic field, and that a magnet also exerts an equal and opposite force on the current-carrying conductor. This is known as Ampere's law.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which scientists discovered the empirical relationship in 1911 between the half-life of alpha decay and the energy of emitted alpha particles?
questions.explanation: Geiger and Nuttall. Alpha decay spontaneously emits excessive energy by emitting the alpha particle, in which an atomic nucleus emits an alpha particle (helium nucleus) and 'decays' into a different atomic nucleus. Ernest Orlando Lawrence - Nobel Prize in Physics (1939) for the invention of cyclotron. William Aston - Nobel Prize in Chemistry (1922) for discovery by means of a mass spectrograph of isotopes in several non-radioactive elements. Frederick Soddy was the first to announce the concept that atoms can be identical chemically and yet have different atomic weights.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Evangelista Torricelli is famous for what discovery?

Piezometer (an instrument for measuring the pressure of a liquid or gas) - Hans Christian Oersted. Vacuum Gauge (measures pressure below the atmospheric pressure) - Marcello Stefano Pirani.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Who was famous for the invention of the vacuum pump in the 17th century and also pioneered the concept of the absolute vacuum of space, measured the weight of air and used air pressure to predict the weather?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Who discovered in 1928 that when a ray of colored light passes through a liquid, some of the scattered light differs in color from the incident light?
questions.explanation: C V Raman was awarded the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics for his discovery of the Raman effect.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What do you call the effect of splitting of a spectral line into several components in the presence of a static magnetic field?
questions.explanation: Zeeman effect. It is named after the Dutch physicist Pieter Zeeman, who discovered it in 1896 and received a Nobel prize for this discovery.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Who is credited with introducing the concept of energy quanta and was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1918 for his contribution to quantum theory?
questions.explanation: Max Karl Ernst Ludwig Planck. Louis de Broglie (Physics 1929, discovery of the wave nature of electrons). Werner Heisenberg (Physics 1932, Creation of quantum mechanics).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Superconductivity was discovered by ______, who was also awarded the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1911.
questions.explanation: Heike Kamerlingh Onnes. Superconductivity - A phenomenon in which certain substances (conductor of electricity) offer zero resistance when it cools below some temperature level called (Tc) critical temperature. Examples of superconductors - Aluminum, Niobium, Mercury.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which scientist is credited with inventing the device known as the Cotton Gin, which revolutionized cotton processing in the 18th century?
questions.explanation: Eli Whitney (In 1794). Cotton gin is a machine that revolutionized the production of cotton by greatly speeding up the process of removing seeds from cotton fiber.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Assertion (A) : The internal jaws of a vernier calliper are used to measure the internal diameter of hollow objects like pipes or cylinders. Reason (R) : The external jaws of a vernier calliper are meant for measuring internal dimensions.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false.
questions.explanation: The assertion is true. In a vernier calliper, the internal jaws (the smaller pair of jaws located on the top side) are specifically designed to measure internal dimensions, such as the inner diameter of hollow cylinders or pipes. However, the reason is false because it incorrectly states that external jaws are used for measuring internal dimensions. In fact, external jaws are used to measure external dimensions, like the thickness or diameter of a solid object.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In 1960, which isotope was used to define the standard measure of length
questions.explanation: Krypton-86. In 1960, the International System of Units (SI) defined the meter as 1.65076373 × 106 times the wavelength of light emitted by the orange-red spectral line of a krypton-86 atom.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following statement/statements is/are true regarding the light year? 1. Light year is a unit of distance. 2. Light is a unit of time. 3. A light year is the distance that light travels in one Earth year. 4. Light year is the measurement of light intensity.
questions.explanation: Only 1 and 3 are correct. Relative Speed of light: Air > Water > Glass > Diamond. In air (3 × 108 m/s), in water (2.26 × 108 m/s), in glass (2 × 108 m/s), in diamond (1.25 ×108 m/s). Light radiation travels at a speed of approximately 299,792,458 (m/s) or 3 × 108 m/s in a vacuum.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A ____ is one billionth of a metre.
questions.explanation: nanometre. In the International System of Units, the prefix "nano" means one-billionth, or 10-9 . Special length units for short and large lengths are: 1 micrometre (µm) = 10–6 m; 1 fermi (f) = 10–15 m; 1 angstrom ( Å) = 10–10 m; 1 astronomical unit (AU) (average distance of the Sun from the Earth) = 1.496 × 1011 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct statement ?

options.b: Joule is the unit of work

questions.explanation: Joule is the unit of work. Some other SI Units : Energy - Joule, Power - Watt, Force or Weight - Newton, Frequency - Hertz, Resistance - ohm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: 1 kilowatt is equivalent to:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Assertion (A) : Stokes is the Gaussian unit of kinematic viscosity. Reason (R) : The joule is the SI unit of energy and is defined as one newton-meter.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: The assertion is true — the stokes is the Gaussian (CGS) unit of kinematic viscosity, equal to 1 cm²/s. The reason is also a true scientific fact — the joule is the SI unit of energy, defined as 1 newton-meter. However, the reason is not related to the assertion, as it refers to energy, not kinematic viscosity.

Units and Measurements : Temperature - kelvin, Electric current - ampere, Luminous intensity - candela, Plane angle - radian and Solid angle - steradian.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Assertion (A) : Gravitational intensity is a vector quantity. Reason (R) : Density is defined as mass per unit volume and is a vector quantity.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false.
questions.explanation: The assertion is true — gravitational intensity (also called gravitational field strength) is a vector quantity because it has both magnitude and direction, pointing toward the mass creating the field. However, the reason is false — while density is defined as mass per unit volume, it is a scalar quantity, not a vector, because it has magnitude but no direction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The number of significant figures in 0.05800 are :
questions.explanation: Four. The first rule is that all non-zero digits are considered as significant. The second rule is that Zeros between non-zero digits are also considered as significant. Example - 4.5006 has five significant figures. The third rule can be given as, Zeroes at the end or on the right side of the number are also significant. Example - 0.500 has three significant figures.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I : A seismograph is an instrument used to measure the intensity and duration of earthquakes. Statement II : Seismographs are primarily used to locate underground water and minerals.

options.a: Both statements I and II are correct
options.d: Both statements I and II are incorrect

questions.explanation: Statement I is correct — a seismograph is an instrument that detects and records the vibrations of the Earth caused by seismic waves, which are generated during earthquakes. It helps in measuring the intensity, duration, and sometimes even the location of an earthquake. Statement II is incorrect — seismographs are not used for locating underground water or minerals; such purposes require different geological or geophysical methods like resistivity surveys or ground-penetrating radar.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A non-SI unit called ‘nit’ is the unit of which of the following photometric quantities used to measure a multitude of light intensity?
questions.explanation: Luminance. One lux is the amount of illumination provided when one lumen is evenly distributed over an area of one square meter. The candela is the unit of luminous intensity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Assertion (A) : Doppler weather radar is used to detect and monitor rainfall, its intensity, and movement. Reason (R) : Doppler radar works by sending out pulses of electromagnetic energy and analyzing the returned signals from precipitation particles.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Doppler weather radar is an advanced instrument used in meteorology to monitor precipitation like rain, snow, or hail, and to determine its intensity, speed, and direction of movement. It achieves this by emitting pulses of electromagnetic energy; when these pulses hit precipitation particles, they scatter, and some of the energy returns to the radar. The radar measures the time delay and frequency shift (Doppler effect) of the returned signals to assess the motion of precipitation.

questions.question: The unit of magnetic intensity in the CGS (centimetre - gram - second) system is _______ .

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: The Hubble constant is used to describe the rate of expansion of the universe. Statement II: Planck’s constant is used to measure gravitational waves in space.

options.a: Both statements I and II are correct
options.d: Both statements I and II are incorrect

questions.explanation: Statement I is correct — the Hubble constant is a unit that represents the rate at which the universe is expanding. It relates the recessional velocity of galaxies to their distance from Earth, providing evidence for the expansion of the universe following the Big Bang. Statement II is incorrect — Planck’s constant is a fundamental constant in quantum mechanics that relates the energy of a photon to its frequency, not something used to measure gravitational waves. Gravitational waves are detected using instruments like LIGO, which do not depend on Planck’s constant for measurement.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the commercial unit of electric energy?
questions.explanation: Kilowatt hour (KWh). 1 kilowatt hour = 3.6 x 106 joules. Electrical Energy : {SI unit: Joule} The energy derived from the flow of electric charge is called electrical energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I : A spherometer is used to measure the radius of curvature of spherical surfaces like lenses and mirrors. Statement II : A spherometer typically has a triangular metallic frame supported on three legs with a central screw for fine adjustment. Statement III: A viscometer is used to measure the radius of spherical objects.

options.b: Only I and II are correct
options.c: Only II and III are correct
options.d: Only I and III are correct

questions.answer_text: Only I and II are correct
questions.explanation: A spherometer is a precise measuring instrument used to determine the radius of curvature of spherical surfaces, such as those on lenses and curved mirrors. It consists of a metal triangular frame supported on three legs, with a central screw for fine vertical movement and measurements. Statement III is incorrect — a viscometer is not related to measuring curvature or radii. Instead, it is used to measure viscosity, which is the resistance of a fluid to flow.

The Boltzmann constant is the physical constant that relates a gas subatomic particle's average kinetic energy to its temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following is the physical quantity for the expression arc/radius?
questions.explanation: Plane angle. It is measured in radians (2π radians in a circle) or degrees (360 degrees to a circle). Solid Angle is measured in steradian.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I : Tera is larger than Giga in the metric system of units. Statement II : Hecto and Deca are larger than Tera.

options.a: Both statements I and II are correct
options.d: Both statements I and II are incorrect

questions.explanation: Statement I is correct — In the International System of Units (SI prefixes), Tera (T) represents 10¹², while Giga (G) represents 10⁹, so Tera is larger than Giga. Statement II is incorrect — Hecto (10²) and Deca (10¹) are much smaller than Tera. Tera is 10¹², which is billions of times larger than both Hecto and Deca.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Assertion (A) : The Svedberg unit is used to express sedimentation rates of particles like ribosomes during centrifugation. Reason (R) : The Svedberg unit is a measure of time, equal to 10⁻¹³ seconds.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: The Svedberg unit (symbol: S) is used in biochemistry and molecular biology to express the sedimentation rate of particles such as ribosomes and macromolecules during ultracentrifugation. It reflects how quickly a particle sediments in a centrifugal field and indirectly relates to its size and shape. While it is often associated with particle size (e.g., 70S or 80S ribosomes), Svedberg is technically a unit of time, specifically 10⁻¹³ seconds. It describes how long it takes for a particle to sediment.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In terms of SI prefixes 10−15 is called:

questions.question: ‘mho’ is the unit of ______ of a substance.
questions.explanation: Conductance. The SI unit of resistance is ohm. Resistance and conductance are inverse of each other (mho = . 1 𝑜ℎ𝑚 )

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I : One calorie of heat energy is approximately equal to 4.2 joules of mechanical energy. Statement II : The calorie is a unit of power used to measure the rate at which energy is transferred.

options.a: Both statements I and II are correct
options.d: Both statements I and II are incorrect

questions.explanation: Statement I is correct — 1 calorie is defined as the amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of 1 gram of water by 1°C, and it is approximately equal to 4.2 joules. This reflects the conversion between thermal energy (calories) and mechanical energy (joules). Statement II is incorrect — the calorie is a unit of energy, not power. Power is the rate of doing work or transferring energy and is measured in watts in the SI system.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Assertion (A) : The unit of measurement for the optical power of a lens is the diopter. Reason (R) : Diopter is defined as the reciprocal of the focal length measured in meters.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: The assertion is true because the diopter is the unit used to measure the optical power of a lens. The reason is also true because the diopter is defined as the reciprocal of the focal length (in meters) of the lens. Hence, the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following two quantities have the same dimensions ?
