questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Assertion (A) : The SI unit of electric current is the ampere. Reason (R) : One ampere is defined as one coulomb of charge passing through a conductor in one second.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: The assertion is correct because the SI unit of electric current is the ampere (A). The reason is also true and provides the correct scientific definition of 1 ampere — it is the amount of current when 1 coulomb of electric charge passes through a point in a conductor in 1 second, i.e.,1 A = 1 C/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I : Joule, calorie, and kilowatt-hour are all valid units used to measure energy. Statement II : Newton is also a unit of energy in the SI system.

options.a: Both statements I and II are correct
options.d: Both statements I and II are incorrect

questions.explanation: Statement I is correct — Joule (J), calorie, and kilowatt-hour (kWh) are all units of energy. A joule is the SI unit of energy; a calorie is commonly used in thermodynamics and nutrition; and kilowatt-hour is a commercial unit of electrical energy. Statement II is incorrect — Newton is not a unit of energy; it is the SI unit of force. One newton is the force required to accelerate a 1 kg mass by 1 m/s². Energy, on the other hand, is the capacity to do work, and is measured in joules.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?

options.a: Light year is the unit of distance.
options.b: Light year is the distance travelled by light in one year.
options.c: Light year is the unit of time.
options.d: Angstrom is a unit of length.

questions.answer_text: Light year is the unit of time.
questions.explanation: A light year is the distance light travels in one year and serves as a convenient unit for measuring large astronomical distances, approximately 9 trillion kilometers (9 × 10¹² km). An astronomical unit (AU) is the mean distance from the Earth to the Sun, used to measure distances to planets, and is equal to 1.496 × 10¹¹ meters.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Consider the below statements regarding the Aditya-L1 mission and its payloads: 1. The SUIT payload on Aditya-L1 is designed to image the solar disk in the near-ultraviolet (UV) spectrum to study the temperature and chemical composition of the Sun's photosphere and chromosphere. 2. The SoLEXS instrument is a high-resolution X-ray spectrometer used to study solar flares and active regions in soft X-ray wavelengths. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. The Aditya-L1 mission is an Indian solar observatory at Lagrangian point L1, launched on September 2, 2023 and was inserted in its targeted halo orbit on January 6, 2024. Aditya-L1 spacecraft in the Halo orbit takes 178 days to complete a revolution around the L1 point. Aditya-L1 carries four remote sensing payloads. The Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) observes the solar corona through imaging and spectroscopy. The Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (SUIT) captures narrow- and broadband images of the photosphere and chromosphere in the near-UV range. The Solar Low Energy X-ray Spectrometer (SoLEXS) functions as a soft X-ray spectrometer for Sun-as-a-star observations, mainly focusing on solar flares. Complementing it, the High Energy L1 Orbiting X-ray Spectrometer (HEL1OS) serves as a hard X-ray spectrometer, also performing Sun-as-a-star observations.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The primary objective of the LUPEX Mission, a collaboration between ISRO and JAXA, is to:

options.a: Study the Martian atmosphere and soil composition
options.b: Deploy a communication satellite in lunar orbit
options.c: Investigate the quantity and quality of water on the Moon and explore its dark side
options.d: Observe solar flares and coronal mass ejections

questions.answer_text: Investigate the quantity and quality of water on the Moon and explore its dark side
questions.explanation: . The LUPEX Mission (Lunar Polar Exploration Mission), is a collaborative lunar mission between ISRO (India) and JAXA (Japan), targeted for launch in 2027–28 aboard Japan’s H3 rocket. The mission’s primary goal is to explore the permanently shadowed regions (PSRs) of the lunar south pole to assess the quantity, distribution, and quality of water ice, which is crucial for future human presence and resource utilization. In this collaboration, ISRO will develop the lander, while JAXA will provide the rover. The payload suite will include 7 scientific instruments, such as a mass spectrometer from ESA and neutron spectrometers from NASA, alongside Indian and Japanese payloads.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which Indian space mission marked the successful launch of 104 satellites in a single mission ?
questions.explanation: PSLV-C37. On 15 February 2017, ISRO’s PSLV-C37 mission created a world record by successfully launching 104 satellites in a single mission from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota. Out of these, 96 satellites belonged to the USA, while the rest were from Israel, UAE, Kazakhstan, Netherlands, Switzerland, and India (Cartosat-2 series satellite being the main payload). Astrosat (a) – India’s first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory (2015). GSLV Mk III (b) – Heavy-lift launch vehicle, used in missions like Chandrayaan-2. Chandrayaan-2 (c) – India’s second lunar exploration mission (2019).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What was the key scientific objective of Chandrayaan-3 ?

options.a: To demonstrate a safe lunar landing and rover operation

questions.answer_text: To demonstrate a safe lunar landing and rover operation
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3, India's third lunar mission, successfully landed on the Moon's south polar region on August 23, 2023. This mission aimed to demonstrate a safe landing and rover operations on the lunar surface. It also marked India as the first nation to land near the lunar south pole and the fourth overall to achieve a soft landing on the Moon.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Square Kilometer Array (SKA) is correct?

options.a: It is managed entirely by the European Space Agency.
options.b: It aims to explore cosmic magnetism and dark matter.
options.c: It focuses solely on detecting visible light.
options.d: It will consist of a single telescope in India.

questions.answer_text: It aims to explore cosmic magnetism and dark matter.
questions.explanation: The Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKAO) is a global project to build the world’s largest radio telescope with over one million m² collecting area. Its headquarters are in the United Kingdom, while the telescope arrays are located in South Africa and Australia. The project aims to study the universe’s history, galaxy evolution, and dark matter. Member nations include Australia, Canada, China, France, Germany, India, Italy, New Zealand, South Africa, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, The Netherlands, and the UK.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Earth remote sensing satellites (EOS) are primarily designed to:

options.a: Drill into Earth's crust for mineral samples
options.b: Monitor weather, land use, and environmental changes on Earth
options.d: Study the internal structure of Earth using seismic waves

questions.answer_text: Monitor weather, land use, and environmental changes on Earth
questions.explanation: Earth Observation Satellites (EOS) are launched to collect data about the Earth's surface and atmosphere. They help monitor weather patterns, land use changes, deforestation, urban growth, agriculture, and natural disasters. These satellites play a vital role in environmental monitoring and resource management, not in drilling or seismic studies.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What advanced technology is being tested in ISRO's new "Next Generation Launch Vehicle" (NGLV) project to replace PSLV and GSLV?

options.a: Reusable booster stage with semi-cryogenic engine

questions.answer_text: Reusable booster stage with semi-cryogenic engine
questions.explanation: Reusable Booster Technology : ISRO is incorporating partial reusability into the NGLV—particularly a recoverable first stage—which marks a shift from its current expendable-only rockets. Semi-Cryogenic Propulsion (LOX–Methane / LOX–Kerosene Engines): The NGLV will utilize semi-cryogenic engines, which use liquid oxygen (LOX) and refined kerosene (or methane). These engines are efficient, offer high thrust, and support reusability. ISRO has already tested key components and ignition systems to validate performance and restart capabilities essential for reusable stages.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which solar phenomenon is responsible for disturbances in Earth's magnetic field?
questions.explanation: Solar flares. These powerful eruptions on the Sun's surface release massive amounts of energy and charged particles into space. When this stream of particles, often carried by a Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) associated with the flare, reaches Earth, it interacts with our planet's magnetosphere, causing geomagnetic storms that disrupt the magnetic field. Sunspots: These are cooler, magnetically active regions on the Sun's surface. While solar flares often originate from sunspot regions. Chromosphere heating: The chromosphere is a layer of the Sun's atmosphere. Photospheric cooling: This refers to the process that creates sunspots (they are cooler areas in the photosphere).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Aditya-L1 mission was launched to replace the INSAT series of weather satellites. 2. Aditya-L1 successfully entered a Halo Orbit around the Lagrange Point 1 (L1) to observe solar activity. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 2 only. Statement 1 – Incorrect. The Aditya-L1 mission (launched by ISRO in September 2023) is India’s first solar observatory, not a replacement for INSAT weather satellites. INSAT satellites provide meteorological, telecommunication, and broadcasting services, whereas Aditya-L1 is purely a scientific mission to study the Sun. Statement 2 – Correct. In January 2024, Aditya-L1 successfully entered a Halo Orbit around the Lagrange Point 1 (L1), which is about 1.5 million km from Earth. Its purpose is to continuously observe solar activity, the corona, solar wind, and space weather without Earth’s shadow interfering.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which high-altitude observatory in India is known for hosting an optical-infrared telescope used for space observation in Ladakh?
questions.explanation: Hanle Indian Astronomical Observatory. The Indian Astronomical Observatory (IAO), Hanle, located in Ladakh at an altitude of about 4,500 meters (14,764 ft), is one of the highest observatories in the world. It hosts the Himalayan Chandra Telescope (HCT), a 2.01 m optical-infrared telescope, used for space observation, optical astronomy, and infrared studies. Udaipur Solar Observatory – Specializes in solar studies, located on an island in Fatehsagar Lake, Rajasthan. Nainital Aryabhatta Observatory – Situated in Uttarakhand, focuses mainly on optical astronomy. Mount Abu Infrared Observatory – Located in Rajasthan, it also has an infrared telescope but not at such a high altitude as Hanle.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is one of the major future impacts of ISRO's Aditya-L1 mission that studies the Sun's chromosphere and corona?

options.b: Enhanced rainfall prediction in monsoon regions
options.c: Improved space weather forecasting to protect satellites and power systems

questions.answer_text: Improved space weather forecasting to protect satellites and power systems
questions.explanation: Aditya-L1, India’s first dedicated solar mission (launched in 2023), is placed at the Lagrangian Point 1 (L1), about 1.5 million km from Earth. It studies the solar corona, chromosphere, solar flares, and solar winds. A key impact is better space weather prediction, which is crucial because: Solar storms can disrupt satellite communications, GPS, navigation, and power grids on Earth. Early warning improves safety of astronauts, satellites, and space missions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: The equation E=mc2 expresses the equivalence of energy and mass. Statement II: Albert Einstein propounded this famous equation in 1905 as part of his theory of special relativity. Statement III: Isaac Newton formulated the equation E=mc2 during his studies on motion.

options.b: Statements I and II are true, but III is false
options.c: Statements II and III are true, but I is false

questions.answer_text: Statements I and II are true, but III is false
questions.explanation: The equation E = mc2 is a cornerstone of modern physics, showing that energy (E) and mass (m) are interchangeable, with c being the speed of light in a vacuum. This relation was first proposed by Albert Einstein in 1905 as part of his theory of special relativity. This equation revolutionized our understanding of energy, mass, and the fundamental workings of the universe. On the other hand, Isaac Newton developed classical mechanics and laws of motion long before this, but he did not formulate or propose this equation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: The anemometer, invented around 1450, is used to measure wind speed and pressure. Statement II: A transmissometer is a historical wind-measuring device used before the invention of the anemometer.

options.a: Both statements I and II are correct
options.d: Both statements I and II are incorrect

questions.explanation: Statement I is correct — The anemometer was invented around 1450 and is still used today to measure wind speed and wind pressure, especially in meteorology and climate studies. Statement II is incorrect — The transmissometer is not an early wind-measuring instrument. Instead, it is a modern optical device used to measure atmospheric visibility by analyzing how much light is scattered or absorbed over a given path through air or water.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Assertion (A): A cyclotron is used to accelerate charged particles to high velocities. Reason (R) : A cyclotron uses a magnetic field and a high-frequency alternating voltage to increase the speed of charged particles in a spiral path.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: A cyclotron is a device designed to accelerate charged particles, such as protons or ions, to very high speeds using a combination of a uniform magnetic field and a high-frequency alternating electric field. The magnetic field forces the particles to move in a spiral path, while the alternating voltage accelerates them each time they cross the gap between the two “dees” of the cyclotron. This process gradually increases the particle’s velocity and kinetic energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: The Dirac equation, derived in 1928, combines quantum theory and special relativity to describe electrons moving at relativistic speeds. Statement II: Bernoulli's equation is used to describe the behavior of electrons at relativistic speeds.

options.a: Both statements I and II are true

questions.explanation: In 1928, Paul Dirac formulated the Dirac equation, which successfully merged the principles of quantum mechanics with special relativity to describe the behavior of electrons moving at speeds close to the speed of light. This groundbreaking equation predicted the existence of antimatter and explained the electron’s intrinsic spin. On the other hand, Bernoulli's equation is a principle in fluid dynamics and has no relation to quantum theory or relativistic electrons.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the name of the thermionic electron tube used to oscillate and amplify microwave frequency signals ?
questions.explanation: Klystron - Developed by brothers Russell and Sigurd Varian. It is based on the principle of velocity modulation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The radius of curvature of a charged particle's passage in a homogeneous magnetic field is proportional to:
questions.explanation: Momentum of Particles. When a moving charged particle enters a magnetic field then the path followed by the charged particle is circular if the magnetic field is perpendicular to the velocity of the particle. The more the radius of the path followed by the particle, the lesser will be the curvature, and the lesser the radius, the more will be curvature. questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Assertion (A): Magnetic lines of force inside a bar magnet run from the South pole to the North pole. Reason (R): Magnetic field lines always form closed loops, running outside the magnet from North to South and inside from South to North.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Magnetic lines of force outside a bar magnet run from the North (N) pole to the South (S) pole, while inside the magnet, the lines continue from the South pole back to the North pole, completing a closed loop. This continuous, closed-loop nature of magnetic field lines ensures the magnetic field is continuous without a beginning or an end. Hence, the assertion that the magnetic lines inside a bar magnet run from the South pole to the North pole is true. The reason correctly explains this fact about magnetic field lines.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which equation was verified by American scientists Nichols and Hull in 1903 by measuring the radiation pressure of visible light?
questions.explanation: P = U/C. Radiation pressure - The mechanical pressure that is applied on any surface due to the exchange of momentum between the electromagnetic field and the object.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: Solar cells are commonly used to power devices such as space probes and artificial satellites. Statement II: Solar cells are widely used in heavy electrical systems like lift (elevator) mechanisms in high-rise buildings.

options.a: Both statements I and II are correct
options.d: Both statements I and II are incorrect

questions.explanation: Statement I is correct — Solar cells are a reliable source of energy for space applications, especially for space probes and artificial satellites, where direct access to sunlight makes them highly efficient and low-maintenance. Statement II is incorrect — While solar technology is expanding, lift systems (elevators) require high and consistent power, which is generally supplied by the main electricity grid. Solar cells are not commonly used in such high-load applications due to limitations in power output and reliability unless integrated with storage and backup systems, which is rare.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What happens to air when it is heated and then cooled?

options.a: It expands on heating and contracts on cooling
options.b: It contracts on heating and stabilizes on cooling
options.c: It expands on both heating and cooling
options.d: It contracts on heating and expands on cooling

questions.answer_text: It expands on heating and contracts on cooling
questions.explanation: It expands on heating and contracts on cooling. Heating air causes the air molecules to gain thermal energy, move faster, and spread out, resulting in the expansion of air and a decrease in air density. Cooling air causes the air molecules to lose thermal energy, slow down, and come closer together, leading to the contraction of air and an increase in air density.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: A gnomon is an essential part of a solar clock used to tell time by casting shadows. Statement II: A bolometer uses a gnomon to measure temperature changes due to radiation.

options.a: Both statements I and II are true

questions.explanation: A gnomon is a component of a solar clock (or sundial) that casts a shadow on the clock face to indicate the time of day based on the sun's position. This device has been used since ancient times to measure daylight hours by tracking the shadow's movement. Therefore, Statement I is correct. However, a bolometer is an instrument used to measure the power of incident electromagnetic radiation via the heating of a material and does not use a gnomon in its mechanism. Hence, Statement II is false.

questions.question: In the Millikan’s Oil Drop experiment, the oil drop is subjected to such forces whose nature does NOT fall under the category of:
questions.explanation: Magnetostatic. Millikan's oil drop experiment measured the charge of an electron. Electrically charged oil droplets entered the electric field and were balanced between two plates by altering the field.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: Maxwell’s equations describe the behavior of electric and magnetic fields and their interaction with charges and currents. Statement II: Newton’s equations primarily deal with the motion of objects under the influence of forces. Statement III: Einstein’s equations are related to the theory of relativity, not electromagnetism.

options.b: Statements I and II are true, but III is false
options.c: Statements II and III are true, but I is false

questions.explanation: Maxwell’s equations are a set of four fundamental equations that describe how electric and magnetic fields are generated and altered by each other, as well as by charges and currents. These equations form the foundation of classical electromagnetism. In contrast, Newton’s equations (Newton’s laws of motion) describe the motion of bodies under the action of forces and are fundamental to classical mechanics. Meanwhile, Einstein’s equations refer to his general theory of relativity, which explains gravity as a curvature of spacetime, not electromagnetic phenomena.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Statement I: Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe. Statement II: Oxygen is the most abundant element in the universe.

options.a: Both statements I and II are true

questions.explanation: Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe, making up about 75% of its elemental mass. It is the primary building block of stars and plays a crucial role in the formation of galaxies and other celestial bodies. Oxygen, while abundant on Earth and important for life, is far less common in the universe compared to hydrogen. Therefore, Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to Bohr's model, what is the significance of an electron transition from a higher energy orbit to a lower energy orbit?

options.a: The electron's angular momentum becomes quantized.
options.c: A photon of energy equal to the energy difference between the orbits is absorbed.
options.d: A photon of energy equal to the energy difference between the orbits is emitted.

questions.answer_text: A photon of energy equal to the energy difference between the orbits is emitted.
questions.explanation: In Bohr’s atomic model, electrons revolve in fixed orbits with definite energies. When an electron jumps from a higher-energy orbit (excited state) to a lower-energy orbit (ground or lower state), it loses energy. This lost energy is released in the form of a photon. The energy of the emitted photon corresponds exactly to the energy difference between the two orbits, given by 𝐸 = ℎ𝜈, This process explains the emission spectra of atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How many electrons does a hydrogen molecule have in its K shell?
questions.explanation: 2. A hydrogen molecule (H2) consists of two hydrogen atoms, each with one electron. Since hydrogen has only one electron in its K shell, a hydrogen molecule will have two electrons in total in the K shell, one from each atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. An electron has a negative charge, a proton has a positive charge, and a neutron is electrically neutral. 2. The proton and neutron both carry positive charges. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 only. The electron is negatively charged, the proton is positively charged, and the neutron carries no charge, making it neutral. These charges are fundamental to atomic structure and determine how atoms interact. Statement 2 is incorrect because, although the proton is positively charged, the neutron does not carry any charge—it is neutral, not positive.

Beryllium : Neutrons (5), Electrons (4), Atomic Number (4), Mass Number (9), Electronic configuration (1s22s2 ).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. London dispersion forces are a type of Van der Waals force found in halogens, noble gases, and other non-polar molecules. 2. London dispersion forces arise due to temporary fluctuations in electron distribution, creating momentary dipoles. 3. Dipole-dipole forces are weaker than London dispersion forces and are found in non-polar substances. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. London dispersion forces are the weakest type of intermolecular forces and are classified under Van der Waals forces. They are present in all atoms and molecules but are the dominant force in non-polar substances such as halogens and noble gases. These forces originate from temporary shifts in the electron cloud, leading to instantaneous dipoles, which then induce dipoles in nearby atoms or molecules — this is the basis of the attraction. Dipole-dipole forces are stronger than London dispersion forces and occur between polar molecules, not non-polar ones.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In ethylene (C2H4), hybridisation of carbon atoms is:
questions.explanation: sp2 . In this hybridization, one 's' and two 'p' orbitals combine to form three new sp² hybrid orbitals, all with the same shape and energy. Hybridization refers to the process of merging two atomic orbitals to create new hybridized orbitals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Identify whether the given statements about ionisation energy are correct or incorrect. Statement A : The ionisation energy of an atom is the amount of energy that is required to remove an electron from a mole of atoms in the gas phase. Statement B : The ionisation energy increases from top to bottom in groups and decreases from left to right across a period.

options.c: Both Statements A and B are correct
options.d: Both Statements A and B are incorrect

questions.explanation: Only Statement A is correct. The ionization energy decreases from top to bottom in groups, and increases from left to right across a period. Thus, helium has the largest ionization energy, while Caesium has the lowest.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The positron is a negatively charged particle discovered by Carl Anderson in 1922. 2. Carl Anderson discovered a positively charged particle, equal in mass to an electron, in 1932. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 2 only. Statement 1 is incorrect - The positron is not negatively charged—it is the positively charged antiparticle of the electron. Also, it was not discovered in 1922. Statement 2 is correct - In 1932, Carl Anderson discovered the positron while studying cosmic rays using a cloud chamber. This particle has the same mass as an electron but carries a positive charge. It was the first discovery of antimatter and was a groundbreaking moment in

Azimuthal (l) - It is defined as the determination of the shape of an orbital. Magnetic (m) - The subshell's overall number of orbitals and their orientation. Spin (s) - The values of n, l, and ml have no bearing on the electron. The 4s subshell contains 1 orbital and can hold up to 2 electrons. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Assertion (A): The element with electronic configuration 2,8,1 is Sodium. Reason (R): An element with 11 electrons has its electrons arranged as 2 in the first shell, 8 in the second, and 1 in the third shell.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Sodium has 11 electrons. According to the shell filling order, the first shell holds 2 electrons, the second holds 8, and the remaining 1 electron goes into the third shell, giving the electronic configuration 2,8,1. Hence, the element with this configuration is Sodium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The number of atoms in exactly 12 grams of carbon-12 is known as Avogadro’s constant. 2. Planck’s constant is used to relate the energy of a photon to its frequency. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Avogadro’s constant (also called Avogadro’s number) is defined as the number of atoms, molecules, or particles present in one mole of a substance. By definition, one mole of carbon-12 weighs exactly 12 grams and contains 6.022 × 10²³ atoms, which is Avogadro’s constant. Planck’s constant is a fundamental physical constant denoted by h, and it is used in the equation E = hν, where E is the energy of a photon and ν (nu) is its frequency. This equation is central to quantum theory and explains how energy is quantized in the form of photons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Gold Foil Model was developed by J.J. Thomson in 1898. 2. The Plum Pudding Model describes electrons embedded in a positively charged sphere. 3. The Plum Pudding Model was proposed before the discovery of the atomic nucleus. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 2 and 3 only. The Plum Pudding Model, proposed by J.J. Thomson, described the atom as a positively charged sphere with negatively charged electrons embedded within it, similar to plums in a pudding. This model was introduced before the discovery of the atomic nucleus by Rutherford in 1911. The Gold Foil Model was not proposed by J.J. Thomson — it was the result of Ernest Rutherford's alpha scattering experiment, which led to the nuclear model of the atom. Thomson had no role in that model’s development.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements are correct postulates of Dalton’s atomic theory ? A. All matter is made up of atoms. These atoms participate in chemical reactions. B. Atoms might be created or destroyed during a chemical reaction. C. Atoms of different elements vary in mass and chemical properties. D. Compounds are combinations of atoms in the ratio of whole or fractional numbers. E. A compound will always have constant relative number and kind of atoms.
questions.explanation: A, C, E. Dalton's atomic theory, proposed by John Dalton, states that all matter is composed of extremely small particles called atoms. In chemical reactions, atoms are combined, separated, or rearranged. Compounds are combinations of atoms in fixed, whole-number ratios, not fractional numbers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Assertion (A) : The space-filling model emphasizes the relative size of each atom based on its van der Waals radius. Reason (R) : The van der Waals radius represents the size of an atom only when it forms a covalent bond.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: The assertion is true — the space-filling model shows atoms with sizes proportional to their van der Waals radii, which reflect the effective space atoms occupy when close but not bonded. The reason is false — the van der Waals radius is not related to covalent bonding. Instead, it represents the size of an atom when it is not bonded to another atom, showing how atoms approach each other without bonding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Ernest Rutherford used gold foil approximately 1000 atoms thick for his alpha scattering experiment. 2. The experiment showed that atoms are mostly empty space with a dense nucleus at the center. 3. Rutherford used beta particles instead of alpha particles in the experiment. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. In his alpha particle scattering experiment, Ernest Rutherford used an extremely thin sheet of gold foil, about 1000 atoms thick, to investigate the structure of the atom. He directed alpha particles at this foil and observed their scattering patterns. Most passed straight through, but a few were deflected sharply, leading to the conclusion that atoms are mostly empty space with a small, dense, positively charged nucleus. Rutherford did not use beta particles; he used alpha particles (helium nuclei) to carry out the experiment. This distinction is critical in understanding the outcome of his findings.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which theory discusses the relationship between ligand bonding and degradation of d orbitals in metal complexes and the geometry of metal complexes and the splitting of d orbitals?
questions.explanation: Crystal field theory : (1929, developed by physicist Hans Bethe) describes the breaking of orbital degeneracy in transition metal complexes due to the presence of ligands.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the atomicity of Phosphorus?
questions.explanation: Tetra-atomic. Atomicity is the total number of atoms present in a molecule. Polyatomic (composed of three or more atoms). Phosphorus was first made by Hennig Brandt in 1669.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The dash-wedge formula is used to represent the three-dimensional structures of molecules on a two-dimensional surface. 2. In the dash-wedge formula, solid wedges represent bonds coming out of the plane, and dashed wedges represent bonds going behind the plane. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. The dash-wedge formula is a common method used in organic chemistry to depict three-dimensional molecular structures on a flat, two-dimensional surface such as paper or a computer screen. This formula uses solid wedges to indicate bonds that project out of the plane toward the viewer and dashed wedges for bonds that go behind the plane, away from the viewer. Straight lines represent bonds in the plane of the paper or screen. This visual representation helps chemists understand the spatial arrangement of atoms, which is crucial for understanding molecular geometry and reactivity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: From which Latin word is the S block element calcium derived ?
questions.explanation: Calx (calcium hydroxide). Formula - Ca(OH)2 . It is used in industrial settings, such as sewage treatment, paper production, construction, and food processing. Calum (calcium carbonate): Formula - CaCO3 .

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which element of Group 17 has two isotopes of masses 35 and 37 amu with average abundance of 75.77% and 24.23%, respectively ?
questions.explanation: Chlorine. Element of Group 17 : The halogens are located on the left of the noble gases on the periodic table. These five toxic, non-metallic elements make up Group 17 of the periodic table and consist of : fluorine (9, F), chlorine (17, Cl), bromine (35, Br), iodine (53, I), and astatine (85, At).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Electrum is a naturally occurring alloy of gold and silver. 2. Constantan is an alloy of copper and nickel. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: (c) Both 1 and 2. Statement 1 is correct. Electrum is a naturally occurring alloy primarily made up of gold and silver, with trace amounts of copper and other elements. It has been used since ancient times, especially in coins and jewellery. Statement 2 is also correct. Constantan is an alloy of copper and nickel (typically 55% copper and 45% nickel). It is well-known for its constant electrical resistance, making it useful in electrical applications like thermocouples.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is a non - metal that can exist in different form?
questions.explanation: Carbon (C). Atomic number - 6. Belongs to the 14th group. It is a tetravalent which makes a chemical bond with four electrons. Each form of carbon is called an allotrope.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass numbers. 2. Isotopes have the same number of neutrons and protons. 3. Isotopes have different atomic numbers but the same mass number. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 only. The defining characteristic of isotopes is that they have the same atomic number (meaning the same number of protons) but different mass numbers due to a different number of neutrons. Therefore, statement 1 is correct. However, statement 2 is incorrect because isotopes do not have the same number of neutrons; they differ in neutron count. Statement 3 is incorrect since isotopes cannot have different atomic numbers but the same mass number.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Assertion (A): Mercury is always present in an amalgam. Reason (R): Amalgams are alloys of mercury with one or more other metals.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: An amalgam is, by definition, an alloy that always contains mercury — making the assertion true. The reason is also true: amalgams are formed when mercury combines with another metal like zinc, silver, or tin. However, the reason, though true, does not fully explain why mercury is always a component — it's part of the definition of an amalgam, not just a general property.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Assertion (A): Oxides of sulphur and nitrogen dissolve in rainwater and form acids. Reason (R): These acids lower the pH of rainwater, resulting in acid rain.

options.a: A is false, but R is true
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Sulphur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NO, NO₂) are released into the atmosphere from burning fossil fuels. These gases react with water in the atmosphere to form sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄) and nitric acid (HNO₃), which dissolve in rainwater — causing acid rain. This acidic precipitation lowers the pH of natural rainwater and harms ecosystems, buildings, and soil.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are NOT correct ? I. The property of metals by which they can be beaten into thin sheets is called malleability. II. The property of metal by which it can being drawn into wires is called ductility.
questions.explanation: Neither I nor II. Malleability - The property of metals to be beaten into thin sheets. Examples - Copper, silver. Ductility - The property of metal to be drawn into wires. Examples - Gold, silver and copper. The density and melting point of metals is high.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Assertion (A): Aqua regia can dissolve noble metals like gold and platinum. Reason (R): Chloroform is a strong acid that reacts with metals to form soluble compounds.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is false, but R is true
options.d: A is true, but R is false

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: Aqua regia (a mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid and nitric acid in a 3:1 ratio) is the only common liquid capable of dissolving noble metals such as gold (Au) and platinum (Pt). It achieves this by generating chlorine and nitrosyl chloride, which help break down the stable metal atoms. The reason is false because chloroform is not an acid at all, but an organic solvent (CHCl₃) used in laboratories, with no ability to dissolve metals, especially noble ones.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the alkali metals ?

options.a: All the alkali metals are silvery white, soft and light metals.
options.b: The ionization enthalpies of the alkali metals are considerably low and decrease down the group from.
options.c: Group 1 metals are known as alkali metals.
options.d: All the alkali metals have two valence electrons.

questions.answer_text: All the alkali metals have two valence electrons.
questions.explanation: Alkali metals have one electron in their valence shell. Group 1A of the periodic table are the alkali metals: Hydrogen (H, 1), Lithium (Li, 3), Sodium (Na, 11), Potassium (K, 19), Rubidium (Rb, 37), Cesium (Cs, 55), and Francium (Fr , 87). Lithium was discovered in 1817, taking its name from the Greek word for "stone".

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Choose the most reactive metal from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Sodium. Reactive metals in order: Potassium (Most reactive metal), Sodium, Barium, Calcium, Magnesium, Aluminium, Zinc, Iron, Nickel, Tin, Lead, Hydrogen, Copper, Mercury, Silver, Gold, Platinum (Least Reactive).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT ?

options.a: Metals react with oxygen to form basic oxides.
options.c: Non-metals do not produce any sound

questions.explanation: Physical Properties of Non metals: Poor conductors of electricity and heat, Non-malleable nor ductile, Brittle solids, May be solids, liquids, or gases at room temperature, These are not sonorous, and Transparent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Assertion (A) : Potassium reacts violently with cold water, producing hydrogen gas and heat. Reason (R) : Potassium is an alkali metal with low reactivity.

options.a: A is true, but R is false
options.b: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.c: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: Potassium (K) is a highly reactive alkali metal that reacts violently with cold water, producing potassium hydroxide (KOH) and hydrogen gas (H₂). The reaction releases enough heat to ignite the hydrogen, which is why it appears explosive. The reason, however, is incorrect. Potassium does not have low reactivity — in fact, it's among the most reactive metals. Its reactivity increases down the alkali metal group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT pair with respect to the substances and their specific heat capacity (J𝑘𝑔 ) at −1𝐾 −1 room temperature and atmospheric pressure.
questions.explanation: Water has a specific heat capacity of 4186 Jkg -1K -1 . Specific heat of some substance - Iron/Steel - 450, Copper - 390, Silver - 230, Mercury - 140, Platinum - 130, Hydrogen - 14000, Air - 718, Ice - 2100, Sea Water - 3900 etc.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Mercury has a boiling point of approximately 357°C. 2. Gallium remains in the liquid state at room temperature. 3. Copper turns into gas at 357°C. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Mercury is a unique metal that exists as a liquid at room temperature and has a relatively low boiling point of 357°C, at which it transitions from liquid to gas. Statement 2 is incorrect because gallium melts just above room temperature (around 29.8°C), meaning it is solid at standard room temperature, not liquid. Statement 3 is incorrect as well; copper has a much higher boiling point — approximately 2562°C — and does not turn into gas at 357°C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements about common metal sulphates: 1. Epsom salt is used as a flame retardant, mordant, and astringent. 2. Potash alum is a double salt composed of potassium, aluminium, and sulphate ions in a 1:1:2 ratio. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 2 only. Statement 1 is incorrect - Epsom salt is magnesium sulphate (MgSO₄·7H₂O) and is mainly used as a laxative, bath salt, or in gardening. It is not primarily used as a flame retardant or mordant. Statement 2 is correct - Potash alum (KAl(SO₄)₂·12H₂O) is a double salt containing potassium, aluminium, and sulphate ions in the molar ratio 1:1:2. It is widely used for its astringent and dye-fixing (mordant) properties.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ozone is an allotrope of ______.
questions.explanation: Oxygen. Ozone (O3) is a triatomic allotrope of oxygen. Ozone is a powerful oxidant (far more so than dioxygen) and has many industrial and consumer applications related to oxidation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Assertion (A): Silicon dioxide has a high melting point due to strong covalent bonds throughout its structure. Reason (R): Silicon dioxide is made up of small, discrete molecules held by weak forces.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: Silicon dioxide (SiO₂), also known as silica, has a giant covalent structure where each silicon atom is bonded to four oxygen atoms in a tetrahedral arrangement. These strong covalent bonds extend throughout the crystal, requiring a lot of energy to break — hence, it has a very high melting point. However, the reason is incorrect because SiO₂ is not made of small, discrete molecules, but of a continuous 3D network.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following minerals has kieserite as its ore ?
questions.explanation: Magnesium. Kieserite is a magnesium sulphate mineral. It is used in the production of Epsom salt and as a fertiliser in agriculture.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Identify the alloy among the following of which lead is a component.
questions.explanation: Solder is a metal alloy usually made of tin and lead. Alnico - aluminium (Al), nickel (Ni), and cobalt (Co). Constantan - A copper-nickel alloy used in electrical work for its high resistance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements about metals used in semiconductor LED technology : 1. Gallium is used in the production of compound semiconductors like GaAs and GaN for LEDs. 2. Copper and zinc are the most commonly used metals in LED semiconductors. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Statement 1 is correct - Gallium is a key component in modern LED technology. Compounds such as Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) and Gallium Nitride (GaN) are semiconductors with excellent light-emitting properties and are widely used in LED manufacturing. Statement 2 is incorrect - While copper and zinc are important in other electrical and electronic applications, they are not the primary metals used in LED semiconductors.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is used as a substitute of mercury in thermometers?
questions.explanation: Galinstan. An alloy composed of gallium, indium, and tin which melts at −19°C and is thus liquid at room temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the product formed when zinc and sulphuric acid react ?
questions.explanation: Zinc sulphate. Zinc reacts with dilute Sulphuric acid to form Zinc sulphate and Hydrogen gas is evolved from the reaction. This is a single displacement reaction of a non-metal by a metal. Both metals and nonmetals take part in displacement reactions. Zn (s) + H2SO4(aq) → ZnSO4(aq) + H2(g).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. When iron reacts with water, a gas is released as a by-product. 2. The gas evolved in this reaction is methane. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Neither 1 nor 2. Statement 1 is incorrect in general conditions. Iron does not react significantly with water at room temperature. However, at high temperatures, steam can react with red-hot iron to form iron oxide (Fe₃O₄) and hydrogen gas — not at room temperature. Statement 2 is incorrect because methane is not produced in this reaction. The gas evolved (if any) when iron reacts with hot water (steam) is hydrogen, not methane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following gases plays an important role in welding titanium, aluminium, stainless steel, and magnesium ?
questions.explanation: Argon (Ag) : a chemical element with atomic number 18. It is a noble gas, meaning it is inert and does not react with other substances.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The metal derived from the medieval Latin word 'Kalium' is the seventh most abundant metal in the earth's crust. 2. Aluminium is derived from the word 'Kalium' and is the seventh most abundant metal. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 only. The metal derived from the medieval Latin word 'Kalium' is potassium. Potassium is indeed the seventh most abundant metal in the earth’s crust. Aluminium, on the other hand, is derived from the mineral name “alumen” and is the third most abundant metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An image of which of the following elements is shown by the map of Cyprus from which the element got its name ?
questions.explanation: Copper (Cu, Atomic no 29). It is a good conductor of heat and electricity. It is in group 11, period 4 and block ‘d’ of the periodic table. It was the first metal used by man on earth.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which radioactive isotope has a half-life of 5770 years, which is commonly used to estimate the age of organic materials such as paper and parchment ?
questions.explanation: 14C - It is an unstable and weakly radioactive isotope of carbon. Three Natural isotopes of carbon : 12C, 13C and 14C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Chromium ions released from tannery industries are a major cause of acute water pollution. 2. Magnesium ions released from tanneries cause significant water pollution. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Chromium, especially in the hexavalent form, is widely used in tanning leather and is a serious pollutant released from tannery wastewater. It causes acute water pollution and is highly toxic to aquatic life and humans. Magnesium, while naturally present in water, is not a significant pollutant from tannery waste.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Alkalis are bases that are soluble in water. 2. All alkalis are bases, but not all bases are alkalis. 3. Alkanes are basic in nature and dissolve in water. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. Alkalis are a specific type of base that are soluble in water, such as sodium hydroxide (NaOH) and potassium hydroxide (KOH). Therefore, statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is also correct because while all alkalis are bases, not all bases are soluble in water, so not all bases are alkalis. Statement 3 is incorrect — alkanes are hydrocarbons (like methane, ethane) and are non-polar, neutral substances. They do not dissolve in water and do not have basic properties.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the correct way to mix acid and water ?

options.a: The water must be added to the acid.
options.b: The water must be heated before mixing.
options.c: The acid must be heated before mixing.
options.d: The acid must be slowly added to the water.

questions.answer_text: The acid must be slowly added to the water.
questions.explanation: The process of dissolving an acid or a base in water is a highly exothermic one. Care must be taken while mixing concentrated nitric acid or sulphuric acid with water. The acid must always be added slowly to water with constant stirring. Mixing an acid or base with water results in a decrease in the concentration of ions (H3O +/OH– ) per unit volume. Such a process is called dilution and the acid or the base is said to be diluted.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Match column A with column B. Column-A Column-B i. Lemon a. Tartaric acid ii. Milk b. Citric acid iii. Vinegar c. Lactic acid iv. Tamarind d. Acetic acid
questions.explanation: i-b, ii-c, iii-d, iv-a.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A 100 mL solution having 0.01 moles of NaOH dissolved in it. The pH of the solution is:
questions.explanation: 13. Concentration of OH ions = = = 0.1 M. 0.01 𝑚𝑜𝑙𝑒𝑠 100 𝑚𝐿 0.01 𝑚𝑜𝑙𝑒𝑠 0.1 𝐿 Hence, [OH− ] = 0.1 M. Now, pOH = −𝑙𝑜𝑔 [OH— ] pOH = − (10–1 𝑙𝑜𝑔 ). pOH = 1 𝑙𝑜𝑔 10 = 1. We know that, pH + pOH = 14 pH = 14 − pOH = 14 – 1 = 13.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Potassium chloride is not used to treat potassium deficiency. 2. Potassium iodide is used to supplement iodine in the human body. 3. Potassium nitrate is used in fertilizers and food preservatives. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 2 and 3 only. Potassium iodide is used in medicine primarily as a source of iodine, especially in the treatment of thyroid conditions and as a protective agent in radiation exposure. Potassium nitrate, on the other hand, is an industrial compound commonly used in fertilizers, gunpowder, and occasionally as a food preservative. However, statement 1 is incorrect. Contrary to what's stated, potassium chloride is in fact widely used as a mineral supplement to treat or prevent low potassium levels in the blood (a condition known as hypokalemia).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The reaction between an acid and a base is known as _______ .
questions.explanation: Neutralisation reaction. When a strong acid reacts with a strong base, it results in a salt which is neutral. Example: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which acid is predominantly present in tomatoes?
questions.explanation: Oxalic acid (C2H2O4). It is found in leafy greens (such as spinach), vegetables, fruits, cocoa, nuts, and seeds. Acetic Acid (CH3COOH) - Vinegar. Malic acid (C4H6O5) is found in apples and apricots. Formic acid or Methanoic acid (HCOOH) is found in bees, nettle stings, ant stings and insects. Carbonic acid is found in all carbonated beverages.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Hydrogen chloride (HCl) is a covalent compound formed by sharing electrons between hydrogen and chlorine atoms. 2. Sodium chloride (NaCl) is also a covalent compound because it is formed by sharing electrons between sodium and chlorine atoms. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Hydrogen chloride (HCl) is a covalent compound because it forms when hydrogen and chlorine atoms share electrons to complete their outer shells. This sharing of electrons creates a covalent bond. On the other hand, sodium chloride (NaCl) is an ionic compound, formed by the transfer of electrons from sodium to chlorine, resulting in oppositely charged ions held together by ionic bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is used as an antacid to neutralise stomach acidity?
questions.explanation: Magnesium Hydroxide {Mg(OH)2}. It is an inorganic compound. It is naturally found as the mineral brucite. It can be used as an antacid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When the litmus solution is neither acidic nor basic, its colour is ______.
questions.explanation: Purple. Litmus solution - It is extracted from lichen. Litmus paper (pH paper) - Made by treating the paper with natural dyes from lichens. The base turns Red litmus to blue, while acid turns blue litmus to red. Some natural Indicators - Red cabbage leaves, turmeric, coloured petals of some flowers (Hydrangea, Petunia and Geranium).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Acetic acid is the main acid present in vinegar. 2. Citric acid is primarily found in citrus fruits like lemons and oranges. 3. Vinegar has a basic pH due to the presence of tartaric acid. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. Vinegar is acidic in nature because it contains acetic acid, which gives it a characteristic sour taste and a pH typically around 2.5 to 3.5. This makes statement 1 correct. Citric acid, mentioned in statement 2, is found in citrus fruits such as lemons, limes, and oranges and is unrelated to vinegar, but the statement about its source is factually correct. However, statement 3 is incorrect — vinegar does not contain tartaric acid, and it is definitely not basic in nature. Tartaric acid is found in grapes and tamarind, not in vinegar.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct ? I. Salts of a strong acid and weak base are acidic with pH value less than 7. II. When electricity is passed through an aqueous solution of sodium chloride (called brine), it decomposes to form sodium oxide.
questions.explanation: Only I. Acids - That gives off hydrogen ions in water and forms salts by combining with certain metals. Strongest acid - Fluoroantimonic acid. Common strong acids: Hydrochloric Acid (HCl), Sulphuric Acid (H2SO4), Nitric Acid (HNO3). Base (pH value > 7) - That can accept hydrogen ions in water and can neutralise an acid. Common strong bases: sodium hydroxide (NaOH), potassium hydroxide (KOH), calcium hydroxide {Ca(OH)2}.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct ?

options.a: Living organisms can survive a wide range of pH change.
options.b: When pH of rain water is less than 8.2, it is called acid rain.
options.c: Our body works within the pH range of 7.0 to 7.8.
options.d: Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth is lower than 1.5.

questions.answer_text: Our body works within the pH range of 7.0 to 7.8.
questions.explanation: The pH (Potential of Hydrogen) range goes from 0 - 14, with 7 being neutral. pH of less than 7 indicates acidity, whereas a pH of greater than 7 indicates a base. Tooth decay begins when the pH of the mouth falls below 5.5.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following substances has a pH value of about 14 ?
questions.explanation: Sodium hydroxide. pH Value: Blood (7.35 to 7.45), Sodium hydroxide (12.3), Milk of magnesia (10.5), Lemon Juice (2.32), Vinegar (2.5), Washing Soda (11). pH Indicator - Phenolphthalein (range pH 8.2 to 10.0; colourless to pink), Bromthymol blue (range pH 6.0 to 7.6; yellow to blue), and litmus (range pH 4.5 to 8.3; red to blue).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Muriatic acid is another common name for hydrochloric acid. 2. Hydrochloric acid is used in the production of chlorides, fertilizers, dyes, and in various industries. 3. Sulfuric acid is commonly known as muriatic acid. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. Muriatic acid is the common name for hydrochloric acid (HCl), especially in industrial and commercial contexts. It is a strong acid widely used in the production of chlorides, fertilizers, and dyes, as well as in electroplating, and in the textile, photographic, and rubber industries. However, statement 3 is incorrect because sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄) is not referred to as muriatic acid. Sulfuric acid has its own distinct applications and nomenclature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What does ‘p’ in pH stand for ?
questions.explanation: Potenz. "pH" is a measure of how acidic/basic water is. It was first described by Danish biochemist Soren Peter Lauritz Sorensen in 1909. The p stands for the power or concentration, and the H for the hydrogen ion (H+ ).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Who synthesised acetic acid for the first time ?
questions.explanation: Kolbe's work was historic because he produced organic compounds from inorganic ones artificially. Acetic acid is produced synthetically as well as from bacterial fermentation. In nature it is found in ants and some fruits.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What happens when an acid or a base is mixed with water ?

options.a: Decrease in the concentration of ions (H2O +/OH– ) per unit volume
options.b: Decrease in the concentration of ions (H3O +/OH– ) per litre volume
options.c: Increase in the concentration of ions (H3O +/OH – ) per unit volume
options.d: Decrease in the concentration of ions (H3O +/OH– ) per unit volume

questions.answer_text: Decrease in the concentration of ions (H3O +/OH– ) per unit volume
questions.explanation: Acids in water dissociate H + ions. When an acidic solution is diluted with water, the concentration of H + ions decreases and the pH of the solution increases towards 7. When an alkali is diluted with water, the concentration of OH– ions decreases, and the pH of the alkali fall towards 7.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The presence of a high concentration of hydrogen ions indicates acidic soil. 2. Nitrogen is the key indicator of soil acidity. 3. Acidic soil typically has a pH value less than 7. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 3 only. Acidic soils are characterized by a high concentration of hydrogen ions (H⁺), which directly corresponds to a low pH value (less than 7). Statement 2 is incorrect — while nitrogen is an essential nutrient for plant growth, its presence does not determine soil acidity. It may exist in various forms regardless of pH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a natural acid-base indicator?
questions.explanation: Thyme leaves is a herb and also has medicinal use. Geranium flowers, Petunia flowers, and Red cabbage act as a pH indicator due to the presence of the water-soluble vacuolar pigment named Anthocyanin.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The pH of curd is lower than that of milk. 2. Curd is more acidic than milk. 3. A substance with a pH around 8 tastes sour. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. The pH of milk is typically around 6.5 to 6.7, which is slightly acidic. When milk is converted into curd, lactic acid is produced by bacterial fermentation, which lowers the pH to around 4.5, making it more acidic. So, both statements 1 and 2 are correct. However, statement 3 is incorrect because a pH of around 8 indicates a basic substance, which would taste bitter or soapy, not sour. Sour substances are acidic and have a pH less than 7.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following raw materials is NOT used to prepare the baking soda?
questions.explanation: Na2CO3 . The raw materials used to prepare baking soda are: Sodium chloride (NaCl): Also known as common salt, this is the source of sodium ions. Ammonia (NH₃): Reacts with carbon dioxide and water to form ammonium bicarbonate. Carbon dioxide (CO₂): Reacts with ammonium bicarbonate to precipitate out sodium bicarbonate. Water (H₂O): Used in the reaction. Reaction: NaCl + H2O + CO2 + NH3 → NH4CI + NaHCO3 .

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct order of basicity ?
questions.explanation: CsOH > KOH > NaOH > LiOH. This order is due to the increasing size of the alkali metal ions, which leads to better solvation and greater basicity. As you move down the group, the basicity increases because the larger alkali metal ions (like Cs⁺) can more easily dissociate and interact with water compared to the smaller ions (like Li⁺).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Sodium bicarbonate is a white crystalline solid used in fire extinguishers. 2. Sodium bicarbonate can act as both an acid and a base. 3. Sodium chromate is commonly used to neutralise acids in household applications. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃) is a white, crystalline powder that is widely used in fire extinguishers because it releases carbon dioxide upon heating, smothering the fire. It also acts as a mild base, but interestingly, it can react with both acids and bases, making it amphoteric — hence, statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because sodium chromate (Na₂CrO₄) is toxic and used mainly in industrial and laboratory settings, not for neutralising acids in household or medicinal uses.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Assertion (A): C₂H₅COOH (propanoic acid) is the most acidic among the given carboxylic acids. Reason (R): The acidic strength of carboxylic acids decreases with increasing alkyl chain length due to the +I effect of alkyl groups.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is false, but R is true.
options.d: A is true, but R is false.

questions.answer_text: A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation: Among the given acids in the statement, the most acidic is HCOOH (formic acid). This is because it has no alkyl group attached to the carboxyl group, meaning it experiences no electron-donating inductive effect, which makes the hydrogen ion (H⁺) release easier. On the other hand, alkyl groups like methyl (CH₃), ethyl (C₂H₅), and propyl (C₃H₇) exert a +I (inductive) effect, pushing electrons toward the carboxyl group and making the release of H⁺ ions less favorable — thus reducing acidity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Why does the milkman add a very small amount of baking soda to fresh milk ?

options.a: To reduce the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly more acidic
options.b: To increase the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly alkaline
options.c: To maintain the pH of the fresh milk at 6 for a longer time
options.d: To reduce the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly alkaline

questions.answer_text: To increase the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly alkaline
questions.explanation: A milkman adds a small amount of baking soda (NaHCO3) to fresh milk to prevent its acidification, allowing him to store it for a longer time. This is because milk in an alkaline condition does not curdle easily.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which acid is used as a souring agent added to vinegar, pickled vegetables, and sauces, and as a raw material for seasoning?
questions.explanation: Acetic acid (CH3COOH). It is a colorless, organic compound that is a carboxylic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Bronsted and Lowry introduced their theory of acids and bases in the year 1923. 2. According to their theory, an acid is a proton donor and a base is a proton acceptor. 3. The Bronsted-Lowry theory replaced the Arrhenius concept in the same year it was introduced. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. The Bronsted - Lowry acid-base theory was proposed independently by Johannes Nicolaus Bronsted and Thomas Martin Lowry in 1923. Their concept defined an acid as a proton (H⁺) donor and a base as a proton acceptor, which was a major advancement over the Arrhenius definition that was limited to aqueous solutions. However, statement 3 is incorrect because while the theory gained acceptance over time, it did not immediately replace the Arrhenius model in the same year. Both models are still taught today due to their relevance in different contexts.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The reaction of an acid and a metal gives:

options.d: carbon dioxide, salt and hydrogen gas

questions.explanation: hydrogen gas and salt. When an acid reacts with a metal, the products are typically a salt and hydrogen gas. For example, when sodium (Na) reacts with hydrochloric acid (HCl), the reaction produces sodium chloride (NaCl) and hydrogen gas (H₂). The balanced chemical equation is: 2 Na (s) + 2 HCl (aq) → 2 NaCl (aq) + H2 (g).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Assertion (A): Clove oil can be used as an olfactory indicator in acid-base reactions. Reason (R): Olfactory indicators show a change in colour when mixed with acids or bases.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is false, but R is true.
options.d: A is true, but R is false

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: Clove oil is an example of an olfactory indicator, which means it shows a change in smell when mixed with acidic or basic solutions. In an acidic medium, clove oil retains its characteristic smell, while in a basic medium, the smell may become faint or disappear. This makes the assertion true. However, the reason is false because olfactory indicators do not show a colour change — they show a change in odour. Colour change is a property of visual indicators like litmus or phenolphthalein, not olfactory ones.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding phyllosilicates: 1. Micas, chlorite, talc, and serpentine are common examples of phyllosilicate minerals. 2. Phyllosilicates are characterized by a sheet-like silicate structure. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Phyllosilicates are a group of silicate minerals known for their sheet-like (layered) structures. The silicon-oxygen tetrahedra in these minerals are arranged in flat sheets, which makes them soft and gives them a perfect cleavage. Common examples of phyllosilicates include micas (like biotite and muscovite), chlorite, talc, and serpentine. These minerals are typically found in metamorphic and some igneous rocks and are often used in industrial applications due to their physical properties.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is the most widely used method for refining impure metals?
questions.explanation: Electrolytic Refining. It is a technique used for the extraction and purification of metals by the process of electrolysis. Metals like copper, nickel, gold, lead, silver, and zinc can be purified using electrolytic refining.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Diaspore is a principal ore of aluminum that commonly occurs in bauxite deposits. 2. Cinnabar is the chief ore of iron found in volcanic regions. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: Only 1. Diaspore is a major ore of aluminum and is often found within bauxite, a rock composed primarily of aluminum hydroxide minerals. However, statement 2 is incorrect because cinnabar is not an iron ore—it's a mercury ore, and hematite or magnetite are typical iron ores.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to a law postulated by ______, the amounts of different substances liberated by the same quantity of electricity passing through the electrolytic solution are proportional to their chemical equivalent weights.
questions.explanation: Michael Faraday. Law of Electrolysis states that the amount of chemical change produced by current at an electrode-electrolyte boundary is proportional to the quantity of electricity used, and the amounts of chemical changes produced by the same quantity of electricity in different substances are proportional to their equivalent weights.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: With reference to metals and their ores, which of the following pairs is INCORRECT ?
questions.explanation: Mercury is either found as a native metal (rare) or in cinnabar, metacinnabar, corderoite, living stoneite and other minerals. Greenockite is a rare cadmium bearing metal sulphide mineral consisting of cadmium sulphide in crystalline form. Major ores of aluminium are Bauxite, Corundum, Feldspar, Cryolite, Alunite and Kaolin. Smelite is an ore of Cobalt.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The process in which metals are extracted from their ores by heating beyond the melting point is called________ .
questions.explanation: Smelting. Roasting is a process of heating a sulphide ore to a high temperature in the presence of air. Calcination - A process of heating some solid material or a substance in a controlled environment. Spinning - The process of converting staple or short lengths of fibre, such as cotton or rayon, into continuous yarn or thread.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding carbon-based substances: 1. Coke is a tough, porous, black substance that is almost a pure form of carbon. 2. Coal gas is a solid fuel rich in carbon and used in making electrodes. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1. Coke is a tough, porous, black solid that is formed by heating coal in the absence of air (a process called destructive distillation). It is almost pure carbon and is widely used as a reducing agent in metallurgy, especially in the extraction of iron. So, statement 1 is correct. On the other hand, coal gas is not a solid, but a mixture of gases like hydrogen, methane, and carbon monoxide. It is used as a fuel but not for making electrodes, and it is not rich in carbon in solid form, making statement 2 incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Dolomite is an ore of :
questions.explanation: Magnesium is found in minerals such as magnesite, dolomite, brucite, serpentinite, etc. and is mostly recovered from seawater, brines and bitterns. Dolomite formula - MgCO3 · CaCO3 .

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: ______ is a process of forming a thick oxide layer of aluminium.
questions.explanation: Anodising. Aluminium oxide coat makes it resistant to further corrosion. It is also useful in architectural finishing.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Assertion (A): Rayon is known as a semi-synthetic fibre used in making soft and lustrous fabrics. Reason (R): Rayon is made from cellulose obtained from natural sources like wood pulp. Codes:

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Rayon is a semi-synthetic fibre because it is chemically processed from a natural source, mainly cellulose derived from wood pulp or cotton waste. It is widely used in making fabrics due to its silk-like appearance, softness, and breathability. The assertion is correct because rayon is used to make soft and lustrous cloth. The reason is also correct, and it directly explains why rayon is classified as semi-synthetic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Assertion (A) : Dienes are hydrocarbons that contain exactly two carbon–carbon double bonds in their structure. Reason (R) : The presence of two double bonds classifies the compound as an aromatic compound. Codes :

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: A is true, but R is false
options.c: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.d: Both A and R are false

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: Dienes are a type of unsaturated hydrocarbon that contain exactly two carbon–carbon double bonds (C=C) in their molecular structure, making the assertion true. However, the reason is false because the presence of two double bonds does not make a compound aromatic. Aromatic compounds must have a planar ring structure with delocalized π electrons, as per Hückel’s rule — a condition not fulfilled by all dienes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Propane and butane are the main components of which of the following gases?
questions.explanation: LPG. Propane (C3H8) and butane (C4H10). Ethyl Mercaptan is added to the gas to make it smell like rotten eggs. Liquefied natural gas (LNG) and Compressed natural gas (CNG) mainly composed of methane (CH4). Biogas is a combination of two-thirds of methane (CH4) and the rest is mostly carbon dioxide (CO2).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Isopentane, also called ______, is a branched-chain saturated hydrocarbon with the chemical formula 𝐶 . 5 𝐻12
questions.explanation: 2-methylbutane. 2, 3 - Dimethylbutane is an isomer of hexane. Isobutane is an alkane that is propane substituted by a methyl group at position two.
