questions.explanation: SF6 . It is a colourless, odourless, non-toxic gas of high chemical stability and inertness. It is also non-flammable and about 5 times heavier than air-one of the heaviest known gases. It is used in the electrical industry as a gaseous dielectric medium for high-voltage sulfur hexafluoride circuit breakers, switchgear.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the IUPAC name of tertiary butyl alcohol ?
questions.explanation: 2-Methylpropan-2-ol. Tertiary Butyl Alcohol, also Tert-butyl alcohol, is a tertiary alcohol used in fuels and fuel additives, intermediates and laboratory chemicals. It is a colorless oily liquid with a sharp alcohol odor.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is a straight-chain alkyl carboxylic acid with the chemical formula CH3CH2CH2CO2H ?
questions.explanation: Butyric acid. It is utilized in the production of various butyrate esters (e.g., methyl butyrate), which have pleasant aromas and tastes and are used as additives in foods, perfumes, flavorings, varnishes, pharmaceuticals, and disinfectants. Methanoic acid (HCOOH), Ethanoic acid (CH3COOH), Propanoic acid (CH3CH2COOH).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Identify the structural formula for magnesium hydroxide.
questions.explanation: Mg(OH)2 . Magnesium hydroxide is an inorganic compound. It is naturally found as the mineral brucite. Magnesium hydroxide can be used as an antacid or a laxative in either an oral liquid suspension or chewable tablet form.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Milk of magnesia contains magnesium hydroxide suspended in water. 2. It is used as a laxative and antacid. 3. Magnesium hydroxide is highly soluble in water. Which of the statements are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 & 2 only. Statement 3 is false: magnesium hydroxide is insoluble in water. Name of base and Found in: Calcium hydroxide - Lime water, Ammonium hydroxide - Window cleaner, Sodium hydroxide/Potassium hydroxide - Soap.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The IUPAC name of an element is Unnilennium. What is the symbol of the element ?
questions.explanation: Une. International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) - It is the world authority on chemical nomenclature as well as terminology. It is basically a method of naming organic compounds according to certain rules, Established - 1919, Headquarters - North Carolina (United States).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the name of the chemical compound having the molecular formula C3H4O which is mostly used for the production of acrylic acid and acrylate ester ?
questions.explanation: Acrolein (C3H4O): It is a colourless to pale yellow liquid with a strong, pungent odour. Uses:- Used as a biocide to control plants, algae, molluscs, fungi, rodents, and microorganisms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Polyatomic positive ions often have common names ending with the suffix _________.
questions.explanation: -onium. Ion - An atom or molecule with a net electric charge due to the loss or gain of electrons. Types of ions : Cation - having positively charged ions. Anions- having negatively charged ions. Monatomic - Containing only one atom. Polyatomic ion - Ion that contains more than one atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the chemical name for ionic compound MgCl2 ?
questions.explanation: Magnesium chloride (MgCl2) consists of one magnesium ion (Mg2+ ) and two chloride ions (Cl- ) in an ionic bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Sodium Hydroxide is the chemical name of which of the following common substances ?
questions.explanation: Caustic Soda. It is used to manufacture soaps, rayon, paper, explosives, dyestuffs, and petroleum products.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Negative ions that consist of a single atom are named by adding the suffix ____ to the stem of the name of the element.
questions.explanation: -ide. Example of some ions : 𝐹 - Fluoride, - Oxide, - Chloride. − 𝑂 2− 𝐶𝑙 − Polyatomic positive ions often have common names ending with the suffix -onium, Example - H3O + - Hydronium, NH4 + - Ammonium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the chemical name of saltpetre ?
questions.explanation: Potassium Nitrate (KNO3 , Saltpetre) is an ionic white crystalline salt made up of potassium ions and nitrate ions. Uses - Main constituents of gunpowder, food preservatives and additives (in meat and fish), fertilizer, and oxidizer for fireworks and rockets, etc.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Identify the chemical formula of ammonium hydroxide.
questions.explanation: NH4OH. Ammonium Hydroxide (ammonia water, ammoniacal liquor, ammonia liquor, aqua ammonia) (NH4OH) colourless liquid with a strong odour. Uses: Cleaning agents, chemical fertilizers, furniture darkening, etc.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which low-calorie sweetener has the chemical formula 𝐶 that is 14 𝐻18 𝑁2 𝑂5 two hundred times sweeter than sugar ?
questions.explanation: Aspartame. It is a methyl ester of aspartic acid (phenylalanine dipeptide). Uses: ingredients in beverages, dairy products, nutrition bars, desserts, chewing gum, sauces, syrups, etc. Saccharin (C7H5NO3S) - 550 times as sweet as sucrose. Sucralose (C12H19Cl3O8) - about 320 to 1,000 times sweeter than sucrose. Neotame (C20H330N2O5) - 8000 times sweeter than sucrose.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is an organic compound with the formula CH3OC6H5 used as a perfume, fragrance and solvent ?
questions.explanation: Anisole (methoxybenzene, CH3OC6H5). Toluene (C6H5CH3) is found naturally in crude oil, and is used in oil refining and the manufacturing of paints. Acetophenone (C6H5C(O)CH3) is used for fragrance in soaps and perfumes and as a flavouring agent in foods. Aniline (C6H5NH2) used to make dyes, drugs, explosives, plastics, and photographic and rubber chemicals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The chemical formula of borax is .
questions.explanation: Na2B4O7 .10H2O. Borax (tincal, sodium tetraborate decahydrate) is a natural mineral and a salt of boric acid. It is also known as sodium borate, sodium tetraborate, or disodium tetraborate. It can be used in the testing of cleaning agent, insecticide, water softening agent and diabetes mellitus.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is soda lime ?
questions.explanation: NaOH + CaO. 3 : 1 mixture of NaOH (Sodium Hydroxide) and CaO (Calcium Oxide) is called soda lime.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is the formula of barium peroxide.
questions.explanation: BaO2 . It is an odourless, greyish-white powder. It is used as a bleaching agent, in making Hydrogen Peroxide, Aluminium welding and textile dyeing. It is a strong oxidizing agent. BaO (Barium oxide), is used as a drying agent for solvents, in cathode ray tubes, catalysts, and crown glass.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following pair of compound names – formulas is correct ? I. Calcium oxide – Ca2O II. Aluminium Oxide – Al2O3
questions.explanation: Only II. Calcium Oxide (CaO), Uses - manufacturing of cement, paper, and high-grade steel. Aluminium Oxide (Al2,O3), Uses - refractories, ceramics, and polishing and abrasive applications etc.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is the scientific name of the mineral called chromite ?
questions.explanation: Iron chromium oxide. Chromite is used as a refractory in the production of steel, copper, glass, and cement. Chromite occurs as a primary accessory mineral in basic and ultrabasic igneous rocks.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is the common name of a natural admixture mineral of zinc carbonate and hydrous zinc silicate?
questions.explanation: Calamine. To differentiate the minerals, they were given new names of: Smithsonite (zinc carbonate) Hemimorphite (hydrous zinc silicate).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Calcium hypochlorite is commonly known as:
questions.explanation: Bleaching Powder (CaOCl2). Laughing gas (Nitrous oxide, N2O) or happy gas, is a colourless, non - flammable gas. Used in medical and dental procedures as a sedative.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of compound names – formula is correct ? I. Hydrogen chloride – H2Cl II. Hydrogen sulphide – HS2
questions.explanation: Neither I nor II. Hydrogen Chloride (HCl) used for cleaning, pickling, electroplating metals, tanning leather, and refining. Hydrogen sulphide (H₂S) used to produce heavy water for nuclear power plants.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct chemical formula of sodium aluminate ?
questions.explanation: NaAlO2 (Sodium Aluminate). In water treatment it is used as an adjunct to water softening systems, as a coagulant aid to improve flocculation, and for removing dissolved silica and phosphates. Sodium Aluminate is a white powder. It is used in the manufacture of milk-glass, soap and cleaning compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Identify the chemical structure for potassium hydroxide.
questions.explanation: KOH. Potassium Hydroxide (Caustic Potash) is an inorganic compound. It is used as an electrolyte in some alkaline batteries. It is used in the thickening of food. It is used in chip fabrication for semiconductors.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ferrum is the Latin name for ___ .
questions.explanation: Iron (Fe). Copper (Cu)- Cuprum, Zinc (Zn) - Zincum, Antimony (Sb) - Stibium, Gold (Au) - Aurum, Lead (Pb) - Plumbum, Mercury (Hg) - Hydrargyrum, Potassium (K) - Kalium, Silver (Ag) - Argentum, Sodium (Na) - Natrium, Tin (Sn) - Stannum, Tungsten (W) - Wolfram.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which type of vehicle is commonly used in zero-emission public transport systems ?
questions.explanation: Electric buses are a key part of zero-emission public transport systems since they run on electricity rather than fossil fuels. They significantly reduce air pollution, greenhouse gas emissions, and noise pollution in cities. Diesel buses – Emit CO₂, NOx, and particulate matter → not zero-emission. Petrol cars – High emissions, unsuitable for zero-emission systems. Hybrid vehicles – Reduce emissions but are not zero-emission (still use fuel).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following figures accurately depicts the inter-conversion of the three states of matter ?
questions.explanation: b. Interconversion of states of matter refers to the process where matter changes between solid, liquid, and gas states, and back, without altering its chemical composition. This physical change is influenced by temperature and pressure. Plasma, the fourth state of matter, is an ionized gas consisting of roughly equal numbers of positively and negatively charged particles.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: One mole of Aluminium Sulphate Al2(SO4)3 contains :
questions.explanation: 12 moles of oxygen atoms. This is because each sulfate ion (SO4) 2- has 4 oxygen atoms, and since there are 3 sulfate ions in the formula, the total is 3 × 4 = 12 oxygen atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which inert gas is used in double-glazed windows to fill the space between the panes?
questions.explanation: Argon. Argon is used in double-glazed windows because it has low thermal conductivity, which enhances the insulating properties of the window. This helps to reduce heat transfer, making the windows more energy-efficient by minimizing heat loss in the winter and heat gain in the summer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Gases, especially oxygen and carbon dioxide, are essential for the survival of aquatic animals and plants. The gases from the atmosphere reach the aquatic animals and plants through:
questions.explanation: Diffusion - It is the movement of molecules from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration, down the concentration gradient. Other applications : Water present in the soil diffuses into plants through their root hair cells; Carbon dioxide moves from cells into the blood. Condensation - Change of the state of matter from the gas phase into the liquid phase. Example - Formation of Rain droplets. Evaporation - Changes of liquid to gaseous states. Sublimation - Conversion of solid to gaseous states.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: To check the presence of adulterated sugar solution in honey, a cotton wick dipped in the sample is ignited with a match stick. Adulteration is confirmed if:

options.a: it burns with a violet coloured flame
options.c: it burns with a green coloured flame
options.d: it burns with a crackling sound

questions.answer_text: it burns with a crackling sound
questions.explanation: It burns with a crackling sound. Honey is composed of water and two types of Sugars (fructose and glucose). Adulterant means any material employed for the purpose of adulteration. To assess the authenticity of Turmeric powder, mix a teaspoon of haldi with water; genuine Turmeric settles at the bottom, displaying a pale yellow hue, while adulterated Turmeric turns dark yellow in water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: At standard temperature and pressure (STP), the value of temperature is:
questions.explanation: 0°C (273.15 K or 32 degrees Fahrenheit). Standard temperature and pressure (STP) refers to the nominal conditions in the atmosphere at sea level. The standard pressure is 1 atm (atmospheric pressure). At STP, one mole of any gas will have a volume of 22.4 litres.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Synthetic fibres, elastomers, polymers and surfactant intermediate are all subgroups of ________ industries.
questions.explanation: Petrochemical. Synthetic fibres: Man-made materials composed of polymers, such as textiles. Elastomers: Polymers with high elasticity and flexibility, commonly used in products like rubber bands and tires. Polymers: Large molecules formed by the repeated linking of smaller units (monomers), often used to create diverse materials such as plastics, rubber, and fibres.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Who among the following coined the name oxygen for the element released by mercury oxide in 1779 ?
questions.explanation: Antoine Lavoisier recognized oxygen as key to combustion and named it from the Greek "oxys" (acid) and "genes" (producer). He initially thought it was essential for acid formation, but later discovered its broader role in combustion and respiration. Martin Heinrich Klaproth was a German chemist who discovered uranium (1789) and zirconium (1789). Jons Jacob Berzelius discovered Thorium in 1829.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the chemical formula for the compound commonly known as 'laughing gas' ?
questions.explanation: N2O. Nitrous oxide, often called “laughing gas,” is a safe and effective sedative mixed with oxygen and inhaled through a small mask over the nose to promote relaxation. Dentists may use it to enhance comfort during certain procedures.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Calculate the oxidation number of ‘S’ in H2S2O7
questions.explanation: 6. To calculate the oxidation number of S in H2S2O7 : Assign oxidation numbers to known elements: H = +1 and O = -2 Write the equation: 2(+1) + 2x + 7(-2) = 0 ⇒ 2 + 2x - 14 = 0 ⇒ 2x = 12 ⇒ x = 6.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The chemical formula of glucose is C6H12O6 . The weight % of carbon in glucose is:
questions.explanation: 40. Calculate the molar mass of glucose (C6H12O6) = (6 x 12) + (12 x 1) + (6 x 16) = 72 + 12 + 96 = 180 g/mol. Total mass of carbon (C) = 6 x 12 = 72 g. We Know that, Percentage by Weight = × 100 𝑊𝑒𝑖𝑔ℎ𝑡 𝑜𝑓 𝑐𝑎𝑟𝑏𝑜𝑛 𝑊𝑒𝑖𝑔ℎ𝑡 𝑜𝑓 𝐺𝑙𝑢𝑐𝑜𝑠𝑒 ⇒ × 100 = 40 %. 72 180

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a greenhouse gas ?
questions.explanation: Nitric oxide. The greenhouse effect is a natural process that warms the Earth's surface by trapping heat from the sun. Greenhouse gases, such as methane, carbon dioxide, nitrogen dioxide, ozone, and water vapor, absorb and emit infrared radiation, functioning similarly to a greenhouse. This process is essential for maintaining the Earth's temperature and climate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Identify an example of plasma as a state of matter.
questions.explanation: Neon sign bulbs. Plasma is a hot, ionized gas made up of roughly equal numbers of positively charged ions and negatively charged electrons. It has distinct characteristics that differentiate it from ordinary neutral gases, making it a "fourth state of matter" (solid, liquid, gas, and plasma). Plasmas are strongly influenced by electric and magnetic fields due to their charged particles, unlike neutral gases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A proton bonds to the oxygen atom of a solvent water to give a _______hydronium ion.
questions.explanation: Trigonal pyramidal. A trigonal pyramidal molecular geometry is a shape where one atom is at the top, or apex, and three atoms form a triangular base, similar to a tetrahedron. The bond angle of a trigonal pyramid is usually 109.5°. A proton is a positively charged hydrogen ion (H+ ). When a proton bonds to a water molecule (H₂O), the resulting ion is called a hydronium ion (H₃O+ ).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which cycle consists of sedimentary and gaseous cycles ?
questions.explanation: Biogeochemical cycle. Sedimentary cycles include iron, calcium, sulfur, and phosphorus, but are imperfect as some nutrients become trapped in sediments. Gaseous cycles, involving nitrogen, oxygen, carbon, and water, are generally considered perfect. Biogeochemical cycles describe the movement of elements and compounds across Earth's systems (Atmosphere, Hydrosphere, Lithosphere, Biosphere, and Pedosphere) and are essential for transforming matter and energy into usable forms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is the main active ingredient of clove oil ?
questions.explanation: Eugenol. Curcumin is the main compound found in turmeric. Malic acid is the main acid in many fruits, including apricots, blackberries, blueberries, cherries, grapes etc. Tartaric acid is an organic acid found in fruits such as bananas, grapes and tamarind, and many vegetables.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which phenomenon is opposite to solidification ?
questions.explanation: Fusion : The process by which a substance transitions from a solid to a liquid state. Solidification refers to the change from a liquid or gas to a solid state. Condensation is the transition from gas to liquid, the reverse of vaporization, which is the conversion from liquid or solid to gas. Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas without passing through the liquid phase.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The synthesis of which chemical is inhibited due to aspirin ?
questions.explanation: Prostaglandins : It stimulates inflammation in the tissue and causes pain. These drugs are effective in relieving skeletal pain such as that due to arthritis. Histamine - A neurotransmitter and a regulator of gastric acid secretion. It is released from Basophil and Mast cell.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following tests is used for starch detection ?
questions.explanation: Iodine test. The light orange-brown colour Iodine solution turns blue-black in colour when it reacts with starch. This indicates the presence of carbohydrates in the food item to which iodine solution was added. Example : If Iodine is added to a peeled potato then it will turn black.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the characteristics of a crystalline solid ?

options.b: There is no precise melting point
options.d: Changes abruptly from solid to liquid when heated

questions.answer_text: Changes abruptly from solid to liquid when heated
questions.explanation: Crystalline solids - They exhibit anisotropic properties, varying in electrical resistance and refractive index values across different directions within the same crystals. Examples: Quartz, calcite, sugar, mica, diamonds, snowflakes, rock, calcium fluoride, silicon dioxide, and alum.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the number of atoms in one mole of CH3OH ?
questions.explanation: 3.6 × 1024 . Given, One mole of methanol contains 6 atoms, including 4 moles of hydrogen atoms, 1 mole of oxygen atoms, and 1 mole of carbon atoms. So C = 1, H = 3 + 1 or 4, O = 1. 1 mole of atoms corresponds to Avogadro's number of atoms which is 6.02 × 1023 . 6 mole of atoms = 6 × 6.02 × 1023 ⇒ 6 mole of atoms = 36.12 × 1023 ⇒ 6 mole of atoms = 3.6 × 1024 .

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Potassium metabisulphite is used as a food preservative. 2. Monosodium glutamate protects food against bacteria. 3. Dihydroxy benzene is used in the manufacture of resins and plastics. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 & 3 only. Statement 2 is incorrect. Monosodium glutamate is a flavour enhancer in foods. Other Food Preservatives - Sodium benzoate, calcium propionate, and potassium sorbate. m - Dihydroxybenzene (Resorcinol) : Uses - Manufacture of resins, plastics, dyes, medicine and other organic chemical compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: ______ is the process of complete or incomplete oxidation or hydrolysis of fats and oils when exposed to air, light, moisture, or bacterial action that spoils food.
questions.explanation: Rancidification (Examples - Milk becomes rancid because of not heating it in the humid atmosphere, Oil becomes rancid (rancid oil) because of the decomposition of fats it has).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct Lewis structure of O3 ?
questions.explanation: Lewis structure: A graphical representation of a molecule, showing the arrangement of atoms and valence electrons using dots to depict bonding and lone pairs. The O3 molecule has no net charge, the Lewis structures reveal a +1 charge on the central oxygen and a -1 charge on the singly bonded oxygen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Assertion (A): Ionic solids are formed by electrostatic attraction between cations and anions. Reason (R): Ionic solids generally have low melting points and conduct electricity in solid state.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false. Ionic solids have high melting points and conduct electricity only in molten or aqueous state.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In a galvanic cell, the half-cell in which oxidation takes place is called ______ and it has a negative potential with respect to the solution.
questions.explanation: Anode. Oxidation takes place at anode. And reduction happens at the cathode in a galvanic cell. Since the reaction at the anode is the source of electrons for the current, the anode is the negative terminal of the galvanic cell.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: NPK is a :

options.a: Fertilizer used for increasing fertility of soil
options.d: Sanitizer used to clean dusty leaves

questions.answer_text: Fertilizer used for increasing fertility of soil
questions.explanation: NPK stands for “Nitrogen, Phosphorus and Potassium”, the three nutrients that compose complete fertilizer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following can be used as a catalyst in Hydrogenation reaction?
questions.explanation: Palladium. Hydrogenation is a chemical reaction between molecular hydrogen (H2) and another compound or element, usually in the presence of a catalyst such as nickel, palladium, or platinum.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Name the densest stable element known on earth.
questions.explanation: Osmium has a blue-grey tint and is the densest stable element, it is approximately twice as dense as lead and slightly denser than Iridium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is a synthetic fluorinated compound with an extremely stable molecular structure known to be the most potent greenhouse gas ever found ?
questions.explanation: Sulphur hexafluoride (SF6). It is a colorless, odorless, non - flammable, non - toxic gas and an inorganic gas made up of sulphur and fluorine used in electrical switchgear, transformers, and substations as an electrical insulation, arc quenching and cooling medium. Other Greenhouse Gases - Carbon dioxide (CO2), Methane (CH4), Nitrous oxide (N2O), Fluorinated gases such as Hydrofluorocarbons, perfluorocarbons, sulphur hexafluoride and nitrogen trifluoride.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How is the molecular weight of fatty acid determined ?
questions.explanation: Saponification value - It is the number of milligrams of potassium hydroxide (KOH) required to neutralize the fatty acids obtained by complete hydrolysis of one gram of fat or oil.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Galvanisation is a process in which a protective _______ coating is applied on iron to prevent it from rusting.
questions.explanation: Zinc. Galvanization protects steel and iron from rusting and is commonly used in construction, pipes, and automotive parts to prevent corrosion, while adding a small amount of carbon to pure iron increases its strength and hardness.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Assertion (A): Vulcanisation makes rubber more elastic and durable. Reason (R): Sulphur forms cross-links between rubber molecules, improving mechanical properties.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Vulcanisation process was discovered by Charles Goodyear. Saponification is the process of converting fats and oils into soap.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which among the following is a cooking procedure in which the sugar in the food gets oxidized, turning into a brown colour ?
questions.explanation: Caramelisation. Emulsification is the process of breaking down fat into smaller blood cells so that enzymes can operate and food may be digested more easily. Filtration is defined as the process of separating suspended solid matter from a liquid, by causing the latter to pass through the pores of a membrane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is not a technique or a step to convert normal water to potable water?
questions.explanation: Bromination - Oxidation of hydrobromic acid by hydrogen peroxide in the absence of any transition metal catalyst. It is used as fire retardant.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What type of isomerism exists in compounds containing two or more complexes, each of which contains a different set of ligands that can in principle be replaced with a ligand of the other complex?
questions.explanation: Coordination isomerism. [Co(NH3)6 ][Cr(CN)6 ] is a coordination isomer with [Cr(NH3)6 ][Co(CN)6 ]. Ionization isomerism involves the exchange of ions inside and outside the coordination sphere. An example of ionization isomerism is [Co(NH3)5SO4 ]Br and [Co(NH3)5Br]SO4 . Solvate (Hydrate) isomerism are the isomers which have the same composition but differ with respect to the number of solvent ligand molecules as well as the counterion in the crystal lattice.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How many anions surround a sodium ion in a crystal lattice of sodium chloride?
questions.explanation: Six. Sodium chloride crystal (NaCl), where ions taking part are Na+ and Cl- . They have 1:1 stereochemistry and thus the coordination number of 6.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is not a natural fibre?
questions.explanation: Rayon. Examples of Natural fibres (Fibres obtained from natural sources like plants and animals) include : Cotton, Silk, Wool, Linen, Jute and Hemp. Examples of Artificial fibres (Fibres which are manufactured in laboratories) include Rayon, Nylon, Polyester, Acrylic and Aramid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Assertion (A): Flame test can detect halogens in organic compounds. Reason (R): Halogens are converted into ionic forms during a flame test.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true, but R is false
options.d: A is false, but R is true

questions.answer_text: A is true, but R is false
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false. A flame test is a qualitative analysis used by the chemist to identify the metal and metalloid ion in the sample.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Carbon monoxide contains approximately ______ of oxygen for each 1.00 g of carbon.
questions.explanation: 1.33 g. Every sample of carbon monoxide contains 16.0 g of oxygen for every 12.0 g of carbon. Carbon Monoxide is used in the purification of nickel. It is used as a reducing agent. It is used in water gas shift reactions to produce hydrogen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: As per WHO (World Health Organization), which of the following is NOT an example of disinfection by-products formed at traditional drinking water treatment plants?
questions.explanation: Titania. Titanium dioxide, also called titania, (TiO2), a white, opaque, naturally occurring mineral existing in a number of crystalline forms, the most important of which are rutile and anatase. It is used in paints, coatings, papers, inks, toothpaste, face powder, and food colouring.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How many pollutants are included to measure the Air Quality Index in India?
questions.explanation: 8. pollutants namely particulate matter (PM) 10, PM 2.5, Ozone (O3), Sulphur dioxide (SO2), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), lead (Pb) and ammonia (NH3) act as major parameters in deriving the AQI of an area.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Topaz is a ______ of fluorine and aluminium.
questions.explanation: Silicate. Topaz {Al₂SiO₄(FOH)₂} is used as a gemstone in jewellery and other adornments.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is a weak electrolyte ?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid. Acetic acid (CH3COOH), also called ethanoic acid, is the most important of the carboxylic acids. Ethanoic or acetic acid is used in making dyes, pigments, and paint, and coating additives.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Iron displaces copper from copper sulphate because it is more reactive. 2. Ferrous sulphate is formed, giving the solution a greenish-blue colour. 3. Iron nails turn bluish after dipping in copper sulphate. Which statements are correct ?
questions.explanation: 1 & 2 only. Iron is more reactive than copper; hence, when iron is placed in copper sulphate solution, it displaces copper, forming ferrous sulphate (FeSO₄). As a result, the solution turns green in colour. A reddish-brown deposit of copper appears on the iron nails, not a bluish coating. Thus, statements 1 and 2 are correct, while statement 3 is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the meaning of the Greek origin word, ‘Elektron’ ?
questions.explanation: Amber, the yellow fossilized resin of evergreen trees, a "natural plastic material" already known to the ancient Greeks.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: __________ is the inflammatory compound in pepper spray.
questions.explanation: Capsaicin. It causes burning, pain and tears when it comes into contact with a person’s eyes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is used to remove the green colour from glass?
questions.explanation: Manganese dioxide. Sodium Permanganate is produced by using Manganese dioxide to remove green from glass that results from the presence of Iron.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the scientific name of the banyan tree, a large evergreen tree of Asia characterised by its trunk-like aerial roots?
questions.explanation: Ficus benghalensis : Family - Moraceae, Order - Rosales, Kingdom - Plantae. Gossypium herbaceum : Levant cotton. Santalum album : Indian Sandalwood. Ananas comosus : Pineapple.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match the columns. Column-A (Class) Column-B (Common name) i. Chlorophyceae a. Brown algae ii. Phaeophyceae b. Green algae iii. Rhodophyceae c. Blue-green algae iv. Cyanophyceae d. Red algae

options.a: i - b, ii - c, iii - a, iv - d
options.b: i - b, ii - a, iii - d, iv - c
options.c: i - d, ii - c, iii - b, iv - a
options.d: i - a, ii - b, iii - c, iv - d

questions.answer_text: i - b, ii - a, iii - d, iv - c
questions.explanation: i-b, ii-a, iii-d, iv-c. Divisions of Algae and their Main Characteristics : Chlorophyceae (Green algae) : Major pigments - Chlorophyll, Stored Food - Starch, Example - Spirogyra. Phaeophyceae (Brown algae) : Pigment - fucoxanthin, Stored food - Mannitol, Laminarin, Example - Sargassum, Laminaria. Rhodophyceae (Red algae) : Pigment - Phycoerythrin, Stored Food - Floridean starch, Example - Gracilaria and Gelidium. Cyanophyceae are prokaryotic and play a significant role in nitrogen fixation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about certain parasitic worms : 1. Ancylostoma is a genus of intestinal parasites commonly known as hookworms, transmitted through contaminated soil. 2. Taenia is a genus of tapeworms, including Taenia solium (pork tapeworm) and Taenia saginata (beef tapeworm). 3. Filaria worms belong to the family Filarioidea and are responsible for malaria. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 only. Statement 3 Incorrect - Filarial worms cause lymphatic filariasis (elephantiasis), not malaria.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is another name for starch found mainly in the pulp of seeds, fruits, tubers, roots and stems of plants, especially in corn, potatoes, wheat and rice?
questions.explanation: Amylum - A polymeric carbohydrate consisting of numerous glucose units joined by glycosidic bonds. Olestra (Olean) - Fat substitute that doesn't add any calories to products. Saponins - They are naturally occurring compounds that are widely distributed in all cells of legume plants. Xanthan (polysaccharide) produced from simple sugars using a fermentation process. Uses - common food additive, thickening agent, emulsifier, and stabiliser that prevents ingredients from separating.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Solanum lycopersicum L. is the scientific name of which of the following highly consumed vegetables?
questions.explanation: Tomato. Tomato is a major contributor of lycopene and is also a considerable source of vitamins K, A, C, fiber, and carbohydrates, besides some amounts of iron, potassium, phosphorus, and sulfur. Potato - Solanum tuberosum, Onion - Allium cepa, and Garlic - Allium sativum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the common name of Parthenium hysterophorus?
questions.explanation: Carrot Grass. This plant causes milk disease in livestock and is also responsible for respiratory malfunction in humans. Lemon grass - Cymbopogon, Lawn Grass - Poaceae, Horsetails - Equisetum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Oleo gum resin (Asafoetida) can be obtained from :

options.a: dried latex from the stem of ferula
options.b: dried latex from the roots of mango tree
options.c: dried latex from the banana leaves
options.d: dried latex from the tap root of ferula

questions.answer_text: dried latex from the tap root of ferula
questions.explanation: Oleo-gum-resin (Asafoetida) can be obtained from the exudates of the roots of the Iranian endemic medicinal plant, Ferula asafoetida. It has cytotoxic, antiulcer, anti-neoplasm, anti-cancer, and anti-oxidative effects.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about certain cnidarians: 1. Pennatula is a genus of sea pens, colonial marine cnidarians with a feather-like appearance. 2. Adamsia is a genus of soft corals, belonging to phylum Cnidaria. 3. Gorgonia is a genus of soft corals, while Obelia is a genus of colonial hydroids. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 3 only. Statement 2 Incorrect – Adamsia is not a coral; it is a genus of sea anemones.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match the following crops with their scientific names: A. Rice 1. Saccharum officinarum B. Cotton 2. Oryza sativa C. Potato 3. Gossypium hirsutum D. Sugarcane 4. Solanum tuberosum
questions.explanation: A–2, B–3, C–4, D–1. Rice is a staple carbohydrate food crop and main energy source. Cotton is a fiber crop used in textiles. Potatoes are a tuber crop and staple vegetable. Sugarcane is a cash crop, source of sugar, jaggery, and ethanol.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding vitamins: 1. Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin) plays a vital role in red blood cell formation, neurological function, and DNA synthesis. 2. Vitamin K (Phylloquinone) is mainly responsible for healthy skin and nerve functioning. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Vitamins (scientific name) and function : Vitamin K (Phylloquinone) - Clotting of blood. Vitamin B1 (Thiamin) - Growth and development. Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin) - Red cell production. Vitamin B3 (Niacin) - Healthy skin, digestion and nervous system. Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid) - Maintenance of ligaments, tendons. Vitamin E (Tocopherol) - Antioxidant, protects cells, good for skin, eyes & immunity. Vitamin D (Calciferol) - Formation of strong bones and teeth. Vitamin A (Retinol) - Keep eyes and skin healthy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If the Glycemic Index (GI) of a specific food is from 70 to 100, then the type of that food is :
questions.explanation: High-GI food causes a rapid increase in blood sugar levels after consumption. These foods are typically processed or refined carbohydrates, like white bread or sugary snacks. Foods with a GI of 55 or lower are classified as low-GI, and those with a GI between 56 and 69 are considered medium-GI.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following groups represents essential amino acids ?
questions.explanation: Histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine. Amino acids are molecules that join together to form proteins, which are the building blocks of life. When proteins are digested or broken down, they yield amino acids. Histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, and valine are classified as essential amino acids, as the body cannot produce them. Therefore, they must be obtained from food. Alanine, Glycine, Proline, Serine, Tyrosine = Non-essential/conditionally essential”.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which is the most important protein component in milk, both quantitatively and nutritionally, that accounts for about 80% of the total protein in bovine milk ?
questions.explanation: Casein. Casein is the major protein in bovine milk, accounting for nearly 80% of the total protein content. It exists in the form of micelles, which help in the transport of calcium and phosphate, making milk an excellent source of these minerals. The remaining proteins (about 20%) are whey proteins, mainly albumin and globulins, which play important roles in nutrition and immunity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which essential amino acid enhances calcium absorption and also plays an important role in the formation of collagen?
questions.explanation: Lysine is an essential amino acid that must be obtained from food sources like meat, fish, dairy, and eggs. Collagen contains hydroxylysine, derived from lysine. Amino acids are classified as acidic, basic, or neutral. L-arginine helps build proteins, histidine is essential for protein biosynthesis, and tyrosine is a non-essential amino acid found in proteins and freely in organisms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which non-essential amino acid is synthesised by the hydroxylation of phenylalanine in a reaction catalysed by phenylalanine hydroxylase ?
questions.explanation: Tyrosine. Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins. When proteins are broken down, amino acids are released. It facilitates various bodily functions such as: breaking down food, repairing tissues, and supporting overall growth and maintenance. Essential amino acids are: histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, and valine. Non-essential amino acids are: alanine, arginine, asparagine, aspartic acid, cysteine, glutamic acid, glutamine, glycine, proline, serine, and tyrosine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match the following vitamins with their scientific names: Vitamin Scientific Names 1. Vitamin A A. Thiamine 2. Vitamin B1 B. Retinol 3. Vitamin B6 C. Pyridoxine 4. Vitamin C D. Ascorbic acid
questions.explanation: 1-B, 2-A, 3-C, 4-D. List of all vitamins with their scientific names : Vitamin A - Retinol; Vitamin B1 - Thiamine; Vitamin B2 - Riboflavin; Vitamin B3 - Niacin (Nicotinic acid); Vitamin B5 - Pantothenic acid; Vitamin B6 - Pyridoxine; Vitamin B7 - Biotin; Vitamin B9 - Folic acid; Vitamin B12 - Cobalamin; Vitamin C - Ascorbic acid; Vitamin D - Calciferol; Vitamin E - Tocopherol; Vitamin K - Phylloquinone (Phytonadione).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which essential micronutrient plays a clear role in the synthesis, storage and secretion of insulin in the hexameric form as well as in the conformational integrity of insulin?
questions.explanation: Zinc. Micronutrients are vitamins and minerals needed by the body in very small amounts. Role of some micronutrients in our body : Fluoride inhibits the initiation and progression of dental caries (tooth decay) and stimulates new bone formation. Selenium (Se) plays a critical role in reproduction, thyroid hormone metabolism, DNA synthesis, and protection from oxidative damage and infection. Phosphorus is a component of bones, teeth, DNA, and RNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match the following food items with the major nutrient they are rich in: Food Item Nutrient 1. Eggs A. Carbohydrates 2. Spinach B. Iron 3. Rice C. Protein 4. Fish D.Omega-3 Fatty Acids
questions.explanation: 1-C, 2-B, 3-A, 4-D. Eggs are an excellent source of complete protein containing all essential amino acids, while spinach is packed with vitamins such as A, C, and K along with minerals like iron and magnesium. Rice serves as a primary source of carbohydrates that provide quick energy, and fish is rich in omega-3 fatty acids, which are highly beneficial for heart and brain health.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following was the first B vitamin discovered in 1897 that is essential in amino acid and carbohydrate metabolism and is active in energy production reactions ?
questions.explanation: Thiamine. Casimir Funk is considered as the 'Father of vitamin therapy'. Vitamin B : B1 (thiamin), B2 (riboflavin), B3 (niacin), B5 (pantothenic acid), B6 (pyridoxine), B7 (biotin), B9 (folic acid), B12 (cobalamin). Fat-soluble Vitamins : A, D, E, and K. Water-Soluble Vitamins - B and C.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the most important health benefit of Vitamin D ?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D (Calciferol) : Source - Oily fish, egg yolks, red meat, etc. Deficiency Diseases - Rickets. Symptoms - Weak and painful bones, Deformities in teeth, Pain in the bones.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement with regards to vitamins.

options.a: Plants can synthesise almost all vitamins.
options.c: Some bacteria in the gut do not produce vitamins.
options.d: Most of the vitamins cannot get synthesised in sufficient amounts in our body.

questions.answer_text: Some bacteria in the gut do not produce vitamins.
questions.explanation: Gut bacteria helps in supplying essential nutrients, synthesizing vitamin K, aiding in the digestion of cellulose. Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble and vitamins C and B (complex group vitamins) are water- soluble.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The food component present in sugar is :
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates. Sugar molecules found in foods and drinks. The body breaks down carbohydrates into glucose (main source of energy for the body). Source - Breads, beans, milk, popcorn, potatoes, cookies, spaghetti, soft drinks, corn, etc. Vitamins - Group of substances that are needed for normal cell function, growth, and development. Proteins are made up of amino acids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct match of column-A with column-B? Column-A (Nutrients) Column-B (Source) i. Protein rich food. a. Wheat ii. Fat rich food b. Lemon iii. Carbohydrate rich food c. Egg white iv. Vitamin C rich food d. Butter and cheese

options.a: i - c, ii - a, iii - b, iv - d
options.b: i - c, ii - d, iii - b, iv - a
options.c: i - c, ii - d, iii - a, iv - b
options.d: i - d, ii - c, iii - b, iv - a

questions.answer_text: i - c, ii - d, iii - a, iv - b
questions.explanation: i-c, ii-d, iii-a, iv-b. Protein-rich food - Egg white (c): Proteins are body-building nutrients, essential for growth and repair of tissues. Fat-rich food - Butter & cheese (d): Fats provide stored energy, insulation, and protection to the body. Carbohydrate-rich food - Wheat (a): Carbohydrates are the primary and quick source of energy for the body. Vitamin C-rich food - Lemon (b): Vitamin C boosts immunity, aids wound healing, maintains skin health, and prevents scurvy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the monomer unit of glycogen?
questions.explanation: Glucose (C6H12O6). Glycogen : The carbohydrates are stored in the animal body as glycogen. Also known as animal starch because its structure is similar to amylopectin and is rather more highly branched. It is present in the liver, muscles and brain. When the body needs glucose, enzymes break the glycogen down to glucose. Found in yeast and fungi. Fructose - It is a natural monosaccharide found in fruits, honey and vegetables.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding vitamins: 1. Vitamins A, D, E, and K are water-soluble and can be stored in the liver and fatty tissues. 2. Vitamins B-complex and C are fat-soluble and generally not stored in the body, hence require regular intake. 3. Vitamin E is lipophilic (fat-soluble) vitamin required for the protection of cell membranes and the formation of red blood cells (RBCs). Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 3 Only. Vitamins A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble and can be stored in the liver and fatty tissues. Vitamins B-complex and C are water-soluble and generally not stored in the body, hence require regular intake. Vitamin E is a fat-soluble vitamin that protects cell membranes from oxidative damage. Vitamin E also plays a role in the formation of red blood cells (RBCs).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which essential amino acid is necessary for the production of our brain’s chemical messengers including melatonin, dopamine, noradrenaline and thyroxine?
questions.explanation: Phenylalanine is an essential amino acid to make proteins and other vital molecules such as neurotransmitters and hormones. Leucine amino acids can be used by skeletal muscle to give energy during exercise. Tryptophan is an amino acid needed for normal growth in infants and for the production and maintenance of the body's proteins, muscles, enzymes, and neurotransmitters.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following vitamins helps to keep our skin and eyes healthy?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A.Vitamin A (Retinol). Function: Essential for healthy vision (especially night vision), maintains skin and mucous membranes, supports immune function, and plays a role in growth and development. Sources: Carrots, spinach, papaya, sweet potato, pumpkin, fish liver oil, milk, butter, and eggs. Deficiency Diseases: Night blindness (difficulty seeing in dim light), Xerophthalmia (dryness of cornea, which may lead to blindness), Irregular tooth growth and poor skin health. Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin stored in the liver.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of minerals – need is correct? I. Iron – formation of hemoglobin II. Sodium – proper functioning of thyroid
questions.explanation: Only I. Iodine is needed to make a hormone called thyroxine. Biological Importance of Sodium : For the generation of nerve impulses, For maintenance of electrolyte balance and fluid balance, For heart activities and certain metabolic functions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which among the following vitamins influences iron absorption?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C (Water soluble). Scientific name : Ascorbic acid (C6H8O6) or ascorbate. It acts as an antioxidant and helps wound healing. It also helps in the formation of collagen. It is used to purify water after it has been Iodine - treated.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about minerals : 1. Phosphorus, found in milk, seafood, nuts, and whole grains, supports bone health and body repair processes. 2. Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is abundantly present in milk along with minerals like calcium, magnesium, and potassium. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Phosphorus is essential for bones, teeth, and tissue repair. Milk contains calcium, magnesium, potassium, selenium, zinc — but Vitamin C is absent in milk.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following vitamins helps our body to use calcium for bones and teeth?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D (Calciferol) - It helps prevent Osteoporosis (a disease that thins and weakens the bones and makes them brittle and more likely to break). Source - Oily fish, egg yolks, red meat, etc.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Zinc (Zn): 1. Zinc is a micronutrient that plays a key role in cell division, wound healing, and fat metabolism. 2. Zinc is essential for the synthesis, storage, and secretion of insulin in its active form. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 2 only. Zinc is indeed required for insulin synthesis and secretion, but statement 1 is incorrect because zinc mainly helps in carbohydrate metabolism, not specifically fat metabolism. “Zinc deficiency leads to growth retardation, hair loss, impaired immunity, and delayed wound healing.”

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of 'mineral - source' is correct ? I. Vitamin A - Papaya II. Iron - Spinach
questions.explanation: Both I and II. Vitamin A - Milk, Eggs, Fish, Butter, Fortified Margarine, Cheese, Green & Yellow fruits and Vegetables, etc. Vitamin E - Meats, Poultry, Eggs, Vegetable oils, Nuts, Olives, Tomatoes, etc. Zinc - Liver, Eggs, Cereals and Seafood.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements : 1. In anaerobic respiration in human muscles, glucose is broken down into lactic acid, causing muscle cramps. 2. In yeast, anaerobic respiration of glucose produces ethanol and carbon dioxide. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Anaerobic respiration occurs in the absence of oxygen and releases less energy, producing lactic acid in animals or ethanol and carbon dioxide in microorganisms. Aerobic respiration occurs in the presence of oxygen and releases more energy (ATP) along with carbon dioxide and water as end products.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which among the following vitamins is known as Niacin ?
questions.explanation: Vitamin B3. Also known as Niacin (Nicotinic acid & Nicotinamide). Functions: Helps in metabolism of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins; important for healthy skin and nerves. Deficiency: Pellagra (symptoms – dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia, and if untreated, death). Sources: Meat, fish, peanuts, mushrooms, whole grains.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match the columns. Nutrients Examples a. Protein i. Calcium, Phosphorous b. Carbohydrate ii. Cholesterol c. Fat iii. Glucose d. Minerals iv. Myosin
questions.explanation: a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i. Protein - Myosin (iv): Structural & contractile protein found in muscles, important for movement. Carbohydrate - Glucose (iii): Simple sugar, primary energy source for the body. Fat - Cholesterol (ii): A sterol lipid, important for cell membranes and as a precursor of hormones. Minerals - Calcium & Phosphorus (i): Essential for bones, teeth, nerve function, and metabolism.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Nuts, vegetable oil and fish are rich sources of__________.
questions.explanation: Omega-3. Most common forms of carbohydrates are sugars, fibers and starches. Minerals which are essential for health : iron, calcium, magnesium, zinc, potassium etc.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which amino acid is essential for healthy skin and teeth, as it is a component of tooth enamel, collagen and elastin?
questions.explanation: Threonine used in the biosynthesis of proteins. Leucine is an essential amino acid for protein synthesis. Arginine is used for the treatment of heart and blood vessel conditions including congestive heart failure (CHF), chest pain, high blood pressure, etc. Phenylalanine is used for a disorder that causes white patches to develop on the skin (vitiligo).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match the following plant types with their correct descriptions: Plant Type Description 1. Heliophytes A. Plants adapted to survive in arid or desert-like conditions 2. Xerophytes B. Plants adapted to live in water or very wet conditions 3. Pteridophytes C. Plants with a vascular system that reproduce through spores 4. Hydrophytes D. Plants adapted to live under plenty of sunlight

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following causes enlargement and extension growth of cells ?
questions.explanation: Turgor pressure. Turgor pressure provides the mechanical force that stretches the cell wall, leading to cell enlargement and extension growth, especially in growing tissues. Pressure potential is controlled by solute potential (when solute potential decreases, pressure potential increases) and the opening and closing of stomata. Osmotic pressure is the minimum pressure which needs to be applied to a solution to prevent the inward flow of its pure solvent across a semipermeable membrane. Imbibition is a special type of diffusion that takes place when liquid is absorbed by solids-colloids causing an increase in volume.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about apples: 1. Apples are a good source of potassium (K), an essential nutrient that helps maintain fluid balance, nerve signals, and muscle contraction. 2. Apples also contain malic acid, a natural compound that contributes to their tart taste. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Potassium-rich fruits and vegetables : Bananas, oranges, cantaloupe, apricots, grapefruit (some dried fruits, such as prunes, raisins, and dates, are also high in potassium). Malic acid : Found primarily in apples. It is a dicarboxylic acid that is also present in grapes, wine and rhubarb.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify a carbohydrate but does not fit into the definition.
questions.explanation: Rhamnose (C6H12O5). Carbohydrates are primarily produced by plants and form a very large group of naturally occurring organic compounds. Some common examples of carbohydrates are cane sugar, glucose, starch, etc. Most of them have a general formula, Cx(H2O)y .

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which protein is found in grains?
questions.explanation: Gluten. Gluten is a storage protein found in grains like wheat, barley, and rye. It consists of gliadin and glutenin, which give dough its elasticity and strength. Note: Some individuals are intolerant to gluten (celiac disease). Other options: Gum proteins (plant exudates), Arginine (amino acid), Delta protein (not relevant).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Pro-vitamin A, also known as Beta-carotene, is a plant pigment that gives carrots their orange color. 2. Deficiency of Beta-carotene directly causes rickets in humans. Which of the statements given above is / are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Beta-carotene is the orange pigment and a precursor of Vitamin A. It is a pro-vitamin A or the anti-cancer compound Deficiency of Vitamin D (not Beta-carotene) causes rickets; deficiency of Vitamin A causes night blindness.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Compounds like gingerol, paradol, shogaols and zingerone are :

options.d: antimicrobial compounds found in citrus fruits

questions.explanation: Antimicrobial compounds found in ginger. Gingerol is derived from ginger (Zingiber officinale Roscoe), which also belongs to the Zingiberaceae family. Ginger has multiple bioactive constituents including gingerols, shogaols, zingerone, paradol and gingerdiol. Gingerols possess an alkyl moiety which imparts anti-oxidative potential to it.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which natural bioactive water - soluble phenolic compound is present in Fruits, vegetables and grains with red, purple, blue or black hues ?
questions.explanation: Anthocyanin (Pigment found in plants). They’re part of a larger category of plant-based chemicals called flavonoids. Foods with high anthocyanin : Fruits - Pomegranates, Black plums, Cherries, black and red grapes etc; Vegetables - Red cabbage, Red onions, Purple corn etc; Legumes and Rice - Black rice, Black beans etc. Coumarins - colourless crystalline solid, sweet odor, bitter taste. Quercetin - bitter flavor, used in dietary supplements, beverages and foods. Naringenin - Anti-obesity, anti-diabetic flavonoid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following grains contain oryzenin ?
questions.explanation: Rice - A source of protein and contains various vitamins, such as thiamin and niacin, and minerals, such as zinc and phosphorus. Oryzenin - A rice glutelin, is an important constituent of rice protein. Glutelin comprises the major protein fraction of the rice grain and constitutes up to 80% of the total protein. Wheat contains protein, B vitamins, dietary fiber, and phytochemicals. Soyabean is high in protein and contains vitamin K1, folate, copper, manganese, phosphorus, and thiamine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about guard cells : 1. When water flows into guard cells, they become turgid, causing the stomatal pore to close. 2. Loss of water from guard cells leads to the opening of stomatal pores and allowing gas exchange. 3. The opening and closing of stomata help regulate transpiration and control the exchange of gases in plants. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 3 only. When water flows into guard cells, they become turgid, causing the stomatal pore to open and allowing gas exchange. Guard cells are kidney-shaped epidermal cells that contain chloroplasts, unlike most other epidermal cells. Loss of water from guard cells makes them flaccid, which leads to the closing of stomatal pores.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about garlic : 1. Garlic is a good source of the essential micronutrients manganese (Mn) and selenium (Se), which play an important role in cell metabolism. 2. The characteristic odour of garlic is due to the presence of Potassium compounds. Which of the above statements is/are incorrect?
questions.explanation: 2 only. The characteristic odour of garlic is due to the presence of Sulphur compounds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The leaves have a green pigment called ____________, which helps leaves to capture the energy from the sunlight.
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll - Element present in chlorophyll is magnesium. Cytoplasm - The fluid inside the cell. It functions as a cellular metabolism, transport, and storage medium while providing structural support and facilitating signal transduction within the cell. Cladophyll - Shoot system in which leaves do not develop. Xanthophylls are yellow pigments that are one of the important divisions of the carotenoid group.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about vascular tissues in plants : 1. Phloem is responsible for the unidirectional transport of water and minerals from the roots to the stems and leaves. 2. Xylem is responsible for the bidirectional transport of food materials prepared in the leaves to other parts of the plant. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Neither 1 nor 2. Xylem is responsible for the unidirectional transport of water and minerals from the roots to the stems and leaves. Phloem is responsible for the bidirectional transport of food materials prepared in the leaves to other parts of the plant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Plants require nutrients for their growth which can be supplied through _______ .
questions.explanation: Soil, water and air. Three elements (carbon, oxygen and hydrogen) are essential to plant growth. Soil - Supplies not only minerals but also harbours nitrogen - fixing bacteria, and other microbes, holds water, supplies air to the roots and acts as a matrix that stabilises the plant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of plastids–stored material is NOT correct? I. Amyloplasts – Starch II. Aleuroplasts – Carbohydrates III. Elaioplasts – Oils and fats
questions.explanation: Only II. Aleuroplasts: Store proteins, not carbohydrates .

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Water comes out of the leaves in the form of vapour by a process called ______.
questions.explanation: Transpiration. Three types of Transpiration : Stomatal transpiration - Evaporation of water through stomata. Lenticular Transpiration - Evaporation of water through lenticels (small minute openings present on the stem), Cuticular Transpiration - Loss of water from the cuticle (waxy layer on the surface of leaves).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about chloroplasts : 1. Chlorophyll pigments are arranged on the thylakoid membranes, which are the actual sites of light reactions of photosynthesis. 2. The stroma of the chloroplast mainly contains enzymes for the dark reaction (Calvin cycle), while grana are stacks of thylakoids. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Chlorophyll & Light Reaction: Chlorophyll pigments are embedded in thylakoid membranes, which are the actual sites of the light-dependent reactions (splitting of water, release of oxygen, ATP & NADPH formation). Stroma & Dark Reaction: The stroma contains enzymes for the Calvin cycle (dark reaction), where CO₂ is fixed into glucose using ATP & NADPH. Grana: Stacks of thylakoids that maximize surface area for capturing sunlight.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem capture about _______ percent of the energy of sunlight that falls on their leaves and convert it into food energy.
questions.explanation: 1. Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants produce carbohydrates by absorbing carbon dioxide, water, and sunlight in the presence of chlorophyll and liberating chemical energy. This energy is converted into chemical energy as food.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which nutrient is chlorella rich in ?
questions.explanation: Protein. Chlorella is known as space alga. It is used for the consumption of carbon dioxide provided by the astronauts and the production of oxygen in the spacecraft.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about modes of nutrition: 1. In autotrophic nutrition, organisms prepare their own food from simple substances like CO₂ and water, usually with the help of sunlight. 2. In heterotrophic nutrition, organisms depend on plants or other organisms for food and cannot prepare it themselves. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Autotrophic nutrition is the mode in which organisms prepare their own food from simple substances like carbon dioxide and water, generally using sunlight; examples include green plants, algae, and some bacteria. Heterotrophic nutrition is when organisms depend on other plants or animals for food, such as humans, animals, and the parasitic plant Cuscuta (Amarbel). Saprotrophic nutrition is found in organisms that absorb nutrients from dead and decaying organic matter, like fungi, yeast, and several bacteria. Phototrophic nutrition is the type in which organisms use light energy to prepare food, as seen in green plants and blue-green algae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Iron, Iodine and Zinc can be considered as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Micronutrients: Nutrients required in very small amounts, but essential for normal growth, immunity, and development. Examples: Micronutrient minerals (trace elements): Iron, Iodine, Zinc, Copper, Fluoride, Manganese. Micronutrient vitamins: Vitamin A, B-complex, C, D, E, K. Macronutrients: Needed in larger amounts (Carbohydrates, Proteins, Fats, Water, and major minerals like Calcium, Magnesium, Potassium). Non-essential nutrients: Produced in the body (Alanine, Asparagine, Aspartic acid).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How is food stored in brown algae?

options.b: In the form of complex carbohydrates that may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol.
options.c: In the form of complex lipids
options.d: In the form of oil droplets

questions.answer_text: In the form of complex carbohydrates that may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol.
questions.explanation: Brown algae store their food primarily in the form of complex carbohydrates. The two main storage forms are laminarin (a polysaccharide) and mannitol (a sugar alcohol). These compounds serve as energy reserves for the algae and are utilized during periods of low light or other environmental stress.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following does NOT figure among the main functions of the root system of a plant ?

options.a: Supply of food to plant parts
options.b: Providing a proper anchorage to the plant parts
options.c: Absorption of water from the soil
options.d: Absorption of minerals from the soil

questions.answer_text: Supply of food to plant parts
questions.explanation: Supply of food to the plant parts. The main function of the root system is to transport water and minerals to the plant. Food is transported by phloem tissue in the vascular system of plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following plant hormones regulates growth, particularly by stimulating cell elongation in stems?
questions.explanation: Auxin. Ethylene is the only plant hormone in gaseous form that regulates fruit ripening in plants. Cytokinin promotes cell division in plant roots and shoots. Gibberellin regulates various developmental processes, including germination, dormancy, flowering, flower development, and leaf and fruit senescence.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the parts of a leaf : 1. The broad, green, flat portion of the leaf that helps in photosynthesis is called the Petiole. 2. The central prominent vein of the lamina is known as the midrib. 3. The stalk that attaches the lamina to the stem is called the lamina. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.explanation: 2 only. The broad, green, flat portion of the leaf that helps in photosynthesis is called the lamina. The stalk that attaches the lamina to the stem is called the petiole.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following foods generally increase blood pressure?

options.b: Food high in salt, sugar and saturated or trans fats
options.c: Food with low salt and low sugar

questions.answer_text: Food high in salt, sugar and saturated or trans fats
questions.explanation: Food high in salt, sugar, and saturated or trans fats. Reason: These foods cause fluid retention, increase arterial stiffness, and put extra workload on the heart, leading to hypertension. Examples: Packaged snacks, fried foods, pickles, sugary beverages, bakery items, fast food. Hypertension (High BP): Normal BP = 120/80 mmHg. Hypertension = ≥140/90 mmHg (persistent). Complications: Can lead to heart disease, kidney damage, stroke, and brain disorders. Healthy alternatives: High-fibre, low-salt, potassium-rich foods (fruits, vegetables, whole grains) help lower BP.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the below is a psychological disorder of refusal to eat food, caused by under- nutrition?
questions.explanation: Anorexia Nervosa. Anorexia Nervosa is classified as a psychological eating disorder, while Kwashiorkor and Marasmus are nutritional deficiency disorders. Kwashiorkor is a nutritional syndrome caused by protein deficiency in the diet, meaning 'the disease of the displaced child'. Marasmus, or 'wasting,' is a form of severe malnutrition that results from a lack of protein and calories. Bulimia nervosa is a serious emotional eating disorder that involves eating excessive amounts of food in a short period (binging) followed by guilt and shame leading to self-induced vomiting, extreme exercise, or laxative abuse (purging).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match the points under Column A with those under Column B. Column A (Disease) Column B (Organism Responsible) i. Malaria a. Vibrio ii. Diarrhoea b. Salmonella iii. Typhoid c. Rotavirus iv. Cholera d. Plasmodium

options.a: i - b, ii - a, iii - c, iv - d
options.b: i - d, ii - c, iii - b, iv - a
options.c: i - a, ii - c, iii - b, iv - d
options.d: i - a, ii - b, iii - c, iv - d

questions.answer_text: i - d, ii - c, iii - b, iv - a
questions.explanation: i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a. Malaria is a disease caused by a parasite. The parasite is spread to humans through the bites of infected mosquitoes. Typhoid is a bacterial disease that spreads through contaminated food and water. The cholera- causing microbes will enter a healthy person through the water they drink and cause disease in them. Diarrhoea is the abnormal frequency of bowel movement and increased liquidity of the faecal discharge. It reduces the absorption of food.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which condition, also known as icterus, causes a yellowing of your skin and the whites of your eyes?
questions.explanation: Jaundice. This yellowing occurs due to high levels of bilirubin in the blood. Bilirubin is a yellow pigment produced during the normal breakdown of red blood cells. Ichthyosis is a group of genetic skin disorders that cause dry, scaly, thickened skin. Eczema is a common skin condition that causes itchiness, rashes, dry patches, and infection. Pemphigus is a rare group of autoimmune diseases that cause blisters on the skin and mucous membranes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match the columns. Column-A (Disorder) Column-B (Hormone/Gland) i. Addison's disease a. Adrenal gland ii. Hashimoto's disease b. Thyroid gland iii. Acromegaly c.Growth hormone iv. SIADH d. Vasopressin
questions.explanation: i-a, ii-b, iii-c, iv-d. Addison’s disease → failure of adrenal cortex → deficiency of cortisol & aldosterone → adrenal gland. Hashimoto’s disease → autoimmune destruction of the thyroid gland → hypothyroidism. Acromegaly → due to excess secretion of growth hormone (GH) by the anterior pituitary after puberty. SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH secretion) → excess secretion of vasopressin (ADH) → causes water retention & hyponatremia.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What are the five Fs of indirect transmission?

options.a: Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fluid
options.b: Fruit, fingers, flu, food and fluid
options.c: Flies, fingers, friends, food and fruit
options.d: Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fruit

questions.answer_text: Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fluid
questions.explanation: Indirect transmission of communicable diseases occurs through various means, commonly referred to as the "5Fs" : flies, fingers, fomites (objects like towels and handkerchiefs that can carry infections), food, and fluids. Some diseases can spread through contaminated water, food, ice, blood, and even body tissues or organs. Examples of such diseases include typhoid, diarrhea, polio, intestinal parasites, and infective hepatitis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding COVID-19: 1. COVID-19 is a zoonotic disease, which can spread from animals to humans. 2. Cholera and Typhoid are also examples of zoonotic diseases. Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Zoonotic disease spreads between animals and humans. COVID-19 (caused by SARS-CoV-2) is zoonotic in origin. Cholera and Typhoid are waterborne and foodborne diseases, not zoonotic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following plants is used to cure cold and cough ?
questions.explanation: Tulsi (Ocimum sanctum). It is an herb commonly used in Ayurvedic medicine to treat various ailments, including respiratory issues (bronchitis, asthma), fever, sore throat, and infections. Babool (Acacia nilotica) is utilized for skin conditions (wounds, eczema), digestive issues, and oral health. Jamun (Syzygium cumini) is beneficial for diabetes management, digestive issues, and possesses antioxidant properties. Arjun (Terminalia arjuna) is used to promote cardiovascular health, address heart conditions, and provide anti-inflammatory benefits.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Kwashiorkor occurs due to deficiency of both protein and calories, leading to severe wasting of body tissues. 2. Marasmus occurs mainly due to protein deficiency, often causing edema (swelling) in children. Which of the above statement(s) is/are incorrect?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Marasmus occurs due to deficiency of both protein and calories, leading to severe wasting of body tissues. Kwashiorkor occurs mainly due to protein deficiency, often causing edema (swelling) in children.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Name a common electrolyte disorder that occurs when the amount of sodium in your blood becomes abnormally low.
questions.explanation: Hyponatremia : It is a common electrolyte disorder characterized by an abnormally low concentration of sodium ions (Na+ ) in the blood, typically less than 135 mmol/L. Hyperkalemia : Elevated potassium levels in the blood. Hypokalemia : Low potassium levels in the blood. Hypernatremia : Elevated sodium levels in the blood.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which set of diseases are caused by bacteria?
questions.explanation: Typhoid, Cholera, Tuberculosis. Typhoid fever is caused by the bacteria Salmonella Typhi. Cholera is caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae. Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by a bacterium (or germ) called Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Viral Disease : Common cold (rhinovirus), Influenza (Influenza), HIV infection (human immunodeficiency virus), Dengue (transmitted by the bite of an infected mosquito, and is spread by the Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus species).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the other name of tetanus caused by toxin producing bacteria called clostridium tetani ?
questions.explanation: Lock jaw. Tetanus, also called lockjaw, is a bacterial infection that causes our neck and jaw muscles to lock up. It occurs when a bacteria found in the environment called Clostridium tetani enter our body through a break in our skin. Other dangerous bacterial diseases include cholera, meningitis, tuberculosis (TB), and Lyme disease.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the name of the inflammatory condition that causes cracks, crusting and scaling at the corners of the mouth due to vitamin B2 deficiency ?
questions.explanation: Cheilosis also known as angular cheilitis or perleche. Psoriasis is a chronic proliferative and inflammatory condition of skin. It is characterized by erythematous plaques covered with silvery scales. Atopic dermatitis (eczema) is a condition that causes dry, itchy and inflamed skin. Hives (urticaria) is a skin reaction that causes itchy welts. Chronic hives are welts that last for more than six weeks and return often over months or years.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the correct option about Kwashiorkor. Statement A : It is a form of malnutrition caused by a lack of fat in the diet. Statement B : Children who develop Kwashiorkor may not grow or develop properly and may remain stunted for the rest of their lives.

options.b: Both statements A and B are correct
options.c: Both statements A and B are incorrect

questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor is caused by deficiency of protein in the diet which causes fluid retention and a swollen, distended abdomen, and most commonly affected babies between 1-3 years of age, particularly in developing countries with high levels of poverty and food insecurity. In 1933, Cicely Williams was the first in Africa who described Kwashiorkor.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a mutation - based disease ?
questions.explanation: Malaria is an infectious disease caused by a parasite. Down syndrome : It is caused by a chromosomal mutation, specifically trisomy 21, where an individual has an extra copy of chromosome 21. Sickle cell anemia: It is caused by the hemoglobin-β gene.
