Oedogonium : Green algae, found in freshwater ponds, streams, and even in some terrestrial environments with high humidity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following cells are found in the liver of mammals?
questions.explanation: Kupffer cells. They are resident liver macrophages and maintain liver functions. They are the first innate immune cells and protect the liver from bacterial infections. Purkinje cells - They are a unique type of neuron, specific to the cerebellar cortex. Microglia cells are resident cells of the brain that regulate brain development, maintenance of neuronal networks, and injury repair. Sensory cells - They occur in specialized organs such as the eyes, ears, nose, and mouth, as well as internal organs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a plant, ______ is present in the middle lamella, primary cell and secondary walls and accumulates in the initial stages of development during cell expansion.
questions.explanation: Pectin (polysaccharide) - A soluble fibre found in fruits. Chitin - A long chain polymer of N -acetylglucosamine, an amide derivative of glucose, forms a long chain polymer. Present in cell walls and septa of all pathogenic fungi and cyst walls of pathogenic amoebae. Gelatin - A food ingredient found in soups, broths, sauces, gummy candies, marshmallows, cosmetics, and medications. Alginate - Naturally occurring anionic polymer typically obtained from brown seaweed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The main function of centriole is :

options.a: to maintain mineral composition in bacterial cell
options.b: to help plant cell for multiplication
options.c: to help cell division in animal cell
options.d: to maintain rigidity in plant cell

questions.answer_text: to help cell division in animal cell
questions.explanation: Centrosome - An organelle containing two cylindrical structures called centrioles. Centrioles form the basal body of cilia or flagella, and spindle fibres that give rise to spindle apparatus during cell division in animal cells. It plays a role in organizing microtubules that serve as the cell's skeletal system. They help determine the locations of the nucleus and other organelles within the cell.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which form of leucoplast specialises in oil synthesis and storage and is mainly found in the layer of cells in pollen grains that develop pollen grains?
questions.explanation: Elaioplasts - These are plastids that are specialized in oil synthesis and found primarily in the layer of cells. Gerontoplasts - Type of plastid formed during leaf senescence (deterioration with age), Derived from - Chloroplasts. Proteinoplasts are specialized organelles found in plant cells. Chloroplasts are organelle that contains the photosynthetic pigment chlorophyll that captures sunlight and converts it into useful energy, Found in green plants and algae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which cells, also called neurilemma cells, are the main glial cells in the PNS and play an essential role in the survival and functions of neurons?
questions.explanation: Schwann cells. Peripheral Nervous System - Part of your nervous system that lies outside the brain and spinal cord. Central nervous system - Includes two organs, the brain and spinal cord. Bipolar cells - One of the main retinal interneurons that provide the main pathways from photoreceptors to ganglion cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which component of the cell contains the hereditary material of the cell, the DNA ?
questions.explanation: Nucleus (Discovered by Robert Brown) - It is a membrane - bound organelle found in eukaryotic cells. It contains the cell's genetic material, including DNA, which carries the instructions for cell function and inheritance. Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) - Discovered by James Watson and Francis Crick.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cells were first observed in cork by __________ in 1665.
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke. Edward Jenner - Discovered the smallpox vaccine in 1796. Theophrastus - The father of botany. Anton van Leeuwenhoek (Father of Microbiology) - He discovered protists and bacteria.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the jelly-like substance between the nucleus and the cell membrane called?
questions.explanation: Cytoplasm. It is the main area for all the activities taking place inside a cell. It is made of water, salts and proteins. Plasma is the fluid that makes up the blood and other bodily fluids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which component of the cell organelles principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered either to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cell?
questions.explanation: Golgi Apparatus (Golgi complex or Golgi body).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the major function of a cell wall?

options.a: It works as a storage for material
options.b: It provides shape and rigidity to the cell
options.c: It is responsible for cell division
options.d: It helps in synthesis of carbohydrate

questions.answer_text: It provides shape and rigidity to the cell
questions.explanation: The cell wall in plants is composed mainly of cellulose and contains three layers in many plants. The three layers are the middle lamella, primary cell wall, and secondary cell wall. It is only found in Plant Cell.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: At high doses, ________ kills cancer cells or slows their growth by damaging their DNA. Cancer cells whose DNA is damaged beyond repair, stop dividing or die. When the damaged cells die, they are broken down and removed by the body.
questions.explanation: Radiation therapy. The X-ray generating methodology is applied to cancer therapy. X-rays discovered in 1895 by W. C. Roentgen. Types of radiation therapy: 1. External beam radiation therapy comes from a machine to deliver radiation. 2. Internal radiation therapy uses implants or drugs to deliver radiation inside the body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: ________ is the chemical process in which different types of chemical reactions are involved in controlling the living state of the cells in an organism.
questions.explanation: Metabolism. The circulatory system is the “transportation system” for the body, and blood serves as the transport vehicle. Respiration - Process in which organisms exchange gases between their body cells and the environment. Excretion - Process by which animals rid themselves of waste products and of the nitrogenous by-products of metabolism.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Golgi apparatus, the maturing face is:
questions.explanation: Concave. The Golgi cisternae are concentrically arranged near the nucleus with distinct convex cis or the forming face and concave, trans or the maturing face. The Golgi apparatus (discovered by Camillo Golgi in 1898) is located close to the nucleus and can be very large in secretory cells, where it fills almost the complete cytoplasm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECT regarding the grade of organisation and its example ?
questions.explanation: Euplectella, is a genus of glass sponges which includes the well-known Venus' Flower Basket, exhibits a cellular grade of organization rather than a tissue-organ grade. A cellular grade of organisation is an aggregation of cells that are functionally differentiated.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the outermost layer found in the cell envelope of the bacterial cell called?
questions.explanation: Glycocalyx. It is a network of polysaccharides attached to the cell wall.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify an option that does NOT represent prokaryotic cells.
questions.explanation: Sperm. Prokaryotic cells - Do not have a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles - single - celled microorganisms. Examples - Bacteria and Archaea, Mycoplasma (Pleuropneumonia-like organism, a genus of bacteria), Blue-green algae (cyanobacteria).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A group of ribosomes attached to mRNA is known as __________.
questions.explanation: Polysomes. They include a piece of the genetic code that is translated by each ribosome and are employed in the synthesis of numerous copies of the same polypeptide. Polypeptide - short chains of amino acids linked by peptide bonds. Long chains of amino acids are called proteins. Polymer - materials made of long, repeating chains of molecules. Monomer - A molecule that forms the basic unit for polymers. Example - Sugar is a monomer of polymers like glycogen, starch, and cellulose.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match Column-A with Column-B Column-A Column-B i. Gl a. Cell synthesises a complete copy of the DNA ii. S b. First gap phase, the cell grows physically larger iii. G2 c. Cell begins to reorganise its contents in preparation for mitosis iv. M d. Cell divides its copied DNA and cytoplasm to make two new cells
questions.explanation: i-b, ii-a, iii-c, iv-d.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An undifferentiated layer, _________is present in between the ectoderm and the endoderm.
questions.explanation: Mesoglea. Coelenterata and Ctenophora show the scattered pouches in between ectoderm and endoderm. Animals in which the body cavity is absent are called acoelomates, such as Platyhelminthes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What happens to the decomposition rate when detritus is rich in lignin and chitin ?
questions.explanation: It is slower. Decomposition is faster if nitrogen and water soluble substances are present.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the function of plasmid DNA.

options.a: None of the given options are correct
options.c: To confer certain unique phenotypic characters to bacteria
options.d: To help in the formation of rRNA

questions.answer_text: To confer certain unique phenotypic characters to bacteria
questions.explanation: A plasmid is a small, circular, double-stranded DNA molecule that is distinct from a cell's chromosomal DNA. Plasmids naturally exist in bacterial cells, and they also occur in some eukaryotes. Often, the genes carried in plasmids provide bacteria with genetic advantages, such as antibiotic resistance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about plant tissues: 1. Meristematic tissue consists of actively dividing cells responsible for plant growth. 2. Permanent tissue consists of matured cells that have lost the ability to divide and perform specific functions. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Meristematic tissues include apical, intercalary, and lateral meristems that help in primary and secondary growth. Permanent tissues include simple tissues (parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma) and complex tissues (xylem and phloem) performing specific functions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cells of meristematic tissue lack ________.
questions.explanation: Vacuoles. They are dividing rigorously so they need not store food or waste products.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of chromosome, on the basis of the location of the centromere?
questions.explanation: Lophocentric. Chromosomes are bundles of tightly coiled DNA located within the nucleus of almost every cell in our body. Depending on the position of the centromere, chromosomes are categorized into the following types: Metacentric, Telocentric, Acrocentric, Submetacentric.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which thin flexible barrier separates the internal environment of the cell from the extracellular fluid?
questions.explanation: Plasma Membrane consists of both lipids and proteins and provides protection for a cell. Lipids are fatty, wax-like molecules found in the human body and other organisms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about plant tissues: 1. Phloem is a complex permanent tissue responsible for transporting water and minerals in plants. 2. Parenchyma is a simple permanent tissue that provides mechanical support to growing parts of the plant. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Neither 1 nor 2. Xylem is a complex permanent tissue consisting of tracheids, vessels, xylem fibers, and xylem parenchyma. Collenchyma is a simple permanent tissue that supports young stems and leaves.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following cell organelles functions both as a passageway for intracellular transport and as a manufacturing surface?
questions.explanation: Endoplasmic Reticulum is a major site of protein synthesis and transport, protein folding, lipid and steroid synthesis, carbohydrate metabolism and calcium storage. Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) are of two types : Smooth ER and Rough ER. Function of lysosomes (digestion and removal of waste).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In plant cell, ______ are primarily organelles in which materials such as starch, oils and protein granules are stored.
questions.explanation: Leucoplasts. The basic function of it is the storage of essential compounds such as starch, lipids, and proteins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What are the projections of varying lengths protruding out of an amoeba’s body, which can appear and disappear, known as?
questions.explanation: Pseudopodia are called the false feet as they are actually extensions of the cytoplasm or the thick liquid that is inside organisms like an Amoeba. The function of the contractile vacuole is to pump water out of the cell through a process called osmoregulation, the regulation of osmotic pressure. Paramecium is a genus of unicellular ciliated protozoa, commonly studied as a representative of the ciliate group.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: ______ is known as the energy currency of the cell.
questions.explanation: ATP (Adenosine triphosphate) is the source of energy for use and storage at the cellular level and has three phosphates. ADP is adenosine diphosphate and contains only two phosphate groups. DNA, or deoxyribonucleic acid, is the hereditary material in humans and almost all other organisms. Ribonucleic acid (RNA) is a nucleic acid present in all living cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the nucleus of a cell: 1. Chromosomes and genes are located in the nucleus and carry hereditary information. 2. The nucleus controls the cell’s activities and contains nucleolus for ribosome synthesis. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Chromosomes and genes in the nucleus store genetic information. The nucleus regulates cellular functions and contains the nucleolus, which produces ribosomes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which cell theory proved that the quasi-fluid nature of lipids enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer?
questions.explanation: Fluid mosaic model describes the cell membrane as a tapestry of several types of molecules (phospholipids, cholesterols, and proteins) that are constantly moving. Cell theory states that the cell is the basic functional and structural unit of all living organisms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the correct statement.

options.a: Mitochondria and nucleus are found in bacteria.
options.b: Ribosomes, mitochondria and lysosomes are found in animal cells.
options.c: Chloroplast, ribosomes and nucleus are present in fungal cells.
options.d: Mitochondria and nucleus are absent in plant cells.

questions.answer_text: Ribosomes, mitochondria and lysosomes are found in animal cells.
questions.explanation: Bacteria do not have a nucleus or membrane-bound organelles. They have ribosomes. Fungal cells have ribosomes and a nucleus. They also have other organelles like endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondria, ribosomes, Golgi apparatus and vacuoles. Plant cells have ribosomes (Responsible for protein synthesis) mitochondria, nucleus, and chloroplasts (responsible for photosynthesis).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Under the electron microscope, which cell organelle is visible as either clusters or single, small dots that float freely in the cytoplasm?
questions.explanation: Ribosome. It is an intracellular structure made of both RNA and protein, and it is the site of protein synthesis in the cell. Vesicles can be used to move molecules, secrete substances, digest materials, or regulate the pressure in the cell.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Choose the correct sequence for central dogma.

options.a: Protein translation, DNA Replication, m-RNA transcription
options.b: DNA Replication, m-RNA transcription, Protein translation
options.c: m-RNA transcription, Protein translation, DNA Replication
options.d: m-RNA transcription, DNA Replication, Protein translation

questions.answer_text: DNA Replication, m-RNA transcription, Protein translation
questions.explanation: The 'Central Dogma' is the process by which the instructions in DNA are converted into a functional product. It was first proposed in 1958 by Francis Crick, discoverer of the structure of DNA. The central dogma of molecular biology: DNA → RNA → protein.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the cell that is amoeboid in shape.
questions.explanation: White Blood Cell. It is also known as leukocytes, are responsible for protecting your body from infection. The basic unit of communication in the nervous system is the nerve cell (neuron). Columnar epithelial cells are elongated and column-shaped and have a height of at least four times their width.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In cell biology, what is a large double-membraned organelle that is sometimes referred to as the ‘central unit’ of the cell because it contains the chromosomes that bear genetic material?
questions.explanation: Nucleus. Peroxisomes are organelles that sequester diverse oxidative reactions and play important roles in metabolism, reactive oxygen species detoxification, and signaling.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In animal cells, which membrane -bound cell organelles are generally smaller and help to separate waste products?
questions.explanation: Vacuole. Cytosol is known as the matrix of the cytoplasm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the component found only in a eukaryotic cell.
questions.explanation: Nuclear membrane. Ribosomes can be found in both prokaryote (bacteria) and eukaryote (animals and plants) cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which is the major microtubule - organising centre (MTOC) in eukaryotic cells involved in various cellular processes, including sensory reception, locomotion, and embryogenesis?
questions.explanation: Centrosome is a cellular structure involved in the process of cell division.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of active transport?
questions.explanation: Sodium-potassium pump present on the cell membrane, which transports 3 sodium ions outside and 2 potassium ions inside of the cell per ATP. Active transport (uphill transport) transports substances against the concentration gradient from lower to higher concentration. Passive transport (Glucose transporters) are a wide group of membrane proteins that facilitate the transport of glucose across the plasma membrane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about cell division: 1. Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells for growth and repair. 2. Meiosis produces gametes with half the number of chromosomes for sexual reproduction. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. There are 2 main types of cell division. Mitosis ensures identical daughter cells for growth, repair, and maintenance. Meiosis reduces chromosome number by half to produce gametes (sperm and egg) for sexual reproduction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which biological stain is used in histology and cytology to colour all cell nuclei red?
questions.explanation: Safranin. It is mostly utilized for the identification of cartilage, mucin, and mast cell granules. Cresol red is a triarylmethane dye, used as an acid-base indicator, or pH indicator.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding indicators: 1. Clove is an example of an olfactory indicator used in acid-base reactions. 2. Olfactory indicators are substances whose smell changes in acidic or basic solutions. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Clove, onion, and vanilla act as olfactory indicators. Olfactory indicators show acid-base changes by altering smell perception instead of color.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the main sense organ that virtual reality displays are aiming for
questions.explanation: Vision. Virtual reality (VR) aiming to create an immersive visual experience that simulates a virtual environment. While some VR systems may also incorporate audio and haptic feedback to engage the senses of hearing and touch, the main focus is on visual stimulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the shape of the eyeball ?
questions.explanation: Spherical. Parts of the human eye: Vitreous humour - This is a gel-like substance which maintains the shape of the eyeball. It is also a refractive media. Anterior chamber - It contains the iris and a fluid called the aqueous humour. Pupil - It is an aperture of variable size in the centre of the iris, which regulates the amount of light entering the eyeball. Retina - It is a transparent layer forming the inner coat of the eye, it supports the choroid layer.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which type of muscles do the uterus, iris of the eye, and bronchi contain?
questions.explanation: Smooth muscles (involuntary muscles) are found in various organs and tissues that require automatic contraction and relaxation. The uterus, iris of the eye, and bronchi all contain smooth muscles. Characteristics of smooth muscles : Involuntary (not under conscious control), Non-striated (no visible striations), Found in internal organs (hollow organs). Cardiac muscles: Found exclusively in the heart, these muscles pump blood.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What do you call the transparent front part of the eye?
questions.explanation: Cornea. It covers the pupil (the opening at the centre of the eye), iris (the coloured part of the eye), and the anterior chamber of the eye (the fluid-filled inside of the eye).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following body parts behaves like a stretched rubber sheet?
questions.explanation: Eardrum. The tympanic membrane (eardrum) which is a thin layer of tissue in the human ear that receives sound vibrations from the outer air and transmits them to the auditory ossicles, which are tiny bones in the tympanic (middle-ear) cavity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the human eye: 1. The retina controls the size of the pupil and regulates the amount of light entering the eye. 2. Vitreous humour is a gel-like substance that maintains the shape of the eyeball. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 2 only. Iris is the coloured part of the eye that adjusts the pupil size depending on light intensity. Vitreous humour provides structural support and refractive function to the eyeball.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: ______ are the vessels which carry blood away from the heart to various organs of the body.
questions.explanation: Arteries - They carry oxygenated blood, which is rich in nutrients and oxygen. The tracheas are the tubes that carry air from the throat to the lungs. They are made of cartilage and have smooth muscles in their walls.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding haemoglobin: 1. Haemoglobin is a protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen throughout the body. 2. Iron is an essential element required for the formation of haemoglobin. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Haemoglobin binds with oxygen and enables its transport to tissues and organs. Iron is the key component of haemoglobin; its deficiency leads to anaemia.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: _____ are the vessels which carry carbon dioxide - rich blood back to the heart.
questions.explanation: Veins - They carry deoxygenated blood (except pulmonary veins). Biggest vein - Vena Cava. Neurons : Fundamental unit of the nervous system specialized to transmit information to different parts of the body. Capillaries : They take waste products away from tissues.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The blood platelets are also known as .
questions.explanation: Thrombocytes. They are cell fragments found in blood and spleen produced from megakaryocytes (special cells in the bone marrow). It helps to form blood clots, prevent bleeding and wounds healing. Blood normally contains 150,000 to 450,000 platelets per microliter of blood. Thrombin - An enzyme that helps in regulating hemostasis and maintaining blood coagulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Muscles are of three types. Which of the following is NOT one of them ?
questions.explanation: Sesamoids. Muscles are tissues that can contract, and therefore they help in the movement of the other body parts. There are about 600 muscles in the human body. The three main types of muscle include skeletal (bones), smooth (organs) and cardiac (heart).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the pH of human blood ?
questions.explanation: 7.4. pH (Potential of Hydrogen) is really a measure of the relative amount of free hydrogen and hydroxyl ions in the water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Lymph is a light clear fluid made up of white blood cells that attack harmful ______ in the blood.
questions.explanation: Bacteria. The corpuscles found in the lymph are called lymphocytes. Diseases caused by Bacteria : Diphtheria, pneumonia, cholera, tetanus, tuberculosis, plague, and gonorrhea. Fungi : Ringworm and athlete's foot.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a large bean - shaped lymphoid organ in the human body ?
questions.explanation: Spleen stores erythrocytes, lymphocytes, and phagocytes. It filters the bloodstream by trapping blood-borne pathogens in its cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about blood pressure is correct?

options.a: The normal systolic pressure is about 80 mm of Hg and diastolic pressure is 120 mm of Hg.
options.b: The normal systolic pressure is about 72 mm of Hg and diastolic pressure is 35 mm of Hg.
options.c: The normal systolic pressure is about 160 mm of Hg and diastolic pressure is 80 mm of Hg.
options.d: The normal systolic pressure is about 120 mm of Hg and diastolic pressure is 80 mm of Hg.

questions.answer_text: The normal systolic pressure is about 120 mm of Hg and diastolic pressure is 80 mm of Hg.
questions.explanation: The maximum pressure at which the blood leaves the heart through the main artery (Aorta) during ventricular contraction is called systolic pressure. The minimum pressure in the arteries during ventricular relaxation of the heart is called the diastolic pressure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the heart of fishes: 1. Fishes have a two-chambered heart consisting of one atrium and one ventricle. 2. The fish heart pumps blood in a single circuit, from the heart → gills → body → back to the heart. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. A fish heart has 2 chambers (1 atrium + 1 ventricle). Blood passes only once through the heart in one complete circulation (single circulation).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Swollen bluish veins resulting from the valves that do not close properly are called ______.
questions.explanation: Varicose veins. These are abnormally dilated, tortuous superficial veins caused by incompetent venous valves. They almost always affect the legs and feet.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify a muscle responsible for the exit of waste material from the body.
questions.explanation: Sphincter. A muscular sphincter (gastro-oesophageal) regulates the opening of oesophagus into the stomach. The small intestine is distinguishable into three regions, a ‘C’ shaped duodenum, a long coiled middle portion jejunum and a highly coiled ileum. The opening of the stomach into the duodenum is guarded by the pyloric sphincter.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about urine colour: 1. Urobilin is the main pigment that gives urine its yellow colour. 2. Bilirubin is responsible for the yellow colour of urine under normal conditions. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only 1. Urobilin (urochrome) is the normal pigment. Bilirubin is not normally present in urine; its excess in blood causes jaundice.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which is a specialised excretory cell found in Platyhelminthes that acts like a kidney, removing waste material through filtration?
questions.explanation: Flame cell. Phylum Platyhelminthes - It belongs to the kingdom Animalia. The organisms are also known as flatworms. They are triploblastic, bilaterally symmetrical, dorsoventra, acoelomate flatworms with organ grade of construction without a definite anus, circulatory, skeletal or respiratory system but with Protonephridial excretory system and mesenchyme filling the space between the various organs of the body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about filtration of waste in humans: 1. The kidney is the main organ responsible for filtration of waste products from the blood. 2. The functional units of the kidney responsible for this filtration are called glomerulus. 3. Each kidney contains nearly one million nephrons, each consisting of a glomerulus and a renal tubule. Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 and 3 only. Nephrons are the structural and functional units of the kidney. Each kidney contains about 1 million nephrons. A nephron consists of two main parts : Glomerulus — a tuft of capillaries where blood filtration begins. Renal tubule — starts with Bowman’s capsule, which encloses the glomerulus, and continues into tubular structures that reabsorb useful substances and secrete wastes. Finally, urine formed in nephrons passes into collecting ducts and then to the ureter. Endocrine/Exocrine system

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the human body: 1. The hypothalamus is a type of exocrine gland. 2. It regulates body temperature, hunger, thirst, emotions, sleep-wake cycle, and sexual behaviour. 3. The pituitary gland controls growth and metabolism but does not directly regulate body temperature. Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: 2 and 3 only. The hypothalamus is a part of the brain (diencephalon) and a neuroendocrine center, not an exocrine gland. The hypothalamus regulates body temperature (thermoregulation), hunger, thirst, emotions, sleep–wake cycle (via circadian rhythms), and sexual behaviour. The pituitary gland secretes hormones affecting growth (GH) and metabolism (TSH → thyroid, ACTH → adrenal, etc.), but direct control of body temperature lies with the hypothalamus, not the pituitary.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is the largest gland in the human body?
questions.explanation: Liver. It is located in the upper right portion of the abdomen and is the only organ that has the ability to regenerate efficiently. Pancreas is a composite gland which acts as both exocrine and endocrine gland.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Proboscis gland for excretion is present in the phylum:
questions.explanation: Hemichordata. Examples - Balanoglossus, Saccoglossus, Protoglossus, Ptychodera.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which gland produces Cortisol often known as a 'stress hormone' in humans ?
questions.explanation: Adrenal gland. The thyroid gland uses iodine from food to make two thyroid hormones: triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: ______ glands release tears from our eyes.
questions.explanation: The lacrimal gland produces tears which are secreted by the lacrimal ducts, and flow over the ocular surface, and then into canals that connect to the lacrimal sac. From that sac, the tears drain through the lacrimal duct into the nose.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is a leaf-shaped flap of cartilage located behind the tongue, at the top of the larynx or voice box called?
questions.explanation: Epiglottis. Its main function is to seal off the windpipe during eating, so that food is not accidentally inhaled. The larynx is a cartilaginous skeleton, some ligaments, and muscles that move and stabilize it.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about human glands: 1. Enlargement of the thyroid gland causes goitre, leading to swelling in the front of the throat. 2. The adrenal gland is located on the anterior part of each kidney and secretes adrenaline and noradrenaline. 3. The pineal gland is located on the dorsal side of the forebrain and secretes melatonin. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2 and 3. Goitre is the abnormal enlargement of the thyroid gland, which lies in the front of the neck near the trachea. It usually occurs due to iodine deficiency, as iodine is essential for the synthesis of the hormone thyroxine. Other glands: Adrenal gland – located above kidneys; secretes adrenaline & noradrenaline (stress hormones). Pineal gland – located in the forebrain; secretes melatonin (regulates sleep cycle). Pituitary gland – called the “master gland”; controls other endocrine glands.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is correct regarding the respiration? 1. Regular traditional breathing exercise (pranayama) can increase the capacity of lungs to take in more air. 2. During inhalation, ribs move up and outwards and diaphragm moves down.
questions.explanation: Both I and II. The lungs and respiratory system allows us to breathe.They bring oxygen into our bodies (called inspiration, or inhalation) and send carbon dioxide out (called expiration, or exhalation). This exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide is called respiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In boys, the growing 'larynx' is visible as a distinct bulge at the front of the throat called _______.
questions.explanation: Kanthamani (Adam's apple). Gullet (esophagus) - it is part of the digestive system, which is sometimes called the gastro-intestinal tract (GI tract). The esophagus is a muscular tube. It connects the mouth to the stomach.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the percentage of carbon dioxide in the air exhaled by human lungs?
questions.explanation: 4.4%. Composition of exhaled air : nitrogen (78%) oxygen (17%) carbon dioxide (4%) other gases (1%). Inhaled air is by volume: 78% nitrogen, 20.95% oxygen and small amounts of other gases including argon, carbon dioxide, neon, helium, and hydrogen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the network of air tubes for gas exchange in insects ?
questions.explanation: Tracheae. Gills are evaginated respiratory surfaces used for breathing in water. The diaphragm, located below the lungs, is the major muscle of respiration. Spiracles are the small opening on the lateral side of the body through which air enters the tracheal system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Breakdown of pyruvate into lactic acid and energy in lack of oxygen takes place in: Statement 1: In yeast, anaerobic respiration converts pyruvate into lactic acid with limited energy release. Statement 2: In human muscle cells, anaerobic respiration produces alcohol and carbon dioxide instead of lactic acid. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Neither 1 nor 2. In human muscle cells, anaerobic respiration converts pyruvate into lactic acid with limited energy release. In yeast, anaerobic respiration produces alcohol and carbon dioxide instead of lactic acid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of calcium in our body?

options.a: It plays an important role in blood clotting.
options.c: It is associated with healthy bones and teeth

questions.explanation: Examples of digestive enzymes include amylase, gelatinase, lactase, lipase, maltase, peptidase, and protease.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: To get relief from constipation, which of the following is prescribed to be eaten in large amounts?
questions.explanation: Fibre is essential for maintaining healthy digestion. It adds bulk to the stool and helps it pass more easily through the intestines, thus providing relief from constipation. Foods high in fibre include fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and legumes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match the following enzymes with their functions in the human digestive system : Enzyme Function 1. Salivary amylase A. Breaks down proteins into peptides 2. Pepsin B. Breaks down starch into maltose 3. Lipase C. Breaks down fats into fatty acids and glycerol 4. Trypsi D. Breaks down peptides into smaller peptides in the small intestine

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which glands help in digestion in the stomach ?
questions.explanation: Gastric glands in the stomach lining secrete digestive juices, including hydrochloric acid (HCl) and pepsinogen, which help break down proteins and activate digestive enzymes. Pituitary gland : Regulates hormone secretion, growth, and development. Thyroid gland : Regulates metabolism, growth, and development. Pineal gland : Regulates sleep-wake cycles and melatonin production.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Grass-eating animals require a Shorter small intestine to digest cellulose. 2. Meat-eating animals usually have a longer small intestine because meat is difficult to digest. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Neither 1 nor 2. Grass-eating animals require a longer small intestine to digest cellulose. Meat-eating animals usually have a shorter small intestine because meat is easier to digest.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Liver gland secretes that are stored in a sac called the gallbladder.
questions.explanation: Bile juice - It is important for the total digestion of different types of fats (fats in food to fatty acids). It also helps in digesting carbohydrates and proteins to some extent. Estrogen - The female reproductive hormone secreted by the membranous granulosa of the Graafian follicle. Mucus - A protective substance that is secreted from multiple areas in the body such as the mouth, sinuses, throat, lungs, and stomach. Produced by the goblet cell of the gastrointestinal tract.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In humans, the digestion of carbohydrates like starch, begins in which of the following parts?
questions.explanation: Buccal cavity. Organs in the digestive system - mouth, pharynx (throat), oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, and anus. Rectum is the terminal part of the intestine from the sigmoid colon to the anus. The small intestine is the longest part of the digestive system. Oesophagus is a muscular tube, which connects the mouth to the stomach.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In ruminants like cattle, bacteria present in ______ helps in digestion of cellulose.
questions.explanation: Rumen is the first chamber of the stomach of ruminants like cattle. It is a large, muscular sac that is filled with bacteria, protozoa, and other microorganisms. These microorganisms help to digest the cellulose in the food that the ruminant eats.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following animals have a single opening in their digestive system that serves both as a mouth and an anus?
questions.explanation: Platyhelminthes. These are also known as flatworms belonging to Animalia Kingdom and they include many free-living and parasitic life forms. The term arachnid refers to a class of animals that includes spiders, scorpions, mites, and ticks.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is able to regenerate our digestive system with good microbes that will neutralize the harmful ones?
questions.explanation: Probiotics. Yogurt is one of the best sources of probiotics. Antibiotics are medicines that fight bacterial infections in people and animals. Prosthesis or a prosthetic implant, is an artificial device that replaces a missing body part, which may be lost through trauma, disease, or a condition present at birth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Where are villi present in the human alimentary canal?
questions.explanation: Small intestine - It receives secretions from the liver and the pancreas. Villi are small finger-like projections found inside the inner walls of the small intestine. They increase the surface area for absorption of nutrients from the food.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In human beings, the small intestine is coiled and is about ______ metres long.
questions.explanation: 7 to 7.5 (about 22 feet). The small intestine has three parts. The first part is called the duodenum. The jejunum is in the middle and the ileum is at the end. The large intestine includes the appendix, cecum, colon, and rectum. The large intestine is about five feet (or 1.5 metres) long.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the function of lipase in the process of digestion.
questions.explanation: Lipase is the enzyme that breaks down the lipids present in the form of emulsified fat and converts them into fatty acids and glycerol. Digestion of protein is done by several enzymes such as Pepsin, Trypsin, Chymotrypsin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which type of carbohydrate CANNOT be broken down by the GI tract, does not provide energy, but helps the body get rid of wastes and keeps the intestinal tract healthy?
questions.explanation: Fibre. It is a type of carbohydrate that the body can't digest. Glycogen is the storage form of carbohydrates in mammals. Simple Sugars, also called monosaccharides, include glucose, fructose, and galactose.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: ______, a fluid secreted by new mothers during the initial days of lactation, contains nutrients that boost a baby's immune system and helps fight infection.
questions.explanation: Colostrum is the first form of breastmilk that is released by the mammary glands after giving birth. Sebum is an oily, waxy substance produced by your body's sebaceous glands. Synovia is a lubricating fluid resembling the white of an egg, secreted by certain membranes, as those of the joints. Cerumen (Earwax), is a brown, orange, red, yellowish or grey waxy substance secreted in the ear canal of humans and other mammals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about the human digestive system: 1. The small intestine is the longest part of the alimentary canal and is responsible for nutrient absorption. 2. The large intestine is longer than the small intestine and mainly absorbs proteins. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. The small intestine (~20 feet) is the longest part and absorbs nutrients. The large intestine (~5 feet) is shorter and mainly absorbs water, not proteins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is the indigestible portion of our diet essential to the health of the digestive system?
questions.explanation: Roughage. It includes all plant products like grains, nuts, legumes, fruits, etc. They are indigestible but act as a source of food for the beneficial bacteria present in our gut. Consumption of roughage maintains body weight and also reduces risk factors of heart disease.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the type of cell that is long and branched.
questions.explanation: Nerve cell. The neural system of all animals is composed of highly specialized cells called - neurons which can detect, receive and transmit different kinds of stimuli. This system is divided into two parts - the Central Nervous System (CNS) and the Peripheral Nervous System (PNS). The CNS consists of the brain and spinal cord. The PNS consists mainly of nerves.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The sensation of feeling full is because of a centre associated with hunger, which is in a separate part of the ______ .
questions.explanation: Forebrain. The brain is the central information processing organ of our body. The brain can be divided into three major parts : Forebrain consists of Hypothalamus (regulation of sexual behaviour, expression of emotional reactions), Cerebrum (controls memory, will power, knowledge etc), Thalamus (controls pain, cold and Heat). Midbrain consists of Tectum (vision and auditory reflexes) and Hindbrain consists of Medulla oblongata (respiration, cardiovascular reflexes and gastric secretions), Pons (tract between brain and spinal cord) and Cerebellum (coordination of Movement, Posture etc).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the human brain: 1. The medulla maintains balance and coordination, enabling a person to walk in a straight line. 2. The cerebellum is mainly responsible for regulating involuntary functions like breathing and heart rate. Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Neither 1 nor 2. The cerebellum maintains balance and coordination, enabling a person to walk in a straight line. The medulla is mainly responsible for regulating involuntary functions like breathing and heart rate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Our brain mainly depends on which of the following foods?
questions.explanation: Only glucose. Glucose is a type of sugar which comes predominantly from starchy foods (bread, rice, pasta and potatoes) as well as fruits, juices, honey, jams and table sugar. The body tightly regulates blood glucose levels; this is known as glucose homeostasis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which part of the human body will you find the 'superior rectus' ?
questions.explanation: Eye. The superior rectus is a muscle in the eye that helps to elevate the eye. This muscle is among four muscles - including the medial rectus, lateral rectus, and inferior rectus, which control the eye’s movement.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How do the muscle cells help in movement ?

options.a: The thickness of the cell layer helps in movement.
options.b: The lining of the vessels inside help in movement.
options.c: The blood flow of the cells helps in movement.
options.d: The contraction and relaxation of these cells result in movement.

questions.answer_text: The contraction and relaxation of these cells result in movement.
questions.explanation: Muscle cells are specialized cells that can contract and relax. This ability is crucial for movement in the body. When muscle cells contract, they shorten, which pulls on the bones or other structures they are attached to, causing movement. When they relax, they lengthen and return to their original state. This cycle of contraction and relaxation is what allows for various movements, such as walking, lifting objects, or even the beating of the heart.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is a degenerative disorder of the brain and one of several conditions that cause dementia, a progressive decline of mental functions resulting in memory loss and confusion ?
questions.explanation: Alzheimer's Disease. Schizophrenia is a mental disorder that affects a person's thoughts, emotions, and behavior. Amnesia can be caused by brain injury, stroke, and Alzheimer's Disease. Concussion is a mild traumatic brain injury that can cause temporary symptoms such as headache, dizziness, and memory loss.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which among the following is a flat bone?
questions.explanation: Ribs are a set of twelve paired bones which form the protective 'cage' of the thorax. The ankle joint, also known as the talocrural joint, is a synovial joint that connects the bones of the leg, the fibula and tibia, with the talus of the foot. Pelvic Bone is a basin shaped complex bone which connects the trunk and legs and supports the urinary bladder. The wrist is formed where the two bones of the forearm, the radius and the ulna meet the carpus. Other bones of the hand - metacarpals and phalanges.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding human teeth: 1. Enamel is the largest dental tissue, forming the bulk of the tooth beneath the enamel. 2. Enamel is the hardest substance in the human body and covers the crown of the tooth. Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 2 only. Dentin is the largest dental tissue, not enamel. Dentin forms the bulk of the tooth beneath the enamel. Enamel is the hardest substance in the human body, covering the crown of the tooth and protecting the dentin underneath.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: ‘The fluid present between joints, that makes the movement of joints easy, is called :
questions.explanation: Synovial. It provides lubrication, reduces friction between bones and makes the joint movements smooth. Examples of such joints are ball and socket joint, pivot joint, gliding joint, hinge joint, and saddle joint.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following parts of the human body is the masseter muscle located ?
questions.explanation: Jaw. The muscle masseter is a facial muscle that plays a major role in the chewing of solid foods. The three layers of the masseter are the superficial layer, the intermediate layer, and the deep layer.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The human shoulder joint is an example of a ______ joint.
questions.explanation: Ball and socket joint. It is a synovial joint, which means it allows for smooth movements between bones.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The vertebrae are a part of which of the following body systems in humans
questions.explanation: Spinal cord. The spine is composed of 33 vertebrae, divided into five sections: the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine sections and the sacrum and coccyx bones.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding joints in the human body: 1. The head and neck are connected by a pivotal joint, which allows rotation. 2. Fixed joints are immovable joints where bones are fused, such as in the skull. Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How many bones are there in the human hand ?
questions.explanation: 27. The human hand has 27 bones : the carpals or wrist contains 8; the metacarpals or palm contains five; the remaining fourteen are digital bones; fingers and thumb.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Venus flytrap is a perennial carnivorous plant of the sundew family that traps insects and digests them with enzymes. 2. Bladderwort is also a carnivorous plant, but it is aquatic and uses bladder-like structures to trap prey. 3. Phytoplankton are autotrophic organisms that form the base of aquatic food chains. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2 and 3. Insectivorous plants are autotrophic plants (make their own food by photosynthesis) but grow in nitrogen-deficient soils (like marshy areas, bogs, swamps). To supplement their nitrogen requirement, they trap and digest insects with the help of digestive enzymes. Examples : Venus flytrap (Dionaea muscipula), Pitcher plant (Nepenthes), Sundew (Drosera), Bladderwort (Utricularia), and Aldrovanda (Waterwheel plant).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hubbardia heptaneuron, which has become endangered, is a species of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Grass. Hubbardia heptaneuron is nearing extinction due to its environmental insensitivity. Other endangered plant species include the Gran Canaria Drago Tree, Mandragora, Castela senticosa, Musli, and Assam Catkin. The IUCN's "Red Data Books" offer the most comprehensive global inventory of the conservation status of plant and animal species.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Taxus wallichiana Zucc (Himalayan yew) is a medicinal plant found in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Himachal Pradesh. The Himalayan yew grows in the high-altitude forests of the Western Himalayas, especially in the states of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and parts of Jammu & Kashmir.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the given statement(s) is/are correct? Statement 1: Monocot leaves have veins that run parallel from the base to the tip. Statement 2: Parallel venation causes vascular bundles in monocot leaves to be nearly equal in size.
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Monocot leaves exhibit parallel venation, where veins run from the base to the tip. This arrangement results in vascular bundles of nearly uniform size throughout the leaf.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The growth form of a plant, comprising its size, shape and orientation is known as :
questions.explanation: habit. The environment is the sum of all living and non-living things, and the forces that affect them, that surround a person, animal, or plant. A habitat is the natural home of an organism, such as a plant or animal. It provides the organism with food, water, shelter, and space to survive.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about pigments in plants: 1. The red colour of beetroot is due to Curcumin, a water-soluble pigment present in the cell vacuole. 2. Betanin is a yellow-orange pigment found in turmeric. Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Neither 1 nor 2. The red colour of beetroot is due to Betanin, a water-soluble pigment present in the cell vacuole. Curcumin is a yellow-orange pigment found in turmeric, while Lycopene is the red pigment in tomatoes and watermelon.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which marine carotenoid is abundant in brown seaweed, macroalgae and diatoms ?
questions.explanation: Fucoxanthin. It is an orange-colored pigment, along with chlorophylls a and c and β-carotene, present in Chromophyta, including brown seaweeds (Phaeophyceae) and diatoms (Bacillariophyta). Astaxanthin: It is a reddish pigment that belongs to a group of chemicals called carotenoids. Neoxanthin: It is a carotenoid and xanthophyll pigment found in plants, algae, and microorganisms. β-Cryptoxanthin, a carotenoid found in fruits and vegetables such as tangerines, red peppers, and pumpkin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following groups, are all plants monoecious ?
questions.explanation: Maize, Cucumber, Fig and Melon. Monoecious plants have both male and female reproductive parts in the same plant. Examples - cucurbits and coconuts, etc. Dioecious plants are referred to when the male and female reproductive organs are distinct. Examples - Cottonwood, plum pine, etc.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT related to reticulate venation ?
questions.explanation: Maize. Reticulate venation : Arrangement of veins in a leaf blade that resembles a net or web, present on both sides of the midrib. Examples of plants with reticulate venation include China rose, Tulsi, and Coriander. Parallel Venation: Arrangement of veins in a leaf blade that run parallel to each other. Plants with parallel venation include Maize, Grass, and Wheat.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match column A with column B. Column A (Type of algae) Column B (Proper Name) a. Blue-green algae i. Sargassum b. Red algae ii. Chlamydomonas c. Green algae iii. Rhodophyta d. Brown algae iv. Cyanobacteria
questions.explanation: a - iv, b - iii, c - ii, d - i.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is related to neem ?
questions.explanation: Pinnately. Compound leaves are classified into two types: pinnately and palmately compound leaves. In pinnately compound leaves, leaflets are arranged along a common axis called the rachis, as seen in neem. In palmately compound leaves, leaflets attach at a common point at the tip of the petiole, such as in silk cotton.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the above statements is/are correct? 1. Guttation results in the loss of water in vapour form, while transpiration results in loss of water in liquid form. 2. Hydathodes are involved in guttation, whereas stomata are mainly involved in transpiration.
questions.explanation: 2 only. Guttation is the loss of water in liquid form through special pores called hydathodes. It occurs at night or early morning, when soil is very moist and transpiration is low. Transpiration is the loss of water in vapour form mainly through stomata. It occurs mostly during the daytime when sunlight and temperature are high.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following plants do roots arise from parts of a plant other than the radicle ?
questions.explanation: Monstera. Three types of roots are found in Monstera deliciosa: aerial roots, aerial roots that have entered the soil (aerial-subterranean roots), and lateral roots that form on aerial-subterranean roots (lateral - subterranean roots). The three root types differed in anatomical development and in growth. It is an example of adventitious roots, which grow from parts of the plant other than the radicle. These roots can be aerial or underground and may develop from nodes (money plant, bamboo), stem cuttings (rose), branches (banyan), or the stem base (fibrous roots in monocots).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements: Statement I: Plants with green, tender stems are usually short and have few branches. Statement II: Creepers are plants with weak stems that cannot stand upright and spread on the ground.

options.a: Both Statement I and II are true, and II is the correct explanation of I
options.b: Both Statement I and II are true, but II is not the correct explanation of I
options.c: Statement I is true, Statement II is false
options.d: Statement I is false, Statement II is true

questions.answer_text: Both Statement I and II are true, but II is not the correct explanation of I
questions.explanation: Both Statement I and II are true, but II is not the correct explanation of I.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the root-like structure at the base of an algae (seaweed) that binds the algae to a hard substrate like a stone?
questions.explanation: Holdfast. Algae are a diverse group of photosynthetic, eukaryotic organisms, representing a polyphyletic grouping that includes species from various clades. The midrib, or midvein, is the central, thick vein running from the base to the tip of a leaf, providing support and structure. A stipe is the stalk or stem that supports a structure in plants, algae, or fungi. A frond refers to a large, divided leaf, typically associated with ferns and some palm trees, but can also denote the leaves of flowering plants like mimosa or sumac.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The structure that produces and holds sperm cells in bryophytes (non - vascular plants) and ferns is called :
questions.explanation: Antheridium - A saclike structure and male sex organ that produces and stores gametes or sex cells called sperm. They produce biflagellate antherozoids. Located on: A thin stalk attached to the gametophyte.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the association of Anabaena with Azolla: 1. Anabaena fixes atmospheric nitrogen while living in the leaves of Azolla. 2. The association between Anabaena and Azolla is an example of parasitism. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 only. Anabaena (a blue-green alga/cyanobacterium) forms a symbiotic relationship with the water fern Azolla. Azolla provides shelter and organic material, while Anabaena fixes atmospheric nitrogen, making it available for the fern. This is a form of mutualism, where both partners benefit. Other examples of symbiosis: Rhizobium with legumes, lichens (algae + fungi).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following are cryptograms ?
questions.explanation: Pteridophyta. It belongs to the vascular plant family. They reproduce through spores rather than seeds. Examples - ferns, horsetails and lycophytes. Four classes of pteridophyta - Psilopsida, Lycopsida, Sphenopsida, Pteropsida. Cryptogams - A flowerless and seedless group of plants having hidden sex organs. Three main divisions - Thallophyta, Bryophyta and Pteridophyte. They are the first-ever terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a perennial herbaceous plant in the nightshade family Solanaceae that is used in alternative medicine as an aid in treating arthritis pain, colds or hay fever?
questions.explanation: Atropa belladonna - It is a perennial herbaceous plant in the nightshade family Solanaceae. It is native to Europe, North Africa, and Western Asia. Arachis hypogaea is the peanut plant. Cynodon dactylon is Bermuda grass, a major tropical grass found in all tropical and subtropical areas. Cicer arietinum is the chickpea plant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which is the only living representative of Sphenopsida that has an underground, creeping and perennial rhizome that gives off aerial as well as underground branches?
questions.explanation: Equisetum - The aerial branches are herbaceous and usually grow to a height of 10-60 cm, but they can attain more height in some species. The pteridophytes are classified into Psilopsida (Psilotum), Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum) and Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the incorrect statement about Gymnosperms.

options.a: Gymnosperms are found as woody shrubs, trees or lianas and include no true aquatics and few epiphytes.
options.c: Gymnosperms are typically slow in terms of reproduction; up to a year may pass between pollination and fertilization and seed maturation may require 3 years.
options.d: Gymnosperms exhibit cones or storbili and naked seeds, but not flowers.

questions.explanation: Gymnosperms are flowerless, seed - producing plants. They belong to the subkingdom Embophyta. Examples - Cycas, Pinus, Araucaria, Thuja, Cedrus, Picea, Abies, Juniperus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sporophyte stage is dominant in which plant group?
questions.explanation: Vascular plants (Tracheophytes) are land plants containing specialized vascular conducting tissues (xylem and phloem). Examples - Trees, shrubs, grasses, flowering plants, and ferns.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match the plant groups with their characteristic features : Plant Group Characteristic Feature A. Angiosperm 1. Seeds enclosed in fruits, flowers present B. Gymnosperm 2. Naked seeds, cones, needle-like leaves C. Bryophyte 3. Non-vascular, depends on water for reproduction D. Pteridophyte 4. Vascular, reproduces via spores, no seeds
questions.explanation: A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4. Angiosperms: Seeds enclosed in fruits; flowers present. Gymnosperms: Naked seeds, often in cones, needle-like leaves. Bryophytes: Non-vascular; require water for sexual reproduction. Pteridophytes: Vascular plants; reproduce via spores, no seeds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which water-soluble pigment belonging to a phenolic group is present in pomegranate, eggplant, black carrots and red cabbage ?
questions.explanation: Anthocyanins. These are blue, red or purple pigments found in plants, flowers, fruits, and tubers. It appears as red pigment in acidic conditions and blue pigment in alkaline conditions. Phenolics - These are chemical components that occur as natural color pigments responsible for the color of fruits of plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Pteridophytes: 1. They are the first vascular plants with well-developed xylem and phloem. 2. Their leaves are known as fronds. 3. They reproduce by seeds enclosed within fruits. 4. Pteridophytes include Azolla and Cyathea. Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2 and 4 only. Pteridophytes are the first vascular cryptogams (plants without seeds but with xylem and phloem). They have roots, stems and leaves (called fronds). They reproduce by spores, not seeds. Examples: Azolla (smallest aquatic fern) and Cyathea (tree fern with entire trunks).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Plants which are grown under shade are known as :
questions.explanation: Sciophytes. Examples : Java Moss, Mountain Fern Moss. Monocots - A group of flowering plants belonging to the class Liliopsida or Monocotyledonae. Examples - Palms, Grasses, Orchids, and Lilies. Halophytes - Any perennial marsh plant that bears its overwintering buds in the mud below the surface. Examples - Salicornia europaea, Big Saltbush. Psammophytes - A plant that grows in sandy and often unstable soils. Examples - Agriophyllum squarrosum, Haloxylon ammodendron.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Bryophytes: 1. Bryophytes are non-vascular plants that include liverworts and mosses. 2. They are called amphibians of the plant kingdom because they grow on land but depend on water for sexual reproduction. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Bryophytes are non-vascular and include liverworts and mosses. They require water for fertilization even though they grow on land, hence called amphibians of the

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which is a multicellular filamentous green alga consisting of thin unbranched chains of cylindrical cells and found in floating masses near the surface of streams and ponds ?
questions.explanation: Spirogyra. Sargassum and Laminaria are the brown seaweed/algae found in brackish or salt water (rarely found in freshwater). Polysiphonia are red algae which are found in salt water. Ectocarpus is a genus of filamentous, marine brown algae. Chlorella is a genus of about 13 species of single-celled green algae of the division Chlorophyta.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which is a flowerless, spore - producing plant that is usually a thin, horn - like, or needle - like a capsule with spores that develops from a flat, green leaf ?
questions.explanation: Hornworts (bryophytes). It grows on rocks in tropical and temperate regions. Scientific Name - Anthocerotophyta. Chara (A green algae) - It belongs to the Characeae family, A multicellular organism usually thrives in freshwater. Celandine - It is a botanical extract derived from a plant of the Poppy family. Genus - Stylophorum. Riccia - It is a genus of liverworts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fungi can grow on which of the following items? I. Bread II. Pickles III. Leather IV. Clothes Select the correct option.
questions.explanation: I, II, III and IV. Fungi are eukaryotic (organisms whose cells contain a nucleus and other membrane - bound organelles) organisms. They grow in moist climatic areas where they get enough nutrition for their growth. The fungal spores are generally present in the air and grow on articles. Examples : Yeasts, smuts, mildews and mushrooms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Plants with green and tender stems are called .
questions.explanation: Herbs. Examples - Cabbage, Tomato, Mustard, Radish, Sunflower, Carrot. Trees have their branches in the upper part of the stem, much above the ground. Examples - Neem, mango, coconut. Shrubs have the stem branching out near the base. Examples - Rose, jasmine, lemon.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which among the following is an example of Angiosperm in Plant Kingdom?
questions.explanation: Tomato. The plant kingdom is classified into five subgroups - Thallophyta, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta, Gymnosperms, Angiosperms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which among the following are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom ?
questions.explanation: Bryophyte. These are land plants which require water for sexual reproduction. Hence, these are found mostly in moist places in close proximity to water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which among the following plant kingdoms are divided into dicotyledons and monocotyledons ?
questions.explanation: Angiosperms - Seed-bearing vascular plants with a well-differentiated plant body. The seeds are enclosed within the fruits. Examples - Mango, rose, tomato, onion, wheat and maize.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not a subgroup of the plant kingdom?
questions.explanation: Hemichordata. Kingdom - Animalia, Subkingdom - Eumetazoa. Plant Kingdom is further classified into subgroups of Thallophyta, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding ecological succession: 1. Lichens are pioneer species that can grow on bare rocks by secreting acids, which help in rock weathering and soil formation. 2. Orchids and lilies cannot colonize bare rocks directly, as they require soil and humus for their growth. Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Ecological succession is the natural, gradual process by which one group of living organisms (community) in an area is replaced by another, leading to the development of a stable and mature ecosystem (called climax community). Lichens are the first colonizers (pioneer species) in primary succession on bare rocks. They secrete acids that break down rocks into small particles, leading to soil formation. Orchids and lilies are advanced plants that grow only when soil is already present; hence, they cannot start succession on bare rocks.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Plants that do not have well - differentiated body design fall in this group. The plants in this group are commonly called algae. These plants are predominantly aquatic.
questions.explanation: Thallophyta. Thallophyta is classified into two subdivisions : Algae and Fungi. Examples - Spirogyra, Chara, Ulothrix, Ulva, Cladophora. Kingdom Plantae includes algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the correct statement about green algae.

options.a: Green algae usually have a soft cell wall made up of an inner layer of pectose.
options.b: Green algae usually have a rigid cell wall made of an inner layer of protein and an outer layer of fibre.
options.c: Green algae usually have a rigid cell wall made of an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose.
options.d: Green algae usually have a rigid cell wall made of an inner layer of fat and an outer layer of protein.

questions.answer_text: Green algae usually have a rigid cell wall made of an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose.
questions.explanation: Green algae have chloroplast and chlorophyll in their cells. Examples are Chlamydomonas, Volvox, Spirogyra, Ulothrox, Oedogonium and Chara.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify a marine alga that is used as food.
questions.explanation: Sargassum (gulfweed, sea holly) is a seaweed (macroalgae, family - Phaeophyceae (brown algae)). It is an edible, nutritious and rich source of bioactive compounds (vitamins, carotenoids, dietary fibres, proteins, and minerals). It is found in the Sargasso Sea in the north - central Atlantic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Most of the Chlorophyceae have one or more storage bodies called_____located in the chloroplasts.
questions.explanation: Pyrenoids are a protein body in the chloroplasts of algae and hornworts that are involved in carbon fixation and starch formation and storage of Chlorophyceae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about plants : 1. Plants with naked seeds, needle-like leaves, and cones as reproductive structures are called gymnosperms. 2. Angiosperms differ from gymnosperms because their seeds are enclosed within fruits. Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2. Gymnosperms (Gymnos = naked, Sperma = seed) : Seeds remain exposed, not enclosed in fruits. They have cones as reproductive structures and needle-like leaves to survive in extreme climates. Examples — Cycas, Pinus, Ginkgo. Angiosperms : Seeds enclosed inside fruits; flowering plants (dicots & monocots). Pteridophytes : Seedless vascular plants; reproduced by spores. Bryophytes : “Amphibians of plant kingdom,” need water for fertilization; grow in damp shady places.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a diverse group of aquatic organisms capable of photosynthesising?
questions.explanation: Algae (photosynthetic eukaryotic organisms) Yeasts are eukaryotic, single celled microorganisms. Protozoa are one - celled animals. A fungus (eukaryotic organism that includes microorganisms such as yeasts, molds and mushrooms).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the name of a protein that polymerizes into long chains or filaments that form microtubules, hollow fibres that act as the skeletal system for living cells?
questions.explanation: Tubulin ("heterodimer" protein). Elastin (protein) allows the skin to be flexible and bounce back to its original shape. Fibrinogen (protein involved in forming blood clots in the body). Ferritin is a blood protein that contains iron.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following statements about Funaria: 1. Funaria is a bryophyte with small, flattened leaves and root-like rhizoids. 2. Its sporophyte has a capsule with peristome teeth that help in spore dispersal. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both 1 and 2.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What do you call the water holding compounds produced in large quantities by marine brown and red algae?
questions.explanation: Hydrocolloids. Algin (red algae) and carrageen (brown algae) are some important sources of natural hydrocolloids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the mode of adaptation done by aquatic plants and animals where the osmotic concentration of the body fluids changes with that of the ambient air and water osmotic concentration?
questions.explanation: Conform. Plant Hormones and its Function: Ethylene - Fruit Ripening and Abscission, the dropping of leaves, fruits and flowers. Gibberellins - Break the dormancy of seeds and buds, promote growth. Cytokinin - Promote Cell Division. Abscisic Acid - closing of stomata and maintaining dormancy. Auxins - Involved in tropisms and apical dominance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following groups of plants are categorised as cryptogams ?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes and Thallophyta. Thallophyta - Plants that do not have well-differentiated body design fall in this group. The plants in this group are commonly called algae. Bryophytes - These are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom. The plant body is commonly differentiated to form stem and leaf-like structures. Gymnosperms and Angiosperms are called ‘phanerogams’.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the component that is unique only to prokaryotes.
questions.explanation: Mesosome is a special membrane structure, which is formed by the extension of the plasma membrane into the cell in a prokaryotic cell.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the plant that shows adaptation through leaves that are reduced to spines.
questions.explanation: Opuntia (cactus). Hibiscus (Orhul) can help boost your immune system. Mimosa (“Touch me not”) helps in the treatment of many disorders like piles, insomnia, diarrhea, etc.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following are non - vascular flowerless plants in the taxonomic division of Bryophyta?
questions.explanation: Mosses. A pine is any conifer tree or shrub in the genus Pinus of the family Pinaceae, it is the sole genus in the subfamily Pinoideae. Pea, (Pisum sativum), an herbaceous annual plant in the family Fabaceae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the nut of an oak tree called?
questions.explanation: Acorn, or oaknut, is the nut of the oaks and their close relatives (genera Quercus and Lithocarpus, in the family Fagaceae). The kola nut is the fruit of the kola tree (Cola acuminata and Cola nitida), indigenous to West Africa. Macadamia is a genus of four species of trees in the flowering plant family Proteaceae. The chestnuts are the deciduous trees and shrubs in the genus Castanea, in the beech family Fagaceae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Camellia sinensis is a plant that produces ______.
questions.explanation: Tea. Jute is extracted from the bark of the white jute plant (Corchorus capsularis) and to a lesser extent from tossa jute (C. olitorius). Sugarcane, (Saccharum officinarum), perennial grass of the family Poaceae, primarily cultivated for its juice from which sugar is processed. The two most popular coffee are - Coffee arabica (commonly known simply as "Arabica"), and Coffea canephora (known as "Robusta").

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match the columns. Column A (Plant Group) Column B (Example) i. Bryophyta a. Rose ii. Pteridophyta b. Pine iii. Gymnosperms c. Mosses iv. Angiosperms d. Selaginella
questions.explanation: i-c, ii-d, iii-b, iv-a. Bryophytes - liverworts, hornworts. Pteridophytes - Equisetum, Fern, Salvinia. Gymnosperms - Cycas, Pinus, Ginkgo. Angiosperms - Orchids, Corn, Tomato, and Hibiscus.

questions.subject: Biology
